chapters.title: Chapter 26 - 25: Simple Star Dust Liquid, Steady Progress
chapters.content:
Chapter 26: Chapter 25: Simple Star Dust Liquid, Steady Progress
Ron carefully observed this material, and with the help of the [Herb Recognition] ability, he could feel the special rhythm contained within it.
"Your acuity surprises me." Lady Allen noticed his focus, "Most people, when they first come into contact with this material, find it hard to detect the ’rhythm’ within."
Ron did not conceal his feelings: "Its frequency of fluctuations is quite similar to the basic meditation rune of spiritual power, but more..."
He paused, searching for the right word: "More fluid, lacking that sense of hindrance."
"A very apt description." Lady Allen nodded in satisfaction, "This is exactly why the Star Dust Liquid can stabilize spiritual power—it provides an ideal ’rhythmic template’ that allows spiritual power to flow more naturally."
She poured some Moonlight Crystals into a specially crafted mortar: "Now, I am going to teach you how to make a simplified version of the Star Dust Liquid, though its effect is not as good as the genuine article, it’s relatively easy to make."
For the next two hours, Lady Allen thoroughly taught every detail of the crafting process.
From the angle of grinding the materials, the control of heating temperature, to the guidance of energy fluctuations, each step required precise operation.
[Magic Potion Refining Experience Points +1]
[Basic Magic Potion Making Experience Points +1]
...
Finally, through Ron’s persistent efforts, a bottle of liquid emitting a faint silver glow was successfully concocted.
"The color is a bit lighter, but overall, it’s a success." Lady Allen picked up the bottle and observed it under the light:
"The effect of this simple Star Dust Liquid can last for about three days, enough for you to complete a full magic experiment."
She handed the bottle to Ron: "However, continuous use can cause slight dependency, it’s best to use it during critical breakthroughs."
Ron solemnly accepted the bottle: "Thank you very much for your guidance, Lady."
"No need to thank me." Lady Allen waved her hand: "I’m merely curious about the research results of that deceased apprentice; if you truly manage to perfect it, remember to show it to me."
After work ended, Ron left the herb store with the bottle of simple Star Dust Liquid.
The gains of today were not just this potion, but more importantly, a deeper understanding of magic potion refining, especially regarding how to guide energy fluctuations.
Walking on the way back to the dormitory, he continually recalled Lady Allen’s teachings in his mind:
"In magic potion refining, the most crucial factor isn’t the materials themselves, but how to harmonize the energies of different materials..."
This concept was so similar to his discovery in meditation.
Whether it was the flow of spiritual power or the fusion of magic potion materials, they seemed to follow some common law.
Ron returned to his room and began organizing his notes and thoughts.
Today, during the concoction of the simple Star Dust Liquid, his understanding of spiritual power deepened another level.
Especially the concept of the "ideal rhythm," which gave him new inspiration.
After completing his notes, he took out his training wooden sword and began practicing the "Corona Swordsmanship".
Every sword strike coordinated with the rhythm of his breathing, and his movements became increasingly fluid.
[Basic Swordsmanship Experience Points +1]
[Basic Swordsmanship Experience Points +1]
[Basic Swordsmanship Experience Points +1]
...
[Current Progress: Basic Swordsmanship (Beginner 28/50)]
In the evening, Ron reopened the "Basic Meditation Technique"; today’s magic potion refining experience gave him a new understanding of spiritual power dynamics, and all of this could be applied to meditation.
[Basic Meditation Begins]
In the Consciousness Space, he began attempting to simulate the fluid rhythm found in the simple Star Dust Liquid.
Though he couldn’t completely replicate it, the attempt itself brought considerable gains.
[Basic Meditation Experience Points +1]
...
[Current Progress: Basic Meditation (Beginner 48/100)]
"The progress is over halfway..."
Ron opened his eyes, looking at the data on the panel, and a trace of anticipation rose in his heart.
With the current progress, plus various profession bonuses, aiming to reach the skilled level of basic meditation within a month should not be an issue.
With this expectation, he tidied up the messy notes and books on the desk and prepared to rest.
Tomorrow would be another fulfilling day, and he needed to maintain enough mental state to face various challenges.
......
Ron’s spirit was somewhat lackluster.
Last night, he lay in bed tossing and turning, with the matters of Darrend replaying continuously in his mind.
After all, of the two souls fused within him, one had only just stepped into society not long before crossing over, and the other was a pampered count’s young master from childhood, neither had experienced such a terrifying killing field when survival was at stake.
Perhaps because of adrenaline induced by tension while being in the midst of it, there wasn’t any particular feeling.
But in the quiet of the night as he lay in bed, the twisted and struggling posture of the other, along with the whimper filled with reluctance and pain prior to death, made him find it increasingly difficult to calm down.
In fact, during the quick battle, Ron vaguely felt some prying eyes around him.
With the heightened perception after multiple body refinings and career changes, he could capture the faint signs of life from the rooms on either side of the corridor.
The candidate apprentices from the same period were hiding behind the doors, secretly observing everything happening outside through the door cracks.
But not until Holt arrived with the law enforcement team did they dare to open the doors and come out to accept inspection.
"Heh, this certainly aligns with the survival rules of the Black Mist Jungle."
He let out a cold laugh, as the weak would only cower in the shadows waiting for the strong to differentiate the victor, and then choose to attach themselves to the victor; such survival strategy was quite common here.
......
After finishing up with Lady Allen’s work and completing his daily exercises, the time was nearing dusk.
When Ron walked into the communal dining hall, he immediately sensed a different atmosphere.
There usually wouldn’t be many people at this hour, but today the hall was crowded.
More unusually, the candidate apprentices who usually lingered in threes and fives were gathering together, frequently casting glances towards him.
"That’s Ron? Heard he took down the mutated Darrend all by himself..."
"I heard he did it with a wooden sword..."
"And he’s still working at the herb store in the marketplace, even Lord Holt..."
The murmuring constantly reached his ears, and Ron, with an expressionless face, carried his tray and went to sit in a corner.Thɪs updatᴇd by NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
Just then, a tall, thin youth came over with a tray: "Ron, may I sit here?"
Ron looked up and recognized him as a fellow candidate apprentice who had arrived at the Black Mist Jungle in the same batch, but he couldn’t quite recall the name.
Before he could answer, two others joined in.
"Ron, I heard you obtained that set of spells Darrend researched? I wonder if I could get a look..."
"I have some Magic Stone Fragments here, if you could offer some guidance..."
Ron put down the black bread in his hand, his face indifferent: "Sorry, I’m very busy right now."
He stood up, holding his tray, intending to leave.
But more people surrounded him, speaking earnestly and animatedly.
As he was about to lose his temper, a familiar voice sounded from the side: "Clear the way."

chapters.title: Chapter 27 - 26: Marcus’s Threat, Monster?
chapters.content:
Chapter 27: Chapter 26: Marcus’s Threat, Monster?
Andre appeared at the restaurant entrance without anyone noticing. He still maintained his elegant noble demeanor, but there was an undeniable authority in his eyes.
The candidate apprentices exchanged glances and quickly dispersed.
Although noble status is not worth much here, as the Thirteenth Prince of the Faruk Kingdom, Andre’s influence is still considerable, at least to these candidate apprentices.
"These guys..." Andre walked over to Ron, chuckling, and said:
"Yesterday, when Darrend mutated, they all hid in their rooms and didn’t even dare to open the door. Now they’re all eager to show off."
Ron nodded slightly: "I really have no interest in interacting with these people, thank you for helping me out, Andre."
"Then let’s go, let’s find a quieter place." Andre invited with a smile:
"I just happen to have some freshly baked scones over there, much better than those black bread."
The two went to Andre’s room, where the setup was noticeably better than other candidate apprentices’.
On a small table were several steaming scones, with a pot of fragrant flower tea beside them.
"Speaking of which," Andre said with a laugh while pouring tea for Ron:
"I didn’t expect you to handle the mutated Darrend with a wooden sword, it’s a pity I wasn’t in the dorm area at the time, otherwise I should have come to lend a hand."
Ron took a sip from his teacup: "Just lucky."
"Lucky?" Andre looked at him playfully:
"You’ve become quite humble now. In the Royal Capital, if you had such achievements, you’d probably be boasting all over the city, wouldn’t you?"
Upon hearing this tease, Ron shook his head helplessly: "Those are things of the past."
"True enough." Andre took a bite of a scone, with a hint of exploration in his eyes:
"But honestly, your changes over this period are quite surprising. Training with the ’Crown Breathing Technique’ daily, soaking in the herb store to learn, and now you’ve conceived Sound Wave Magic..."
He paused, smirking faintly as he looked at Ron:
"If I hadn’t watched you step by step to where you are now, I’d suspect you’d been possessed by some powerful being."
"Possession?" Ron’s heart stirred, recalling his talent for "Dual Soul," but outwardly he remained calm:
"I just don’t want to wait here to die."
"Indeed." Andre’s expression suddenly grew serious: "But recently, you should be careful, especially with that Marcus."
Ron put down his teacup: "Why do you say that?"
"Although he’s just an ordinary elementary apprentice, his brother, close to becoming an Official Wizard, stands behind him—Oliver."
The blond boy’s voice became very low:
"In the school, Oliver is on the same level as Lord Holt, a seasoned advanced apprentice, and he’s made significant progress in Curse Witchcraft research."
He paused, seemingly choosing his words:
"With such a powerful support, Marcus dares to act without restraint. Most candidate apprentices he takes as servants end up as materials for his brother’s magic experiments."
Ron fell into contemplation; no wonder Emily met such a tragic end after turning to Marcus. Perhaps the outcome was already set when she chose that path.
"So..." Andre’s tone carried a warning:
"You’ve been too conspicuous lately. Although Marcus himself is merely an elementary apprentice, his brother Oliver is studying some incredibly bizarre special magic, seemingly related to spiritual power extraction."
He hinted:
"With the talent and potential you’ve shown now, you might very well catch their attention. Although Lady Allen and Lord Holt are here, it’s better to be cautious."
"I understand."
Ron nodded. He had long noticed that apprentice who liked collecting "beautiful servant" often casting a cold glance at him.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"But don’t worry too much." Andre resumed his elegant smile:
"With those two acquaintances of yours, he probably wouldn’t dare be too blatant. Besides..."
He looked at Ron probingly: "With the strength you’re showing now, even if he does make a move, he likely won’t gain much."
Ron smiled but didn’t continue the topic. Instead, he asked about something else: "By the way, any new news from the market?"
"You mean those black market merchants?" Andre shook his head: "Since Darrend’s incident, they’ve been more restrained. But..."
He gazed deeply out the window: "This calm probably won’t last long. As the assessment deadline approaches, those with nowhere left to go will surely take desperate measures."
"You’re right." Ron looked at the gradually darkening sky outside, calculating inwardly.
Darrend’s incident deeply affected him. Although his progress is quite smooth now, time is still pressing.
He needs to quickly grasp the conception of Sound Wave Magic and continue to enhance abilities in other areas.
"It’s getting late." Andre stood up: "I guess you have your matters to attend to?"
Ron nodded, tidying up his things to leave.
The next plan is to thoroughly study the notes Darrend left behind and attempt to advance this unfinished prototype of Sound Wave Magic to a new level.
At the door, Andre suddenly called his name: "Ron."
"What is it?"
"Do you know?" Andre’s face showed a playful smile: "I’m a bit grateful now that back in the Royal Capital, I never had any conflict with you."
Ron was momentarily stunned before understanding his meaning.
"Don’t worry, that playboy has already died on the way to the Black Mist Jungle." He half-turned, answering calmly.
"Indeed." Andre gave him a meaningful look: "In his place is a terrifying, unpredictable monster."
Ron couldn’t help but laugh at this description: "A monster, huh..."
In this world, it’s survival of the fittest. If one wishes to survive, perhaps turning into a monster is indeed necessary.
He turned and left Andre’s room, the hallway outside already shrouded in twilight.
The chaotic shadows alongside were like ghostly claws under the dim sky.
Still, curious glances were cast at him now and then, but Ron no longer cared.
What he has to do now is to continue getting stronger until he’s powerful enough to fully control his fate in this harsh world.
Any coveting and scheming will all turn to nothing in the face of power.

chapters.title: Chapter 28 - 27: "Sharpness" Trait, the Thief
chapters.content:
Chapter 28: Chapter 27: "Sharpness" Trait, the Thief
Sunlight streamed through the window lattice, filling the room. Ron had completed his meditation for the day and was preparing to practice the "Corona Swordsmanship".
Ever since he slew Darrend previously, his understanding of this swordsmanship had leaped to a new level.
Especially during that life-and-death struggle, he had more profoundly realized the subtlety of combining swordsmanship with the Breathing Technique.
"Let’s begin."
Ron adjusted his breathing, slowly raising the wooden sword in his hand.
Guided by the "Crown Breathing Technique," every movement of his carried a peculiar rhythm.
The first breath cycle, inhale for seven counts.
The wooden sword sketched a graceful arc from bottom to top, its tip pointing to the sky, as if a knight saluting the sun.
This was the "Ring of Dawn" move in Corona Swordsmanship, which emphasized dissolving attacks from all angles with a smooth arc.
The second breath cycle, hold the breath for three counts.
The sword parallel to the ground, held with both hands at the chest, forming a classic blocking posture.
This defensive stance, derived from ancient traditions, could redirect the enemy’s force to the surroundings.
The glow on the surface of the wooden sword gradually brightened, as the unique energy of the "Crown Breathing Technique" accumulated on the sword body.
The third breath cycle, exhale for five counts.
The sword momentum suddenly changed, shifting from a horizontal grip to a stabbing motion, with the sword tip swift like a snake unsheathing.
This move was named "Dawn Cross," a rare technique in Corona Swordsmanship that combined both offense and defense.
The sword blade swept a perfect cross in the air, capable of blocking incoming attacks while containing powerful counterattack strength.
As the full set of sword techniques was practiced, the wooden sword traced a beautiful arc in the air, perfectly matching his breathing.
Unlike the previous awkwardness, now every move appeared smooth and effortless.
[Current Progress: Basic Swordsmanship (Entry Level 49/50)]
"Just a bit more..."
Ron took a deep breath and began to perform the final set of sword techniques.
This was the most complex set of moves in the "Corona Swordsmanship," requiring multiple direction changes in a short time.
But this time, he found his body seemed to have an autonomous consciousness.
Every transition was just right, with seamless connection between sword momentums.
A set of moves completed smoothly, Ron could clearly feel some kind of change within his body.
[Basic Swordsmanship Breakthrough!]
[Basic Swordsmanship (Entry Level 50/50) → Basic Swordsmanship (Skilled Level 1/100)]
[Gained Additional Trait: Sharpness (Increased penetration when using sword techniques)]
He lifted the wooden sword, gently swaying it.Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs
The trajectory carved by the sword edge seemed to carry some invisible fluctuation, causing even the air to tremble slightly.
If he were to face Darrend again now, he could probably subdue him in a single encounter.
"Is this the difference between skilled and entry levels..."
Ron sighed to himself. After all, so-called "entry" and "skilled" evaluation standards were determined by the panel itself.
He felt that his swordsmanship, now merely at the "skilled" level on that panel, was already comparable to the acclaimed swordsmanship champions of the Kingdom.
Putting away the wooden sword, he began to prepare for today’s Body Refining.
As he delved deeper into the "Crown Breathing Technique," his familiarity with the process of this Breathing Body Refining increased.
[Breathing Body Refining Experience Points +1]
[Current Progress: Breathing Body Refining (Entry Level 43/100)]
He could now roughly differentiate this skill, as skills like [Breathing Body Refining] and [Basic Meditation] belonged to cultivation skills.
The distinction from other skills was that these required more experience points, and accumulating experience was harder than other skills, but breaking through brought cross-level power enhancement.
Even though progress was just halfway, Ron wasn’t in a hurry.
Body Refining differed from other skills, requiring a special oil, and needed time for body recovery after each refining session.
Additionally, rushing through foundational work often caused issues.
Having completed the Body Refining, Ron felt himself drenched in sweat and oil, deciding to head to the public bath for a wash.
Gathering his belongings, he was about to leave when he suddenly remembered Andre’s warning.
In this world, even going for a bath required caution, as bathing and using the bathroom were moments of greatest relaxation.
"Hopefully, today will be quiet."
Ron murmured to himself, pushing open the door and stepping into the corridor.
The heat in the public bath was steamy. He chose a spot in the corner and began washing off the oil and sweat from his body.
Warm water flowed over his body, gradually relaxing his tense muscles.
The recent Body Refining made his physique even more robust, especially the lines of his meridians and muscles became extremely distinct.
When several Candidate Apprentices entered the bathhouse and saw Ron’s figure, they instinctively avoided him, choosing positions farther away.
After the Darrend incident, coupled with Andre helping him out before, they were both in awe and somewhat fearful of this neighbor who could single-handedly take down an Aberration with a wooden sword.
After finishing his wash, Ron dressed and grabbed his toiletries, preparing to return to his room.
The corridor was quiet, with only a few dim Magic Crystal Lamps flickering.
Just as he was about to reach his room, a figure suddenly emerged from around the corner.
"Master Ron."
It was a well-dressed young woman, whom Ron recognized as one of Marcus’s servants.
Compared to other servants, her attire was more luxurious, with a gem-studded necklace around her neck.
"I’m Danni, Marcus’s personal maid," she said, slightly bowing, her voice gentle and pleasant:
"I heard that you work at Lady Allen’s herb store?"
Ron looked at her expressionlessly, "What’s the matter?"
"It’s like this." Danni gave a polite smile:
"My master has always been very interested in Magic Potion Making. I’ve heard you’ve achieved quite a lot in it recently. I wonder if you could..."
"No." Ron directly cut off what she was about to say.
He was too aware of these servants’ tricks, initially probing for information indirectly and then trying to find leverage.
Besides, he and Lady Allen had a confidentiality agreement; this kind of knowingly playing dumb act was rather clumsy.
"This..." Danni showed a troubled expression:
"If it’s a matter of price, we could negotiate. My master said that he is willing to offer if you’re willing to share some recipes..."
"Not interested, step aside."
Ron did not want to continue this meaningless conversation, bypassing her to leave.
At that moment, as he brushed past Danni, a cold glint flashed in her eyes, and a triumphant smile curled her lips.
Her slender fingers made a subtle gesture beneath her sleeve, silently uttering a spell at the same time.
This was a zero-ring spell called "Light-Handed Skillful Extraction," which had no offensive effect but was concealed and hard to detect.
A scarcely perceptible dark energy tendril seeped from her fingertips, drifting towards Ron like a wisp of smoke.
At this distance, even an experienced Apprentice, caught off guard, would find it hard to detect such an energy fluctuation.
While casting, her eyes were fixed tightly on the bulging pouch at her target’s waist.
Inside it were not only Magic Stone Fragments but also a few Potions Ron had painstakingly refined.
The energy tendril had nearly reached the pouch, just needing another moment to teleport the pouch into her hands with this theft spell.
Then, she would just need to falsely accuse him of attempting to steal her belongings, effortlessly...
—— At the critical moment, Ron’s Spiritual Perception suddenly captured that trace of bizarre energy fluctuation.
It was an extremely subtle discordance, like something repeatedly plucking at the strings of his spirit, making him irritable and unsettled.
Danni saw the young Apprentice, who had walked past her, suddenly stop in his tracks, and alarm bells rang in her heart.
But it was too late. The speed at which the wooden sword was drawn was astonishing, showing for the first time the terrifying power of Skilled Level "Corona Swordsmanship."
The sword light flashed, followed by a sharp, chilling scream.
Danni’s right hand, along with the dark energy touch, was sliced open, blood spraying out instantly.
She looked in horror at her severed wrist, about to scream again, when Ron, without any compassion, kicked her viciously away.
At the same time, he quickly caught his pouch that was about to fall to the ground, which contained his Magic Stone Fragments and Potions.
"If it weren’t for being in a public area with ’Surveillance Eyes’..."
Ron flicked the blood off the wooden sword, his gaze biting cold: "You’d already be a dead person."
Danni rolled to the ground, taking a long time to get up, her once magnificent dress tarnished with dirt and dust, a conspicuous footprint on it.
She struggled to hold her bleeding wrist, her elegance completely gone, leaving only fear and pain: "How dare you..."
At this moment, a cold voice suddenly came from the end of the corridor:
"Hmph, just like the rumors say, a brawn-for-brains brute!"
Marcus had no idea how long he had been lurking there, wearing a dark gray apprentice robe, a green badge on his chest gleaming faintly in the dim light.
"I’ve just witnessed with my own eyes how you cruelly injured my servant."
This somewhat ugly, short man’s face showed a grim smile:
"The School explicitly forbids internal fighting, especially you, a mere Candidate Apprentice, daring to lay such a heavy hand on the property of an Official Apprentice..."

chapters.title: Chapter 29 - 28: Battle with Marcus, the Power of "Sharpness
chapters.content:
Chapter 29: Chapter 28: Battle with Marcus, the Power of "Sharpness
Ron coldly looked at him: "Your servant intended to steal, I think the Law Enforcement Team can easily prove that."
"Oh?" Marcus squinted his eyes:
"Unfortunately, there’s only the three of us here now. By the time the Law Enforcement Team arrives, there might be only my and Danni’s testimony left."
As he spoke, his eyes radiated a strange light, and an invisible spiritual wave began to permeate the hallway.
This is the mental interference ability after breaking through to Apprentice, which can directly affect the target’s thinking and reactions, and it’s the essence of Wizards being stronger than other Extraordinary Systems.
In the Mortal Realm, this kind of spiritual interference is enough to throw any powerful Knight into confusion, and only the Demon Hunters, who are spiritually adept, can resist it.
At the Official Wizard Level, this spiritual wave is no longer interference; it’s a brain explosion.
Ron felt his thoughts blur just for a moment but quickly regained clarity.
He gripped his wooden sword tightly, and a flash of cold light appeared in his eyes.
Marcus was slightly surprised to see Ron resist the spiritual interference, but soon a sinister smile appeared on his face:
"No wonder you were able to kill the abomination, your spiritual power is indeed not weak, but..."Thɪs updatᴇd by N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
While Ron was in a brief daze, he began to gather a dark red energy in his hand, it was some kind of attack-type zero-ring magic.
"Do you think just relying on a broken wooden sword, you can withstand an Apprentice’s power?"
Ron held the wooden sword, his mouth slightly raised in a smile.
This sword had been replaced once, he had bought it at the Apprentice market a few days ago for six magic stone fragments, made from a rare wood called "Black Heart Iron Wood."
This tree, growing deep in the Black Mist Jungle, has wood hardness comparable to refined steel, and more rare, it contains a trace of natural anti-magic.
Ron calmly looked at Marcus, the Ironwood Sword gently spinning in his hand, the tip slightly lowered, posing a seemingly loose yet deadly stance:
"If we don’t try, how do we know it’s enough?"
Marcus’s eyes flashed with anger, his ugly face almost contorting into a ball.
The dark red energy in his palm continued to gather, now forming a fist-sized energy ball.
Electric arc-like dark light constantly flickered across the energy ball’s surface, an uncomfortable scorching atmosphere diffusing in the air.
"Die!"
Marcus shouted furiously, and the energy ball shot out.
This was his most proficient zero-ring magic "Burning Ball," with improved power by his brother.
The energy ball left a dark red trail in the air, the air it passed warped and deformed due to high temperatures.
Knowing he couldn’t dodge in time, just as the energy ball was about to hit, Ron’s body moved slightly.
The breathing rhythm of the Crown Breathing Technique perfectly blended with his sword techniques at this moment.
The moment he inhaled, the Ironwood Sword began to gather momentum; when he held his breath, the sword momentum condensed but did not release; as he exhaled, the sword light poured out like flowing water.
The skilled level Swordsmanship showed astonishing power.
"Buzz buzz buzz..."
The energy ball crashed head-on into the sword blade, making a heart-throbbing roar.
The dark red energy fluctuation spread like stormy waves, leaving scorch marks on the hallway walls.
But Ron’s Ironwood Sword remained unmoving.
The unique magical resistance of Black Heart Iron Wood, combined with the rhythm of Corona Swordsmanship, perfectly dissolved the frenzied energy.
Ripple-like patterns appeared on the sword’s surface, and after slicing the energy ball, it showed no significant damage.
"This...this is impossible!"
Marcus widened his eyes, the brutality on his face turning into disbelief instantly.
He knew too well the power of his attack, even weapons made of refined steel would continuously warp and deform under high temperatures.
But his shock wasn’t over yet.
Just as the energy ball was neutralized, Ron’s figure veiled like a ghost approached.
The Ironwood Sword drew a mysterious arc in the air, the sword momentum seeming light, yet containing a chilling power.
"Energy Barrier!"
Marcus hastily activated his protective magic.
A shield formed in front of him, faintly transparent with complex runes shimmering on the barrier.
As an Elementary Apprentice, the spells he mastered and could use in combat were actually very few; he originally had no ability to instantly cast such a solid energy shield.
But blessed with a powerful brother who fixed him with an auto-activated one-time magic model.
Marcus just secretly rejoiced, the next moment he felt a massive force strike on the shield.
Ron’s sword techniques seemed bland, yet concealed a unique rhythm of the Crown Breathing Technique.
Perfectly matching the sword momentum with breathing, each breath could drive the sword momentum change, making seemingly ordinary slashes possess some special penetration.
["Sharp" trait triggered, weak-point penetration! Basic Swordsmanship experience points +2]
"Crack!"
Spider-web-like cracks appeared on the shield’s surface suddenly.
Marcus felt a chilling sensation surge from his spine to the crown of his head, hurriedly retreating to increase distance.
His prideful spiritual shield was nearly shattered by a Candidate Apprentice’s single strike!
"You...how can you..."
His voice trembled slightly.
As someone with backing and who bullies the weak, he’d never suffered such humiliation within the school before; moreover, his opponent was just a Candidate Apprentice!
At this critical moment, a series of hurried footsteps sounded from the other end of the hallway.
"Law Enforcement Team, everyone stop!"
A team of law enforcement personnel in gray-white uniforms quickly approached, led by a somewhat listless-looking Advanced Apprentice wearing a sapphire badge.
He yawned casually, glancing around the scene.
"It’s you restless folks again."
The Law Enforcement Captain helplessly shook his head, "How many times has this made?"
Marcus immediately donned a respectful face:
"Honorable Captain Peter, this Candidate Apprentice assaulted my servant without cause, and moreover..."
"Shut up!" Peter impatiently interrupted him:
"Oliver is your brother, right? I know him, but that doesn’t mean you can cause trouble here."
He casually glanced at Danni’s severed hand and the bloodstains on the ground, lazily said:
"My judgment is—you both go to the Detention Room for half a month, just to cool off together."
Marcus’s face turned extremely ugly, unexpected that his opponent wouldn’t yield at all: "But..."
"No buts." Peter waved his hand, signaled other law enforcement personnel to step forward: "Take them away."
Just as the officers prepared to escort them, Peter suddenly whispered in Ron’s ear:
"Holt asked us to pay some attention to you, consider this a favor for him. However, best not to make such a commotion next time."
This commotion, it wasn’t what he wanted to create at all...
Ron felt a bit helpless, nodded slightly, and secretly marked Holt’s favor in his heart.

chapters.title: Chapter 30 - 29: Meditation Technique Breakthrough, [Wizard Apprentice]
chapters.content:
Chapter 30: Chapter 29: Meditation Technique Breakthrough, [Wizard Apprentice]
The ventilation window of the Detention Room was very small, only letting in a sliver of daylight.
But for Ron now, this was more than enough.
In this stone chamber of only about ten square meters, there was but a simple wooden bed, a bucket for waste, and a slanted wooden table missing a leg.
Yet this simple environment instead allowed him to focus more on cultivation.
"It’s actually a good place for quiet cultivation." Ron smiled self-deprecatingly.
The management of detainees by the Law Enforcement Team was still relatively lenient. Who knows if it’s because Holt exerted some influence behind the scenes.
Every day a somewhat adequate meal was delivered punctually to the Detention Room, and they were even allowed to keep some personal items—of course, these items had been strictly inspected to ensure they posed no safety hazards.
Ron took out Darrend’s notebook from his pocket and studied it carefully in the dim light.
Now he had a deeper understanding of the conception of Sound Wave Magic.
Especially through this period’s insight into "Rhythm," he noticed many details he hadn’t before.
[Sound Wave Vibration (Prototype) Experience Points + 3]
[Current Progress: Sound Wave Vibration (Prototype 87/100)]
"The key is here..."
He finally understood why Darrend had hit a bottleneck in his research.
In fact, the initial approach of using musical notes to perfect the Sound Wave Magic was undoubtedly correct, but this process was clearly laborious.
After repeated setbacks, Darrend, pressed by time, attempted to use external force to enhance the output of Spiritual Power.
By abandoning the correct path at the beginning, he ended up taking it to extremes, resulting in tragedy.
Just like how the Crown Breathing Technique imitates the movement of the sun, this Sound Wave Magic should also find its own rhythm.
Setting aside the notebook, Ron began his daily meditation.
In this environment isolated from the outside world, his mind reached an unprecedented level of concentration.
[Basic Meditation Start]
[Trigger Special Effect: Intense Focus—This Meditation Effect Enhances]
[Basic Meditation Experience Points + 1]
[Basic Meditation Experience Points + 1]
[Basic Meditation Experience Points + 1]
...
[Current Progress: Basic Meditation (Beginner 93/100)]
In the Consciousness Space, the rune composed of three arcs became increasingly clear.
Unlike the previous rigidity, the current rune seemed to carry a certain lively rhythm.
Every flow of Spiritual Power became exceptionally smooth, as if finding the most suitable path.
Ron could feel that he was not far from a breakthrough.
......
On the penultimate day in the Detention Room, Ron completed his routine morning meditation.
Two weeks of isolation from the world had brought his Spiritual Power to an unprecedented new height.
This barren and confined environment instead allowed him to focus more on exploring his inner world.
As he immersed himself into the Consciousness Space, the basic rune composed of three arcs became exceptionally clear, almost tangible.
Every arc slightly trembled, and each node emitted a gentle glow.
Ron could sense that he stood on some critical point, needing only a slight push to break through that invisible barrier.
He took a deep breath, concentrating all his attention on the rune.
Unlike the mechanical control of the past, this time he tried to resonate with the rune, allowing his consciousness to fully integrate into it.
At that moment, Ron suddenly understood—the essence of the Basic Meditation Technique lay not in controlling the rune, but in becoming the rune.
With this insight, the rune in the Consciousness Space began to vibrate intensely, emitting unprecedented brilliance.
Spiritual Power, like a flood breaking through a dam, surged and roared as if having found the most suitable way of flowing.
[Basic Meditation Breakthrough!]
[Basic Meditation Experience Points + 1]
[Basic Meditation (Beginner 99/100) → Basic Meditation (Proficient-max)]
[Acquired Additional Traits:
Spiritual Flow (when changing to a higher tier Meditation Technique, you can directly retain experience points to proficient level)]
Reaching proficiency seemed to be the limit for Basic Meditation, a slight sense of regret crossed his mind.
But the breakthrough did not stop there; Ron felt his internal Spiritual Power undergoing an unprecedented qualitative transformation.
The originally disorderly Spiritual Power was now spontaneously reorganizing according to some mysterious order, forming a more stable and purer energy structure.
In the Consciousness Space, streams of light began to emerge from the rune, weaving into a network in his consciousness world, forming a brand-new Spiritual Force Field.
This change was not only happening internally; Ron’s perception ability was also rapidly improving.
Every detail of the Detention Room, even the faint energy fluctuation outside the walls, vividly etched into his perception.
[Spiritual Power Qualitative Transformation Complete]
[Spirit: 1.6→2.0]
[Power Level Improvement: Knight’s Squire→Elementary Apprentice]
The crossing of the 2.0 threshold by his Spiritual Power meant he had officially reached the standard of an Elementary Apprentice.
The change was not just an increase in numbers but a qualitative leap in strength.
His consciousness became exceptionally clear, the speed and breadth of thinking greatly improved, and even his perception of the outside world became unprecedentedly keen.
More surprisingly, Ron suddenly found himself able to perceive a novel ability
—Spiritual Power was no longer just energy circulating internally but could now extend outward as waves, exerting tangible effects on living beings.
Was this the Spiritual Interference ability Marcus used on him that day?
Ron tentatively released a small stream of Spiritual Power outward, feeling its flow through the air.
The feeling was both wondrous and unfamiliar, as natural as breathing from birth, yet full of novelty.
Under his control, the Spiritual Power easily formed a weak interference wave radiating outward.
"I see..."
Ron murmured, realizing that this ability did not require deliberate learning but was an instinctual mastery when one’s Spiritual Power reached a certain level.
Just as a baby does not need to consciously learn how to swallow, a Wizard Apprentice would naturally learn how to release Spiritual Power outward.
The instinctual ability to interfere with spirits was very frightening to most Extraordinary Professionals who did not train in Spiritual Power, easily disrupting their thought processes.
But with opponents who are also apprentices, the specific effect depended on the disparity in Spiritual Power between the two.
In the space before him, a semi-transparent information panel automatically appeared:
[Spiritual Power Reached 2.0√]
