Almost the moment the voice sounded, Aksa moved.
His speed was astonishingly fast, almost unimaginable for such a large creature.
In the blink of an eye, he crossed more than half the arena, the giant sword slicing a dreadful arc, aiming straight at Ron’s waist to slice him in half.
Ron barely managed to raise his sword to block, but the massive impact still sent him flying, rolling a few times on the ground before barely steadying himself.
His arm trembled violently from the blow, nearly unable to grasp the sword hilt.
"Is this all the strength you have? Pathetic weakling..." Aksa snorted dismissively, advancing with relaxed steps.
Ron adjusted his breathing, enduring the painful ache in his arm, and once again assumed a defensive posture.
He understood that he was no match in strength and could only seek breakthroughs through skills and agility.
A second wave of attacks came quickly, this time Aksa used a series of rapid and precise thrusts, each directly targeting the vitals.
He tried his best to dodge and block, but was still hit multiple times, soon covered with small wounds.
"Your defense has gaps, your movements are too slow, and your sword grip is not firm enough."
Aksa critiqued coldly and professionally as he attacked: "As a swordsman, you are far off."
Ron felt a wave of frustration, knowing it was just a simulation battle, but being so thoroughly crushed still left him feeling deeply powerless.
The most disheartening part was that Aksa’s every comment was incredibly accurate, pointing directly at the weaknesses in his swordsmanship.
The battle lasted about ten minutes, leaving him exhausted and covered in wounds, while Aksa seemingly had not even broken a sweat.
"I expected you to perform better." The Tiger-man Weapon Master shook his head, disappointment in his eyes:
"Seems it was a complete waste of time, we can end this."
After speaking, he suddenly accelerated, the sword’s tip aiming straight for Ron’s throat.
At that critical moment, time seemed to slow down.
Ron watched the deadly sword edge approach, and a thought suddenly flashed through his mind—he had always tried to counteract strength purely with technique, but in the face of an absolute power gap, it was futile.
The real breakthrough was not in the perfection of moves, but in understanding the essence of the sword—all weapons exist to kill.
At that moment, he stopped thinking about technique and posture, his awareness entirely immersed in the connection between the sword and his body.
He forgot all his training, all his movement memories, everything accumulated fused into a new understanding.
[Basic Swordsmanship Experience Points + 1]
[Breakthrough! Basic Swordsmanship(Skilled 100/100)→Basic Swordsmanship(Master max)]
[Trait Advancement: Sharpness→Sharpness Unveiled (Weakness Insight Rate and Attack Speed Increased)]
Just as the sword was about to pierce the throat, Ron made a move that would normally be considered foolish...
He advanced instead of retreating, turning his body slightly to narrowly dodge the fatal blow.
At the same time, his longsword pierced Aksa’s defense from an incredible angle, directly targeting the opponent’s heart.
Aksa’s movements suddenly halted, a hint of surprise flashing in his amber eyes, followed by appreciation.
"A good strike, human." he said in a deep voice: "It seems you have understood the mystery of the weapon."
Ron stood in place, seeing his sword tip deflect before piercing Aksa’s chest, yet he felt an unprecedented clarity.
At this moment, he was no longer using the sword but had become the sword itself—sharp, precise, deadly.
"The essence of swordsmanship lies not in flashy moves, but in the determination to kill."
Aksa retracted his giant sword, with a hint of appreciation in his tone:
"At that moment, you succeeded. Had my strength and speed not greatly surpassed yours, I fear I would have been pierced through the heart by now."
Ron took a deep breath, feeling the upheaval within his body.
Achieving Master Level Basic Swordsmanship brought him not only an enhancement in skills but also a brand new understanding of swordsmanship.
"Thank you for your guidance, Master Aksa," Ron said sincerely, bowing to the other party.
The Tiger-man Weapon Master nodded, "You have a lot of potential, human! But this is only the beginning. The path to greatness is endless, keep moving forward."
As soon as he finished speaking, the entire arena began to twist and dissolve, reverting to that spacious circular room.
"Simulation battle concluded. Congratulations on your breakthrough," announced a mechanical voice. "Welcome to use the Simulation Battle Device again."
The iron door slowly opened, and Ron stepped out of the room to see Andre anxiously waiting outside.
"Ron! Are you okay?" The blonde boy quickly approached, worriedly examining Ron, "You were inside for nearly two hours; I was starting to worry."
"Two hours?" Ron asked in surprise, "It felt like only about ten minutes."
"Time perception in a simulation battle can be distorted," Andre explained. "How do you feel? Did you have a breakthrough?"
Ron nodded, a satisfied smile appeared on his face:
"Yes, I’ve gained some understanding of the essence of swordsmanship, it’s not just mechanically repeating actions, but integrating will into every strike."
He raised his hand, performing a simple sword-swing motion.
Though there was no actual sword in hand, the motion carried a chilling sharpness, as if slicing through the air itself.
Andre watched in astonishment: "This... this is completely different! Your swordsmanship was already good before, but now, it’s like you’ve become a different person."
"Indeed, it’s as if I’ve suddenly had an epiphany."
Ron laughed, "Thanks to this Simulation Battle Device, I had the opportunity to spar with a true Sword Master."
The two left the Central Tower, walking along the path back to the workshop, with Ron still immersed in the joy of his breakthrough.
"Those devices crafted by Alchemists are truly amazing."
He said to Andre, "They can construct such a realistic combat environment, even simulating touch and smell flawlessly."
"Yes, I heard it was a project jointly developed by several veteran Alchemists and Spiritual Mages years ago, aimed at training the School’s combat forces."
Andre nodded in agreement, "The School later shifted its research direction to more theoretical fields, leaving such practical devices neglected."
"But the potential of this technology is immense." Ron’s eyes gleamed with excitement, "If further researched, perhaps even more practical alchemy devices could be developed."
His thoughts raced, imagining various possibilities:
An alchemy furnace capable of precisely controlling heat, a device for automatically extracting essences from herbs, and devices that could aid in cultivation...
"I must accelerate my study of Alchemy," Ron decided inwardly, "Its potential is far greater than I imagined."Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
He glanced back at the training room enveloped in dust, "I plan to train there regularly, thirty magic stone fragments may be considerable, but compared to the gains it brings, it’s definitely worth it."
Back at the workshop, Ron eagerly took out his sword, wanting to personally experience the changes following his breakthrough.
As the Sword Momentum unfolded, he could clearly feel every move becoming smoother and more natural, as if the sword had become part of his body.
The Sharpness Unveiled trait imbued each strike with heart-stopping precision and sharpness, even the training wooden sword in his hand seemed to possess the power to cut gold and jade.
"This feeling... is amazing," Ron whispered, his eyes sparkling with excitement.
Mastery of Basic Swordsmanship has undoubtedly laid a solid foundation for his future breakthrough to become a Magic Swordsman.
Moreover, he was delighted that the breakthrough gained in this manner seemed more profound and internalized than merely relying on system prompts.
It’s not only an increase in Experience Points, but a true insight into the essence of skills.
In the corner of the room, Ailan quietly observed Ron’s sword practice, vines gently swaying, seemingly also rejoicing at their master’s breakthrough.
"Ailan, I’ve made a breakthrough," Ron said to the Tree Spirit, his face beaming with joy, "This is yet another important milestone since I came to the Black Mist Jungle."
The Tree Spirit’s vines formed words in the air: "Congratulations, master."
Ron smiled and nodded, carefully placing the sword back on the rack, beginning to ponder the next step of his plan.
With the experience from this breakthrough, he was ever more certain that some seemingly insurmountable obstacles might only be due to lacking the correct method or environment.
.........
Several days later, Ron’s workshop was brightly lit.
On the table lay the "Sun Flame Essence" formula scroll gifted by Magnus, and Ron was carefully configuring various materials based on the formula.
"Red Phosphorus Grass Powder, three units... Starfire Stone Marrow, two drops... Sun Orchid Root, four inches..." Ron silently recited the materials and quantities from the formula, his fingers deftly weaving between various herbs.

chapters.title: Chapter 118 - 108: Forest Nymph
chapters.content:
Chapter 118: Chapter 108: Forest Nymph
Ron focused intently on the cauldron in front of him, carefully controlling the heat.
The refining of the Forge Potion was far more stringent than that of ordinary Qi Blood Potions, not only because of the special ingredients, but because every step of the refining process had to be precise to the minutest detail.
"The amount of Red Phosphorus Grass Powder needs to be doubled compared to ordinary Qi Blood Potions, but it must be added in three parts, each twelve breaths apart..."
Ron murmured the key points of the formula to himself.
Even with the professional skills and experience of an Alchemist, the refining of such an advanced potion remained full of challenges.
The liquid in the cauldron changed color with the addition of each ingredient, from pale yellow, to orange-red, and now to a dim red with a faint golden glow, like molten metal..ɴet
"Ordinary Qi Blood Potions can only promote blood circulation and enhance muscle vitality, but the Forge Potion does more than that..."
While he carefully stirred the potion, he recalled Magnus’ notes next to the formula:
"The uniqueness of the Forge Potion lies in its ability to activate the ’positive energy’ within, providing extra assistance to those practicing Yang Attribute Techniques, which ordinary Qi Blood Potions cannot achieve."
Ailan stood nearby, her vines gently extending, carefully passing over a small bottle filled with the Starfire Stone Marrow.
"Thank you, Ailan." Ron took the bottle and smiled gratefully.
He opened the cap, letting the shimmering crimson liquid inside drip slowly into the cauldron, each drop sizzling slightly upon contact with the potion, producing small puffs of golden steam.
"Starfire Stone Powder is not a material used in ordinary Qi Blood Potions; it can guide energy towards a positive transformation."
Ailan’s vines formed a few words in the air: "Need to increase the heat?"
Ron observed the state of the potion carefully and shook his head slightly:
"No, the current temperature is just right; too high will destroy the activity of the Sun Orchid, and too low won’t fully integrate the Starfire Stone Powder."
Although he followed Magnus’ formula to the letter, Ron still incorporated his own understanding into the details.
For instance, the cutting method for the Sun Orchid Root—he didn’t use the traditional horizontal cut but opted for an angled cut, which better preserved the positive energy within.
Additionally, during the addition of the Starfire Stone Powder, he stirred the potion in a specific manner.
While not written in the formula, as a Professional Alchemist skilled in Magic Potion Making, he understood that this slight change allowed for a more even distribution of positive energy.
"The last step..." Ron took a deep breath and picked up the Powdered Heart of the Volcano Lizard.
The moment the heart powder touched the potion, the entire liquid in the cauldron suddenly began to boil, emitting a nerve-wracking "sizzling" sound, the golden light becoming even more dazzling.
Ron didn’t panic, but maintained an even preparation rhythm, his right hand continuous in stirring, while his left hand used specific gestures to guide the energy flow, another of his own improvements, which was never written in the formula.
Minutes later, the boiling gradually subsided, the potion stabilized, and finally presented an awe-inspiring flowing gold, glowing as if it were liquid sunlight.
[Special Effect of the Alchemist Profession Triggered!]
[Forge Potion Successfully Refined! Effect Slightly Improved Over Original Formula]
[Magic Potion Refining Experience Points +2]
"Success!" Ron looked with delight at the perfect Forge Potion before him, filled with a sense of accomplishment.
He carefully poured the potion into several already prepared Crystal Bottles, each emitting a faint golden glow, as if containing a small piece of sunlight.
"Ordinary Qi Blood Potions expire in about ten days, but this Forge Potion can maintain its activity for at least a month, though you’ll need to check their condition frequently when you have time."
Ron explained to Ailan, who was beside him, while labeling each bottle.
Then, he poured the remaining residues into a specially made small basin:
"Ailan, these residues should provide you with plenty of nutrients, you can absorb them."
The tree spirit gently nodded, her roots stretching towards the pile of faintly glowing residue.
This wasn’t the first time.
In the recent potion refinements, Ron noticed that Ailan seemed to particularly enjoy absorbing the remaining residues, especially those containing plant essences or energy remnants.
What surprised him more was that after Ailan absorbed these residues, she seemed to undergo some subtle changes.
Initially, these changes were subtle—the color of the vines became deeper, branches more resilient, and roots extended further.
But gradually, the changes became more pronounced.
The initially light green skin became more lustrous, vines more flexible and powerful.
Ailan’s form started to slowly transform into a humanoid shape, the previously rough outline of the tree trunk gradually forming a gentle feminine silhouette.
Its branches no longer just plant tissue but began forming textures akin to hair and garments, with woven emerald leaves like a beautiful green dress.
Ron pondered as he watched Ailan absorb the residues.
The vines would glow faintly upon contact with the residues, as if performing a kind of energy conversion.
The magical power fluctuations emanating from her also became much more intense compared to when she first arrived, no longer weak and passive, but active and rhythmic, like a silent song of life.
"Could this be what Magnus meant with those words before he left?"
Ron recalled the elder alchemist saying: "Treat it well, and it will repay you more."
He remembered searching the library for information about the bloodline origins of the tree spirits. According to legend, the ancestors of tree spirits came from the Divine Era’s "Forest Nymphs."
They were transcendent beings with divine nature, known as "fairies of the forest," and while not strong in combat, they possessed many incredible talent abilities.
Forest Nymphs could communicate with plants, sense the pulse of the earth, and even foresee futures related to nature.
In some ancient texts, Forest Nymphs are described as the kin of the Earth Mother Goddess, responsible for maintaining the balance and vitality of the forest.
If these legends are true, then the changes happening to Ailan might be a return to the form of her ancestors?
"Ailan, how... do you feel?" Ron asked tentatively.
Ailan looked up, and in those once calm eyes, there seemed to be a hint of liveliness. Vines spelled out letters in the air:
"Very warm, like basking in the sunshine."
This answer was longer and more emotional than usual.
Ron nodded slightly, more convinced of his hypothesis.
Ailan was undergoing some transformation, and the energy in the potion residue was the catalyst.
"If such effects can be produced by potion residue, then what about the more compatible bloodline activation agents..."
However, the recent changes in Ailan had slowed, possibly because the energy stimulation from the residue no longer had much effect.
Thinking about it, if the tree spirit’s bloodline concentration were high enough to be easily activated, the slave merchants would not have let him get such a bargain.
However, at least this transformation proved that the tree spirit had deep bloodline potential to be explored...
Ron’s thoughts raced, and he began to form plans in his mind.
Tomorrow, he plans to enroll in new courses in the teaching area.
After all, working behind closed doors always yields limited results, and the systematic teaching provided by the school can help him master new knowledge faster.
"Alchemy Practice" and "Elemental Affinity" are the two courses he is most interested in.
With this in mind, Ron focused his attention back on the work before him.
There were still a few customer orders for magic potions to be completed today, and time waits for no one.
......
Early the next morning, Ron arrived at the school’s teaching area.
The buildings here were much more magnificent than in the dormitory area, with towering stone towers and suspended corridors connecting the various buildings, creating a spectacular sight.
He walked towards the registration area with a well-organized course list.
The center of the teaching area was an octagonal hall, where sunlight filtered through the stained glass ceiling, creating kaleidoscopic beams of light.
In the center of the hall stood a large three-dimensional star map, surrounded by registration areas for various courses.
When Ron walked to the enrollment area, he unexpectedly saw a familiar figure—Holt, a regular at the herb store since his candidate apprentice days and one of the Law Enforcement Team’s leaders.
At this moment, Holt stood at the registration desk for "Advanced Elemental Magic," handing over Magic Stone Fragments.
He wore the standard dark gray uniform of the Law Enforcement Team, with a special badge representing authority on his waist, exuding an aura that was both restrained and powerful.
Noticing Ron’s gaze, Holt turned his head, his sharp eyes narrowing slightly, then showing a hint of surprise that turned into a look of approval.
"Alchemist Ron," he approached with a courteous smile, his voice deep and steady: "I heard you recently became a Professional Alchemist. It seems the news is true."
"Lord Holt." Ron responded politely with a slight nod: "Long time no see."
Holt’s gaze lingered briefly on Ron’s Alchemist Badge, then swept over his overall magic power fluctuations, as if assessing something.
"You shouldn’t address me with such respect now."
Holt said softly: "You are now a Professional Alchemist, and as I know, certified personally by Master Magnus. In the school system, we are now equals."
This direct change in attitude surprised Ron a bit, but he soon realized that in a place like the Black Mist Jungle, strength and ability are the keys to everything.
Holt was obviously a very rational and pragmatic person.
"Alright, I intend to enroll in ’Alchemy Practice’ and ’Elemental Affinity’ courses."
Ron adjusted his approach and got straight to the point: "Does Senior Holt have any insights on these courses?"
"What a coincidence, I just graduated from the ’Elemental Affinity’ course not long ago."
Holt said, leading Ron to the registration desk with a rare warmth in his tone:
"If you’re looking to broaden your knowledge, these two are indeed excellent choices."
They arrived at the registration desk for "Alchemy Practice," where the responsible apprentice looked up wearily.
"Name, authority rank?" the apprentice asked mechanically.
"Ron Ralph, Professional Alchemist." Ron handed over his badge.
The apprentice’s attitude immediately became respectful:
"Alchemist Ron, according to the discount regulations, your tuition fee for ’Alchemy Practice’ after the discount is thirty-five pieces of Magic Stone Fragment for one month. Do you have any special requirements?"
"No special requirements, thank you." Ron replied, while taking out the prepared Magic Stone Fragments.
Just then, Holt suddenly spoke: "Assign him to Master Thompson’s class."
The apprentice hesitated as he looked at the Law Enforcement Team badge on Holt’s chest, then nodded: "Master Thompson’s class... okay, I will arrange for that."
After they walked away, Ron looked at Holt in confusion: "Master Thompson?"

chapters.title: Chapter 119 - 109: Clues to Profession Fusion
chapters.content:
Chapter 119: Chapter 109: Clues to Profession Fusion
"One of the best Alchemy teachers in the academy, though his Spiritual Power level is only that of an Advanced Apprentice, he is a seasoned Alchemist."
Holt whispered as he guided Ron towards the "Elemental Affinity" registration desk:
"His teaching isn’t bound by textbooks and focuses more on practical application. For someone who is already a Professional Alchemist, this method of teaching is more efficient."
Ron nodded gratefully, "Thank you for the recommendation."
Holt slightly shook his head, "No need to thank me. Within the school, we are all happy to provide some guidance to those who truly have talent."
After completing the "Elemental Affinity" registration, the two walked out of the hall and came to a relatively quiet small courtyard.
A gentle breeze blew past, bringing with it a faint scent of flowers.
"Ron," Holt suddenly stopped and his tone became more serious, "How much do you know about ’Grace’?"
This direct question startled Ron.
"Grace" is one of the secret knowledges in the Wizard World, usually not openly discussed among apprentices.
Holt bringing it up suddenly was clearly testing him.
Ron decided to respond cautiously, "Lady Allen mentioned a few things."
Holt’s gaze flickered slightly, then he nodded, seeming satisfied with the answer.
"As expected," he said softly, a sense of relief in his voice:
"Lady Allen rarely imparts this core knowledge to ordinary apprentices. It seems she holds you in high regard."
He looked around, ensuring there was no one else, then continued:
"Since you’re aware of the existence of ’Grace’, there is some information that might be useful to you."
"Many courses in the school, on the surface, are teaching knowledge, but in reality, they are also looking for apprentices with the potential to provide ’Grace’."
Holt explained, his voice low and calm:The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
"Like the two courses you’ve registered for—they both have advanced options. After completing the basic courses, the masters will selectively offer more in-depth guidance based on the performance of the students."
Ron nodded thoughtfully, which was roughly consistent with what he had learned from Lady Allen.
"What’s most noteworthy," Holt continued, his eyes flashing a rare enthusiasm:
"In the advanced course of ’Elemental Affinity’, the master will offer standout students a Magic Model for free."
"A Magic Model?" Ron raised an eyebrow, intrigued by this information.
"Yes, but not the kind of complete model that can be used directly," Holt explained:
"It is an incomplete prototype, the master’s personal idea."
"I see," Ron realized:
"So that’s one of the mechanisms of ’Grace’—the master provides unfinished ideas and prototypes, and the students improve them through their understanding and efforts. The growth and breakthroughs that occur in this process feedback to the master."
Holt’s eyes showed a hint of approval:
"You understand quickly. In fact, this is why there are so many academic journals freely circulated within the Wizard World, containing a large number of spell prototypes and theoretical ideas that need completion."
"By inspiring and inducing others to perfect one’s immature ideas, more ’Grace’ can be obtained."
Ron mused, "It’s a win-win strategy."
"Exactly," Holt nodded:
"Unfortunately, the Black Mist Jungle is too secluded, and those more valuable academic journals rarely circulate among apprentices. This is also one of the reasons many apprentices choose to take paid courses—it’s their only way to access high-quality extraordinary knowledge."
The two continued walking along the stone path, the flowers and trees around them gently swaying in the breeze.
"However, I noticed many people are simultaneously learning multiple wizardry skills."
Ron expressed his doubt, "Doesn’t that scatter one’s focus?"
Holt shook his head, offering a knowing smile:
"That’s a common misconception. Actually, all wizardry skills are essentially interrelated, especially at the foundational theoretical level. Once you master one skill, the speed of learning other related skills will greatly increase."
He paused, seeming to ponder how to simply explain the complex concept:
"Take for example—Magic Potion Making and Alchemy both involve the transformation of material properties and Energy Conversion, but they are applied in different directions. An Alchemist with mastery in Magic Potion Making will learn Alchemy much faster than the average person."
"That puts my mind at ease," Ron chuckled lightly, "I’ve always worried that learning multiple skills at once would overly divide my attention."
Holt glanced at the sky, nodding slightly:
"It’s getting late, I still have tasks with the Law Enforcement Team to handle. Your first ’Alchemy Practice’ class should be this afternoon, good luck."
"Thank you for the information and advice, Senior Holt."
Ron said sincerely, "If there’s anything I can help with in the future, feel free to send someone to find me."
"No need to say that. Within the school, knowledge sharing benefits both sides. Next time I have questions about Magic Potion Making, I hope I can consult you any time as well."
Holt waved his hand, a hint of ephemeral regret in his eyes:
"To be honest, I’ve been studying Magic Potion Making for nearly ten years, yet I still consider myself just a more advanced Magic Potion Apprentice, far from being a Professional Alchemist. That might be the huge gap between the average and the true genius..."
Watching Holt leave, Ron’s mind was filled with thoughts.
"Alchemy Practice, Elemental Affinity..." he muttered to himself: "Adding in the research on bloodline activation, this month is going to be busy."

chapters.title: Chapter 120 - 109: Clues to Profession Fusion_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 120: Chapter 109: Clues to Profession Fusion_2
In the afternoon, Ron arrived on time at the "Alchemy Practice" classroom.
The classroom was a spacious hexagonal space, with a massive alchemy workstation in the center, surrounded by twelve smaller student stations.
Each station was equipped with basic alchemy tools and some commonly used materials.
The trainees arrived one after another, most of them wearing the gray robes of an Elementary Apprentice, with only a few wearing professional badges.
Ron noticed that among the trainees present, the youngest still seemed several years older than him.
Once everyone was seated, an elderly man with silver hair entered the classroom.
He wore a dark brown robe, with silver trims on the cuffs and collar, clearly identifying him as the lecturer here.
"Welcome to ’Alchemy Practice’." The old man’s voice was deep and powerful:
"I am the professional Alchemist, Thompson, and I will be guiding you into the world of Alchemy over the next month."
His gaze swept over every trainee present, and when he looked at Ron, a hint of interest flashed in his eyes.
"Today, we will learn the first basic skill of Alchemy—Material Purification,"
Thompson said, while taking out what appeared to be an ordinary black stone from the inside of his robe:
"Ensuring the purity of materials is the most basic requirement before any alchemical transformation."
He placed the stone on the workstation and made a peculiar gesture above it with his hands, causing the stone’s surface to start glowing, gradually separating into different colored substances.
"A seemingly simple stone actually contains various elemental components," Thompson explained: "The first step in Alchemy is to learn to identify and separate these components."
For the next two hours, Thompson explained in detail the basic principles of Material Purification and several common methods, personally demonstrating some fundamental operations.
Ron focused intently, recording every detail. As an Alchemist, he already had a deep understanding of materials, making it relatively easy to learn the basic knowledge of Alchemy.
"Now, each of you has a piece of stone to work with," Thompson announced: "Please attempt to use the methods I’ve just taught to perform preliminary elemental separation."
Ron looked at the gray stone in front of him and took a deep breath.
He had previously read similar operational descriptions in "Alchemy Basics," but this was his first time performing it.
He followed the gestures he had just learned, simultaneously mobilizing his Spiritual Power, and carefully touched the stone’s surface.
At first, there was no response.
Ron adjusted his method of outputting Spiritual Power, attempting to guide the energy more gently.
Suddenly, the stone’s surface began to glow faintly, and strands of different colored lights appeared.
[New Skill Detected]
[Alchemy (Beginner 1/50)]
[Alchemy (Beginner) Experience Points + 1]
"Very good, Ron the Alchemist." Thompson’s voice suddenly came from behind:
"Your control of Spiritual Power is very precise, which is the most critical fundamental in Alchemy."
Ron was somewhat surprised that the old man remembered his name, but he still humbly nodded in thanks:
"Thank you for your guidance, Master Thompson. Magic Potion Refining also requires precise control of Spiritual Power, which might give me some advantage."
"Magic Potion Making and Alchemy indeed have many similarities,"
Thompson agreed, his eyes shining with approval:
"Both seek to achieve specific purposes through changing the form of matter, but they focus on different aspects."
The old man pointed to the few lines of light appearing on the stone:
"Do you see these? The red represents the Fire Element, the blue is the Water Element, and these tiny golden particles are the extremely rare Light Element."
Ron observed carefully and indeed felt that the energy fluctuations emitted by the different colored lights were distinct.
Thompson seemed pleased with his ability to comprehend, and continued to explain:
"The next step is to learn how to separate these elements and preserve them. In advanced courses, we will teach you how to recombine these elements to create new substances with specific properties."
"Is that the core of Alchemy?" Ron asked, a questing light in his eyes.
"You could say that," Thompson nodded slightly:New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"Decomposition and recombination, understanding the makeup of the world, and then reshaping it according to your will—that is the essence of Alchemy."
The old man’s words reminded Ron of the Simulation Battle Device, undoubtedly a product of Alchemy combined with Spiritual Magic, creating a virtual yet real experience by altering the perception of reality.
"Master Thompson."
Ron hesitated for a moment, but then asked a question lingering in his mind: "How much do you think Alchemy can change reality?"
Thompson’s eyes flashed with a deep light as he looked at Ron meaningfully:
"That’s a good question. Where is the limit of Alchemy? This is the ultimate question that every Alchemist explores."
He slowly said:
"Some say Alchemy can only change the form of matter; others believe it can touch the essence of reality. If one day you can fuse all three major Wizardry Skills into one, becoming a legendary [Ancient Alchemist], you might find the real answer."
[Ancient Alchemist] requires fusing all three major Wizardry Skills into one?
The information provided by the other party fully piqued Ron’s interest.
Perhaps the advancement path of future high-tier professions lies in this kind of fusion... he speculated to himself.
In the subsequent time, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to learning Alchemy Basics, not missing any detail.
[Alchemy Experience Points + 1]
[Alchemy Experience Points + 1]
[Alchemy Experience Points + 1]
...
[Current Progress: Alchemy (Beginner 6/50)]
By the end of the class, Ron’s understanding of this new skill in Alchemy had also reached the preliminary stage.
It was indeed like Holt had said before, these Wizardry Skills are transferrable, as his foundation in Magic Potion Making allowed him to quickly get started.
"Today’s class ends here."
Thompson concluded:
"I hope you all review what you learned today when you go back. In the next class, we will learn how to preserve the separated elements and study their basic properties."
The trainees began to leave one after another, and Ron was about to pack up his tools when Thompson approached him.
"Ron the Alchemist."
The old man’s voice was deep: "You seem to have an extraordinary understanding of Alchemy. If you’re interested, you can stay after class for some extra practice."
Ron understood this was a rare opportunity—Master Thompson had obviously noticed his potential and was willing to offer more guidance.
"Thank you very much for your proposal, Master Thompson." He said sincerely: "I would love to take this opportunity."
Thompson nodded in satisfaction: "Very well. Alchemy is a field that requires constant practice, theory alone is far from enough."
After the other trainees had left, Thompson took out a small metal box from inside his robe: "I think you might be interested in this."
Ron took the box and carefully opened it, revealing a crystal that emitted a faint purple glow inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 121 - 110: Philosopher’s Stone
chapters.content:
Chapter 121: Chapter 110: Philosopher’s Stone
"What’s this?" he asked curiously.
Thompson explained softly:
"An attributeless energy crystal, one of the fundamental materials of alchemy, able to store and transform various elemental energies. Alchemists often use it as a core material to construct various alchemy devices."
Ron observed the crystal in his hand curiously, feeling a subtle energy fluctuation emanating from it.
"For beginners, this type of crystal is an excellent tool for practicing elemental manipulation."
Thompson continued: "It can intuitively reflect whether your spiritual power output is precise."
Ron carefully channeled his spiritual power into the crystal, which immediately lit up with brighter purple light and began to vibrate slightly.
"Very well controlled," Thompson praised:
"Now, try to guide this energy in a specific direction—imagine it forming a vortex within the crystal."
Ron closed his eyes, focusing on sensing the energy flow within the crystal, guiding it according to Thompson’s instructions.
The glow of the crystal began to change, presenting spiral light patterns from the center outward.
[Alchemy Experience Points + 1]
"Outstanding." Thompson smiled and said, "It seems you truly have a remarkable talent for spiritual control, and you are an excellent alchemist yourself, so..."
He pondered for a moment, a hint of hesitation flashing in his eyes, as if considering whether to share some secret knowledge.
Finally, he decided to continue:
"Do you know? Although the attributeless energy crystal is very practical, in the ultimate pursuit of alchemy, it is but the most basic step."
"Ultimate pursuit?" Ron asked curiously.
Thompson lowered his voice, his tone becoming mysterious and reverent:
"The Philosopher’s Stone—it’s the ultimate dream of all alchemists. It’s said to create anything the heart desires, even things that don’t exist in the world."
Ron’s eyes lit up: "Does such a thing really exist?"
"This question has troubled countless alchemy masters for several eras."
Thompson sighed lightly: "Some call it a fictional myth, some claim to have glimpsed its true form, and others believe it is not truly a material, but a realm or state."
He took a book from the shelf and turned to a page, where a complex circular pattern was drawn, with a red crystal at the center surrounded by countless runes and lines.
"The ancient tablet ’The Jade Record’ once recorded:
’The Philosopher’s Stone, neither stone nor material, born of nothing, dies in reality. It is both the beginning of all things and the ultimate destination. He who masters it holds the power to rewrite reality; he who seeks it may gain eternal wisdom, or fall into eternal madness.’"
Thompson closed the book, his gaze deep:
"It’s said that the Philosopher’s Stone can transform base metals into pure gold, cure all diseases, and even grant the bearer immortality. But more alchemy masters believe its true power lies in crossing the bounds of reality and the void, creating miracles that should not exist."
His words carried a hint of warning:
"However, all records of those who pursued this item inevitably recount terrifying costs—most ancient alchemists who touched upon the ultimate secrets lost their sanity or completely disappeared in the river of history."
Ron pondered: "It sounds very much like symptoms of deep spiritual contamination..."
"Keen observation," Thompson nodded appreciatively:
"Indeed, some scholars speculate that the Philosopher’s Stone may be related to some ancient chaos existence, and perhaps the pursuers’ spirits couldn’t withstand the collapse when facing that existence."
He returned the book to the shelf and resumed his calm tone:ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
"In any case, as a beginner, you just need to master basic alchemy techniques. As for those ultimate secrets, consider them after you become an official wizard. After all, secrets that even official wizards spend their entire lives unable to reach are too distant for an apprentice."
The extra guidance lasted for nearly half an hour, and by the end, Ron felt his understanding of alchemy had progressed further.
But he also felt a strange unease about that legendary Philosopher’s Stone, as if it was a taboo that should not be touched by mortals.
Next was the "Elemental Affinity" course, which was vastly different from "Alchemy Practice" but equally captivating.
The classroom was a circular space with walls painted with complex runes representing various elements.
At the center was an elemental pool, where different elemental powers flowed freely, creating a dazzling spectacle.
The instructor was Laila, an advanced apprentice, a graceful woman with a long grey robe embroidered with silver edges, long hair cascading to her waist, and holding a magic wand inlaid with a water-blue gemstone at the top.
"Elemental affinity is a fundamental ability for every wizard." Laila’s voice was as gentle as a breeze:
"No matter what specialization you choose in the future, understanding and mastering the essence of elements will benefit you for a lifetime."
The first lesson primarily explained the basic traits and identification methods of different elements.
Laila demonstrated through the elemental pool, showing students the traits of foundational elements like fire, water, earth, wind, light, and darkness.
"Close your eyes, feel the elemental fluctuations around you."
Laila instructed: "Each element has its unique frequency and rhythm. Learning to identify them is the first step to mastering elemental affinity."
Following the instructions, Ron closed his eyes, carefully extending his spiritual power outward.
Initially, he could only sense a chaotic energy fluctuation, but as his focus increased, the fluctuations of different elements gradually became clear.

chapters.title: Chapter 122 - 110: Philosopher’s Stone (2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 122: Chapter 110: Philosopher’s Stone (2)
The Fire Element is lively and jumping, the Water Element is gentle and flowing, the Earth Element is stable and solid, the Wind Element is light and graceful...
[New Skill Detected]
[Elemental Perception (Beginner 1/50)]
[Elemental Perception Experience Points +1]
"Everyone has an inherent elemental affinity."
Laila continued to explain, "Some people are naturally close to the Fire Element, while others are more compatible with the Water Element. Finding your most compatible element is the key to unleashing your potential."
During the class training session, students needed to try to guide various elements from the Elemental Pool.
When it was Ron’s turn, he found that guiding the Light and Fire Elements was particularly smooth, as if intuitively making those golden and red light points swirl around his fingertips.
"Oh... this is rare." Laila observed Ron’s performance, a hint of surprise flashing in her eyes:
"Besides the Fire Element, you seem to have a natural affinity with the Light Element."
She looked at Ron thoughtfully, "Typically, those with Light Element affinity often come from families with extraordinary bloodlines. What about your family background...?"
"I come from an ordinary Bloodline Knight family in the Faruk Kingdom."
Ron replied somewhat reservedly, "As far as I know, there’s no particularly prominent Light Element bloodline heritage in my family."
Laila nodded slightly, not feeling surprised, "The mysteries of bloodlines sometimes span several generations before they manifest. Keep practicing, you obviously have an extraordinary talent in this area."
After class, Ron pondered over Laila Master’s words.
His affinity with the Light Element might be related to the special talent "Sun’s Protection (Fragment)," which also vaguely aligned with the "Sun Flame Dragon" mentioned by Andre.
Leaving the teaching area, Ron decided to go to the library to further research this area of knowledge.
The library remained serene and peaceful, with a soft light filtering through the tall stained-glass windows, illuminating the dust floating between the ancient bookshelves.
Ron came to the Guiding Stone, clearly expressing his needs: "Extraordinary Bloodlines, Alien Race Extraordinary Professions."
The light points guided him to a section dedicated to racial studies and bloodline research materials.
He took a few books from the shelves that seemed most relevant:
"Extraordinary Bloodline Encyclopedia," "Examination of Extraordinary Professions of Alien Races," "Dragon Descendant Bloodline Origin," and "Ancient Bloodline and Modern Mutation."
Finding a quiet corner to sit down, Ron began reading seriously.
Turning to "Examination of Extraordinary Professions of Alien Races," he discovered that apart from their innate bloodline talents, each race has developed a corresponding system of extraordinary professions:
"The Beast Race’s ’Weapon Master’ specializes in various weapon uses, able to quickly adapt to different weapon types in battle..."
"The Forest Elf’s ’Natural Priest’ possesses various innate natural attribute-like magic techniques;
Above them, there are the royal family guarding the Life Tree - Moon Elves, but they are now rarely seen..."
"The Dwarf’s ’Rune Artisan’ can create special objects that are lasting and stable..."
"The Sea Siren’s ’Tide Singer’ manipulates water flow through special melodies and can even summon terrifying storms that sweep over everything across the sea surface..."
"Extraordinary Bloodline Encyclopedia" details the known types of extraordinary bloodlines and their level divisions:
"Bloodlines are generally divided into six ring levels based on their purity and strength: Copper Ring, Silver Ring, Golden Ring, Star Ring, Moon Ring, and Sun Ring bloodlines, named after celestial bodies and metals, symbolizing their power levels and rarity."
"Copper Ring bloodline can only provide slight enhancements to perception or constitution, such as night vision or cold resistance traits;
Silver Ring bloodline begins to show clear extraordinary traits, capable of granting basic abilities like Elemental Affinity or Animal Communication."
"Golden Ring bloodline holders often display extraordinary talents, such as Elemental Manipulation or Body Transformation;
Star Ring bloodline transcends mortal limits, granting possessors rare abilities such as Space-Time Perception or Prophecy.
Moon Ring bloodline can be called mythical, possessing the potential to distort reality;
And Sun Ring bloodline is almost only found in ancient legends, believed to possess the power to alter rules."
Ron continued reading and learned that now most knights, even after bloodline activation, at most possess a Silver Ring bloodline.
Even old clans like the royal family rarely have anyone reach the Golden Ring level.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
To preserve bloodline capabilities of Golden Ring and above for each generation, it seems one has to rely on mysticism methods...
The following description of Dragon Species again opened his eyes:
"Dragon Species possess the strongest and purest bloodlines known among all races. Even mixed descendants often have talents far exceeding ordinary races. Ancient Dragon Kings were not without Moon Ring bloodline holders, and the mythological First Dragon was believed to have reached the Sun Ring level."
"Dragon Descendants typically have powerful Elemental Affinity, outstanding physical constitution, and long lifespans."
"The quantity of Dragon Descendants decreased drastically after the Third Era, with pureblood Dragon Species almost extinct. Nowadays, the so-called ’Dragonmen’ mostly only retain very thin Silver Ring or Golden Ring Dragon Bloodlines, far from the true Star Ring or Moon Ring Dragon Species."
"Over time, high-purity bloodlines gradually diluted, and today’s ’Dragonmen’ are as distant from ancient True Dragons as fireflies from the sun’s light."
The book also mentioned a key concept - "Bloodline Retracing":
"In theory, all diluted bloodlines could potentially be retraced to more pure states through specific rituals. This retracing process is extremely dangerous, with low success rates, but if successful, it could grant the bearer powerful abilities akin to their ancestors."
After reading these materials, Ron gained a more systematic understanding of extraordinary bloodlines.

chapters.title: Chapter 123 - 110: Philosopher’s Stone (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 123: Chapter 110: Philosopher’s Stone (Part 3)
At the same time, he found a thought-provoking conclusion at the end of "Examination of Extraordinary Professions of Alien Races":
"Although various races have developed diverse systems of extraordinary professions, in terms of overall potential, the path of the Wizard remains the most expansive."
"The reason lies in the fact that the Wizard’s path does not rely on inherent bloodline, but rather continually breaks limits through acquired learning and knowledge accumulation. The inherent bloodline abilities of various alien races are certainly powerful, but are often limited to specific directions, whereas Wizards can almost touch any field through learning."
"As the ancient saying goes: ’Bloodline determines the starting point, effort determines the endpoint.’"
"However, each extraordinary profession has its unique advantages and highlights. The comprehensiveness of Wizards often comes at the cost of a longer learning path, whereas specialized professions can quickly reach peaks in specific areas."
[Extraordinary Biology Experience Points + 1]
[Extraordinary Biology Experience Points + 1]
[Extraordinary Biology Experience Points + 1]
...
Returning the book to its place, Ron was filled with a multitude of thoughts.
These insights further reinforced his determination to develop multiple paths in parallel — combining the Wizard’s broadness with various bloodline activations might just be the ideal growth path.
When returning to the workshop, night had fallen deeply.
Ailan stood at the door to welcome him, vines gently swaying, appearing more lively than before.
"Master, welcome back."
She no longer needed to laboriously join letters with vines, but directly used large leaves as writing boards, generating text on them.
"Ailan, you look... different." Ron cautiously said.
Ailan’s vines gently danced: "I feel... clearer, my thoughts more coherent, this sensation is quite astonishing."
"That’s great." Ron said with a smile: "I’m very happy to see your growth."
Walking into the studio, Ron saw a bottle of Sun Essence on the table, the latest version he had refined that morning.
It included more Sun Orchid extracts than the previous formula, theoretically capable of better activating positive energy within the body.
"It’s time." he muttered to himself, picking up the potion that emitted a golden glow: "Let’s see how the improved effect is."
Ron took a deep breath and drank it all at once.
In an instant, a surge of scorching energy rushed from his throat to his limbs, as if liquid sunlight was flowing through his veins.
He could feel every meridian in his body lighting up, every muscle vibrating, and every inch of his skin emitting a mild heat
"This effect... is much stronger than expected!"
Ron was surprised to discover that the positive energy within him was rapidly activated, creating a strong resonance with the Crown Breathing Technique.
He immediately sat cross-legged, adjusting his breathing according to the principles of the "Crown Breathing Technique."
With each inhale, the energy activated by the potion gathered toward the central hub;
With each breath hold, the energy circulated through the meridians, strengthening vessels and muscles;
With each exhale, impurities and congestion were expelled out of the body.
Ron could clearly perceive that the potion’s effect and his breathing technique formed a perfect synergy, mutually enhancing, creating a positive cycle.
Concentrating all his attention, he adjusted his breathing to the most optimal state, guiding the energy to launch an assault on the final barrier.
At the crucial moment, his perception suddenly became extremely acute as if he could see every drop of blood, every meridian inside himself.
In this nearly transparent perception, he discovered a peculiar energy flowing in his blood - an ancient and formidable force, dormant in the genes of every individual, just waiting to be awakened.
This force seemed to sense Ron’s call and began gradually awakening.
[Breathing Body Refining Experience Points + 1]
[Current Progress: Breathing Body Refining (Novice 100/100) → Breathing Body Refining (Proficient max)]

chapters.title: Chapter 124 - 111: Magma Dew
chapters.content:
Chapter 124: Chapter 111: Magma Dew
At the moment of breakthrough, Ron felt an unprecedented energy fluctuation erupt from within him, like the wings of a butterfly emerging, gently trembling, yet carrying a heart-pounding power.
The meridians in his body seemed to be rewoven, and the fiber structure of his muscles underwent subtle changes, becoming denser and more elastic.
As the Breathing Body Refining reached the Skilled Level, his Physical Attribute directly increased to 2.0, just reaching the critical point for advancing to Bloodline Knight.
[Basic Attributes Enhancement: Constitution 1.7→2.0 (+0.3)]
He felt his control over his body had reached a new realm, with every muscle, every bone, every blood vessel within his perception.
The feeling was like a blurred world becoming clear, a chaotic universe suddenly becoming orderly.
[Gained Additional Trait: Traceback
(When bloodline is activated, it can be traced back to a more primitive and pure bloodline form, enhancing the bloodline level)]
"Traceback..." He saw the name of this trait, with a gleam of excitement in his eyes.
The description of this trait made his heart involuntarily accelerate.
Being able to trace back to a more original and pure bloodline upon activation, this was practically tailor-made for him!
Among the current cultivators of the Crown Breathing Technique, most can only awaken lower-level bloodlines such as Fire Lizard or Two-legged Flying Dragon.
Because human bloodlines have been diluted and mutated through too many generations, connection to ancient creatures is almost imperceptible.
The Traceback Attribute, however, can break this limitation and directly trace back to the original source of the bloodline.
If this trait can function as described, then Ron hopes to awaken a bloodline that is more powerful and purer than that of ordinary cultivators.
"If I combine it with my improved Bloodline Activation Potion..." Ron’s eyes gleamed with a burning light:
"Perhaps I really could activate a dragon bloodline close to the Sun Flame Dragon!"
The Sun Flame Dragon, a pure-blooded dragon species from the Star Ring of the Divine Era.
They can freely manipulate the powers of flame and light. According to records, the ancient dragons of this lineage have even acquired the divinity of the Sun God, which might also be why the Crown Breathing Technique can trace back to them.
Ron does not dream of ascending in one step and directly awakening such a terrifying Star Ring Bloodline.
But with the dual aid of the Bloodline Activation Potion and the "Traceback" trait, awakening a subordinate branch of draconic species is not unattainable.
"However, all this still requires practical validation."
Ron calmed himself, analyzing rationally.
The theoretical feasibility often greatly differs from actual effect, not to mention bloodline activation is a high-risk process itself.
Rash attempts could lead to irreversible outcomes, the worst being mutation into a creature abandoned by reason and humanity.
Thinking of this, he opened the letter Andre had the messenger deliver today.Thɪs Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
The handwriting of the blond youth was slightly hurried, but between the lines, an uncontrollable excitement was evident:
"Since your Bloodline Activation Potion has made significant progress, I will immediately prepare the materials needed for the Bloodline Activation Ceremony and proceed with activation ahead of you..."
Ron was not surprised to see this, but the latter part of the letter made him frown:
"Regarding the third stage of the Crown Breathing Technique, I need to tell you something in person. This involves the core secrets of the Bloodline Knight, not suitable to write in a letter. Tonight, I’ll come see you with Magma Dew."
"Magma Dew..."
Ron softly uttered this name, recalling the special Body Tempering Medicine Andre mentioned before. (Forget about looking at Chapter Four)
According to the manuscript of the Crown Breathing Technique, the third stage requires the use of "Magma Dew" to temper the physique, allowing the meridians to withstand stronger energy flow.
But the specific effects are not detailed in the manuscript.
Ron carefully put the letter aside and continued to study the Bloodline Activation Potion formula on the table.
After repeated scrutiny and improvement over this period, he has basically finalized the plan:
Using Sunfire Essence as a guiding medium, combined with the bloodline factor extracted from Fire Lizard Scales, along with several stabilizers and directional enhancement components.
Theoretically, this formula should accurately activate the bloodline fragments related to the Sun Flame Dragon in the body, while firmly locking the activation direction and avoiding the possibility of random mutation.
[Magic Potion Refining Experience Points +1]
Ailan quietly organized the herbs on the side, the once calm and unruffled eyes now sparkled with evident wisdom.
Its morphological changes have gradually slowed—the body contour is almost humanoid, except the skin is still a light green, and the hair is composed of dense vines.
"Master." Ailan generated words with leaf blades: "The Powdered Heart of the Volcano Lizard is running low."
Ron nodded: "Thanks for the reminder, I’ll arrange for the purchase of new materials."
He couldn’t help but marvel at the dramatic transformation of Ailan.
In just a few days since it was purchased, it has grown from an almost non-communicative semi-plant to an assistant capable of understanding complex instructions and offering proactive advice.
"How do you feel today, Ailan?" Ron asked, organizing the workbench.
Ailan’s leaves gently swayed, generating a response much longer than usual:
"It feels wonderful, Master. My thoughts have become clearer, I can recall more things. I even... started dreaming."
"Dreaming?" Ron paused his work in surprise: "What did you dream about?"
"Dreamt of a forest..." Ailan wrote:
"A forest completely different from here, filled with sunlight. The trees are tall, flowers and grass abundant, teeming with life everywhere. And many... beings like me, but they are more human-like, able to speak and dance."
Ron nodded thoughtfully, further confirming his suspicion—that these dreams were likely the awakening of bloodline memory, echoes from an ancient era.
"That sounds like a beautiful place," Ron said gently. "Maybe one day, you’ll remember more."
Ailan’s vines quivered slightly, seemingly expressing some emotion, but it chose not to continue the topic, instead focusing its attention on organizing the herbs.
Ron also returned to his work.
For the next few hours, he completed several client orders for magic potions while continuing to refine the details of the bloodline activation potion formula.
As the sun began to set, Andre arrived as promised, holding a delicate wooden box.
"Finally finished today’s Law Enforcement Team tasks. Helped them chop dozens of experimental wood today, and my arms feel almost numb..."
Besides his own knight training, he actually spends a lot of time on various tasks assigned by the Law Enforcement Team to earn Magic Stone Fragments.
Being able to accept such miscellaneous tasks within the School was due to the connections of the Farouk Royal Family. Apprentices without such backing had to risk their lives on field duties.
The blond youth, although slightly exhausted, had a gleam of excitement in his eyes:
"In this box is the Magma Dew, and... some information you need to know."
Ron led him to the meeting room on the second floor of the workshop, where Ailan thoughtfully prepared hot tea for the two before quietly stepping aside.
Andre carefully opened the wooden box and took out a small crystal bottle.
The bottle contained a dark red liquid, with golden sparks flickering inside, resembling a miniature flow of lava.
"Magma Dew," Andre said solemnly, speaking in a low voice:
"The third-stage Body Tempering Medicine of the Crown Breathing Technique, and it’s also the last of the secret potion I could bring from the Royal Family."
Ron took the crystal bottle, feeling the heat emanating from the bottle, the temperature inside remaining astonishing despite the thick crystal.
"What exactly is this?" Ron asked curiously, gently shaking the bottle to observe the flow of the liquid inside.
Andre glanced around to ensure no outsiders were present before beginning his explanation: "Magma Dew isn’t simply used for meridian enhancement like Scorching Oil."
His tone became unusually serious: "Its true purpose... is to help Bloodline Knights get through the dangerous post-awakening period."
He retrieved a parchment from his bosom and carefully unraveled it:
"This is a part of records I secretly copied from the royal archives:
After the awakening ceremony, a Bloodline Knight enters a rapid growth period of about six months.
During this time, the awakened bloodline power grows at an astounding rate, but it also brings a significant risk of mutation."
Ron frowned: "Mutation risk?"
"Yes," Andre nodded affirmatively:
"If the body cannot fully harness the awakened ancient bloodline, it will start to erode the host’s body and spirit, leading to irreversible mutations. This is why many who attempt bloodline awakening eventually turn into monsters."
He pointed to the crystal bottle: "The role of Magma Dew is to stabilize the awakened bloodline power, allowing it to integrate into the host’s body at a controllable speed, preventing uncontrolled mutations."
Ron finally understood the true meaning of the third stage of the Crown Breathing Technique:
"So the third stage is essentially a transition period to help knights master the awakened bloodline power?"
"Exactly," Andre nodded. "Even among the Royal Family, most people’s inheritance of the Crown Breathing Technique only reaches the third stage."
"What about the ultimate stage leading to the Crown Knight?" Ron pressed further.
Andre gave a wry smile and shook his head:
"Unfortunately, as an unfavored Thirteenth Prince, I don’t have the inheritance for the final stage. As far as I know, only the King and Crown Prince have the right to access that part."
Ron nodded thoughtfully.
This meant that if he wanted to further pursue the cultivation of the Crown Breathing Technique, he might have to return to the Faruk Kingdom someday in the future.
"However, although I don’t have the detailed content for the final stage, I have indeed heard some rumors."
A trace of cunning flashed in Andre’s eyes:
"It is said that the complete Crown Breathing Technique not only helps Bloodline Knights master their bloodline power but also guides them to higher realms——becoming a ’Crown Knight,’ a terrifying being capable of directly channeling solar energy."
He lowered his voice: "Since the founding of the Faruk Kingdom, only two knights have reached that level, and both were at the most critical moments of the kingdom. Their power is said to rival that of an Official Wizard and even surpass some research-focused Wizards."
Ron fell into deep thought. If these rumors were true, then perhaps in the future, when he became an Advanced Apprentice, he would indeed need to find time to meet the King:
"When do you plan to start the ceremony?"
"As soon as your potion is ready..." Andre replied, "However, it’s best to perform the ceremony at noon when the positive energy is most active."
The two then discussed the details and preparations for the ceremony and agreed to conduct it early in the morning in three days.
After seeing Andre off, Ron returned to the laboratory, fully immersing himself in the final adjustments of the bloodline activation potion.
Now aware of more secrets about Bloodline Knights, he had clearer requirements for the potion’s formula:
Not only must it precisely guide the direction of bloodline awakening, but also minimize the risk of post-awakening mutations.

chapters.title: Chapter 125 - 112: Hydra
chapters.content:
Chapter 125: Chapter 112: Hydra
The first ray of morning sunlight shone through the window, casting a warm golden spot on the wooden floor of the workshop.
Ron stood in the center of the training room, took a deep breath, and felt the ever-growing flow of power within his body.
He closed his eyes, his thoughts drifting towards the origins of his bloodline.
The Ralph Clan—a venerable family that existed since the founding of the Faruk Kingdom.
According to family ancient texts, their bloodline traces back to the Hydra Giant Poison Snake from the Divine Era.
However, every knight nobility with a bloodline inheritance can trace their ancestors to extraordinarily powerful creatures.
It’s not surprising; our ancestors were affluent, but the current Ralph Clan can at most awaken the ordinary Swamp Multi-headed Snake bloodline.
The Ralph Clan’s crest, adorned with the image of a multi-headed snake, symbolizes the family’s roots and power.
In the past, while in the kingdom, he was puzzled as to why humans would possess the bloodlines of giant serpents or dragon species.
He even had inappropriate fantasies because of it, but now it seems... everything is just the experimental products of wizards.
"But now..."
Ron murmured softly, his fingers brushing over his arm where golden meridian patterns were faintly visible beneath the skin, a trait gained from practicing the "Crown Breathing Technique" called the "Sun’s Protection".
Since consuming the modified "Sun Flame Essence" to break through, he often felt a heat flowing within, a sensation both unfamiliar and strangely familiar, as if some long-dormant power was gradually awakening.
"The Ralph Clan’s Multi-headed Snake bloodline and the Sun Flame Dragon Subspecies bloodline evoked by the Crown Breathing Technique... two distinct extraordinary bloodlines coexist within me."
Ron fell into deep thought:
"Along with the ’Origin Tracing’ trait I just acquired, perhaps I can trace back to a purer, more ancient bloodline form."
The possibility of multiple bloodline overlays made Ron’s heart race.
Of course, there was caution amidst this anticipation.
Bloodline activation is a double-edged sword; uncontrolled direction or excessive intensity can lead to mutation.
But with the "Origin Tracing" trait and his precisely concocted Bloodline Activation Potion, he might be able to minimize these risks.
"In any case, in a few days, I’ll have the chance to uncover the answers," Ron said softly, slowly opening his eyes.
He raised his hand and picked up the Ironwood Sword placed to the side, executing a series of basic sword techniques with ease.
Each movement flowed like water, with natural and smooth sword momentum, devoid of any excessive force.
Every muscle in his body worked in precise coordination, each swing of the sword carried a chilling precision and sharpness.
The sword light traced a graceful arc in the morning light, emitting a slight whistling sound, as though slicing the air.
[Current Progress: Basic Swordsmanship (Mastery max)]
"It really has reached its peak..." Ron murmured to himself, sheathing his sword, "Continuing to practice won’t increase my experience points any further."
His basic swordsmanship had reached its limit, and the profession panel indicated no more improvements.
In this situation, merely practicing sword techniques was clearly a waste of time, given the panel’s fixation, his skill wouldn’t regress even without practice.
"To further advance in swordsmanship, it seems I have to wait until I advance to [Magic Swordsman]."
"Until then, I’ll focus on magic." Ron decided.
Today marked the beginning of his second week living in the workshop. To save unnecessary travel time, Eric and Leia scheduled the weekly assessment together; passing it would allow direct entry into the second phase of courses.
"The weekly assessment is this afternoon, better practice some magic first." Ron smiled slightly, turning his hand towards the spellcasting medium—a delicately crafted silver bracelet.
He had purchased this specifically some time ago to better guide the flow of magic power and increase spell efficiency, costing about a dozen Magic Stone Fragments.
Though a basic alchemical artifact, for his current stage, it was sufficient as an aid.
Standing in the open area of the workshop, Ron took a deep breath, adjusting his breath and mental state. Raising his hands, he closed his eyes to sense the flow of magic power within.
He first concentrated on perceiving the room’s energy field, then gradually shifted attention to the special training subject: a white lab rat placed under a transparent glass dome.
This specially bred mouse was extremely sensitive to spiritual power fluctuations, making it an ideal subject for practicing spiritual interference spells.
"Spiritual Interference..."
Ron’s spiritual power started to gather, forming a barely visible fine ripple.
This ripple seemed fragile but encapsulated a meticulously constructed spiritual interference model, able to act on a creature’s nervous system, causing temporary confusion or dizziness.
He repeatedly adjusted the ripple’s frequency and intensity, striving to find the optimal balance point.
Too weak, it wouldn’t have any effect; too strong, it could permanently harm the test subject.
The initial attempts were not ideal.
The first time, the test mouse barely reacted;
The second time, it merely twitched its ears slightly;
The third time, it briefly halted its actions but quickly returned to normal.
"Not precise enough..." Ron frowned.
He closed his eyes, fully immersed in the mental construction, attempting a more complex ripple structure.
This time, he constructed a looped spiritual wave, theoretically able to act more precisely on specific brain regions.
"Fourth attempt..."Thɪs NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
With the spiritual power released, an invisible ripple precisely aimed at the glass dome.
This time, the effect was immediate—the lab rat suddenly stopped all movements, as if frozen in place, its gaze became bewildered and vacant.
To be precise, it wasn’t just stopped but put into a specific state of nerve disturbance. Ron could clearly sense the brain activity of the lab rat being temporarily halted by him.
Dozens of seconds later, the lab rat returned to normal but appeared a bit fatigued and confused, the typical aftermath of spiritual interference.
[Spiritual Interference Experience Points + 1]
[Breakthrough! Spiritual Interference (Beginner 50/50) → Spiritual Interference (Proficient 1/100)]
[Gained Additional Trait: Lag Circle (Within a specific range, interference effect slightly increases)]
"Success!" Ron softly cheered, feeling the slight changes in the flow mode of spiritual power within him.
After a brief rest, he began practicing "Magic Construction," the foundation of all spells, determining the caster’s control over magic power and the stability of the magic model.
He picked up a special crystal ball, a tool specifically used for practicing magic construction.
The crystal ball could reflect the caster’s magic power control in real-time, with any slight fluctuation and instability manifesting inside it.
"This time I’ll try the triple overlay structure..."
Ron muttered to himself, referring to an advanced technique he saw in the book "Wizard Modeling Essentials", usually only achievable by seasoned casters.
He infused a strand of spiritual power into the crystal ball, beginning to construct a magic model within it.
Initially a simple ring structure, gradually increasing in complexity, adding the second and third configurations, each maintaining a specific resonance relation with the preceding layer.
The interior of the crystal ball gradually revealed complex light patterns, initially somewhat blurred, becoming clearer and more stable with Ron’s continuous adjustments.
This process was extremely consuming of spiritual power, sweat beading on Ron’s forehead, his breath growing slightly labored.
But he persevered, continually fine-tuning every detail until the triple configurations in the crystal ball reached perfect balance.
"It’s now..."
When the last bit of instability was eliminated, the light patterns inside the crystal ball suddenly became exceptionally bright and stable, the three ring structures perfectly overlaying each other, forming a harmonious and unified whole.
[Magic Construction Experience Points + 1]
[Breakthrough! Magic Construction (Beginner 50/50) → Magic Construction (Proficient 1/100)]
[Gained Additional Trait: Stable State (Slight increase in stability of the magic model, slight decrease in magic power consumption)]
"Accumulated for so many days, finally made a breakthrough today."
Ron softly spoke to himself, satisfied with his achievements.
These advancements in the two skills would just be helpful for today’s weekly assessment.
After finishing his spell practice, Ron sat cross-legged, ready to begin his daily meditation cultivation.
As he entered the meditation state, his consciousness gradually immersed into the familiar starry sky—the unique realm of "Star Eater’s Ravings".
As always, countless living stars flickered with eerie glows in the vast universe, as though whispering secrets.
But today, Ron found the stars appeared more active than usual, their glow more dazzling, the whispers more distinct.
He even seemed to discern fragmented words among the murmurs:
"...come...back..."
Ron’s heart skipped a beat, the first time he had heard such clear "voices" in meditation.

chapters.title: Chapter 126 - 113: Chaos Cube
chapters.content:
Chapter 126: Chapter 113: Chaos Cube
What shocked him even more was that when he tried to focus and listen, some stars seemed to sense his attention and began to slowly move towards him.
For a moment, Ron hallucinated seeing the eyes of some giant creature gazing at him from the depths of the universe.
"Damn!" He abruptly broke out of the meditation state, cold sweat soaking through his clothes.
Breath quickened, heart pounding like a drum, his entire body felt as if he’d just awakened from a nightmare.
"Spiritual contamination... has it already reached such a level?" He trembled as he grabbed the pocket watch placed beside him to recheck his state.
Indeed, the accumulated spiritual contamination was nearing a moderate level, which was already a dangerous signal.
According to the information he had reviewed some time ago, moderate spiritual contamination could lead to hallucinations, affect sleep quality, and even interfere with daily judgment.
If left unchecked, once the contamination reached severe levels, madness and mutation wouldn’t be far off.
Ron immediately activated the "reset" function of the pocket watch, a cool sensation spreading from the point of contact throughout his entire body, gradually purifying the contamination lurking deep within his spirit.
[Successfully reset negative state: Moderate Spiritual Contamination, Energy -6]
Six energy points... This was the largest consumption since he had used the pocket watch.
Ron’s heart sank, feeling an instinctive unease.
In theory, this level of spiritual contamination should be a problem faced only by advanced apprentices.
A significant reason why those advanced apprentices actively took on roles as teaching assistants was to gain "favors" to purify their spiritual contamination.
"Is it because I’ve been cultivating too fast?" Ron pondered, "Or is it the aftereffects left by those two instances of ’special inspiration’?"
A more terrifying possibility slowly emerged in his mind, but the thought was too frightening for him to continue pondering.
"In any case, I must find a better solution." Ron looked at the pocket watch, his desire to advance it growing even stronger in his heart.
The current pocket watch, though powerful, had limited energy. If the spiritual contamination continued to accumulate at this rate, one day it would surely exceed the pocket watch’s cleansing capability.
"Once Andre and I both advance to bloodline knights, combined with various magic-like techniques as support, together we will have the strength to contend even with advanced apprentices. At that time, we must explore Lizard Alley again."
Ron silently decided in his heart, "Perhaps through that goblin, the half-beastman mercenary squad, or even the mysterious old woman’s backing, we can find clues about the origin of the pocket watch."
After calming his emotions, Ron began to prepare for today’s weekly test.
This was something he had promised Eric and Leia, and it was also crucial for him to ascend to the next level of courses.
Once he finished washing up, he changed into a clean and tidy robe, secured the pouch containing magic stone fragments at his waist, ensuring he looked energetic.
Before leaving, he glanced back at the "Star Eater’s Ravings" notes on the workbench, a complex emotion fleeting across his eyes.
Although this meditation technique had brought him many troubles, he couldn’t deny that it had significantly accelerated his spiritual power growth.
This conflicting feeling left him in a dilemma, but the immediate priority was passing the weekly test to reach a higher stage.
"Ailan, I’m going to the weekly test, please look after the workshop."
Ron said to the dryad who was organizing herbs in the corner.
Ailan’s leaves gently swayed, forming characters: "Good luck, master."
Ron smiled and nodded, stepping out of the workshop and heading towards the teaching area.
The black mist jungle was damp and refreshing in the early morning, and Ron took a deep breath, allowing his thoughts to gradually calm down.
Today was an important day. He must give his all and not let the shadow of spiritual contamination affect his performance.
As he crossed a dim grove, the outline of the teaching area gradually became clearer.
The ancient and solemn stone tower appeared particularly dignified in the morning light, where countless wizards had embarked on their path of the extraordinary, and countless others had fallen here, never reaching the end.
In the hallway of the teaching area, people came and went, apprentices of various levels holding scrolls or books hurriedly moving through.
Following the signs, Ron found the weekly test location—a spacious classroom on the third floor.
As he opened the door, he saw Eric already inside, organizing some documents on the table.
There were also a few apprentices in the classroom, looking like they were there to participate in the weekly test.
"Oh, Ron." Eric looked up and greeted him with a smile, "You’re early. It seems you value this test greatly."
"Of course, Master Eric." Ron respectfully responded, "This is an important step for me to enter the next phase of study, and I’ve prepared thoroughly."
Eric nodded, indicating for him to find a seat in the front row.
Ron scanned the room, recognizing a few classmates from previous lessons; some looked confident, while others appeared nervous.
"Today’s weekly test covers the ’Magic Circuit Optimization’ and ’Spiritual Stability Techniques’ courses."
When the scheduled time arrived, Eric immediately began announcing the exam rules:
"These two courses are foundational for apprentices, and their content is interrelated, so we have arranged for the tests to be held on the same day to save everyone the travel time."
He continued to explain, "First is the theoretical test, followed by practical operation. Each part accounts for half of the total score, and you need to pass both parts to advance."
Leia entered the classroom from the side door, holding a stack of exam papers.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet

chapters.title: Chapter 127 - 113: Chaos Cube (2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 127: Chapter 113: Chaos Cube (2)
She nodded to everyone, then started distributing the test papers: "Please stay quiet and answer carefully. The test time is one hour."
Ron took the test paper and quickly skimmed through it.
The content covered the basic theory of the magic circuit, core techniques for spiritual power stability, and an analysis of their relevance.
For general apprentices, these questions were undoubtedly quite challenging, but for Ron, who had already raised both skills to a skilled level, they seemed relatively simple.
He picked up the pen and began to answer; the tip of the pen moved smoothly across the paper without the slightest hesitation.
The concepts that once required repeated consideration had now integrated into his way of thinking, becoming instinctual understanding.
The last question in the theory part was especially complex, requiring students to analyze how to maintain the stability of a magic circuit under high pressure environments.
This required a comprehensive use of the core knowledge of both courses, along with personal practical experience.
After a moment’s thought, Ron picked up his pen and wrote:
"In high-pressure environments, magic circuits are prone to disorder, mainly due to spiritual wave causing the energy flow to lose control. The solution lies in constructing a ’buffer ring,’ which forms a secondary energy flow around the main circuit..."
He described in detail some techniques he discovered during magic construction practice, things not mentioned in regular textbooks, insights he gained through practical exploration.
