Soron’s voice was low and magnetic:
"Although you cannot yet cast a complete Spiritual Shock, you are all seed candidates for Wizards, and learning its theoretical foundation and simplified version in advance is important for enhancing spiritual control."
After class, Ron deliberately slowed his packing speed, waiting until the other students bowed to the Master and left the classroom before approaching Soron.
He noticed that Soron seemed to intentionally stay there, and from his posture, it didn’t seem like he was waiting for the next class.
"Master Griffith..." Ron steadied his nerves and quietly asked:
"I noticed that the Spiritual Shock you mentioned, is it somehow related to the Spiritual Interference Wave that I currently master?"
The pressure unique to an Official Wizard, despite being restrained, still made him somewhat uncomfortable.
Sitting on the edge of the podium, Soron, deep in thought, looked up at Ron in slight surprise:
"You’ve mastered the high-precision beam-type use of spiritual interference? This is something even Intermediate Apprentices find challenging, and its short-term practicality is far less than practicing direct attack magic."
"I find it very useful in certain situations." Ron answered cautiously, "Especially against opponents who rely on thought and perception."
Soron’s eyes flashed with a hint of approval:
"Your thinking is very correct. Spiritual interference is indeed a simplified version of the Spiritual Shock, or rather its foundational form. The essence of an Official Wizard’s Spiritual Shock is to amplify the effect of spiritual interference a hundredfold and add a direct physical impact."
After a brief thought, he added, "Since you already have this foundation, perhaps I can give you some extra guidance to help strengthen the effect of your spiritual interference."
Ron immediately expressed his gratitude, "That would be an immense honor, Master."
"Good." Soron nodded, "Stay after the next class, and I will give you some special exercises. Now, go to your next lesson."
As Ron left the classroom, he felt an inexplicable sense of relief.
Though Soron’s status and power kept him instinctively alert, today’s interaction went unexpectedly smoothly.
"He seems to be very interested in me." Ron pondered, "But I don’t know if this is a good thing or a bad thing."
..........
In the afternoon, there was the weekly Alchemy test, and Master Thompson gave high praise for Ron’s performance.
Since he showcased his superb energy conservation ability last time, Ron has gained a certain reputation in the class.
"Apprentice Ron’s alchemy perception is extraordinary." Thompson announced in front of the class:
"His latest work—an improved version of the energy conversion array, is nearly 20% more efficient than the standard version. This kind of innovative thinking is what we encourage."
After the weekly test, Thompson kept Ron behind.
"Starting next week, you can directly participate in the advanced alchemy courses."
He said satisfactorily, "You have mastered the basic knowledge well enough, there is no need to waste time in the beginner courses."
"Thank you for the recognition, elder." Ron replied sincerely, "I will continue to work hard."
The same situation happened in the Elemental Affinity Class.
After observing Ron’s excellent control over the Light and Fire Elements, Laila also approved his early entry into the advanced class.
"I must say, your talent in elemental affinity is quite outstanding."
Laila evaluated, "Especially your perception and guidance of the Light Element, which has reached the level of an Advanced Apprentice.
Thus, within just two weeks, Ron had gained qualifications for three advanced courses simultaneously, an extremely rare achievement within the School.
"Everything is going according to plan." One night, Ron muttered to himself in the private laboratory of the workshop:
"As long as I maintain this momentum, the road ahead will become increasingly broad."
He took out the ranking table of the Candidate Wizard sequence, noting his position had risen from the initial thirtieth to twenty-fourth, and now further up to nineteenth.
This speed of improvement far exceeded expectations and confirmed that his efforts were being recognized.
..........
Another half a month passed.
Ron busily shuttled between the workshop and classroom every day, living a hectic yet fulfilling life.
In the workshop, his bloodline modulation experiments made significant progress.
The Autophagic Slime Monster exhibited various peculiar changes under his hands, from early simple color transformations to now being able to briefly maintain complex shape shifts.
[Bloodline Modulation Experience Points +1]
[Current Progress: Bloodline Modulation (Beginner 42/50)]
The study of Extraordinary Biology was also not neglected; through extensive reading and practice, he had acquired quite in-depth knowledge.
[Extraordinary Biology Experience Points +1]
[Current Progress: Extraordinary Biology (Beginner 48/50)]
The growth of Little Sea Siren Dale was even more astonishing.
With Ailan’s meticulous care, she had grown to seventy or eighty centimeters, nearly the size of a three-year-old human child.
Meanwhile, her language ability had made a leap forward.
"Master, look at me!" Dale joyfully turned somersaults in the crystal vat, her voice clear and melodious: "I’ve learned to swim upside down!"
Ailan watched with satisfaction, having formed an almost mother-daughter-like bond with Dale.
The dryad’s vines often gently stroked the Little Sea Siren’s hair, as a sign of encouragement and praise.
"Dale progresses so fast." Ailan’s leaves wrote:
"She has already started attempting to control water flow, though still very weak, but has demonstrated the unique talent of a Sea Siren."
Ron nodded in agreement, "Yes, her potential far exceeds my expectations. In another two months, I think she can start accepting memory editing."
Meanwhile, Ron also began to stand out in the School’s courses.
Soron’s advanced spiritual control course was far deeper and more challenging than the basic courses, but this only stimulated Ron’s potential.
His learning speed was astonishing, especially in enhancing spiritual interference; his progress was rapid.
During the special guidance time after class, Soron personally explained the basic theory of Spiritual Shock to Ron.
"The core of Spiritual Shock lies in energy compression and explosion."
Soron patiently explained:
"Ordinary spiritual interference only slightly disrupts the opponent’s thoughts, while Spiritual Shock instantly releases highly compressed spiritual power, forming a compound attack that affects both spirit and causes severe impact."
He demonstrated a simplified version, with an invisible energy wave spreading from his fingertips, shattering a crystal glass five meters away.
"It seems simple, but it actually requires extremely high precision in spiritual power control. The tighter the energy is compressed, the greater the explosion’s power, but it also puts a heavier burden on the caster’s spirit."
Ron studied intently, trying to imitate Soron’s method.
At first, he could only generate faint energy fluctuations, barely able to blow a piece of paper.
But with deepened practice, his control became increasingly precise, and the intensity of the energy waves steadily increased.
[Spiritual Interference (Proficient) Experience Points +1]
"An astonishing speed of progress." Soron praised, "Your talent in spiritual power control is quite rare."
He drew closer to Ron, lowering his voice:
"I’ve noticed that your recent accumulation of spiritual contamination is very light, almost negligible. Does this relate to your ’Medicinal Body Resonance’ talent?"
Ron feigned a thoughtful look:
"It might be, Master. I have indeed found that after taking certain magic potions, my spiritual state becomes particularly clear and stable. This might be a manifestation of ’Medicinal Body Resonance’."
Soron’s gaze revealed an elusive expression:
"This is a rare second-tier talent, with very few records; perhaps it indeed has the effect of effectively resisting spiritual contamination."
He paused for a moment, then added:
"However, even with this talent, don’t rely on it too much. The accumulation of spiritual contamination is a complex process. Sometimes seemingly insignificant changes can eventually lead to serious consequences."
Ron respectfully nodded, "I will heed the Master’s warning."
As he left the classroom, Ron recalled Soron’s words, feeling somewhat puzzled in his heart.

chapters.title: Chapter 171 - 136: Old Acquaintances
chapters.content:
Chapter 171: Chapter 136: Old Acquaintances
In the afternoon of the Black Mist Jungle, the clouds were heavy, and sunlight could barely penetrate those dense branches and leaves, casting mottled shadows on the ground.
Ron walked along the stone path towards the tower in the central area of the school.
Today was his first day attending the "Advanced Elemental Magic" course.
Compared to Spiritual Control and Alchemy, Elemental Magic had always been a weaker area for him, even though he had a decent natural affinity for Light and Fire Elements.
"I hope this course can make up for my shortcomings..."
Ron pondered silently.
Since the activation of his bloodline, his sensitivity to elements had indeed improved.
But compared to those apprentices specialized in Elemental Manipulation in the school, his foundation still seemed somewhat thin.
Passing through a gray-white archway, Ron arrived at the Elemental Magic classroom on the seventh floor of the tower.
The setup here was entirely different from the basic courses’ classroom:
The walls were inlaid with various colorful crystal stones, and the ceiling depicted complex Elemental Cycle diagrams.
In the center of the room was a massive Crystal Ball, within which various Elemental Energies flowed, like a miniature elemental vortex.
Several students were already present, and Ron noticed they all wore Middle Apprentice’s sapphire badges, and most appeared much older than him.
He recognized a few faces—it was those renowned for Elemental Manipulation within the school, and some were even Advanced Apprentices.
Ron chose a seat towards the back, silently observing the surroundings.
He had long adopted the habit of not showing off in the school, at least when encountering a new environment for the first time.
As the students whispered to each other, the classroom door opened again, and an elderly woman in a robe with purple edges stepped in slowly.
Her long silver hair was neatly coiled at the back, and the wrinkles on her face appeared deliberately sculpted, yet her eyes were exceptionally bright, gleaming with a rare purple light.
"Wizard Yuni," one student whispered in surprise, and the classroom immediately fell silent.
Ron instinctively sat up straight.
Yuni’s name was not unfamiliar to him; she was one of the official Wizards specializing in Elemental Magic within the school, renowned for her unique research on element combination and transformation.
It was said she had even participated in the design of the gigantic Elemental Pool in the Central Hall of the school.
"Welcome, everyone, to Advanced Elemental Magic."
Yuni’s voice was unexpectedly crisp and pleasant, entirely unlike that of an elderly person:
"I am Yuni Seraphin, succeeding my student Laila, and I will be your guide for the next three months."
She walked slowly to the center of the classroom in front of the Crystal Ball, raised her hand slightly, and the Elemental Energy within the ball immediately formed into more complex vortex structures.
"You have all mastered basic Elemental Perception and Control, and now it’s time to delve into deeper learning."
Yuni’s gaze swept across every corner of the classroom:
"The core of Advanced Elemental Magic lies in understanding the essence of elements and their relationships rather than simply manipulating one or more elements."
Ron took notes earnestly, paying extra attention to each word Yuni said.
Unlike Soron’s introverted and profound teaching style, Yuni’s explanation was more vivid and intuitive, using many specific examples and immediate demonstrations to clarify complex theories.
"Please remember,"
Yuni emphasized, forming a complex symbol with her hands above the Crystal Ball, causing the elements inside the ball to disassemble and reassemble:
"Elements are not fixed entities but different manifestations of energy. Under specific conditions, one element can transform into another, which is the core of the ’Element Transformation Law.’"
With a gentle wave of her hand, a cluster of Water Element within the Crystal Ball gradually turned hot and eventually transformed into Fire Element.
This transformation seemed simple, but Ron knew it required extremely high precision in Energy Control.
"Today’s first exercise,"
Yuni announced: "Try to perceive the elemental fluctuations in the classroom and draw them on this special paper. This not only tests your perception ability but also the precision of your Spiritual Control."
Elemental Servants distributed a special sheet of paper emitting a faint silver glow.
Ron took the paper and sensed a subtle energy fluctuation; evidently, this was not ordinary paper but a special medium capable of recording impressions of Spiritual Power.
Ron closed his eyes and began to concentrate his Spiritual Power.
As his awareness extended, he could feel the flow of various Elemental Energies in the classroom.
Fire Elements danced like flames, Water Elements were smooth and gentle like flowing water, Earth Elements were solid and stable, Wind Elements were light and elusive...
What surprised him even more was that he could sense some rarer elements, such as light, shadow, and thunder, which moved rhythmically with specific rhythms in space.
[Elemental Perception Experience Points + 1]
Slowly opening his eyes, Ron began to illustrate the elemental distribution he perceived on the paper.
His hand glided gently across the paper, his Spiritual Power flowing into it, forming a complex elements mapping chart.
An hour later, Yuni started to collect the students’ works.
When she reached Ron, her eyebrows slightly raised, clearly surprised by his work.
"Ron Ralph..." she murmured his name softly, her gaze alternating between the paper and his face:
"Your range of elemental perception is quite broad, able to capture even those relatively rare elements. Especially your depiction of light elements, the precision is quite high."
Ron nodded humbly:
"Thank you for your evaluation, Master Yuni. I do have some natural affinity for Light and Fire Elements."
"It’s not just a question of affinity," Yuni remarked thoughtfully:
"Your precision in Spiritual Control is also exceptional, which is crucial for Elemental Manipulation. Keep it up, young man."
The latter part of the course involved practical exercises.
Yuni guided the students to try simple element transformations—turning Water Elements into steam or compressing Wind Elements into a visible form.
Ron focused on his practice, surprised to find the theory of Element Transformation remarkably similar to the principle of Energy Conversion he learned in Alchemy.
This interdisciplinary connection deepened his understanding of the elements.
[Elemental Perception Experience Points + 1]
After the class ended, most students quickly packed their belongings and bowed to Yuni to bid farewell.
Ron noticed that Yuni didn’t leave immediately; instead, she stayed in the classroom, seemingly organizing some materials.
Recalling the tremendous help from Soron’s special guidance, Ron decided to try once again.
He organized his notes, and waited until only he and Yuni remained in the classroom before slowly approaching her.
"Master Yuni?" Ron politely began, "I have some questions about Element Transformation. May I seek your advice?"
Yuni lifted her head, her purple eyes gleaming with approval:
"Of course, Apprentice Ron. In fact, I’ve been looking forward to your questions."
Ron was a bit surprised: "You...were expecting my questions?"
"Soron and I are old friends."
Yuni smiled slightly: "He mentioned you to me, saying you’re a student with a strong thirst for knowledge. Moreover, Lady Allen has also recommended you to me."
Hearing Lady Allen’s name, Ron’s heart stirred: "You know Lady Allen?"
"Of course, we were contemporaries at the Crystal Tower, most of the old folks in the school know each other, haha..."
A trace of nostalgia flashed in Yuni’s eyes:
"Allen has a special talent for Magic Potion Making, just like my obsession with Elemental Magic. Although she chose to reside in the herb store, her academic prowess is no less than Magnus’s, if not higher."
Yuni gestured for Ron to sit opposite her: "So, what would you like to ask?"
Ron organized his thoughts and raised the doubts he had during the class:
"I noticed that in the process of Element Transformation, controlling energy loss is a key issue. When water turns into steam, some energy always dissipates as heat. Is there a way to retain energy to the maximum extent?"
Yuni’s eyes lit up: "You’re very smart! This is indeed one of the core challenges in Element Transformation."
She took a small crystal from inside her robe and placed it on the table:
"Look at this, it’s a special Alchemy item—an ’Energy Anchoring Crystal’, capable of capturing and recovering part of the lost energy during Element Transformation."
The crystal shimmered with an exotic light under the lamp, and Ron could sense the intricate energy structure within it.
"Most apprentices focus only on the transformation itself and neglect the importance of energy conservation."
Yuni explained, her fingers lightly drawing a trace of energy above the crystal:
"Truly mastering Element Transformation, a wizard can retain about 95% of the energy during the transformation, while beginners typically retain around 50%."
She pushed the crystal towards Ron:
"Take it. Since you’re Allen’s student, consider this a meet-and-greet gift from a master. The ’Energy Anchoring Crystal’ will help you perceive and capture the energy flow during the transformation, aiding in improving transformation efficiency."
Ron looked at the precious gift in surprise: "This...is too valuable, Master Yuni."
"To me, it’s just a useless old item. Knowledge and tools should flow to where they can be most valuable."
Yuni waved her hand, indicating him to accept it:
"I can see you have an extraordinary talent and are diligent. This crystal will be much more useful in your hands than in my drawer."
"Thank you, Master Yuni," Ron said sincerely, carefully putting the crystal into his pocket.
In the next half an hour, Yuni explained to Ron the advanced theories of Element Transformation, and the interrelations between elements in detail.
This knowledge exceeded the depth and breadth of classroom content, and Ron eagerly absorbed every detail.
"The Elemental World is far more complex than most people imagine," Yuni said, her eyes sparkling with enthusiasm:
"There is a relationship among basic elements that I call ’resonance’. Once you understand this resonance, you can guide elements to transform and combine according to your will with minimal effort."
She described a complex meditation method, said to help casters feel this resonance more intuitively.
Ron took note of every detail, already planning in his mind how to integrate this knowledge with his own cultivation.
"By the way, about your relationship with Lady Allen..."
Upon parting, Yuni gazed at Ron with words of implicit significance:
"That fellow is actually quite stingy. Even among us old friends, it’s hard to get anything from her. She seldom shows such generosity to others, yet you..."
Ron responded humbly: "Lady Allen has given me much guidance. I am very grateful for her help."
"Good, keep up this humble attitude."
Yuni smiled and said: "After next week’s class, if you have more questions, you can continue to stay and consult with me."
Leaving the tower, Ron felt exceptionally at ease.
......
Back at the workshop, Ron immediately immersed himself in the Elemental Meditation practice taught by Yuni.
He sat cross-legged in the center of the training room on the workshop’s second floor, carefully placing the Energy Anchoring Crystal gifted by Yuni in front of him.
The skill of "Extraordinary Recognition" allowed him to see that there were no traps left within it, indeed merely a gift from an elder.
In the faint light, the crystal emitted a gentle glow, like a miniature star.
"First, concentrate, feel the elemental fluctuations around..."
Following Yuni’s instructions, Ron slowly closed his eyes, adjusting his breathing to a calm rhythm.
With the extension of his spiritual power, his perception gradually penetrated the surface of matter, touching deeper energy structures.
The various elemental energies in the workshop gradually appeared in his perception:
The herbs on the rack emitted faint life element fluctuations, the residual warmth in the furnace contained traces of fire element, and the water element flowed quietly in the bucket in the corner...
Most striking was the special energy fluctuation emitted by the crystal in front of him.
It was like a miniature elemental vortex, gently attracting and releasing the surrounding elemental energy, forming a peculiar rhythm.

chapters.title: Chapter 172 - 137: Differential Treatment
chapters.content:
Chapter 172: Chapter 137: Differential Treatment
Ron attempted to integrate his spiritual power into the rhythm, trying to understand the "resonance" relationship between elements.
At first, it felt like trying to discern a specific sound in a noisy market.
The fluctuations of various elemental energies were mixed together, making it difficult to distinguish them.
But as time went on, Ron gradually began to recognize subtle patterns and rhythms.
The Water Element and Fire Element were not as completely opposed as he previously thought; there was a subtle balance between them.
The Wind Element acted as an intermediary, capable of connecting and harmonizing the other elements.
The Earth Element seemed dull but contained the most stable and enduring energy.
"So that’s how it is..."
Ron silently recited in his mind as a whole new understanding formed in his consciousness:
"Elements are not isolated; they are an interconnected whole system."
As his understanding deepened, he felt his control over the elements becoming more natural.
Processes that once required precise calculations and deliberate guidance could now almost be completed by intuition.
[Elemental Perception Experience Points +1]
After several hours of meditation, Ron felt a slight dizziness, his spiritual power having reached its current limit.
He slowly opened his eyes and saw that the Energy Anchoring Crystal had changed from its original light blue to a deep purple-blue, evidently having absorbed a large amount of energy.
"The effect is even better than I imagined." Ron murmured, his fingers lightly touching the crystal, sensing the energy contained within.
In the days that followed, Ron dedicated most of his spare time to elemental meditation and practice.
The courtyard of the workshop often witnessed various strange elemental phenomena—a small vortex of flame, floating water spheres, even brief showers of light.
Ron’s control power over elements steadily improved, especially his command of the Light Element and Fire Element.
The techniques Yuni taught him allowed greater elemental effects with lower energy consumption.
[Elemental Perception Experience Points +1]
After each class, Ron would stay behind to seek Yuni’s guidance.
The old Witch highly praised his diligence and progress, and became more generous in sharing her knowledge and experience.
"Your speed of improvement is astonishing, Ron."
After the third class, Yuni commented, purple eyes sparkling with appreciation:
"Especially your understanding of elemental resonance, which has already approached the level of an Advanced Apprentice."
Back at the workshop, Ron immediately immersed himself in further study.
Following her earlier guidance, Ron set up a special meditation environment:
Crystals representing different elements were placed around him, with the Energy Anchoring Crystal at the center, and several specialized lamps providing a stable energy field.
When meditation began, Ron attempted to synchronize his spiritual power with the wave frequencies of specific elements as described in his notes.
This process was very delicate, requiring extremely high spiritual control, where the smallest error would set him back to the beginning.
After several attempts, Ron finally found that special feeling of "resonance":
Like two tuning forks sensing each other, his spiritual power began to perfectly match the wave frequency of the Light Element.
At that moment, he felt an unprecedented surge of elemental power flowing into his body, like a bright river nourishing every inch of his spiritual space.
[Elemental Perception Experience Points +1]
[Breakthrough! Elemental Perception (Beginner 50/50)→ Elemental Perception (Skilled 1/100)]
[Gained Additional Trait: Resonance
(Increased efficiency in controlling the affinity element, with a significant power boost to the corresponding elemental magic)]
When Ron awoke from meditation, he felt as if enveloped in a layer of soft radiance.
He could sense a much closer connection between himself and the elements, especially the Light Element and Fire Element, which felt almost like an extension of his own body.
"Incredible..."
Ron whispered softly, gazing at the miniature light flame gathered in his palm.
This flame was more stable and brighter than any elemental structure he had previously created, while consuming only about half the magic power.
Validating his theories, Ron began to try constructing the "Ring of Brilliance" spell.
This spell earlier required preparation and precise energy control, consuming a significant amount of spiritual power.
But now, the spell model almost naturally formed within his spiritual space, flowing as if by instinct.
To his pleasant surprise, under the resonance trait’s influence, both the spell’s power and efficiency had noticeably increased.
The halo not only formed faster, but the light flame was much brighter, with its potency increased by at least twenty to thirty percent.
[Magic Construction (Skilled) and Elemental Perception (Skilled) have generated a synergistic effect]
[Increased rate of experience point acquisition for Elemental Magic]
[Ring of Brilliance Experience Points +1]
[Current Progress: Ring of Brilliance (Beginner 42/50)]
"Skills can interact with each other!"
Ron’s eyes lit up, realizing that once Magic Construction and Elemental Perception reached the Skilled Level, they produced an unexpected synergy effect.
This synergy significantly accelerated the learning speed of Elemental Magic, nearly tripling his previous pace.
At this rate, he could soon raise the "Ring of Brilliance" to the Skilled Level, a feat that usually required months or even years of rigorous cultivation.
"Truly a delightful surprise." Ron smiled, feeling extraordinarily cheerful.
......
On the morning of the next day, Ron got up early, preparing to engage in his daily "Star Eater’s Ravings" meditation.
Ever since the Time Guardian Pocket Watch advanced, the energy cost for resetting mild spiritual contamination had reverted to just a single point, giving him more leeway to attempt deep meditation.

chapters.title: Chapter 173 - 137: Differential Treatment (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 173: Chapter 137: Differential Treatment (Part 2)
Ron took a bottle of pale blue potion from the workbench—"Amber Thought Liquid", unlike the ones sold in the workshop, the ones he kept for himself were absolute masterpieces.
By adding a small amount of Star Dust and Moonlight Water, the potion’s effect became more focused on aiding spiritual meditation.
He carefully took a drop and placed it on the tip of his tongue.
The taste of the potion was surprisingly good, like a mix of fresh mint and sweet honey, but the effect was extraordinarily strong.
Almost instantaneously, Ron felt his spirit elevate to a higher level, his thoughts became exceptionally clear, and his range of perception greatly expanded.
"Perfect state..." Ron muttered to himself, then sat cross-legged and began the meditation of "Star Eater’s Ravings".
The potion’s assistance allowed him to enter a deep meditation state more quickly.
As his consciousness submerged into that familiar starry sky, he found his perception of the star clusters clearer than ever before.
Those living stars were no longer just blurry dots of light but revealed more details.
He could see the textures on their surfaces, feel the subtle connections between them, and even discern the unique "personalities" of certain stars.
"Everything has just begun..."
Ron silently chanted the meditation technique’s spell in his heart, extending his spiritual power in the starry sky, reaching for more knowledge and power.
["Star Eater’s Ravings" Experience Points + 1]
[Current Progress: "Star Eater’s Ravings" (Proficient 180/300)]
After two hours of meditation, Ron’s spiritual power had a slight improvement.
This accumulation, though slow, was indeed steady and lasting.
[Spirit: 3.7→3.8 (+0.1)]
"Finally reached 3.8." Ron opened his eyes, feeling the abundant spiritual power within him.
This value meant that his spiritual power was near the standard of an advanced apprentice, just one step away from reaching the 4.0 standard line.
Of course, considering the non-linear nature of spiritual power growth, this last portion might be more challenging than all previous accumulations.
"At the current pace, when ’Star Eater’s Ravings’ reaches proficiency (200/300), my spiritual power should progress further, officially becoming an advanced apprentice, and by then, the day for the bloodline altar should not be far away."
Ron calculated.
As this thought crossed his mind, a prompt quickly appeared on the panel:
[Warning: Mild Spiritual Contamination Detected]
Although the potion’s assistance greatly enhanced meditation efficiency, it seemed to also accelerate the accumulation of spiritual contamination.
Ron had to activate the reset function of the Time Guardian Pocket Watch again to clear these potential threats.
[Negative State Reset Successfully: Mild Spiritual Contamination, Energy -1]
Compared to the previously increasing consumption, the now stabilized recovery made Ron breathe a sigh of relief.
This meant he could engage in deep meditation more frequently without worrying too much about the pocket watch’s energy consumption.
In the following week, Ron’s life was full and busy.
The morning was dedicated to the cultivation of "Star Eater’s Ravings", followed by elemental meditation and magic practice.
When he had classes, he attended various advanced courses at the school in the morning, and without classes, he practiced on his own. In the afternoon, he studied potions and alchemy in the workshop.
In the evening, he would take some time to check on the Sea Siren Dale and handle the daily affairs of the workshop.
In Soron’s spiritual control class, Ron’s performance was as outstanding as ever.
Especially in constructing multiple magic models, he was almost always the first student to complete the exercises.
"Very good, Ron."
Soron praised as he looked at the three stable coexisting magic models in Ron’s crystal ball:
"Your spiritual control has reached a very high level. Keep it up."
After class, Soron, as usual, kept Ron for special mentoring.
This time, the content was the compression technique of spiritual shock—how to load the maximum energy in the smallest volume without affecting the stability of the energy.
"The power of spiritual shock is proportional to the compression rate, but so is the risk."
Soron explained, his fingers sketching a complex energy structure in the air:
"Over-compression can lead to energy loss of control, not only causing spell failure but also possibly leading to rebound on the caster."
Ron carefully studied every detail, trying to simulate the compression process in his spiritual space.
"You seem to easily grasp the essentials."
Soron observed Ron’s attempts, a flash of exploration in his eyes: "Is it because of the ’Star Eater’s Ravings’?"
Ron’s heart skipped a beat, not expecting Soron to know the name: "You... know this meditation technique?"
"Yes, Allen mentioned it."
Soron continued, his gaze mixed with admiration and concern:
"The ’Star Eater’s Ravings’ is one of the few meditation techniques that can directly enhance the essence of spiritual power, but its dangers are equally daunting. Many wizards who attempt to cultivate it end up eroded by the accumulated spiritual contamination."
Ron maintained a cautious attitude:
"Lady Allen did warn me of the risks, and I’ve been careful to control the cultivation progress."
"I can see that."
Soron nodded: "Your spiritual state is very stable, showing almost no signs of contamination. This either means you have extraordinary talent, or you have found some effective purification method."
He gave Ron a meaningful look:
"Either situation demonstrates that you are a young man worth paying attention to."
Ron felt a bit uneasy, but it was soon dispelled by Soron’s next words:
"Don’t worry, I have no other intentions. As the overseer of the candidate wizard sequence, my duty is to observe and guide those potential seeds, not to hinder their growth."
In the subsequent mentoring, Soron appeared more generous than usual, sharing some advanced techniques on spiritual stability and contamination resistance.
This knowledge is usually only accessible to advanced apprentices, clearly a recognition of Ron’s special talents.
[Spiritual Interference (Proficient) Experience Points + 1]
When Ron left the classroom, he didn’t notice that his special treatment had already attracted the attention of other apprentices.
.........
"Again with the special mentoring, how many times has it been now?"
In class, Ron’s enhanced extraordinary senses inadvertently picked up on the whispered conversation of two apprentices behind him.
"I heard Lord Griffith pays him special attention, giving him at least half an hour of individual mentoring every time after class."
"What’s so strange about that? Isn’t it said that he has the rare ’Medicinal Body Resonance’ special talent of the second tier?"
"But still, he’s just a newcomer to the status of middle apprentice, what gives him the right to such preferential treatment?"
Ron stopped listening and focused on the crystal ball in front of him.
But these discussions indeed alerted him—the special treatment he received seemed to have become an open secret.
After the class, Soron, as usual, kept Ron for special mentoring.
However, this time, when the other apprentices left, two people hesitated for a moment and then boldly stayed behind.
"Lord Griffith..." A middle-aged apprentice who appeared to be at least thirty gathered the courage to speak:
"I also have some questions about the theory of spiritual shock; could you possibly offer some guidance?"
A hint of almost unnoticeable displeasure flashed across Soron’s face, but he quickly regained his composure:
"Of course, Apprentice Maurice, what is your question?"
The other apprentice also took the chance to step forward, clearly a planned action.
Soron did not reject their request and patiently answered the questions they posed.
However, Ron keenly noticed that Soron’s attitude towards them was noticeably less invested and enthusiastic than it was towards him.
The mentoring continued for about a quarter of an hour before Soron frowned slightly, seemingly uncomfortable with the apprentices’ lack of comprehension.
"Your questions will end here for today."
He said lightly: "Before the next class, I suggest you review the fundamentals of spiritual power fluctuations to better understand advanced concepts."
The two apprentices, somewhat disappointed, did not dare to say more and could only bow respectfully and depart.
When only Ron was left, Soron’s demeanor visibly relaxed:
"Now, let’s continue with last time’s compression technique for the shock..."
Ron noticed a special focus in Soron’s gaze as he looked at him, as if evaluating a precious item.
After the special mentoring, Ron rose to leave:
"Thank you very much for your guidance, Lord Griffith. The techniques you taught were of great help to me."
Soron nodded slightly: "Your enthusiasm for learning and talent are both very impressive, Ron. I look forward to seeing your future achievements."
As he left the classroom, Ron hadn’t walked far before encountering the two apprentices who had stayed behind for mentoring earlier.

chapters.title: Chapter 174 - 138: Diligence Can Make Up for Incompetence
chapters.content:
Chapter 174: Chapter 138: Diligence Can Make Up for Incompetence
They leaned against the corridor pillar, seemingly waiting deliberately.
"Apprentice Ralph."
Maurice stopped him, with a tone full of complex emotions:
"It seems you are quite popular with Lord Soron."
Ron maintained a polite smile: "Master Griffith is a very good mentor, very generous to all students."
Another trainee sneered:
"Don’t give us that, we can all see that his attitude towards you is noticeably different. He dismissed us in just a quarter of an hour, yet he is willing to spend half an hour or even longer guiding you alone."
Ron did not respond directly, only feeling a bit sorry for these people in their incompetence and rage:
"Everyone’s learning progress and needs are different. Naturally, Master Griffith will adjust his guidance according to the situation, teaching students in accordance with their aptitude."
"Ha!" Maurice scoffed, "Are you saying we’re not qualified to receive more guidance?"
"Heh... If even you think so yourself, then it seems there’s nothing more I need to say."
Ron smiled faintly and spoke calmly: "If there’s nothing else, I must leave now."
Having said that, he nodded politely and walked past the two, visibly showing they wanted to erupt yet were desperately holding it in.
"Don’t think you’re something just because you have some special talent."
Behind came Maurice’s voice full of resentment: "There have been plenty of gifted wizards in history who died young, where you end up ultimately depends on real skills!"
Ron did not look back, only continuing on his own path.
Such jealousy and hostility were not uncommon at the Black Mist School, especially when someone showed extraordinary talent and progress speed.
In the following days, similar incidents kept occurring.
After every class with Soron, there were always one or two trainees trying to stay behind for special guidance.
Soron did not refuse them, but his attitude was noticeably different.
Towards Ron, he would explain every concept in detail, even demonstrating some advanced techniques;
But for the others, his guidance was more basic and concise, as if he was just going through the motions.
"There’s nothing strange about this." One day, Soron explained to Ron:
"The essence of the ’favor’ rule dictates that mentors will naturally lean towards students who can provide more in return."
There was a rare frankness in his tone:
"You should already understand the concept of ’favor,’ so I won’t hide it. The ’favor’ gained from you is clearly much richer than from other trainees, which shows your growth and breakthroughs are more valuable."
Ron was not surprised by this.
According to Lady Allen’s explanation, ’favor’ is the feedback given to a mentor based on a student’s growth and breakthroughs.
And students with higher talent and quicker progress naturally provide a richer ’favor.’
"Don’t be troubled by others’ reactions."
Soron continued:
"In the extraordinary world, resources are always scarce, and competition is inevitable. Those who can obtain more resources are often those who can create greater value."
Ron nodded in understanding, now counting as a beneficiary of this ’favor’ rule.
And those trainees who are somewhat lacking in skills and talent are doomed to face more obstacles and setbacks in this harsh system.
"As long as you maintain this rate of progress," a light of expectancy flashed in Soron’s eyes:
"Your ranking in the candidate wizard sequence will soon rise another level."
.........
The morning sunlight filtered through the sparse canopy of the Black Mist Jungle as Ron walked along the familiar path, the surroundings reminded him of the scene when he first came here.
Back then, he was just a candidate apprentice barely meeting the minimum standard for spiritual talent.
Now, he was the nineteenth-ranked intermediate apprentice in the candidate wizard sequence, as well as a young professional alchemist.
"Time flies, it’s been about two months since I got my alchemist certification."
Ron mused to himself, his eyes falling on a wild herb with small flowers by the roadside.
During this period, he had been busy with various advanced courses and cultivating himself, hardly finding time to visit Lady Allen.
As his first guide on the path of the extraordinary, Lady Allen’s help was immeasurable.
"I wonder how she is doing now." Ron pondered, while also thinking of another matter.
Since acquiring the ’extraordinary recognition’ fusion skill, he found himself able to perceive the essence of items and even discern the talents and aptitudes of people to some extent.
This sparked an idea in him: maybe he could visit the candidate apprentice area to see if he could discover some overlooked talented seedlings.
These thoughts whirled in his mind, and he decided to first visit the candidate apprentice dormitory area, then go to Lady Allen.
The candidate apprentice dormitory area looked almost unchanged from his memory, still the same low and simple huts, with the air filled with the damp musty smell and the pungent scent of failed experiments.
Walking along the familiar cobblestone path, Ron noticed several candidate apprentices practicing basic magic in the courtyard.
They appeared exhausted, their robes stained with traces of various potions and mud, evidently just returning from some experiment or task.
When these apprentices noticed Ron approaching, their expressions immediately changed.
The professional alchemist badge and the intermediate apprentice badge on his chest shimmered in the sunlight, showcasing his extraordinary status in the supernatural world.

chapters.title: Chapter 175 - 138: Diligence Can Make Up for Incompetence (2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 175: Chapter 138: Diligence Can Make Up for Incompetence (2)
"It’s... it’s Ron, the Alchemist, sir!"
A tall and skinny Candidate Apprentice exclaimed, then nervously lowered his head, fearing that his gaze might offend this great figure.
The other Candidate Apprentices quickly stopped what they were doing upon hearing this, and stepped to the roadside, bowing respectfully.
Their gazes dared not meet Ron’s, as if he were some fearsome presence.
"Continue with your tasks, don’t mind me."
Ron said calmly, understanding their reactions, as he himself once had to show such respect to those lofty "Apprentice Lords."
In an environment with such a vast gap in status, the reverence from the lower ranks to the upper becomes almost instinctual.
Moreover, his current position was significantly higher than that of the ordinary Intermediate Apprentice, second only to the Official Wizards within the School.
The Candidate Apprentices expressed their thanks continuously, but still kept their heads down until Ron walked away, then dared to raise their heads, their eyes filled with envy and yearning.
Ron deliberately slowed his pace, while quietly employing his "Extraordinary Recognition" ability, attempting to sense these Candidate Apprentices’ talents and potentials.
But the results were disappointing.
Most of these apprentices’ spiritual talents were at the lower segment of the Fifth-class Star or Sixth-class Star, similar to what he had been, if not worse.
Their talents were mediocre, their potential limited, and even with diligence, they were likely to barely become Elementary Apprentices, getting stuck at that level for life.
Continuing along his walk, Ron heard the excited voices of some young people behind him.
"That’s Ron Ralph! The genius who supposedly became an Intermediate Apprentice from an ordinary person in just six months!"
A familiar voice said excitedly.
Ron recognized it as the voice of the tall and skinny Candidate Apprentice from earlier; it seemed he had heard of Ron’s achievements from somewhere.
"Really? Just six months?"
Another voice was filled with disbelief:
"How is that possible? It typically takes at least three to five years, doesn’t it? Even that Third-class Star genius Trish reportedly took over six months. Could his talents be even above Third-class Star?"
"It’s absolutely true! He is also a Professional Alchemist, and I’ve heard he’s recently jumped directly into the top twenty in the Candidate Wizard rank!"
The tall and skinny voice grew more excited: "And when he first came here, it’s said his spiritual talent was only at the upper Sixth-class Star, much like ours!"
"This..." The other voice was full of shock, and then turned to excitement:
"Doesn’t that mean we also have hope?"
"Exactly! As long as we find the right method and put in enough effort, we might achieve what he has!"
"Yes! We can’t give up! We can also do this!"
Listening to the excited discussions behind him, Ron shook his head with a hint of helplessness.
He knew these Candidate Apprentices didn’t understand the true reasons behind his success:
The golden finger of infinite profession slots, the special talent of a dual soul, and the Time Guardian pocket watch, an artifact that allowed him to work tirelessly.
Without these, no matter how hard he tried, he couldn’t have achieved what he did in such a short time.
These Candidate Apprentices saw him as a model of rising against the odds, motivating themselves not to give up, which was inherently good.
But thinking about how they would likely hit the harsh realities repeatedly and eventually be compelled to accept a mundane fate...
One can only say that everyone has their own destiny.
"I made a round and haven’t seen any, it seems that discovering a forgotten genius isn’t as easy."
Ron wasn’t too disappointed, he was originally just having a go with a carefree mindset, and, seeing no harvest, he left the Candidate Apprentice Area and headed towards Lady Allen’s herb store.
As he passed through the stone archway of the apprentice market and the bustling merchants of various alien races, arriving at that familiar herb store, a warmth welled up in his heart.
It was here that his path to the extraordinary truly began.
From a Candidate Apprentice with mediocre talents, he grew into the Intermediate Apprentice and Professional Alchemist he is today.
He pushed open the door, familiar herbal fragrances greeted him, with various bottles and jars neatly arranged on the shelves.
Behind the narrow counter, Lady Allen was looking down at a ledger.
However, unlike before, the store now had two young female apprentices, seemingly fifteen or sixteen years old, busy organizing various herbs.
One of them was slender, with an ordinary face, brown short hair neatly tied back, with a focused and serious look between her eyebrows.
She carefully separated leaves and stems of a herb in her hand, her actions precise and orderly.
The other was tall, with long, purple-black hair flowing smoothly to her waist, like the deep starry sky.
Her face seemed to have some makeup, but it couldn’t hide her exquisite features.
She was wiping a row of glass bottles, her movements swift and skilful, occasionally consulting a notebook.
"Long time no see, Madam." Ron greeted softly.
Lady Allen looked up; her deep green eyes lit up immediately, her face relaxing into a few more wrinkles:
"Oh, Ron! You’ve finally remembered this old lady."
Her voice carried reproach, but couldn’t hide the joy:
"I thought you’d forgotten about me after entering the Candidate Wizard ranks."
Ron shook his head with a smile, "How could I? Recently, the courses and training have been overwhelming, I couldn’t find the time. How’s your health?"
"Thanks to you, I’m still stable in all aspects."
Lady Allen let out a small huff, putting down her ledger:
"Just the other day, that old fellow Yuni mentioned you, saying you’ve been doing well in the element courses."
"Yuni Master indeed has given me much guidance."
Ron said sincerely, then his gaze turned to the two Candidate Apprentices who had stopped their work, looking at him curiously.
"This is Fina and Lilia, my new assistants."
Lady Allen followed his gaze and introduced:
"This is Ron Ralph, once my student, now an Intermediate Apprentice in the Candidate Wizard ranks, and also a Professional Alchemist."
The instant these introductions were made, the two young women widened their eyes in shock, seemingly surprised that such brilliance would visit here.
"Greetings, Mr. Ralph."
The ordinary-looking one, Fina, bowed respectfully, her voice gentle and humble:
"Lady Allen often speaks of you, saying you were her most outstanding student."
"Greetings, Mr. Ralph."
The exquisite Lilia also bowed, her voice more melodious, her eyes gleaming with curiosity and some ambition:
"It’s an honor to meet you, Lady Allen says you’re one of the most gifted Alchemists she’s ever met."
Ron casually responded with a few words while quietly using his "Extraordinary Recognition" ability to observe the talents and gifts of the two young women.
Fina’s spiritual talent was at the upper range of the Fifth-class Star, slightly above ordinary Candidate Apprentices, but not extraordinary.
She had good comprehension in Magic Potion Making, precise technique, and a rigorous thought process.
Perhaps with a decade of honing, she might become a Professional Alchemist, but that would be her limit.
Regrettably, Ron sensed no special talent in her.
However, when his gaze turned to Lilia, a peculiar energy fluctuation caught his attention.
Lilia’s spiritual talent was only mid-range Fifth-class Star, slightly lower than Fina, but within her lay a distinct energy flow pattern.
[Lilia
Spiritual Talent: Mid-range Fifth-class Star
Special Talent: Diligence Can Make Up for Incompetence (Second Tier)
Learning ability grows with time when focusing on a skill, reaching an extremely high upper limit]
Ron’s heart stirred slightly; by mere chance, he had encountered a Second Tier special talent here again!

chapters.title: Chapter 176 - 139: Love Dew
chapters.content:
Chapter 176: Chapter 139: Love Dew
Although the initial effects are not obvious, given enough time, this talent can allow someone with mediocre aptitude to grow into a true strong figure.
"You two continue with your work."
Lady Allen waved her hand, indicating for the two assistants to return to their positions, then turned to Ron:
"Come, let’s go to the backyard and have a good chat."
The backyard was still that tranquil little world, with a few simple wooden chairs placed under the shadow of an ancient oak tree.
Various rare herbs were planted in the corner, and a faint floral fragrance permeated the air.
"Seeing them, does it remind you of yourself back in the day?"
Lady Allen asked with a smile, handing Ron a cup of hot tea.
Ron took the teacup, sipping gently.
The familiar taste made him feel very warm: "There are some similarities, but they seem to be working much harder in the store than I did back then."
"Diligence is part of it." Lady Allen nodded, her gaze shifted to the two busy figures inside the store:
"Fina is very smart, with a strong understanding of herbs and formulas, but she sometimes lacks the courage to break norms."
She paused, then added:
"Lilia, on the other hand, starts slowly, but she is very diligent and good at innovating, not afraid of failure. Most importantly, she possesses rare perseverance and patience."
Ron understood in his heart; this matched his earlier observation.
Lady Allen’s eyes reflected a hint of complex emotions:
"In fact, in some ways, she resembles you, doesn’t she? You both have unexpected potential."
"To be honest, I didn’t expect you to find two new assistants just months after I left."
Not picking up on that thread, Ron replied half-jokingly: "Did I not perform well enough?"
"Nonsense." Lady Allen gently tapped the back of his hand:
"You’ve graduated, have your own workshop and clients, you can’t always follow this old lady learning those basics, right?"
She took a sip of tea, a hint of concern in her eyes:
"Besides, I heard you’ve been doing quite well in the Candidate Wizard sequence recently?"
"Not bad." Ron humbly said, then briefly recounted his main experiences during this time.
Including entering various advanced courses, receiving special guidance from Soron and Yuni, and improving his ranking in the Candidate Wizard sequence.
Lady Allen listened quietly, a trace of complexity in her expression:
"Your growth rate is indeed astonishing, it seems my initial judgment was right. But..."
Her tone suddenly became serious:
"The faster you grow, the more you’re exposed to the gaze of those in higher positions. Be especially cautious, especially towards those who suddenly show abnormal interest in you."
Ron felt a chill in his heart, understanding what Lady Allen meant.
"I will be careful." Ron nodded seriously, then shifted the topic elsewhere.
The two chatted about many things, ranging from new formula development to rumors about the Bloodline Altar, internal power changes in the School, and the latest movements of the Crystal Tower in the distance.
Ron found that although Lady Allen was secluded in this small herb store, her understanding of the outside world was far more extensive and deep than he had imagined.
"It’s getting late; I should be going back."
Ron glanced at the sky, stood up to say goodbye:
"Next time you have time, you can visit my workshop and see its development."
"Hehe... I appreciate the thought, but these old bones can’t stand the hassle."
Lady Allen stood up with the help of her cane, seeming not to have any other feelings due to her student leaving.
"By the way, Lilia learned about your identity and seems to be a bit interested in you. She might come to you in the upcoming days. If you lack a Magic Potion Assistant, feel free to keep her."
She slightly squinted her emerald green eyes, her words carrying a hidden meaning:
"You should somewhat appreciate the beauty of receiving ’grace,’ right? How about letting this child be your first personal apprentice?"
"This... wouldn’t it affect your work on this side...?"
Ron was a bit hesitant but also tempted, unsure what to say when he noticed that Lady Allen had already waved her hand, giving a gentle order to leave:
"Alright, we’ve talked enough, if there’s nothing else, hurry back."
......
Elsewhere, Lilia stood at the herb store’s window, watching Ron’s departing figure, a trace of complex emotion in her eyes.
She gently smoothed out non-existent creases on her apron, as if this could calm the ripples in her heart.
From the earlier conversation between Ron and Lady Allen, she had already comprehended how high the status of this young Alchemist is, far beyond her imagination.
"Intermediate Apprentice, Professional Alchemist, Member of the Candidate Wizard Sequence..."
She silently counted in her heart, each title seemed as distant and insurmountable as a chasm.
"Lilia, come help me sort out this batch of Moonlight Grass." Fina’s voice interrupted her thoughts.
"Okay, coming right away."
Lilia snapped back to reality, quickly walking toward the workbench.
But her peripheral vision still involuntarily drifted towards the door, as if she could still see the figure that had already disappeared.
"You’re quite interested in that Ron apprentice?"
Fina asked calmly, while meticulously sorting through the Moonlight Grass.
Lilia was slightly taken aback, then forced a smile:
"Just curious. After all, a genius like him... is rare among the School, right?"
"Indeed, it’s rare." Fina nodded, a hint of admiration in her eyes:
"To achieve such accomplishments in such a short time, one must surely possess extraordinary talent and effort."
Lily didn’t respond, just kept her head down and continued working, but her mind was already calculating something.
The next evening, after Fina left, Lily stayed behind alone to organize the day’s accounts and inventory.
This was a job she had volunteered for, just to have some time alone.
She sat behind the counter, opened a small, exquisite notebook, densely packed with various information she had gathered:
The location of Ron’s workshop, daily activity patterns, known achievements and capabilities... each entry written in extreme detail.
"A year ago... came to Black Mist Jungle from the Kingdom... Sixth-class Star Spiritual Power talent... became an Intermediate Apprentice in less than six months... the only private apprentice of Lady Allen..."
Lily murmured the contents of the notes, a certain resolute light flickering in her eyes.
She closed the notebook and walked to the small well in the backyard, fetched a basin of water and began washing up.
The water reflected her delicate and charming face:
A high nose bridge, clear eyes, lips as soft as petals, every feature seemingly crafted with perfection.
Lily stared expressionlessly at her reflection in the water, her memories involuntarily flashing back to a distant past.
A small territory located on the southwestern border, the ancient castle of Visor Baron.
A chance encounter between a beautiful maid and the lord, leading to the birth and growth of a bastard daughter...
"Wretched girl, do you know why you’re still alive?"
The baroness’s icy voice still echoed in her ears:
"All thanks to that face of yours, identical to that of your wretched mother. If it weren’t for your resemblance to her, you’d have been thrown into the moat with that woman to feed the fish."
Due to this upbringing, Lily learned from a young age how to appease anyone who could potentially help her, honing her survival skills in the cracks.
At fifteen, she overheard a conversation between her stepmother and older sister in the corner of the castle.
Upon discovering that the baron had agreed to give her as a "gift" to a lustful old noble from a neighboring country, she almost despaired and wanted to escape immediately.
Thankfully, fate provided a way out—the annual "seed selection" of Wizards granted her a chance to leave her family.
Though the Spiritual Power test results were not outstanding, it at least allowed her the opportunity to become a Candidate Apprentice.
However, the harsh reality soon made her realize that ordinary people without strong talent would also struggle here.
Just as she was about to give up hope, she met Fina: a girl with a remarkable background and talent.
Using her learned methods, Lily flattered Fina in numerous ways, becoming her best friend here.
And when Fina successfully gained Lady Allen’s favor, Lily cleverly secured her own spot at the Herb Store.
All this was to avoid the Intermediate Apprentice who had taken an interest in her: Ogg Keynes, a man who delighted in collecting beautiful female slaves.
"I will never become his plaything." Lily looked at her reflection in the water, her gaze firm and cold.
She knew that Keynes had collected three female slaves, none of whom met a fair fate:
Either discarded after being tired of them or perished painfully in bizarre experiments.
After finishing her wash, Lily returned to her dormitory and retrieved a flat wooden box from the bottom of her suitcase.
Inside was a set of exquisite dresses and cosmetics, precious heirlooms left by her mother.
"Ron Ralph..."
She whispered the name: "A genius in the Candidate Wizard sequence, Lady Allen’s prized student, Professional Alchemist..."
Through observation and intelligence gathering, Lily had confirmed Ron to be her best ally at present.
He was strong enough to protect her from Keynes’s harassment;
His character appeared gentle, and it was never heard that he deliberately made things difficult for others;
Most importantly, it was said that he had so far had no intimate relations with any woman here, which was a significant advantage for Lily.
She had already discovered the exact location of Ron’s workshop, even having observed it secretly a few times.
Tomorrow, she would risk approaching him, asking to become his assistant or... any role he needed.
"Far better than being treated as a plaything by Keynes, at least Ron appears to be a normal person."
Lily murmured to herself with a bitter smile, yet her eyes flashed with determination.
In this cruel Extraordinary World, clinging to the strong is the only survival strategy for the weak.
At dawn the next day, Lily requested leave from Lady Allen, falsely claiming she had to care for a sick roommate.
She returned to her residence, carefully washed and dressed.
First, she bathed her entire body with special petal dew, letting her skin exude a faint fragrance;
Then donned the treasured attire: a well-tailored light blue dress that maintained elegance while perfectly outlining a graceful figure;
Finally, she applied a touch of light makeup, just enough to emphasize the contours of her eyes and lips.
The girl in the mirror was breathtakingly beautiful, possessing innocence alongside a mature allure from her makeup.
Lily practiced several expressions in front of the mirror, ensuring she appeared both humble and respectful.
"The final preparation..." She retrieved a small bottle from the bottom of the cabinet, containing a light pink liquid:
"Love Dew," a mild and harmless potion that slightly enhanced allure.
She carefully applied a drop on her neck and wrists.
The potion quickly absorbed into her skin, releasing an irresistibly subtle fragrance, rumored to evoke protective instincts and favorable feelings in the opposite sex.
With everything ready, Lily took a deep breath and walked out of the room.
Today would be the turning point of her destiny.
......
Ron stood in the center of the workshop’s training ground, carefully sensing the elemental energy flowing within him.
The recent intensive training had made him much more adept at controlling the light and fire elements, almost to the point of free will.

chapters.title: Chapter 177 - 140: Ranking Rise
chapters.content:
Chapter 177: Chapter 140: Ranking Rise
"Master, there is a visitor." Ailan’s voice interrupted his meditation.
Ron frowned slightly, he hadn’t arranged any visitors today: "Who is it?"
"It’s a girl in a blue dress, claiming to be Lady Allen’s new assistant."
Ailan answered, with a barely noticeable trace of caution in her tone.
Ron was somewhat surprised, then recalled the two new assistants he had seen at the herb store earlier.
He straightened his robe and walked towards the front hall: "Invite her in please."
As he entered the front hall, a delicate fragrance greeted him.
A girl in a light blue long dress stood by the window, the sunlight streaming through the window outlined her graceful silhouette.
Hearing footsteps, the girl turned around, revealing a delicate and enchanting face:
It was Lilia, but vastly different from her plain appearance at the herb store yesterday; now she was radiantly beautiful, almost unreal.
"Lord Ralph, I apologize for the interruption." Lilia bowed slightly, her voice soft and pleasant:
"I am Lilia, Lady Allen’s new assistant, and I was fortunate to meet you yesterday."
Ron nodded, his expression calm: "I remember you, what brings you here today?"
Lilia lowered her head slightly, displaying precisely the right amount of shyness and humility:
"I... I would like to request to assist in your workshop, to learn more about Magic Potion Making."
She carefully lifted her eyes, observing Ron’s reaction:
"Lady Allen often mentions your achievements, saying you’re the most talented student she has taught. I believe your guidance would be greatly beneficial to me."
Ron raised an eyebrow slightly, not responding immediately.
He keenly sensed that there must be a reason behind this sudden request.
In the Black Mist Jungle’s unique environment, he had developed a habit of staying alert to sudden events.
"Aren’t you currently studying under Lady Allen?"
Ron asked calmly: "Why do you want to come here?"
Lilia seemed to have anticipated this question, she sighed lightly, a worry flashed in her eyes:
"Lady Allen has limited resources, and both Fina and I can only do basic work. I heard you have your workshop and are conducting more advanced research..."
She hesitated for a moment and then added: "Additionally, I... have some personal reasons for wanting to leave there temporarily."
Ron watched her, discreetly using his "Extraordinary Recognition" ability.
Various talents were the same as observed at the herb store yesterday; what caught his attention was the peculiar energy fluctuation emanating from the girl.
It was clearly the effect of some charm-type magic potion, though its potency was weak, the intent was obvious.
This woman indeed has impure motives...
Ron understood in his heart but did not expose it, instead, he continued to ask:
"Do you have any special skills? My workshop already has someone managing daily affairs, and I don’t really need an ordinary assistant."
Lilia’s eyes flashed with a trace of panic, but she quickly composed herself:
"I have some experience in processing magic potion materials and beginner formulas, though limited, I learn quickly."
She paused and added:
"Additionally, I am proficient in housework and cooking, I studied etiquette and stewardship in a noble family before coming to the Black Mist Jungle."
Ron nodded thoughtfully.
Lilia’s special talent was indeed precious, and if properly cultivated, her potential was boundless.
Especially since he currently needed an apprentice, as someone to receive "favors."
Previously, he had tried to teach Ailan some mysticism and magic potion knowledge.
The dryad’s comprehension wasn’t bad, but gave him no feedback of favors, perhaps such favor rules were limited to those within the Wizard System.
"I can temporarily let you help in the workshop."
Ron finally decided: "But there are certain rules you must follow."
Lilia’s eyes sparkled with joy, she nodded quickly: "Of course, Lord Ralph, please instruct me."
"Firstly, the experimental area in the workshop is off-limits without permission; secondly, everything you see and hear must not be disclosed externally; lastly..."
Ron’s tone became serious: "I want you to honestly tell me the real reason for coming here."
Lilia’s expression stiffened slightly, then she lowered her gaze: "Actually, I... I’m hiding from someone."
Her voice turned low, carrying a hint of fear:
"There is an Intermediate Apprentice, Ogg Keynes, and he has been eyeing me. Rumor has it he already has three female slaves, and their fates have been tragic. I don’t want to be the next."
Ron listened expressionlessly, showing no sympathy or anger:
"So you chose me as a protector?"
Lilia nodded lightly, tears in her eyes, this time not feigned:
"I know it’s presumptuous, but your strength and status are enough to deter him. I promise to work hard and not cause you any trouble."
Ron was silent for a moment before finally speaking:
"I can provide you shelter, but only if you genuinely intend to study and work, not with other motives."
Lilia sighed in relief, nodding quickly: "Of course, I promise to give it my all!"
"Ailan." Ron turned to the dryad: "Take Lilia to the small room in the backyard to settle down, then explain the basic rules of the workshop to her."
Ailan nodded, her vines swaying gently: "As you command, Master."
The dryad’s mood appeared not very high, her response seemed a tad slower than usual.

chapters.title: Chapter 178 - 140: Ranking Rise (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 178: Chapter 140: Ranking Rise (Part 2)
When the two left, Ron stood alone by the window, pondering this sudden variable.
"No matter. If anyone dares to spy on my research results, I’ll just bury them in the yard as fertilizer... From what Lady Allen indicated yesterday, I should have full disposal rights."
Ron shook his head, turned around, and went back to his laboratory to continue his research.
.........
At the same time, in a secret conference room of the Central High Tower of the School.
Soron Griffiths and Yuni Seraphin were having a private conversation.
"So, you’ve noticed that little guy called Ron too?"
Yuni played with a piece of crystal in her hand, her eyes flashing with amusement.
Soron nodded, reaching to rub his temple:
"His talent is indeed exceptional, and his rate of progress is astonishing. I’ve never seen anyone grasp so much knowledge and skills in such a short time."
"It’s not just a matter of speed."
Yuni added:
"What’s most surprising is that he seems to excel in numerous fields beyond ordinary comprehension. Whether it’s Spiritual Control, Elemental Affinity, or Magic Potion Making, he performs like a seasoned expert."
"Moreover, from my observations, he has also successfully activated some kind of bloodline ability."
Soron squinted his eyes: "This kind of all-rounded development is extremely rare, most apprentices focus on one or two fields."
Yuni set down the crystal: "Do you know who this reminds me of?"
Soron nodded lightly: "Corina’s student, Trish. Although her comprehensiveness is not as good as Ron’s, her growth rate is also astonishing."
The two exchanged a glance, with a knowing look in their eyes.
"Do you think he might also have other special talents?" Soron inquired.
Yuni pondered for a moment: "’Medicinal Body Resonance’ is indeed a rare talent, but it doesn’t explain his astonishing progress in all fields, unless..."
"Unless he is hiding an even more powerful talent or ability," Soron continued the thought, "or he used some unconventional method."
The two lapsed into silence, each contemplating the implications of this possibility.
Finally, Soron broke the silence:
"In any case, his potential cannot be overlooked. We should adjust his ranking in the Candidate Wizard sequence."
Yuni nodded in agreement: "He’s currently ranking nineteenth, I suggest promoting him at least two places, into the top seventeen."
"Why not directly into the top fifteen?"
Soron proposed: "At the Candidate Wizard sequence meeting in half a month, we can officially present this suggestion."
Yuni hesitated slightly: "The top fifteen is an important threshold, are you sure he’s reached that level?"
Soron smiled: "Don’t forget, we’ve both gained quite a bit of ’favors’ from him. Wouldn’t it be a waste not to cultivate such a talent early?"
Yuni thought for a moment and finally nodded: "Alright, I’ll support your proposal, but..."
A hint of caution flashed in her eyes: "Corina seems to have shown interest in him as well, which might create some... competition."
Soron’s smile remained calm:
"Competition is common, but true talent will always be discovered. I believe the future of Ron Ralph will be more brilliant than we imagine."
.........
As night fell, the workshop was brightly lit.
The familiar big-mouthed parrot flew in from the open window and delivered a letter into Ron’s hand.
He smiled faintly, unsurprised to see the rank promotion displayed in the booklet.
Feeding the prepared honeyed treat to the messenger, he received a grateful chirp in return.
Meanwhile, in a small room at the backyard, Lilia sat at the bedside, gently caressing her newly arranged humble abode.
Though only marginally better than her room in the Candidate Apprentice dormitories, at least here it’s safe and clean.
Most importantly, she was away from Keynes’ threat.
She changed out of the elaborately prepared fancy dress into the ordinary work clothes Ailan provided for her.
As she looked at her now plain self in the mirror, Lilia sighed lightly.
Ailan had already explained the rules to her, the most stringent of which was not to enter any experimental areas without permission, especially those rooms on the second floor.
"It seems I still need some time to fully integrate here," Lilia muttered to herself, a hint of determination flashing in her eyes:
"But it’s okay, I have patience."
She took a small bottle of potion from her bag and gently shook it.
This was a calming potion she made herself, helping her sleep soundly in unfamiliar environments.
"Tomorrow begins a whole new life." Lilia took a sip of the potion, lay down on the bed, and closed her eyes.
Whatever the future holds, at least for now, she has found a temporary safe haven.
And for someone like her, being safe for a day is already a great fortune.
.........
The first rays of morning sunshine poured through the window onto the floor of the simple bedroom, Lilia had already woken up, sitting by the window, combing her long hair.
This was her third day at Ron’s workshop, and each day she tried to reassess her value and identity.
She had already reported her whereabouts to Lady Allen, but the elderly lady was not surprised by her choice.
She merely reminded her to study well under Ron, while Fina seemed a bit reluctant.
Yesterday, Ailan assigned her the task of organizing the potion materials inventory, and the complicated names and properties of the materials gave her a headache.
"Today, I must do better." Lilia spoke softly to the small mirror, her eyes showing a rare determination.
Initially, when she came here, she held thoughts of seeking shelter and aligning herself with those in power, but the experiences of the past few days gradually changed her mind.
Ron was neither cold nor overly familiar with her, always maintaining an appropriate distance, which greatly surprised her.
In her past experiences, men almost always showed some degree of desire in the face of her beauty.
But Ron seemed entirely indifferent to this, his eyes focused only on Magic Potion Making and extraordinary knowledge.
More importantly, she discovered Ron’s strength was far more unfathomable than rumored.
Yesterday evening, Lilia accidentally saw Ron practicing Elemental Manipulation in the backyard.
With a gentle movement of his fingertips, the gold-red halo shone brilliantly like a miniature sun, its power awe-inspiring.
Such elemental control ability, perhaps even some Advanced Apprentices receiving individual instruction might be around this level.
"I must seize this opportunity and study diligently..."
Lilia took a deep breath, stood up and tidied her clothes, ready to start a new day.
When she arrived in the main hall of the workshop, she found Ron already waiting there, with various Magic Potion materials and tools laid out on the long table.
"Good morning, Master Ralph." Lilia greeted respectfully.
"Good morning, Lilia."
Ron nodded in response: "Today, I want to teach you some basic magic potion knowledge to test your learning ability."
Lilia’s eyes lit up: "Really? Thank you very much!"
Ron smiled slightly: "No need to thank me excessively, teaching a student with potential also benefits the mentor."
Over the next few hours, Ron patiently explained the core concepts of Basic Magic Potion Making and some simple formulas.
Unlike Lady Allen’s stern and direct teaching style, Ron focused more on guiding thought, often helping Lilia understand complex concepts through questions and demonstrations.
"You see, although Moonflower and Silver Star Vine seem contradictory in properties on the surface, if mixed in a specific ratio and added with a suitable amount of stabilizer, they can create a unique synergistic effect."
Ron explained while demonstrating the handling of materials.
Lilia observed and learned with full concentration, occasionally asking questions.

chapters.title: Chapter 179 - 141: Master and Disciple
chapters.content:
Chapter 179: Chapter 141: Master and Disciple
To her surprise, Ron never showed impatience at her basic questions. Instead, he encouraged her to ask more and think deeply.
"When learning Magic Potion Making, the most important thing is not to memorize formulas, but to understand the relationships between materials and the principles of their reactions."
As Ron prepared a simple Healing Potion, he explained:
"Only by truly understanding these basics can you make appropriate judgments and adjustments in practice."
Lilia nodded thoughtfully. This teaching method was completely different from her past experiences.
In her noble family, when she learned etiquette and the art of housekeeping, her teachers only required rote memorization and imitation, never explaining the reasons behind them.
"Give it a try. Prepare a Stimulant Potion using the method I just demonstrated."
Ron pushed the materials in front of Lilia. "Don’t worry about failure. Mistakes in the learning process are often the best teachers."
Lilia took a deep breath and carefully began to follow the steps she remembered.
Her movements were clumsy, yet unexpectedly precise, as if some intuition was guiding her.
Ron observed silently from the side, having already sensed something.
Perhaps this is the unique trait of the ’Diligence Can Make Up for Incompetence’ gift:
A seemingly ordinary starting point, but with a learning curve that steepens over time.
Every attempt Lilia made invisibly enhanced her understanding and operational skills.
[Extraordinary Recognition Experience Points +1]
He discreetly utilized his ’Extraordinary Recognition’ ability, observing the energy flow within Lilia.
As she focused on preparing the potion, that special energy fluctuation became more evident, like a tiny yet resilient stream, slowly and steadily strengthening.
"Not bad." When Lilia completed her first potion, Ron commented:
"Although there’s room for improvement in purity, for a first attempt, it’s quite outstanding."
A delighted smile appeared on Lilia’s face. This heartfelt praise gave her a long-lost sense of accomplishment.
It was not because of her appearance or charm, but sourced from her genuine effort and ability.
"Thank you for your guidance, Lord Ralph."
Lilia said sincerely, her eyes sparkling with gratitude.
"No need to be so formal," Ron replied with a smile. "On the path of learning, we are all seekers of knowledge."
For the rest of the day, Lilia fully immersed herself in the basics of Magic Potion Making.
She was surprised to find an unexpected affinity for the subject, especially in material identification and handling.
Ron also noticed this and timely provided more challenging content.
"Your learning ability is strong," Ron remarked when dusk fell and the day’s teaching concluded.
"Tomorrow, we can try some more complex formulas and begin practicing basic Spiritual Control."
Lilia raised her head in surprise. "Spiritual Control? But my Spiritual Talent is only a Fifth-class Star upper tier..."
"The basics of Spiritual Control are not entirely dependent on innate talent."
Ron explained, "The correct methods and persistent practice can also bring significant improvement. Besides, for an Alchemist, basic Spiritual Control is an essential skill."
A warmth surged through Lilia’s heart.
In her past life, few people would see her potential and be willing to invest time and effort in cultivating her.
Most only saw her appearance, viewing her as something to be used or possessed.
"I will work hard, Lord Ralph," she promised in a low voice.
Returning to her small room, Lilia sat quietly at the bedside, her mind filled with countless thoughts.
The schemes and cunning from when she first arrived at the workshop seemed so shallow and ridiculous now.
Compared to gaining protection through seductive tactics, earning achievements through her own effort and learning seemed a brighter and more tangible path.
"Perhaps my value is more than just this face," Lilia murmured, a new hope gleaming in her eyes.
