"Having a genius like you constantly helping me makes me begin to believe, maybe it’s not just an unattainable dream."
Ron didn’t respond, just quietly picked up the cold tea liquid, took a sip, and moistened his throat.
Everything he was doing for Andre now, was done within his own abilities, as a convenient gesture.
No one can predict the future.
But one thing is certain, he believes he can make it to the end, even if it might take a long time...

chapters.title: Chapter 199 - 153: Melting Furnace Concept
chapters.content:
Chapter 199: Chapter 153: Melting Furnace Concept
The wind howled outside, but the endless research in the workshop left Ron feeling both exhausted and fulfilled.
Clearly, in this Extraordinary World, true security could only be achieved through mastering power.
At dawn, as the first rays of sunlight spilled onto the laboratory floor through the window, Ron put down his Alchemy Tools.
He rubbed his sore shoulders after six hours of continuous work.
On the workbench in front of him, dozens of metal plates were neatly arranged, each engraved with runes in different configurations.
Some had already oxidized and changed color, while others retained their original luster.
"After so many attempts, there’s finally progress," Ron murmured to himself, cautiously picking up the last metal plate.
The rune configuration on this special alloy differed subtly from the dozens of previous attempts.
In earlier experiments, Ron had tested various rune combinations, but none achieved the desired isolation Effect.
Some runes caused the metal to overheat and melt, others made it extremely brittle, and some could not form a stable Energy Field at all.
But this last one—marked as Ψ-23—showed delightful Traits in testing.
When Ron injected two mutually repelling Energies into it, the metal plate successfully isolated them into two completely separate regions, without any leakage or interference.
Ron picked up a specially-made glass rod and carefully touched the runes on the left side of the metal plate.
The metal emitted a faint blue glow immediately, but this light was limited to the left half, while the runes on the right remained completely inert.
"The Energy isolation layer is theoretically feasible."
Ron detailed the observations in his notebook:
"But the duration still needs improvement."
He glanced at the hourglass on the wall; the isolation effect of this metal plate could only last about five minutes once activated, far from meeting practical application needs.
Ron opened the thick notebook on the table, densely packed with detailed data from previous experiments and reasons for failures.
Every failure brought new insights, and every mistake paved the way for ultimate success.
"The key to the isolation layer lies in the arrangement of runes, not the runes themselves."
Ron muttered, his fingers sliding over the lines of small text in the notebook:
"It’s like building a dam; the way the stones are placed is more important than the stones themselves."
This research into the metal isolation layer originated from the information about Black Wizards he had read in the Library some time ago.
The ancient texts mentioned that during the Awakening Process, Black Wizards were gradually eroded by polluted Energy, leading to personality distortion.
However, Ron noticed a detail:
A few Black Wizards could remain rational for quite a long time, even growing continuously stronger.
They often wore some special amulets or equipment or used other unique methods to create a "buffer zone," slowing the direct impact of pollution on the soul.
"If a perfect isolation layer could be created..."
Ron pondered, a cautious light flickering in his eyes:
"Theoretically, it should be possible to completely separate two Energy Fields, allowing no interference."
This idea sparked his interest in researching the isolation layer.
Pursuing power requires constant calmness and rational thinking; Ron never considered stepping directly onto the path of a Black Wizard, which represented irreversible distortion and madness.
"Power only has value when it is under Rational Control." This was a creed etched in the Library of Consciousness.
Ron checked the parameters of the Ψ-23 metal plate once more, then carefully placed it into a specially-crafted wooden box.
He then took down another notebook from the shelf, bearing the words "Soul Steel Data."
During the past week’s full School lockdown, aside from various daily practices, he had been working on two research lines in parallel:
On one hand, the energy isolation layer experiments; on the other, the preliminary analysis of that precious piece of Soul Steel.
These two studies seemed unconnected, but in Ron’s plan, they would perfectly merge at some point in the future.
The analysis of Soul Steel’s Traits was exceptionally complicated.
This mysterious metal had extremely high plasticity and Magic Conductivity, yet it was also highly selective, seeming to "perceive" the intent and capability of the handler.
Ron had already spent dozens of hours attempting to establish preliminary "communication" with this metal, allowing it to gradually adapt to the characteristics of his Spiritual Power.
"If the principles of the isolation layer could be successfully applied to Soul Steel..."
He gently caressed the rare metal, glowing with a silvery-gray sheen:
"Perhaps it could create a whole new type of Alchemy Item, with unprecedented Traits."
But he hadn’t fully determined what kind of tool it would be specifically.
Ron was not someone who acted solely on intuition; every step had to be based on thorough research and rigorous experimentation.
He closed his eyes, letting his tired brain rest for a moment, but his thoughts drifted involuntarily to those records he had seen in the Library.
"...The Awakening process is essentially a process of fusion with polluted Energy. As the Awakening Level increases, they gain stronger Erosion abilities, but at the cost of their sanity."
Ron recalled those textual descriptions while contemplating a question that seemed almost heretical to a normal Wizard:
Is it possible to acquire the power of a Black Wizard while completely avoiding its negative impacts?
Theoretically, if the Awakening process could be confined within some external container instead of one’s own soul, it might avoid direct personality Erosion.

chapters.title: Chapter 200 - 153: Melting Furnace Concept (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 200: Chapter 153: Melting Furnace Concept (Part 2)
But this requires a vessel capable of bearing soul fragments, a container that can safely coexist with pollution energy.
Ron’s gaze unconsciously turned to the soul steel on the shelf, as a bold and crazy idea gradually took shape:
If a special "activated" magic sword were to be forged using soul steel, and part of his soul fragments were to be infused into it, allowing the sword, rather than the human, to "awaken"...
Moreover, since the soul is connected, is it possible to then channel all the spiritual contamination produced by his meditation into the sword, thus once and for all solving the problem of spiritual contamination?
Even using the spiritual contamination to nourish the magic sword’s growth in reverse, turning it into a "furnace" that incinerates pollution and transforms it into his pure strength!
Instead of relying on the pocket watch’s reset ability to repeatedly purify, which ultimately is not a long-term solution.
"However, at this stage, it’s still too risky."
Ron shook his head, interrupting his own thoughts:
"Take it slow, more research and preparation are needed."
This idea is too radical, involving the manipulation of the soul, and any mishandling could lead to soul trauma.
He needs more information, more experimental data, to further consider this possibility.
Ron stood up, walked to the window, gazing at the gradually brightening sky.
The recent experiment on the energy isolation layer achieved some preliminary progress, but there is still a long way to go before actual application.
"Step by step, securely," he repeatedly warned himself in his heart.
.........
The atmosphere in the Black Mist Jungle became unusually heavy.
The busy figures once seen in the school’s Central Square were no longer there, leaving only patrol teams of Law Enforcement Officers, watching every passing apprentice with vigilant eyes.
"Don’t look around, keep your head down and walk."
An older Elementary Apprentice whispered, pulling on his companion’s sleeve.
They walked briskly through the avenue, avoiding eye contact, relaxing only after turning into a secluded path.
"All fieldwork assignments have been canceled, my Magic Stone Fragment quota for this month is only a third of what it was."
The older apprentice cursed:
"If this continues, even basic subsistence will become an issue."
"You’re actually better off."
His companion sighed:
"Randall is worse off, he tried to sneak out of the school to collect rare herbs the day before yesterday and was caught red-handed by the Law Enforcement Team. He’s still in the Detention Room now."
Since Oliver defected and prompted the school’s crackdown on the "Eye of the Abyss," the entire school had become like a pot about to boil over, calm on the surface but turbulent underneath.
Everyone could feel the unprecedented oppressive atmosphere.
More seriously, the sharp reduction in Magic Stone allocation.
No fieldwork assignments mean no extra rewards from completing commissions;
No collection permits mean no chance to search for valuable materials to sell on their own.
The income source for most Elementary Apprentices was cut off abruptly, making life suddenly difficult to manage.
The Central Hall has received dozens of apprentices seeking loans in recent days, but there’s a limit to how many they can help.
The situation at the marketplace was even worse.
The once-flourishing shops were now deserted, with many vendors simply closing and taking a break.
Those vendors who continued to persist had already increased their goods’ prices multiple times over.
"The price of bread has increased tenfold, why don’t you just rob us!"
A skinny Candidate Apprentice shouted angrily.
The bread vendor shrugged:
"It’s not my fault, the material prices have gone up. I can’t do business at a loss, can I?"
"It’s all because of that damn Oliver!"
The skinny apprentice spat on the ground:
"If he hadn’t defected, we wouldn’t be in this situation!"
This wasn’t the first person to blame their hardships on Oliver.
In the eyes of many apprentices, Oliver was not just a traitor but the main culprit behind their difficult living conditions.
If he were here, he might have already been torn to shreds by the angry apprentices.
In the temporary camp for law enforcement stationed outside the Edge Forest, the atmosphere was even tenser.
"Did the third squad discover any abnormal situations?"
Law Enforcement Captain Rein Koester asked with a frown to a scout who had just returned.
"Reporting to the Captain, no traces of Oliver or other Awakened have been found."
The young Middle Apprentice replied respectfully:
"However, near the stream at the northeast corner, some strange black slime was discovered, samples have been collected and brought back."
Rein nodded: "Send it to the Alchemy department for analysis. Also, strengthen the night patrol, report every two hours."
"Understood, Captain."
The Law Enforcement Captain turned and looked into the depths of the Edge Forest, a trace of worry in his eyes.
Since Oliver’s defection, more than five Law Enforcement Officers have gone missing, including Norris among them, a number of Middle Apprentices.
This is not just a serious loss of personnel but a blatant challenge to the school.
"The defectors must be apprehended and brought to justice."
Rein murmured to himself, a fierce look in his eyes, as this was a mandatory task set by the school’s higher-ups.
.........
In the following days, Ron’s research entered a whole new phase.
He was no longer content with a simple metallic isolation layer and began trying to replicate the same effect on different materials in hopes of finding the most suitable vessel.
Wood, crystals, fabrics, and even some biological tissues were all meticulously tested by him.
Each material reacted uniquely.
Some could maintain isolation effects for longer periods, some could carry more types of energy, and some could either enhance or weaken the isolation strength under specific conditions.

chapters.title: Chapter 202 - 154: Following This Arduous Journey, At Last Among the Stars
chapters.content:
Chapter 202: Chapter 154: Following This Arduous Journey, At Last Among the Stars
These pieces of information confirmed the shape-shifter’s words.
Just one last step, and the shape-shifter’s skin could become a true "Glory Legacy," gaining the essential complete isolation capability for Ron’s plan.
"What does ’pure soul energy’ mean?"
Ron further inquired, "Is there a specific source or method to obtain it?"
"The souls of extraordinary creatures," the shape-shifter replied:
"Especially those with special bloodlines or talents. The rarer the bloodline, the purer the soul energy. Moreover, the extraction of soul energy must be completed at the moment of the creature’s death; otherwise, the energy will dissipate rapidly."
Ron fell into contemplation.
Extraordinary creatures’ soul energy is not easy to obtain, especially under the strict control of the School.
But if at the Bloody Gladiatorial Games...
"I understand." Ron finally nodded, "You can rest now."
The shape-shifter’s outline melted promptly, reattached to the surface of Ron’s skin, and resumed a concealed state.
Ron returned to his workbench, took out a new notebook to jot down data briefly, and began recording today’s discoveries and thoughts in the Library of Consciousness.
His plan started to become more specific:
First, he needed to further study isolation layer technology and attempt to apply it to soul steel, preparing for future magic sword creation;
Second, he needed to find a method to obtain pure soul energy to help the shape-shifter’s skin complete its final advancement;
Lastly, he also needed to consider the potential negative effects of soul splitting and how to safely handle the split soul fragments.
"The Bloody Gladiatorial Games..." Ron muttered softly, a gleam of contemplation flashing in his eyes.
The gladiatorial games might not only provide an opportunity to obtain soul energy, but the champion’s reward—the legendary "stand-in puppet"—might also be the key to solving the soul handling problem.
Ron recalled the information he acquired from the slave merchant:
The stand-in puppet could carry the user’s consciousness, creating an almost identical "copy" to the original, unaffected by the original’s injuries.
"If the split soul fragments could be placed within the stand-in puppet..."
Ron pondered this possibility, "Perhaps it could avoid direct soul damage and provide greater operational space."
But all this was based on a series of bold assumptions:
Can the shape-shifter’s skin successfully advance?
Can the isolation layer technology be applied to magic swords?
Is the stand-in puppet truly as powerful as the legends claim?
"More experiments and verification are needed," Ron reminded himself, maintaining his usual calmness and rationality.
He walked to the window, gazing at the gradually brightening sky, his thoughts whirling.
Power is a tool, not a goal.
The pursuit is for mastery over power, not to be controlled by it.
With this mindset, Ron returned to his workbench to continue his experiments.
Under the light, the soul steel shimmered with a cold luster, as if telling ancient secrets.
He stood before the experiment table, then turned to look at the crystal that had successfully inscribed a complete isolation rune system, a sense of accomplishment welling up inside.
This crystal could simultaneously contain three different energy fields, isolating them completely and interfering with each other, lasting up to a week.
In the past few weeks of research, he had spent substantial time daily on energy isolation layer testing, applying what he learned in his alchemy classes.
It was this focused research that ultimately rewarded him:
[Alchemy (Beginner) Experience Points + 1]
[Breakthrough! Alchemy (Beginner 50/50) → Alchemy (Skilled 1/100)]
[Gained Additional Trait: Conception (Enhancing creative inspiration for alchemy items)]
Ron was momentarily stunned, then felt a new vitality surge in his spirit.
Breaking through to the skilled level in alchemy, his understanding seemed to have reached a brand new level.
Of course, at his current level, merely breaking through to the skilled level was unlikely to stir significant emotions within him.
"Conception..." Ron saw the name of this additional trait and, in an instant, felt sparks of inspiration blooming in his mind.
In recent weeks, progress in energy isolation layer research had been slow, but now he seemed to see more possibilities.
Design schemes naturally formed in his mind, as if someone were gently guiding him by his ear.
In retrospect, this breakthrough was not accidental.
Since he started researching energy isolation layers, every failure had brought new insights.
He had tried dozens of rune combinations and various materials, undergoing countless setbacks.
Metal overheating and melting, materials becoming brittle, unstable energy fields... behind every failure was a reason worth learning.
Ron looked at the densely packed data in his notebook, and his understanding of alchemy had shifted from original theoretical mastery to genuine internal comprehension.
This improvement was directly reflected in his other skills, including magic potion research and magic practice.
What surprised him even more was that the "conception" trait brought not only an enhancement of inspiration but also a new perspective.
He started to see the delicate balance of energy flow inside alchemy items, perceiving the resonance and repulsion between different materials.
Looking at the panel to view his alchemist advancement conditions, Ron gently shook his head and smiled:
[Profession Advancement Information Unlocked: Alchemist (Two Stars)]
[Transfer Conditions:
1. Alchemy reaches Skilled √
2. Alchemy reaches Mastery
3. Extraordinary Recognition reaches Skilled √
4. Independently completes the creation of more than three kinds of basic alchemy items √

chapters.title: Chapter 203 - 154: Following This Arduous Journey, At Last Among the Stars (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 203: Chapter 154: Following This Arduous Journey, At Last Among the Stars (Part 2)
5. Successfully improved at least one existing alchemy item blueprint
He had already taken the time to complete the refining of three different attribute energy crystals, bringing more stability and energy savings to the workshop, and also fulfilling the conditions for creating three types of basic alchemy items.
"Only two conditions left." Ron refocused his attention on the experiment:
"Now with the help of the ’Concept’ trait, completing the remaining conditions should be much easier."
With proficient-level alchemy and the ’Concept’ trait, he made breakthrough progress in his research on the energy isolation layer.
The process that originally required repeated trial and error has now become more intuitive; he can foresee the effect of a certain rune combination without needing to test it every time.
The path to becoming an alchemist is now clear, and this is just the first step of the ’Melting Furnace Concept’.
"Time is still relatively sufficient." He calculated to himself:
"Because of this whole thing with Oliver, the bloody duel has been postponed to a month and a half later, which is enough for me to make more preparations."
In this month or so, he needs to raise his alchemy skills to a higher level to lay the foundation for the forging of the magic sword;
at the same time, he has to train Dale to ensure she stands out at the duel.
Thinking of this, Ron took a deep breath and continued with his meticulous work at hand.
Outside the window, the day had already dawned, and a new day began...
.........
Oliver leaned against the cold rocky wall, his breath weak.
His gaze still retained a certain clarity, a gleam of reason utterly disproportionate to his degree of deformation.
Once robust, his body now shriveled up like a mummy, skin showing an unnatural grayish-white, eyes deeply sunken, cheekbones protruding.
His once handsome features were barely recognizable, with the right side of his face more severely deformed, black liquid continuously oozing from his pores, exuding a putrid scent.
The most terrifying were his eyes; they were no longer eyeballs but two slender tentacles, hanging feebly on either side of his cheeks, occasionally twitching slightly like dying snakes.
"My... dear... little Oliver..." Cynthia’s voice came from deep within the cave, viscous and distorted:
"Haven’t... died yet?"
Oliver struggled to turn his neck to look at the woman who was once beautiful.
Cynthia’s lower body had swelled at least three times, covered with thick mucus, countless tentacles extending in various directions, some as thin as hair, some as thick as arms.
Her face still retained human beauty, but around her eyes had grown rows of small compound eyes, and her mouth formed an exaggerated crack like a creature from ancient tales.
"Why haven’t you drained me completely?" Oliver’s voice was hoarse, a trace of confusion flashing in his eyes.
Cynthia moved her already fully mutated body gracefully, but contrary to her grotesque appearance, all her movements carried a bizarre sense of beauty.
The tentacles seemed to be meticulously designed dance props, drawing perfect arcs in the air.
Though her skin was covered in mucus, it shone with a pearly luster, flickering alluringly under the dim cave light.
Cynthia’s voice was thick like honey: "Do you think I’m just mindlessly squeezing you dry?"
A thick tentacle stretched over, gently stroking Oliver’s cracked lips, secreting a viscous liquid.
As soon as the liquid touched Oliver’s skin, it was greedily absorbed.
His eye tentacles slightly rose, seeming to have gained a flicker of vitality.
"Don’t look at me like that, dear."
Cynthia’s tone suddenly turned gentle: "I just... need energy too much; this newly reborn body needs a massive amount of nutrients to stabilize."
"Moreover, I’m actually helping you." She chuckled lightly:
"Your spiritual contamination has reached the critical point; if left unchecked, you would have already become an unconscious monster."
Oliver paused, recalling the first time he saw those fully awakened comrades in the cave.
They had almost lost all reason, retaining only primal desires and instincts.
"It’s me..." Cynthia proudly raised her head, her voice filled with pride:
"Regularly extracting the excess contamination energy from your body, helping you maintain the balance between reason and contamination."
Her tentacles wrapped more affectionately around Oliver’s body, her tone becoming charming and gentle:
"Isn’t this beneficial for both of us? You stay lucid, while I..."
Cynthia’s mutated body stretched out in the darkness, showcasing that bizarre but undeniable beauty.
"I become even more perfect."
Oliver stared in shock at this creature in front of him, gradually understanding everything.
The awakened Cynthia had indeed turned into a monster, but she hadn’t completely lost her reason.
On the contrary, she seemed to have found a way to skew the mutation towards a twisted ’evolution’ rather than chaotic degeneration.
"How did you do it?" Oliver couldn’t help but ask.
Cynthia’s compound eyes flickered with mysterious light:
"Dear Oliver, that’s my unique secret. Maybe one day I’ll tell you, provided you behave well enough."
Her tentacles secreted that energy liquid once more, nourishing not only Oliver but also subtly strengthening the near-symbiotic relationship between them.
Oliver could clearly feel that every time Cynthia drew energy from him, she would return a portion of processed energy to him.
This cycle not only maintained his life but, more importantly, helped him preserve conscious awareness.

chapters.title: Chapter 204 - 154: Following This Arduous Journey, At Last Among the Stars
chapters.content:
Chapter 204: Chapter 154: Following This Arduous Journey, At Last Among the Stars
Her tentacles wrapped around Oliver’s body, gently lifting him up:
"And, I haven’t abandoned you, have I? Everyone else has already fled."
Indeed, the cave was already empty.
Just before dawn, the middle-aged man in his thirties, who claimed to represent the "Eye of the Abyss," suddenly changed his expression and announced that the clearing troops were on their way.
He didn’t even notify the other members in the cave but disappeared through a secret passage.
The other Awakened, upon discovering this, scattered in all directions to save themselves; no one was willing to help Oliver, who had been drained by Cynthia.
Only Cynthia, for some twisted emotion or attachment to the Energy Spring, prepared to escape with Oliver.
At this moment, both of them simultaneously felt the terrifying wave of magical energy from afar.
"It’s time." Cynthia’s voice suddenly became solemn: "We can start leaving now..."
"Those mindless guys will only run in panic, not knowing that all passages to the outside have long been sealed off..."
Cynthia sneered, her lower body swelling rapidly, completely enveloping Oliver.
The tentacles, through continuous extraction, were now brimming with energy, rotating at high speed like some biological drill, digging deeper into the ground.
"They’re coming..."
Cynthia’s voice came from all directions, tinged with a hint of undisguisable fear:
"That massive magical energy... that’s... Vice Principal Hayek..."
......
Hayek hovered above the Edge Forest, his purple robe billowing in the wind.
His face was as calm as a still pond, but his eyes carried a terrifying brilliance like a stormy sea.
When this Moon Level Wizard looked down, the entire forest seemed to tremble under his aura.
"Are you ready?" he asked.
His voice wasn’t loud, yet it penetrated hundreds of meters, clearly reaching every Law Enforcement Officer’s ears.
"Yes, Vice Principal."
The Law Enforcement Team Captain stood respectfully, head bowed, not daring to look directly at this eminent figure:
"We have set up the blockade array, and all possible escape routes have been cut off."
Hayek nodded indifferently, not even sparing a glance at the captain.
In his eyes, these Law Enforcement Officers were no different from ordinary apprentices, insignificant cogs in the school system.
"Begin."
This Moon Level Wizard raised his right hand, deftly drawing a purple arc.
He took a deep breath and began preparing for super magic casting.
This preparatory action alone caused the surrounding air to twist, distant trees to move without wind, making a rustling sound, as if paying homage to this powerful being.
Without even chanting a spell, he lightly waved his fingers, causing the array to expand visibly, quickly covering the entire target area, forming visible energy ripples in the air.
The complex spell configuration left bright trails in the sky, with the array composed of countless micro-components interlocking.
Each component floated in the air with millimeter precision, forming a grand and complex energy structure.
Hayek’s expression was calm and unhurried, as if constructing such a complex spell was as easy as lifting a finger.
The Law Enforcement Officers looked up at the sky in horror, some less experienced were even stunned by the spectacular scene.
High-density energy flowed from Hayek’s fingertips, like a river, pouring into the spell structure, making its light even more dazzling.
The array in the sky began to rotate, emitting a piercing hum.
——Super Magic・Multi-Layered Superimposition!
With its magical power drawn, the spell configuration suddenly erupted with a thick dark purple beam of light.
With a diameter of hundreds of meters, it blasted directly toward the location of the underground cave.
Wherever the beam passed, the air was instantly ionized, forming countless tiny lightning bolts, enveloping the main beam like a spider web.
The ground trembled violently under this terrifying energy shock, everything around the cave—trees, rocks, soil, even moisture in the air—was instantly vaporized or decomposed by the high heat.
Within dozens of miles, all life was reduced to ashes by this strike, with no creature able to survive such an attack.
The earth’s surface was melted by the high temperature, forming a huge glassy crater, with gray smoke still rising from its edges.
Throughout this world-destroying attack, Hayek’s expression remained calm and indifferent.
Even amidst the continuous bombardment of the beam, he leisurely straightened the folds on his robe.
For this Moon Level Wizard, the spell he just unleashed, capable of destroying an entire region, was but a small display of his many techniques.
When the beam finally dissipated, he slowly landed on the edge of the massive crater, surveying the scorched earth with indifference.
"Continue the search, confirm if there are any remnants."
Hayek’s tone remained flat: "I’ve cleaned out the rat’s nest, the remaining cleanup is up to you."
After speaking, he didn’t even wait for the Law Enforcement Captain’s response, turning to leave, his figure gradually fading and disappearing into the air.
Leaving only the devastated ground, silently telling everyone about the terrifying power of a Moon Level Wizard.
At the same time, on the top floor of the Black Mist School’s workshop, Ron gazed at the colossal light beam in the distance, his mind equally turbulent.
Even from such a great distance, the destructive magical energy wave was still so clear.
The entire Black Mist Jungle seemed to hold its breath under that earth-shattering strike, all life instinctively recoiling in fear of that power.
"That’s the power of a Moon Level Official Wizard..." Ron murmured to himself, his eyes glimmering with endless yearning.
He may have a huge gap with those Elementary Apprentices, but that’s merely the difference between a carp and a small shark;
While the difference between Moon Level Wizards and apprentices like them is as vast as a deep-sea devourer whale compared to a shrimp in the shallows.
His gaze lingered, his mind churning.
If Vice Principal Hayek, a Moon Level Wizard, could effortlessly annihilate an area spanning dozens of miles, then how terrifying would the even more powerful Dark Sun Level be?
As for the legendary Great Wizards and the Witch King, what kind of existence are they?
Behind him came the soft sound of footsteps, Lilia approached, gazing at the sky that had returned to peace.
"Teacher, was that just now..."
"The Vice Principal’s clearing operation." Ron explained simply: "It seems the ’Eye of the Abyss’ hideout has been completely destroyed."
Lilia shivered slightly: "That kind of power... is simply unbelievable."
"Yes, unbelievable." Ron turned, a hint of a smile flashing in his eyes:
"But this also reminds me that we have a long way to go and much to learn."
Lilia seemed to feel the determination in his words, nodding seriously: "Yes, teacher."
Back inside the workshop, Ron unconsciously took another look at the distant place, his thoughts once again drifting far.
This extermination operation will undoubtedly have a major impact on the situation in Black Mist Jungle.
Where will the members of the "Eye of the Abyss" who managed to escape go?
Are Oliver and Cynthia among them?
The terrifying power displayed by the Vice Principal, what level of strength does it represent?
Can a Moon Level Wizard truly count as a strong enough to be a formidable force on this endless world chain?
These questions flickered like stars in Ron’s mind, but he knew he wasn’t yet qualified to seek these answers.
What he needed to do was continue honing each of his skills, improving every attribute.
Until one day, he could truly stand at that supreme height, overlooking all life.
"Per aspera ad astra (Through hardship to the stars)"
This is a famous adage in the mystical world, engraved on the stone tablet in the Central Hall of the school, its origin long lost, but its meaning undeniably profound.
Many have tried to interpret this ancient phrase, and Ron has his own understanding:
"No matter how small, the road to the stars will ultimately have an end."
With this thought, he pulled back his wandering thoughts and returned to his work at hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 205 - 155: The Thirteenth Seat
chapters.content:
Chapter 205: Chapter 155: The Thirteenth Seat
The sun gradually set in the west, and Ron walked out of the laboratory to the training field in the backyard of the workshop.
Dale was already there waiting, her silver hair shimmering brilliantly in the glow of the setting sun.
These days, the growth speed of the Little Sea Siren was astonishing.
Now she had the build of a ten-year-old human and was becoming increasingly skilled in Water Element control.
"Master!" Seeing Ron, Dale waved joyfully, "Look at my new skills!"
She drew a graceful arc in the air with her hands, and Water Elements gathered to form a delicate Crystal Ball, sparkling with rainbow colors in the sunset.
"Not bad." Ron smiled and nodded:
"The control is very stable."
"There’s something even more impressive!" Dale proudly announced, then took a deep breath, a hint of focus flashing in her eyes.
The Crystal Ball suddenly split into dozens of smaller balls, orbiting around her like planets around a star, forming a flowing protective barrier.
Each small ball maintained a perfect trajectory, running precisely along the predetermined path, showcasing the Little Sea Siren’s meticulous control over the Water Element.
"I came up with this myself yesterday!" The Little Sea Siren said proudly, "Lily sister said this could be used to protect myself."
Ron walked around Dale, carefully observing the movement trajectory and energy composition of the water balls.
This skill seemed simple but contained ingenious Elemental Control and spatial planning, far surpassing the abilities of ordinary same-aged Sea Sirens.
The extraordinary growth speed from the "Big Eater" trait was gradually showing astonishing effects.
"Truly creative." Ron praised while taking out a small bottle:
"Today I brought you some new ’food’ that will make you stronger."
Dale looked curiously at the liquid glowing red in the bottle, her eyes sparkling with anticipation.
Since discovering she could grow by consuming substances containing Extraordinary Energy, Ron had been preparing various special "foods" for her.
Today’s bottle was a meticulously crafted Red Blood Enhancement Liquid he spent three days concocting, containing a small amount of Red Blood Flying Dragon Bloodline Essence extracted from himself.
Purified and stabilized through multiple processes, it was specially tailored to the Little Sea Siren’s unique constitution.
"Drink it, but savor it slowly, feeling the flow of energy."
Ron advised: "Try to understand each different sensation; this will help you better absorb and transform the energy."
Dale took the bottle, sipping carefully, and soon her eyes lit up.
"So warm!" She exclaimed in surprise, "It feels like little flames dancing in my tummy!"
Ron watched her with a smile as she enjoyed this special "food" in small sips, carefully observing her changes.
As the Red Blood Enhancement Liquid was absorbed, subtle changes began to appear on Dale’s skin.
Some almost invisible scale patterns faintly appeared on her arms, quickly disappearing, blending into her original Sea Siren form.
This was exactly the effect Ron hoped for, guiding her bloodline towards a more diverse direction by providing different types of Extraordinary Energy.
Of course, the aggressive nature of the Dragon Bloodline had been removed during the preparation.
The enhancing liquid at present was purely high-energy food, possibly supplementing Dale’s Fire Element Affinity, but nothing more.
As for whether to consider incorporating Dragon Species factors into her Sea Siren bloodline later, careful experimentation was needed before any conclusions could be drawn.
"Dale, what do you think about participating in the gladiatorial contest?"
Ron suddenly asked, "There will be many strong opponents and generous rewards."
The Little Sea Siren’s eyes lit up immediately, nodding excitedly: "I want to join! I will show everyone how amazing Master’s Dale is!"
Ron chuckled lightly, patting her head:
"I believe you’ll do great. However, before that, we need more training to fully master these new abilities."
.........
In the ensuing time, Ron’s research entered a more focused phase.
He decided to temporarily devote all his energy to Soul Steel because only by truly mastering the traits of this mysterious metal could the feasibility of subsequent plans be determined.
Soul Steel is an extremely rare material, possessing plasticity and magic conductivity far beyond conventional metals, making it an ideal choice for forging advanced magic items.
Ron spent hours each day "communicating" with Soul Steel, continuously inputting his Spiritual Power, allowing the metal to gradually adapt to his energy signature.
This was a slow and labor-intensive process, but the results were remarkable:
The surface of the Soul Steel gradually showed subtle changes, the metal’s texture becoming softer and smoother, responding more sensitively to Ron’s Spiritual Power commands.
"The core characteristic of Soul Steel lies in its special internal crystalline structure."
Ron recorded in his notes:
"This structure can ’remember’ the Spiritual Power wave patterns of the user and adjust its own energy flow accordingly. Theoretically, after sufficient adaptation time, Soul Steel can form a resonance state completely matching the user’s Spiritual Power."
At this stage, Ron began attempting preliminary shape-shifting of Soul Steel.
He concentrated his Spiritual Power, first imagining the simplest short sword shape, then slowly and steadily transmitting this image to the metal.
Initially, the Soul Steel showed almost no response.
But as Ron continued to experiment, adjusting the way and intensity of Spiritual Power input.
The metal finally began to show a slight response on the fourth day—the edges became slightly sharper, and the overall outline started advancing towards a sword shape.

chapters.title: Chapter 206 - 155: Thirteenth Seat_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 206: Chapter 155: Thirteenth Seat_2
[Alchemy (Proficient) Experience Points +1]
"Progress is slow but steady," Ron recorded in the Library of Consciousness:
"Soul Steel needs time to adapt to its new form. Forcing the process could lead to internal energy structure instability, affecting the final product’s quality."
Just then, when the Soul Steel underwent a critical change, the professional panel suddenly provided a key piece of information:
[New Profession Advancement Method Confirmed:
Special Talent "Dual Soul" + "Active" Magic Sword + Thousand Transformations (Glory Legacy) + Stand-In Puppet (Rare Artifact)
→ Black Wizard (Three Stars)
Effect: Upon implementation, the Magic Sword will possess the erosion traits of the Black Wizard, while the main body remains unaffected by contamination]
This information made Ron’s eyes light up.
The panel’s confirmation also indicated that his research direction was fundamentally correct, only needing further refinement in the details.
Even more exciting was that the panel continued to display more information:
[Additional Idea: Transfer to Demon Hunter through Stand-In Puppet, for Demon Beast Organ Integration
This stand-in shares ability gains with the main body, but not the negative impacts
Effect: Upon implementation, the main body will acquire the abilities of a Demon Hunter]
This additional idea perfectly matched his own thoughts!
He had indeed been considering how to obtain the powerful abilities of the Demon Hunter without the potential distortion risks associated with that path.
The Stand-In Puppet was clearly the perfect solution to this problem: let the stand-in take the risks while the main body enjoys the benefits.
Ron took a deep breath, suppressing his excitement.
This confirmation information gave him great confidence, but he remained vigilant.
"Every step must be precisely controlled, with no margin for error."
The critical points are:
1. Secure division and transfer of Soul Fragments
2. Advancement of the Transformer Skin
3. Acquisition and proper activation of the Stand-In Puppet
4. Perfect forging of the Active Magic Sword
This time, he returned to the School Library, using his Candidate Wizard sequence member privileges to peruse a substantial amount of ancient texts on soul theories.
From ancient soul doctrines to modern Spiritual Power research, from soul divination theories to discussions on the essence of life, Ron meticulously studied all relevant materials he could find.
These studies helped him build a more complete theoretical framework:
The soul has a certain divisibility, but division must follow specific rules and limitations.
Excessive division will lead to energy insufficiency in the soul fragment, making it unable to maintain its own stability;
and improper division methods may damage the overall soul structure, affecting the caster’s mind and personality.
"Safe soul splitting needs to meet three conditions."
"First, the division must follow the soul’s ’natural texture,’ like cutting a diamond along its crystalline structure;
second, the split fragments must be immediately placed into a suitable vessel to prevent energy dissipation;
finally, a stable connection must be established between the original body and the fragments, while maintaining enough isolation to prevent mutual interference."
This is precisely why the advancement of the Transformer Skin is so important; only the isolation capability on the "Glory Legacy" level can ensure safe separation between soul fragments and the main body.
And the Stand-In Puppet is the perfect solution to the vessel problem.
According to legend, this mysterious item from the Great Abyss can replicate the user’s consciousness and abilities, creating a nearly perfect "copy."
If the split soul fragments can be placed in the Stand-In Puppet, theoretically, it can avoid the risks of energy dissipation and structural collapse.
In a long-sealed ancient text, "Path of the Apostle: Awakening and Transcendence of the Black Wizard," Ron found records of successful cases.
This book was heavily sealed and restricted, and even with his privileges, he could only read a small portion of its contents.
"The Thirteen Supreme Apostles, Masters of Contamination..."
The ancient text described:
"Among them, the most powerful was ’Void Spider’ Maggs, once just an ordinary Morning Star Mage with the ’Soul Weaving’ talent. Through unique soul splitting, he successfully housed his soul fragments in numerous specially crafted crystal balls, each maintaining a marvelously intricate connection with him."
The book roughly documented how Magnus used this division to manage spiritual contamination, channeling it into the crystal balls, then converting it into pure energy through special rituals.
Because of this power, even before becoming an Apostle, he once instantaneously killed three Moon-level Mages in a battle and could even return the full-powered strike of a Dark Sun-level Mage.
Another case was "Transmutation’s Daughter" Isabella, who possessed the "Empathy" talent, allowing her to perceive and mimic others’ emotional states.
She used a special mask as a vessel to successfully split her soul fragments while retaining complete consciousness control capabilities.
This allowed her to exist in multiple different locations simultaneously and even be reborn through the mask when the main body was "killed."
However, the ancient text also clearly warned about the dangers for those without special talents attempting this technique:
"Experimenters without the corresponding talent are likely to perish in the ritual.
The collapse of the soul structure is more painful than physical death, and those lucky enough to survive often fall into a permanent state of madness due to soul fragmentation.
In the chaotic dark period of the Second Era’s many Abyss sects, more than twenty ancient wizards attempted to emulate the ’Void Spider’ method.
Ultimately, only two survived, and both inevitably became mindless zombies, forced into permanent captivity in the ’Garden.’
Ron closed the book, falling into contemplation.
The risks of soul splitting are apparent, but the potential rewards are equally tempting.
Nearly all successful cases possessed some special talent, leading him to wonder if his "Dual Soul" could offer any protection in this process.
"There is still more I need to learn."
He muttered, his gaze drawn deeper into the bookshelves:
"But the starting point for all of this is still the Bloody Gladiatorial Games."
He must obtain that "Stand-In Puppet," which is one of the key components of the entire plan.
Simultaneously, he needs to find more specific methods for soul splitting and possible risk mitigation measures.
Ron turned to the window, watching the ever-changing clouds over the Black Mist Jungle.
The Bloody Gladiatorial Games have been postponed, but it will inevitably take place.
And before that, he has a vast amount of preparation work to do.
"Careful and cautious, step by step," he reminded himself:
"Since this is a pursuit of the eternal path, naturally, it cannot be rushed. More advanced content can be attempted once I reach the critical point before becoming an Official Wizard."

chapters.title: Chapter 207 - 156: Charm Song
chapters.content:
Chapter 207: Chapter 156: Charm Song
The emerald blue water rippled in the enormous pool, with sunlight streaming through the school’s specially designed transparent dome, casting dappled shadows on the water’s surface.
The protective barriers surrounding the arena shimmered with light, preventing participants from escaping and ensuring the spectators’ safety.
The arena was packed, with apprentices of every level filling the circular stands, engaging in lively discussions.
For apprentices who long immersed themselves in harsh cultivation and dangerous experiments, the Bloody Gladiatorial Games were among the rare entertainment venues where one could relax.
The annual gladiatorial feast always managed to attract a large audience.
Some advanced apprentices even spared no expense, spending precious magic stone fragments to enjoy this cruel yet magnificent performance from the front row.
In the center of the pool, a beautifully formed silver-haired sea siren swam leisurely.
Her long fish tail moved elegantly, with each stroke creating perfect ripples, showcasing extraordinary control power.
Her silvery long hair spread out in the water like a splendid silk fabric, her slightly purple-red eyes intently observing her adversary.
Confronting her was a massive blue-skinned merman, standing over three meters tall.
His upper body was covered with hard scale armor, while his lower body was a powerful, sturdy fish tail with fin edges sharp as knives.
At first glance, the size disparity between them seemed as vast as heaven and earth.
The merman wielded a rust-covered trident, his face ferocious and tusks prominent, eyes gleaming with a cruel light.
This was a meticulously modified combat creature, muscles knotted, exuding an uncontrollable desire to kill.
Each tail whip sent up tremendous sprays, demonstrating colossal strength.
"That merman is a rare catch from the ’Salvagers,’ reportedly tearing apart adult demon sharks effortlessly in deep-sea environments."
An intermediate apprentice introduced to his companion on the stands, speaking in a tone filled with expectation:
"I saw it myself in the previous match, where it devoured a sea python in three bites. They say its owner spent several hundred magic stone fragments to buy it."
"And whose combat slave is that sea siren? Seems just an ordinary-blooded sea siren, even quite immature."
The companion questioned, eyes flashing with puzzlement:
"Isn’t this contrast too stark? It’s practically a death sentence."
"The slave of Ron from the candidate wizard sequence."
The intermediate apprentice lowered his voice, a look of awe crossing his face:
"That genius alchemist who started from the sixth-class star, becoming an intermediate apprentice in less than a year. Amazingly, he rescued this little sea siren from a critical state, raising her for less than half a year..."
He paused, adding mysteriously:
"This showdown seems uneven, but I hear insiders are betting on her. In the previous elimination rounds, she’s already taken down three opponents twice her size."
With the referee’s command, the battle officially began.
The blue-skinned merman let out an ear-splitting roar, sending ripples across the water surface as he charged at Dale like an arrow released.
The trident carved a cold gleam through the water, unstoppable.
The size difference was especially evident at this moment, with the merman’s enormous body almost enveloping Dale in shadow.
An ordinary sea siren facing such an onslaught would likely have no chance to flee, being impaled on the spot.
However, there was not a trace of fear in Dale’s eyes, instead revealing a chilling, sinister smile.
Just as the trident was about to strike, her body suddenly twisted bizarrely in the water, as if boneless, easily dodging the fatal blow.
Simultaneously, a strange syllable escaped her lips, with sound waves traveling through the water, forming visible ripples.
"Hula~"
This syllable sounded like some ancient language, carrying peculiar charm.
"Hmm?" The merman was momentarily stunned, his movements visibly slowing, a trace of confusion flickering in his murky eyes.
Dale seized this chance, swimming to the pool’s center, beginning to circle the merman slowly, drawing a perfect circle.
Her silver hair floated in the water, forming a beautiful arc like a graceful ribbon, wrapping around her prey tightly.
The merman snorted coldly, shook his head to disperse the brief bewilderment, and once again raised the trident to launch a ferocious attack.
However, this time, Dale no longer dodged, but met the attack head-on.
Amid the spectators’ surprised gazes, she spread her arms, as if welcoming a hug.
"Is it crazy?" Someone exclaimed from the stands, "Isn’t this courting death?"
At the moment when the trident was about to pierce Dale’s chest.
The water surface suddenly surged, with dozens of water spheres emerging from all directions, precisely striking the merman’s joints and eyes.
The water spheres appeared soft yet were as tough as steel, containing high-concentration acid inside, causing intense pain upon hitting the eyes.
This move was evidently meticulously designed to maximally disrupt the opponent’s actions and vision.
The merman let out a cry of agony, his offensive interrupted.
He blinked forcefully, attempting to dispel the intense stinging sensation.
Dale seized this moment, approaching the merman, but without direct attack, she began to sing.
The sound was like a heavenly melody, spreading through the water, forming an eerie resonance.
Each note seemed to carry magic, causing the entire pool to tremble.
The audience found themselves unwittingly drawn by the song, their thoughts becoming hazy.

chapters.title: Chapter 208 - 156: Charm Song (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 208: Chapter 156: Charm Song (Part 2)
Some intermediate apprentices with weak willpower even began to sway slightly, as if they had fallen into a mild state of hypnosis.
This was not an ordinary song, but a unique "chanting" ability of the sea sirens, capable of directly affecting the listener’s mental state.
In ancient legends, countless ships were wrecked and sunk because of this kind of singing, with sailors enticed to jump into the sea and become the sirens’ feast.
"What a magical technique!"
Someone exclaimed from the stands:
"Is this the unique ’Charm Song’ of the sea sirens? I thought only adult sea sirens could master it."
"It’s certainly that kind of magic-like technique, but it seems to be stronger than the usual sea siren effect."
An elderly advanced apprentice explained, a glint of professional appreciation in his eyes:
"This level of sound wave control requires a fairly pure bloodline. There must have been some special bloodline transformation in this little sea siren."
The movements of the merman became slower and its gaze steadily grew more confused.
Dale’s song was like an invisible net, slowly entangling its consciousness and tightening with every moment.
Its eyelids began to grow heavy, and it could no longer hold the trident steadily, slowly sinking to the bottom.
Its consciousness had been mostly controlled, trapped in a state of haziness between wakefulness and slumber.
Dale approached slowly, continuing to sing softly near the merman’s ear.
The song was like a snake’s venomous tongue, infiltrating every inch of its prey’s mind and body.
"The strength of this little sea siren... is extraordinary."
An advanced apprentice commented, a hint of contemplation in his eyes:
"Her talent magic-like technique ’Charm Song’ has at least reached the level of our spiritual magic. Even among adult sea sirens, this is rare. What kind of bloodline modulation has her owner conducted on her?"
Just as the merman was about to fall completely into a coma, Dale’s actions suddenly changed.
The sea siren suddenly opened her mouth, revealing a row of sharp and fine teeth, biting fiercely into the merman’s exposed neck!
"Ah!" The merman suddenly awoke, roaring in pain, but its reaction was already too late.
Blood dispersed in the water, forming a cloud of crimson.
Dale’s teeth were deeply embedded in the merman’s flesh, greedily sucking in the fresh life energy.
Her eyes had turned completely purplish-red at this moment, with pupils like an animal’s vertical slits, revealing an almost maddening hunger.
In the audience, many apprentices gasped in shock.
This seemingly cute little sea siren surprisingly revealed such a bloody and cruel side.
The merman struggled desperately, trying to shake off this tiny yet terrifying parasite.
But Dale held on tightly, like a hungry vampire, persistently drawing every drop of blood.
The merman rolled in agony under the attack, but its strength was visibly draining away.
Dale was like a finely tuned hunting machine, each bite accurately targeting vital spots, tearing off chunks of flesh.
Even more haunting was that the water surrounding her began to spin faster, forming a mini whirlpool.
The whirlpool grew larger and faster, soon enveloping the merman completely.
The bloody water and shredded flesh spun rapidly within the whirlpool, creating a scene reminiscent of hell.
"My God..." An onlooker gasped, their face pale:
"This resembles more a reversion to the form of some deep-sea predator, what kind of bloodline experiment did Ron conduct on her?"
At the center of the whirlpool, the merman let out one last despairing scream before being crushed into pieces.
Its body was compressed, disassembled, and finally completely vanished into Dale’s mouth.
The entire process was surreal and terrifying, like a nightmare.
The gruesome scene plunged the entire gladiatorial arena into brief silence, followed by deafening cheers.
In this extraordinary world, where strength is revered, such an astonishing predatory ability undoubtedly stirred reverence and excitement among the crowd.
"The victor, the combat slave of Apprentice Ron Ralph——Dale!"
At the highest part of the stands, a few watching masters whispered among themselves, discussing the match fervently.
"The little sea siren has great potential."
A middle-aged man in meticulously groomed hair and a robe commented:
"Her bloodline is very pure, and she seems able to absorb the traits of her prey. Ron’s bloodline modulation technique is advancing rapidly."
It was Soron Griffiths, and since this was the final elimination match of this round, with his favored apprentice’s combat slave entering the ring, he took the time to come and watch.
Meanwhile, a veiled tall girl sat in the most inconspicuous corner of the stands.
She held a transparent crystal ball in her hand, recording the entire battle process.
Ron was busy with other matters and did not come, leaving the task to his disciple, and now Lilia was intently observing Dale’s performance.
Moreover, the tree spirit could not get too far from the workshop, and more importantly, she was currently at a critical moment.
The crystal ball in Lilia’s hand was a special tool Ron had recently refined, with intricate runes on the surface, capable of capturing the subtle processes of energy flow and bloodline change in detail.
While ordinary spectators could only see surface changes, through this crystal ball, Lilia could roughly observe the flow and transformation of bloodline energy within Dale.
"The terrifying nature of the ’Big Eater’ special talent lies in its ability to completely absorb all the advantages of its prey..."
Lilia murmured softly, her eyes gleaming with the light of a researcher:
"The master’s prediction was entirely correct."
Inside the crystal ball, energy points flowed along specific trajectories.
The deep-sea adaptability, strength, endurance, and even parts of water element resistance of the merman, were successfully absorbed and integrated into Dale’s bloodline.

chapters.title: Chapter 209 - 156: Charm Song_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 209: Chapter 156: Charm Song_3
This is not simple consumption and digestion, but a more advanced form of bloodline assimilation and purification.
Lilia gently caressed the crystal ball, her face showing genuine admiration.
The master’s bloodline modulation techniques have reached an unimaginable level, allowing a young sea siren to undergo such an astounding transformation in just a few months.
"If I could grasp even a tenth of the mastery, I would be more than satisfied."
She murmured softly, a hint of longing in her eyes:
"However, with my qualifications and talent... it seems I have a long way to go."
As the battle concluded, the audience gradually left, only a few apprentices still discussing this remarkable victory.
Lilia put away the crystal ball, carefully placing it in a specially made storage pouch, then walked towards the waiting area to pick up Dale.
"Lilia Sister!"
Dale leaped out of the pool, the water droplets on her silver hair sparkling in the sunlight:
"I won!"
At this moment, she had completely reverted to her girlish innocence, as if the earlier bloodthirsty and cruel side had never existed.
"Well done, Dale."
Lilia softly praised, handing her a soft towel:
"The master will be proud of you."
Dale happily wiped her body, her excitement beyond words:
"That big guy was not difficult at all, much easier than the training the master arranged for me! After each training, the master would give me special ’food,’ and those things are much tastier than today’s mermen!"
Lilia smiled faintly, feeling a subtle sense of pride inside.
This is the creation of Ron Workshop, each far exceeding the norm.
"Shall we go back?" Dale asked, eyes shimmering with anticipation:
"I want to tell the master about my victory! I can’t wait to tell him how I devoured that big guy!"
"No rush."
Lilia shook her head, a hint of anticipation in her eyes:
"There is another important task, I need to certify the qualification of an elementary apprentice."
Dale’s eyes widened: "Lilia Sister is going to become an apprentice too? That’s great!"
In fact, this gladiator match was supposed to be held a month earlier, but was postponed due to the Oliver incident.
Most members of the candidate wizard sequence are busy with their own research and tasks.
Thus, such elimination competitions are usually supervised by assistants.
.........
The two walked along the stone path outside the arena towards the Central Hall of the school.
The autumn sun shone on them, adding a rare warmth to the Black Mist Jungle.
"Why didn’t the master come?"
Walking on the road, Dale asked somewhat disappointedly, pouting with the particular defiance of a young girl:
"I clearly performed so well."
"The master is preparing for more important matters."
Lilia comforted, her tone gentle and firm:
"Those major plans concerning the future require his full attention. Besides, he has complete confidence in you, knowing you are sure to defeat your opponents."
Seeing Dale still with a bit of discontent, she patted the little silver-haired head:
"If he didn’t have confidence, why would he let you participate in the competition alone? This itself is an affirmation of your abilities."
As they walked, Lilia continued to explain:
"Today is the last elimination match, you have successfully advanced. The next round is the beast battle, where all the slaves who come out from the elimination rounds will face off against the experimental subjects selected by the wizards."
Dale nodded, a gleam of excitement in her eyes.
Lilia noticed that whenever battle or hunting was mentioned, the little sea siren’s pupils would unconsciously narrow slightly, revealing a predator’s instinct.
"In the melee, you need to be more cautious."
Lilia advised:
"Other combat slaves may join forces against you, after all, the strength you have shown has attracted quite a bit of attention."
She paused, continuing:
"After the melee, the four most outstanding combat slaves will enter the final to compete for the championship. Most masters will then personally attend the spectacle."
Dale’s eyes lit up:
"Will the ’stand-in puppet’ be awarded to the champion? The master has always wanted that."
"Exactly."
Lilia nodded, a hint of contemplation in her eyes:
"So the upcoming matches will only get tougher, but with the capability you showed today, I believe you can make it to the end."
The little sea siren grinned, revealing a row of fine little white teeth, looking seemingly harmless.
Only Lilia knew how terrifyingly lethal these fine teeth could become in combat.
Inside the Central Hall, people came and went, and Lilia brought Dale through the bustling crowd to the duty area.
Here, there was a long line, mostly apprentices coming to handle various formalities.
After a brief wait in line, a kind-looking middle-aged female duty officer received them.
The woman’s gaze was sharp yet gentle, clearly experienced and seasoned.
"Name?"
The duty officer routinely asked, the feather pen in her hand ready to record.
"Lilia, from Ron Ralph’s workshop."
She answered respectfully, her heart involuntarily racing.
The duty officer’s eyebrows lifted slightly, her feather pen paused for a moment:
"Ron Ralph? The genius alchemist of the candidate wizard sequence?"
Lilia gently nodded, feeling both nervous and proud inside.
The master’s name already carries substantial weight in the school, drawing notable attention from the duty officer.
"Interesting."
The duty officer’s tone carried a bit more curiosity, she carefully examined Lilia, seemingly trying to discern something unique about this veiled young woman.
Lilia couldn’t help but feel a wave of unease.
The duty officer led her to a room to test her spiritual power and then flipped through a hefty tome, skillfully finding Lilia’s information amidst a dense list of names.
"Your spiritual power test result is... a middle fifth-class star, initial meditation passing, elementary potion configuration qualified."
The duty officer read, her tone calm yet slightly appreciative:
"The time in Black Mist Jungle... about half a year."
She nodded slightly, revealing some approval in her eye:
"A candidate apprentice with fifth-class star talent, breaking through to elementary apprentice within half a year is already quite an impressive performance. Ralph’s apprentice indeed cultivates extraordinary students."
Lilia lowered her head slightly, her expression humble: "This is all due to the master’s meticulous guidance."
"Interesting." The duty officer set down the pen, her expression turning somewhat nostalgic:
"This reminds me of Ron Ralph’s own growth trajectory back then."
She closed the hefty tome:
"When he first came here, he was but an ordinary candidate apprentice with sixth-class star spiritual talent, yet within less than a year, he directly broke through to an intermediate apprentice, creating a miracle in the history of Black Mist Jungle."
A reminiscent glow crossed the duty officer’s eyes:
"I still remember him standing here to certify his elementary apprentice qualification back then."
She gave Lilia a meaningful look:
"Now, his student shows a similar growth trajectory, though not as astonishingly rapid, but for a fifth-class star talent, this is already remarkably impressive."
Lilia quietly listened, feeling a complex surge of emotions inside.
She knew being compared to Ron was a great honor, yet there was an unspoken pressure as well.
"I still have a long way to go."
She secretly warned herself:
"Not to be blinded by superficial success."
However, one thing gave her a slight comfort, the duty officer said her growth trajectory resembled that of her master’s...
"If I can persist, perhaps one day, I too can stand shoulder to shoulder with the master."
This thought quietly took root in Lilia’s heart.
Leaving the Central Hall, Lilia and Dale embarked on the return path to the workshop.
She touched the elementary apprentice badge on her chest, her heart filled with mixed feelings.
"This is just the starting point, not the endpoint."
Lilia silently reminded herself: "If satisfied with the status quo, I will never catch up with the master’s footsteps."
.........
Meanwhile, in an ancient tower deep in the Black Mist Jungle, Ron sat upright before an old silver-haired man—Alchemist Thompson.
The air was filled with the unique aroma of various alchemy materials, and in the corner, ancient alchemy equipment exuded the traces of time.
"Your question is very profound."
Thompson slowly set down the alchemy tools in his hand, a hint of appreciation flashing in his eyes:
"The combination of special materials and energy isolation layers is indeed a direction worth exploring. Few apprentices can think of such an innovative combination in such a short time."

chapters.title: Chapter 210 - 157: Trait "Boiling Blood
chapters.content:
Chapter 210: Chapter 157: Trait "Boiling Blood
Opportunities for paid consultations are rare.
In the Black Mist Jungle, this kind of one-on-one high-level guidance is usually an exclusive privilege for students with outstanding achievements or special contributions.
Thompson pondered for a moment, took an ancient tome from the shelf, and carefully turned to a page.
The edges of the page were yellowed and curled due to age, and the ink was somewhat blurred, obviously having been read countless times.
"Some advanced extraordinary materials have ’memory’ traits that can indeed be enhanced, but this requires a special ’marking ceremony’, the most typical example being Soul Steel."
The old man knowingly smiled, not revealing anything, as he pointed to the yellowed pages with his finger, which were adorned with complex diagrams and runes:
"This is a ritual used by ancient alchemists to strengthen the connection between Soul Steel and the user. By inputting energy in a specific sequence, a unique ’energy circuit’ can be established within the Soul Steel, making it easier to accept the user’s will."
Ron focused intently on the diagram, committing every detail to memory.
The arrangement of the runes, the trajectory of the energy flow, and even the subtle energy balance points were all being recorded by him one by one.
This was precisely the key information he needed, invaluable knowledge that he couldn’t acquire from ordinary tomes.
He solemnly took a complete Magic Stone from his pocket and handed it to Thompson.
The other party would naturally not provide such precious ancient books for free.
However, even a regular apprentice, although possessing a complete Magic Stone, rarely had the chance to share in such valuable knowledge, let alone receive accompanying guidance services.
"Of course, although this book looks quite old, it is a duplicated edition that has passed through countless hands. You can take it back to refer to the ritual, but by no means copy it verbatim..."
After handing the book to him, Thompson deftly received the Magic Stone and then continued to explain:
"Another point to note is the caster’s state of mind, which must remain highly focused and calm. Any emotional fluctuation could lead to the ritual’s failure."
Ron nodded, already beginning to plan the specifics of the implementation in his mind.
"As for the isolation layer..."
Thompson closed the book, his expression becoming more serious:
"This is an extremely complex and dangerous area. Isolating different energy fields is an advanced application in alchemy, and even the slightest mistake could lead to an energy leak or even an explosion."
A trace of warning flashed in the old man’s eyes:
"I noticed your research direction... is very special. If you intend to combine Soul Steel with isolation technology for energy division and storage, then I must warn you that such experiments are extremely dangerous."
Ron’s heart clenched, but he maintained a calm exterior.
"I understand the risks, Master. My research is still in the theoretical stage and I will not rashly proceed with actual operations. I will repeatedly verify every step to ensure absolute safety before proceeding."
As the consultation drew to a close, Thompson elaborated on several key alchemy techniques, particularly on advanced theories of energy conversion and material fusion.
This knowledge is absent from ordinary tomes, passed down from generation to generation of alchemists as esoteric mantras and mindsets.
After the paid consultation ended, Ron left the tower, setting off on the path back to his workshop.
The night had fallen, and the Black Mist Jungle remained eerie and frightening.
In the distance, strange howls could be heard occasionally, with tree shadows swaying in the moonlight as if countless eyes were watching in the dark.
Starlight sprinkled, illuminating the path ahead.
Ron’s thoughts returned to today’s gains.
As the research deepened, he grew increasingly confident that his direction was correct.
After all, predecessors had succeeded before. Even though transforming into an "apostle" left an infamous legacy, it still marked a significant presence in wizard history.
And those thirteen Supreme Apostles could rival top-tier Great Wizards...
Approaching the workshop, Ron saw the warm light streaming from the windows from a distance.
He heightened his magic power perception, already sensing the familiar presence inside the workshop—Lilia and Dale had already returned.
Pushing open the door, a small silver-haired figure quickly darted toward him.
"Master!"
Dale exclaimed excitedly, her eyes gleaming with the joy of victory:
"I won! That big guy didn’t even see half of my strength!"
Her eyes shone brightly, and her entire body radiated a satisfied aura, like a predator that had just feasted.
Ron smiled and patted her head:
"Well done, Dale. I knew you wouldn’t disappoint me."
He immediately noticed the changes in Dale, particularly her increasingly bright violet-red eyes.
This was a sign of successfully devouring spoils, indicating that her bloodline was evolving to a higher level.
"Next time, try to swallow two at once," he jokingly said.
"Lilia, how did it go?" Ron turned to the girl standing to the side.
Lilia slightly bowed, her face bearin a restrained yet pleased smile:
"Everything went smoothly, Teacher. Dale excelled in the elimination rounds, advancing easily. I have also completed my Elementary Apprentice certification, rated as ’Middle Potential’."
Ron noted the brand-new badge pinned on her chest, nodding in approval:
"Well done, reaching a fifth-class star qualification within half a year is already a rare achievement."
"I’ve recorded all of Dale’s combat."
Lilia carefully handed Ron the Crystal Ball:
"Based on observations, she successfully absorbed part of the merman’s abilities, particularly in deep-sea adaptability and strength, which have significantly improved."

chapters.title: Chapter 211 - 157: Trait "Boiling Blood" (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 211: Chapter 157: Trait "Boiling Blood" (Part 2)
Ron took the Crystal Ball, briefly sensing the internal records, and nodded in satisfaction:
"Very good, the devouring efficiency is even higher than expected. It seems the potential of the ’Big Eater’ far exceeds our imagination."
He raised the Crystal Ball to his eye, carefully observing the energy flow patterns within the recorded data.
Dale’s bloodline energy had nearly reached the Golden Ring critical point, far surpassing the Silver Ring level of ordinary Sea Sirens.
If they continued at the current pace of training, with a few more targeted devourings, she might very well step into the ranks of the Golden Ring bloodline before the end of the gladiatorial games.
"The next beast battle might be even more dangerous."
He turned to Dale: "Take a break. The upcoming melee will be more arduous. But I believe, with your current abilities, you should be able to advance smoothly to the finals."
Dale lifted her delicate chin confidently:
"Master, rest assured, I will definitely win the championship! That puppet is bound to be ours! Those guys are just delicious snacks in my eyes."
Ron smiled and nodded, yet his mind was contemplating more long-term plans.
......
In the laboratory, candlelight flickered, shadows swaying unpredictably on the walls.
Ron stood at the workbench, spreading out over a month’s worth of experimental data records, examining them one by one.
Those charts and formulas bore witness to his daily sweat and thought, every failure and breakthrough.
"It’s time for a comprehensive inventory."
Ron gently closed his eyes, constructing his unique Library of Consciousness in his mind.
He had long since crafted this magnificent palace of knowledge within his spiritual space.
Every book, every shelf, was arranged with precise logic, allowing him to retrieve and organize information at any time.
His avatar of consciousness strolled among the towering bookshelves, arriving at the "Personal Growth" section.
In this area, rows of books were neatly arranged, each documenting his progress and insights in different fields of cultivation.
Ron took down the first book, its golden-embossed cover read "Star Eater’s Ravings Meditation Progress."
Opening the pages, it detailed each instance of his meditation state, energy flow, and skill improvement.
"The progress in the Meditation Technique is very stable, with no significant breakthroughs, but there is substantial improvement every day."
Ron added the latest progress to the book:
[Current Progress: Star Eater’s Ravings (Proficient 192/300)]
With his continuous practice, his Spiritual Power steadily increased, only a step away from the Advanced Apprentice’s 4.0 standard line.
"If I maintain the current pace, I will break through to Advanced Apprentice by the end of the Bloody Gladiatorial Games at most, and by then, the next sequence’s quarterly meeting won’t be far."
He placed the book back in its place, taking down another, this one recording the progress of Magic Construction and Spiritual Interference.
[Current Progress: Magic Construction (Proficient 65/100)]
[Current Progress: Spiritual Interference (Proficient 78/100)]
Under Soron’s additional guidance, these two skills progressed rapidly, especially Spiritual Interference which had begun to show the nascent form of "Spiritual Shock."
Although leagues apart from an Official Wizard, for him at this stage, it undoubtedly added an extremely effective auxiliary attack method.
During continuous practice, even Soron was surprised, stating that Ron’s Spiritual Control precision far exceeded that of his peers.
A flicker passed through Ron’s eyes, then he regained his calm.
He was deeply aware that this wasn’t due to extraordinary talent, but the result of countless days and nights of precise practice.
Every bit of progress was exchanged with time and sweat.
The third book was about Elemental Perception, detailedly recording the characteristics and interaction modes of various elemental fluctuations.
[Current Progress: Elemental Perception (Proficient 67/100)]
"Yuni Master’s ’Energy Anchoring Crystal’ is indeed a treasure, enhancing my understanding of Elemental Perception to a new level."
Aside from that, there were the additional lessons after the courses. Without Yuni Seraphin’s special attention, he might have needed several times the time to reach his current level.
However, the advance courses were all fully completed, and now, if he wanted such additional lessons, he would have to pay for private consultations at his own expense.
And such paid consultations were available only once a week.
Leaving the bookshelves, Ron brought up the special "Assets List" scroll in the Library of Consciousness.
It detailed his every income and expense, clear and transparent.
"Financially, there’s also been a considerable accumulation."
In the past month, he completed several large Magic Potion orders, plus ten reserved Magic Stones from the Transformer’s side.
After deducting various workshop expenses, he now had fifteen complete Magic Stones, as well as three to four hundred scattered Magic Stone Fragments as assets.
"Not particularly wealthy, but for an Apprentice, it’s quite considerable."
Ron scrutinized this wealth, feeling slightly relieved; this was the strong money-attracting ability of a "Professional Alchemist."
A sufficient reserve of Magic Stones meant he could purchase necessary materials and information in emergencies, and support more complex experiments and research.
"Finally, there’s the training for Bloodline Activation."
Ron exited the Library of Consciousness, reopening his eyes, his gaze falling on the exquisite glass bottle at the other end of the experiment table.
Inside it was containing a dark red liquid, gently swirling under the light, seemingly wriggling with life.
"Magma Dew" — an essential Body Tempering Medicine for the third stage of the Crown Breathing Technique.
"Let’s aim to complete and break through the Bloodline Activation tonight."

chapters.title: Chapter 212 - 157: Trait "Boiling Blood" (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 212: Chapter 157: Trait "Boiling Blood" (Part 3)
Ron glanced out the window, the bright full moon hanging high in the sky.
Since it wasn’t daytime, there was an insufficiency of Yang Attribute Factor, making it not the best time to practice the "Crown Breathing Technique."
However, with a breakthrough imminent, he couldn’t wait any longer, and there were other matters to attend to tomorrow...
With this in mind, Ron carefully picked up the glass bottle and walked to the center of the training field.
The ground here was paved with special energy-absorbing stone, capable of withstanding high temperatures without damage.
He took a deep breath, sat cross-legged, and adjusted his breathing.
Upon opening the glass bottle, a wave of heat immediately rushed out, as if facing the mouth of an erupting volcano.
"Now is the time."
Without hesitation, Ron evenly applied the "Magma Dew" onto several crucial bloodline junctions on his body.
In an instant, it was as if a mass of magma had been poured directly onto him, burning all the way beneath his skin, and then quickly spreading throughout his body.
Every inch of skin, every muscle fiber, every blood vessel was filled with scalding energy.
"Ugh..."
Even though he had attempted this many times before, Ron couldn’t help but let out a painful groan.
