This pain far exceeded his imagination, like all the blood in his body had been ignited, roaring and surging inside him.
His skin quickly turned red, seemingly scorching from within, with sweat instantly evaporating at the high temperature, forming a thin mist around his body.
"Must... control it..."
Ron gritted his teeth against the intense pain and began to regulate his breathing according to the Third Stage of the "Crown Breathing Technique."
Each inhale felt like swallowing more fire; each exhale seemed like releasing scorching lava.
However, as his breathing gradually stabilized, the pain began to transform into a peculiar sensation:
Scalding but not entirely painful, more like a profound purification.
Ron could feel the "Magma Dew" altering the components of his blood, making it more active and aggressive.
The blood affected by the potion seemed to come alive, actively seeking out impurities and blockages in his body to burn them away completely.
"First Breath..."
Ron muttered the mantra softly, coordinating with a specific breathing rhythm.
His chest expanded accordingly, as if able to hold more air and energy.
"Second Breath..."
With the onset of the second breath, Ron felt the flow of heat inside begin to circulate and change, forming an Energy Circuit.
This circuit started from the heart, traveled through his arms, abdomen, legs, and finally back to the heart, cycling repeatedly, making the energy purer and stronger with each cycle.
However, when he attempted to enter the third breath, he suddenly encountered resistance.
"Third Breath..."
The energy within seemed to reach a certain limit, unable to proceed further.
It was like a small stream trying to accommodate the volume of a raging river, almost bursting its banks.
"Just a little more... just a little more..."
Ron clenched his teeth, enduring the sensation of his body about to burst.
He knew this was the most critical moment of Bloodline Activation—the critical point of breaking through the bottleneck.
But no matter how he tried, the resistance remained persistent, like an invisible wall.
The energy-absorbing stone beneath him had already turned slightly red from the heat, emitting a scorching aura.
"Since it’s Bloodline Activation... why not continue to try mobilizing the power of the Chimera Core?"
He closed his eyes, attempting to communicate with the core within.
This wasn’t his first attempt, just that it always fell short of that final push, but this time was undoubtedly the last gate before the breakthrough...
As he circulated the searing energy within repeatedly, a strange and ancient power began to awaken inside him.
It was a primal life force, teeming with traits of change and adaptation.
"Now!"
Ron seized this faint connection and suddenly fused his bloodline with it.
In an instant, as if a dam had burst, an unprecedented force exploded from within him.
He could feel beneath his skin, blood vessels rapidly expanding, muscle fibers being stretched to their limits, then contracting again.
This cycle repeated, making them tougher and more resilient in the process.
The blood initially altered by the "Magma Dew" came fully alive at this moment.
As if possessing its own consciousness, it actively searched every corner of the body, delivering energy to where it was most needed.
This state lasted for an unknown duration, until Ron could finally regain control over his body again.
He found himself lying on the floor, drenched in sweat.
But unlike previous exhaustion, he now felt an unprecedented sense of lightness and strength.
As if he had shed heavy shackles, he felt much more agile.
"Did it succeed?"
Ron slowly sat up, sensing the flow of energy within him.
The familiar and powerful bloodline force had thoroughly integrated into his blood and bones, becoming a part of his body.
It was like an ever-burning furnace, always ready to unleash astonishing heat.
[Bloodline Activation Experience Points +1]
[Breakthrough! Bloodline Activation (Beginner 100/100) → Bloodline Activation (Proficient 1/300)]
[Acquired Additional Trait: Boiling Blood
(Enhances the Life Burst effect of the "Bloodline Knight" and reduces the negative state of physical fatigue)]

chapters.title: Chapter 213 - 158: Abyssal Creatures Atlas
chapters.content:
Chapter 213: Chapter 158: Abyssal Creatures Atlas
"Boiling Blood..." Ron silently mouthed the name of this newly acquired trait, feeling the changes it brought.
He closed his eyes and entered the Library of Consciousness again, swiftly adding this important breakthrough to the "Bloodline Knight" section.
Comparing past experience data, Ron clearly recognized the value of this trait.
Previously, each time he used bloodline energy to burst, he would experience prolonged weakness and fatigue.
Just like when combating those mercenaries sent by the Transformer alongside Andre, after the Dragon Breath Spray, he entered a weakened state, making it so easy for them to successfully hypnotize him. Even after the hypnosis was lifted, he remained semi-conscious for a long time before recovering;
Or like when facing Marcus, the powerlessness after the burst prevented him from reacting in time to avoid being bitten.
This aftereffect had always been a fatal weakness of Bloodline Knights, making them particularly vulnerable at critical moments.
But now, this "Boiling Blood" trait could undoubtedly greatly improve this issue.
Ron stood up, attempting to mobilize a small amount of bloodline energy.
To his delight, the energy came not only more quickly but also more powerfully, as if it were compressed.
When he stopped mobilizing, the energy quickly dissipated, leaving little feeling of fatigue.
"This is almost like an upgraded version of ’Bloodline Burst.’ Not only is the power stronger, but it also has almost no side effects."
Ron gently clenched his fist, feeling the power surging through his knuckles.
This power was full of vitality and life, like a campfire that was warm and enduring.
He walked to the edge of the training field and picked up a test stone.
This was a hard black stone, which even ordinary people would find difficult to leave a mark on with full force.
Ron took a deep breath, mobilized his bloodline energy to a boiling point, and then punched out fiercely.
"Bang—!"
The test black stone cracked on impact, with a fissure spreading from the point of contact and eventually splitting the entire stone into several pieces.
"The burst power is at least fifty percent stronger than before, and the accompanying burning effect has also significantly improved, though the stone shattering doesn’t fully showcase it."
He examined his hand and found no discomfort other than a slight redness on his knuckles.
In the past, even this level of short-term burst would have left him with muscle soreness for at least one or two hours.
"The greatest benefit is still the reduction of the fatigue state."
Ron recalled Andre’s previous combat experiences, each burst leaving him as weak as a shrimp.
Therefore, Ron had never tried the "Bloodline Activation" effect in formal combat; having a period of weakness was simply too cumbersome.
But with the "Boiling Blood" trait, he could not only achieve more powerful bursts but also significantly reduce the post-burst weakness period and even perform consecutive bursts in emergencies.
This undoubtedly gave him a powerful trump card.
"However, more actual testing is still needed."
Ron thought calmly.
Although the initial results were exciting, he wouldn’t jump to conclusions easily.
Only rigorous practical testing could truly determine the practicality of this trait and any potential limitations.
"Continue forward, step by step."
He casually extinguished the Magic Crystal Lamp and walked toward his bedroom.
Tomorrow would be a new day, with a thousand and one things waiting for him to handle.
.........
The night slowly receded from the Black Mist Jungle, and the surrounding dark creatures became less active, but occasional low growls and eerie rustling could still be heard.
The light inside the workshop, however, was particularly warm and bright.
Only a familiar green figure was missing, but there was now an ancient tree in the yard, continuously emanating vibrant life force...
Ron stood in front of the experiment table, carefully observing the Little Sea Siren before him.
In two days of Beast Fighting Arena matches, Dale’s performance far exceeded expectations.
She had already defeated three opponents in a row and successfully absorbed all the essence of her opponents.
However, this rapid energy absorption also brought hidden dangers.
"Dale, put your hand out; I need to check your energy flow," Ron ordered directly.
"Okay, Master!"
Dale excitedly extended her little hand.
Her eyes shimmered with a peculiar gleam, and her originally pure blue irises now had hints of deep purple and dark red, forming a mysterious gradient color.
Ron gently touched her wrist, activating the "Extraordinary Recognition" and "Tracing" abilities, meticulously sensing the energy flow within her.
A complex bloodline landscape immediately unfolded in his mind:
The originally pure Sea Siren bloodline was now mixed with various alien energies.
The Deep Sea Adaptability of the Fishmen, the subtle manipulation of Water Elements, and even a trace of the Red Blood Flying Dragon factor he provided.
Most of these energies had been well integrated into Dale’s bloodline, but at certain nodes, there were clear signs of instability.
"As expected..." Ron murmured to himself:
"The energy intake was too fast, leading to excessive pressure on bloodline integration."
If this situation was not adjusted, it could trigger energy disruption at critical moments, negatively affecting Dale’s growth and combat effectiveness.
"Little one, you’ve eaten too much ’food’; now you need a little help to digest them."
Ron chuckled as he ruffled Dale’s silver hair.
Dale blinked her big eyes:
"Master, it seems like there’s a lot of power fighting inside me; sometimes it feels ticklish."
"That’s exactly why I’m going to help you with some adjustments."
Ron turned to the medicine cabinet, taking out several carefully prepared potions and a specially made fine silver needle.

chapters.title: Chapter 214 - 158: Abyssal Creatures Atlas (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 214: Chapter 158: Abyssal Creatures Atlas (Part 2)
This is a bloodline harmonization procedure designed specifically for Dale.
By using specific potions to regulate the flow of energy within the body and precisely guiding it with Spiritual Power, it helps different bloodline factors find the optimal balance point.
Lilia was assisting by preparing the equipment, her movements skillful and quiet.
"Teacher, do you need me to prepare the Stabilizing Liquid?" she asked softly.
Ron nodded: "Take the light blue bottle and modulate it to a concentration of three to seven."
Lilia immediately followed the instructions, accurately preparing the potion.
After months of working closely together, Ron and Lilia had developed a highly coordinated collaboration.
Although Lilia’s aptitude was initially mediocre, her "Diligence Can Make Up for Incompetence" Special Talent had led to noticeable progress in various aspects, making her undoubtedly the best assistant.
Once the preparations were complete, Ron indicated for Dale to lie down on the specially made Crystal Bed.
This bed, made from special crystals, aids in the conduction of Spiritual Power and the stability of energy.
"Will it hurt a lot?" Dale asked nervously.
"No, at most it will feel a bit tingly," Ron reassured:
"Just like last time, maybe a little itchy."
The Little Sea Siren relaxed her body, trusting, she closed her eyes.
Ron first dipped Silver Needle in the potion and gently tapped several key acupoints on Dale’s body.
The potion quickly penetrated the skin and began to flow along the energy meridians.
Then, he concentrated his Spiritual Power, placing his hands on Dale’s forehead and chest area, guiding the chaotic energy within her to realign.
This is an extremely delicate task, requiring precise control over each type of energy’s traits and flow patterns.
A single misstep could lead to energy conflict and even cause bloodline collapse.
Fortunately, Ron had conducted sufficient experiments on the Autophagic Slime Monster.
[Bloodline Modulation (Proficient) Experience Points + 1]
Ron could clearly sense the bloodline flow within Dale gradually becoming regular.
Those disparate energies, previously repelling each other, now found their places under his guidance, forming a marvelous complementary relationship.
"Sea Siren’s bloodline should primarily align with water, but Dale seems to have a natural affinity for the Wind Element too."
Ron observed attentively:
"Perhaps these two elements could be guided to form a symbiotic state."
He slightly adjusted the output direction of his Spiritual Power, diverting portions of the Water Element energy towards the Wind Element concentration area, creating a special buffer zone at their contact surface.
This adjustment was immediately effective—previously repelling elements began to slowly fuse, forming a unique "Wind and Water Symbiosis."
[Bloodline Modulation (Proficient) Experience Points + 1]
Dale’s expression became serene and comfortable, her skin began to emit a faint blue light.
He continued adjusting each newly absorbed energy, properly integrating them into Dale’s bloodline core.
In this way, these energies were no longer external intruders but became an organic part of her bloodline, completely controllable and usable.
When dealing with the trace of Dragon Blood Factor, Ron was particularly cautious.
The Dragon Bloodline’s aggressiveness is extremely strong, even in trace amounts, it could suppress or assimilate other bloodlines.
He considered whether he should completely remove this energy, but then noticed an interesting phenomenon:
The Dragon Blood Factor did not expand aggressively as expected but formed a stable small Energy Core that coexisted harmoniously with the surrounding Sea Siren bloodline.
"Interesting..." Ron raised an eyebrow:
"The Dragon Bloodline has not produced an erosion effect but rather formed something akin to a ’seed’."
With the "Tracing" ability, he could see the potential developmental path of this "seed."
If given proper guidance and nourishment, it could impart some Dragon Species traits to Dale without affecting the main Sea Siren bloodline.
"This is indeed a rare opportunity."
Ron decided to retain this special structure and create a more stable energy environment for it.
He injected some specific Enhancing Potion into Dale, guiding the energy flow around the "seed" to form a protective barrier.
This would allow it to develop steadily without interfering with the primary bloodline.
"Just like the tender flesh wrapped inside a clam shell..."
Ron thought of a fitting analogy: "The exterior forms a protective layer, while the interior can grow slowly."
The entire harmonization process lasted nearly three hours, and when the final energy flow settled into balance, Dale’s bloodline state finally reached its optimal condition.
[Bloodline Modulation (Proficient) Experience Points + 1]
Ron took a deep breath and slowly withdrew his Spiritual Power.
This high-intensity operation of Spiritual Power was quite burdensome even for him, but the outcome was worth it.
Dale slowly opened her eyes, the brilliance in her pupils shining brighter and clearer than ever before.
"Master, I feel so light!"
She sat up excitedly, tracing an arc in the air with her hands.
A perfect stream of water appeared out of thin air with her movement, forming a graceful spiral in the air.
There was a faint trace of wind entwining the edges of the water flow, making the entire structure more stable and flexible.
"Wind and Water Dual Elements Affinity." Ron nodded with satisfaction: "The effect is even better than expected."
The Little Sea Siren cheered as she jumped off the Crystal Bed, spinning joyfully around the room.
Her movements were more agile than before, her skin faintly glowing with a pearly luster, emitting a unique vitality.
Through this bloodline harmonization, Dale’s state had reached a new equilibrium.

chapters.title: Chapter 215 - 158: Abyssal Creatures Atlas (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 215: Chapter 158: Abyssal Creatures Atlas (Part 3)
The energy absorbed from the arena opponents was perfectly integrated, becoming part of her own power.
"Teacher, it’s truly amazing!" Lily couldn’t help but exclaim, her eyes filled with admiration:
"You used almost no external energy, merely guided by Spiritual Power with the gentle aid of a Potion, to accomplish such a complex bloodline harmony."
Ron humbly shook his head:
"This primarily owes to Dale’s superior bloodline and the special role of the ’Big Eater’ talent. I just played a supporting role."
But he knew in his heart that the success of this operation proved his Bloodline Modulation techniques had reached a new realm.
From simple Bloodline Purification to complex Elemental Fusion, and now to comprehensive bloodline harmony.
Each step was built on countless experiments and a vast amount of theoretical research.
Achieving harmonious coexistence of different bloodlines in the same organism has always been considered an incredibly difficult goal in traditional Bloodline Modulation theory, with some conservative Bloodline Modifiers even claiming it to be impossible.
Ron demonstrated its possibility through practical action, although the process required extremely precise Spiritual Control and a deep understanding of the essence of the bloodlines.
However, just as he took comfort in this success, a fact made him slightly uncomfortable.
Despite the smooth progress in enhancing his bloodline modulation skills, breakthroughs in Extraordinary Biology seemed to have hit a bottleneck.
[Current Progress: Extraordinary Biology (Entry 48/50)]
This number had been stagnant for several days; although breaking through the entry phase should have been easy, the delay exceeded his expectations.
Ron frowned, recalling a similar situation he encountered during his Swordsmanship breakthrough.
At that time, no matter how much he practiced, the last bit of Experience Points in Basic Swordsmanship stubbornly refused to break through.
It wasn’t until he truly applied these techniques in actual combat that he finally achieved a breakthrough.
"Perhaps Extraordinary Biology is the same."
Ron was well aware of his problem:
"Pure theoretical research can no longer provide a breakthrough point; more practical experience and direct observation are needed."
He looked at Dale with some regret.
Although he gained a lot of experience by adjusting her bloodline, the types of extraordinary creatures available in the Black Mist Jungle were ultimately limited, and opportunities for in-depth research were rare.
"What’s on your mind, Master?"
Dale tilted her head and asked, her purple-blue eyes full of curiosity.
Ron gently stroked her silver hair:
"Nothing much, just contemplating the next plan. You’ve successfully advanced to the top sixteen of the Bloody Gladiatorial Games; the next opponents will be stronger, we need better preparation."
Dale confidently waved her small fist: "Don’t worry, Master, I’ll devour them all!"
Ron nodded with a smile, but internally he was pondering another question.
How could he obtain more firsthand information about extraordinary creatures?
Just then, Lily reported another piece of news she had gleaned:
"Teacher, when I went to retrieve the Beast Fighting Arena qualification proof for you today, I exchanged Magic Stone Fragments with the officer there to get some information. This time, the experimental subject for the beast fight comes from the private collection of Vice Dean Hayek, and the specific rules will also change."
Ron’s eyes lit up: "Oh? Elaborate on that, please?"
"It’s said many parts of the experimental subject are sourced from the Great Abyss, but the officer didn’t have much detailed information."
Lily seemed a bit embarrassed as she twirled her hair with her finger, then continued saying:
"I’ve heard that after this beast fight, participants have a special privilege to join Vice Dean in Anatomy Guide of the subject. That’s why even those firmly entrenched in the sequence compete annually."
"Anatomy Guide..." Ron mused.
This was a rare opportunity. As a Moon-level Wizard, Vice Dean Hayek’s insight and experience were unparalleled.
Witnessing him dissect and analyze an extraordinary creature was akin to a priceless practicum in Extraordinary Biology.
Usually, acquiring consulting opportunities with a wizard of the Vice Dean’s caliber is nearly impossible; even paid consultations have extremely strict quota limitations.
"Moreover,"
Lily continued, her voice involuntarily carrying a hint of excitement:
"I heard that the champion rewards include the puppet and a book titled ’Abyssal Creatures Atlas.’ Though it’s unsure if true, if it is, it would be invaluable."
The Great Abyss — a place shrouded in countless legends and mysteries, said to be the origin of many mysterious creatures.
Knowledge about it is classified within the School, and even members of the Candidate Wizard sequence find it difficult to obtain complete information.
And now, if a special atlas could be acquired, it would be priceless for his research in Extraordinary Biology.
The difference between Abyssal creatures and ordinary extraordinary creatures might be the critical information needed for him to break through the bottleneck in Extraordinary Biology.
"It seems the championship of this tournament is far more valuable than I imagined."
Ron said softly, possibly considering a triple triumph at that moment.
Not only would he gain substantial rewards and rank advancement, but his breakthrough in Extraordinary Biology could also derive from the Anatomy Guide and the ’Abyssal Creatures Atlas.’
Dale tugged at his sleeve:
"Master, don’t worry, I will win the championship and bring back that atlas for you!"
Ron felt a surge of warmth fill his heart as he looked at the determined expression on the Little Sea Siren’s face.
From a frail, dying little life to the vibrant and confident girl she is now, Dale’s growth has exceeded everyone’s expectations.
"I believe in you, Dale." He said gently:
"But remember to protect yourself in battle; don’t be greedy and take unnecessary risks."
Afterwards, Ron began planning Dale’s training schedule and nutrition supplementation for the next few days.
With only three days left before the top sixteen matches, every second of training time must be maximized.
"Lily." Ron turned to address his student:
"I need you to prepare the following Potions, specially made for Dale..."
He meticulously listed several Enhancing Potion formulations.
These were specially designed based on Dale’s bloodline traits, capable of significantly enhancing her combat abilities in a short period.
Lily noted every detail attentively, then swiftly moved to action.
Meanwhile, Ron returned to the laboratory to review the limited information he’d gathered about Abyssal creatures.
He needed a fundamental grasp of the potential knowledge he might encounter, so he could pose valuable questions during the Anatomy Guide and garner maximum insight.
"Let me see, the known Abyssal tier distinctions..."
Ron opened one of the volumes, which recorded fragmentary data on the Great Abyss.
It is said the Abyss comprises thirteen layers, each possessing unique environmental features and biological populations.
The deeper the layers, the higher the degree of biological mutations and power levels.
Creatures capable of surviving below the sixth layer often display some form of adaptive mutation or evolution.
"These pieces of information are too fragmented and incomplete." Ron frowned: "It’s difficult to form a systematic understanding."
It is this missing comprehensive knowledge of the Abyssal ecosystem that hinders his further breakthroughs in Extraordinary Biology.
Acquiring that atlas might unlock this mystery.
"As the old saying goes: Boldly hypothesize, cautiously verify."
Ron closed the book.
He was acutely aware that power only holds true value when under control.
Both Dale’s bloodline harmonization and his quest for extraordinary knowledge require this calm and cautious attitude.
Too much ambition can be counterproductive; rashness will only lead to disaster.
On this path toward the pinnacle of the extraordinary, every step must be solid and steady.
Standing by the window, Ron gazed at the distant silhouette of the tower, with a clearer goal crystallizing in his heart:
The Abyssal Creatures Atlas, the Anatomy Guide of a Moon-level wizard, and the Stand-In Puppet possibly determining his future course.
All three await him among the champion rewards of the Bloody Gladiatorial Games.
And the key to obtaining them lies in this Little Sea Siren before him, with her astounding devouring ability.
"The championship..." Ron silently vowed to himself:
"No matter what, I must claim the championship."

chapters.title: Chapter 216 - 59: Three Powers as One
chapters.content:
Chapter 216: Chapter 59: Three Powers as One
Ron gazed at the parchment spread out on the workbench, its complex rune arrangement and intricate ceremonial procedure stirring his emotions.
"Soul Seal..."
This was a ritual recorded in the ancient texts he purchased from Thompson, specifically used to strengthen the bond between the user and Soul Steel.
The ritual patterns seemed simple but actually contained countless subtle balance points.
Every rune’s position, angle, and stroke order were precisely calculated to form a perfect energy recycling system.
"Such a delicate structure..."
Ron studied every detail with an almost obsessive focus, letting time slip away unnoticed.
He suddenly realized that with the long-term accumulation of knowledge in various fields, his comprehension seemed to have undergone a qualitative change.
Especially after breaking through to Mastery in Magic Potion Making a few months ago, the advanced Trait of "Extensive Knowledge and Records" allowed him to show astonishing performance in integrating knowledge across disciplines.
Combined with the newly acquired "Insight" trait, this boost in creative thinking was truly a powerful addition.
"The combined effects of the two traits are unexpectedly strong."
Ron keenly perceived:
"I’m able to understand this ancient ritual to a certain extent even at the apprentice stage, and can even foresee the principles behind it. This is not ordinary at all. It seems my snowball is starting to roll forward with each additional boost."
Complex theories that used to require repeated reading to grasp, he could now discern the core essence at a glance;
Skills that once needed dozens of experiments to master were now often grasped intuitively in the first few attempts.
This gradual improvement in comprehension, like a snowball, grew bigger and bigger, granting him creativity and understanding far beyond what was expected at the apprentice stage.
Ron turned to the other side of the workbench, where the silvery-gray Soul Steel lay quietly in a specially-made tray, its surface glinting with a cold sheen.
After nearly a month of "dialogue" and adaptation, the Soul Steel had initially adapted to his spiritual power fluctuations, becoming more compliant and sensitive.
But to achieve a perfect alignment, he still needed this ancient "Soul Seal" ceremony.
"According to ancient texts, the standard ritual requires a large expenditure of spiritual power and might even cause some life energy depletion to the caster..."
Ron frowned in thought, his gaze shifting between the Soul Steel and the ritual diagram.
At this moment, a bold idea formed in his mind—
"If I integrate the energy conversion array from modern alchemy into the ancient ritual, could it significantly reduce the cost?"
Once this idea emerged, it spread like wildfire.
He picked up a pen and began drawing an improved version of the ritual diagram on another piece of parchment.
The core part of the traditional Soul Seal ceremony was retained, with none of the ancient runes directly interacting with the Soul Steel missing.
But on the periphery, Ron added a circle of modern alchemy runes, specifically responsible for efficient energy collection and conversion.
These runes formed a precise closed-loop system, capable of reclaiming and utilizing the dissipating spiritual power, greatly enhancing overall efficiency.
Several hours later, the design of the improved Soul Seal ceremony was initially completed.
Ron carefully checked every detail to ensure there were no logical errors or energy incompatibility points.
"Theoretically, this improved ritual should reduce the cost by nearly half, while keeping the core effect unchanged."
He looked at his work with satisfaction and then began to prepare the materials needed for actual operation.
According to ancient texts, the Soul Seal ceremony is best performed under specific astrological conditions, usually chosen on nights when the moon is relatively full.
And tonight was an ideal moment.
Ron looked out the window, the night was deep, and a bright crescent moon was slowly rising in the sky.
"Everything is ready."
He carefully placed the Soul Steel in the center of the ritual, then used special silver powder to draw the complete improved ritual diagram on the ground.
The runes shimmered with a soft silver glow under moonlight, making the entire ritual array seem like a living artwork, breathtakingly beautiful.
Ron took a deep breath and stood outside the ritual circle, beginning to activate the array.
His spiritual power, like a precise scalpel, was injected along the pre-set path of the ritual array.
The silver powder runes immediately lit up with a faint glow, which was initially a light bluish-white, gradually turning bright silver, and finally achieving a dazzling platinum glow.
Energy flowed along the complex paths, generating specific resonances and transformations at each node.
Ron could clearly sense that the energy that should have dissipated was successfully intercepted by the peripheral modern alchemy runes and redirected back into the main loop.
"The effect is even better than expected."
He smiled slightly, continuing to maintain a stable output of spiritual power.
As the ceremony progressed, the central Soul Steel began to undergo visible changes.
Its color became deeper, as if it could absorb surrounding light;
The surface began to ripple slightly, like a pool of living water;
More marvelously, it seemed to start generating some kind of rhythm, as if it had its own "heartbeat".
When the ceremony reached the critical stage, Ron did not hesitate to cut his finger, letting three drops of fresh blood fall onto the surface of the Soul Steel as a catalyst.
As soon as the blood touched the metal, it was immediately absorbed without a trace.
Immediately, countless tiny runes appeared on the surface of the Soul Steel, manifested from Ron’s spiritual imprint.
These runes arranged into a unique pattern, forming a "code" only Ron could interpret.
As the last thread of energy was injected, the light of the entire ritual array gradually dimmed, eventually reverting to ordinary silver powder lines.

chapters.title: Chapter 217 - 159: Trinity 1_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 217: Chapter 159: Trinity 1_2
But the Soulsteel had completely changed its appearance—it became darker and deeper in hue, and its surface bore a subtle, flowing gloss, like a living liquid metal.
Ron cautiously picked up the Soulsteel and immediately felt an unprecedented sense of familiarity.
This metal was no longer a cold, inorganic object but had transformed into something that could resonate with him.
Merely by touching it lightly, he could feel the energy flow within the Soulsteel, as clear and direct as feeling his own pulse.
To his surprise, when he attempted to use Spiritual Power to guide the Soulsteel to change shape, the metal’s response was several times more sensitive than before.
With just a simple thought, the Soulsteel could instantly transform into the basic shape he desired.
"It’s amazing..."
Ron watched the Soulsteel in his hand continuously change form with his mind:
At one moment it was a small knife, the next a coin, and then it turned into a delicate little bird.
Through this Soul Seal Ceremony, he had somewhat achieved an affinity with the Soulsteel.
The next step was solely about figuring out how to shape it into a Demon Sword Embryo, an undoubtedly lengthy process...
But for him at the moment, through the improvement and application of the ’Soul Seal’ ceremony.
His understanding of Alchemy had already ascended to a brand-new height.
[Alchemy (Proficient) Experience Points +1]
[Breakthrough! Alchemy (Proficient 100/100)→Alchemy (Mastery 1/200)]
[Additional Traits Advanced:
Resonance→Three-in-One
(The synergy effects among Wizardry skills like Alchemy, Magic Potion Making, Enchantment, etc., will be moderately enhanced)]
An unprecedented sense of enlightenment rose in Ron’s heart.
The essence of Alchemy was not just about the transmutation and restructuring of matter but also about a profound understanding and communication with the substance itself.
[Advancement conditions for Alchemist (Two Stars) have been met:
1. Proficiency in Alchemy√
2. Mastery in Alchemy√
3. Proficiency in Extraordinary Recognition√
4. Independently making more than three kinds of basic Alchemy Items√
5. Successfully improved at least one existing Alchemy Item blueprint√]
[Would you like to immediately change profession to—Alchemist (Two Stars)]
Ron was slightly surprised, not expecting the last condition: improving an existing Alchemy Item blueprint, would be fulfilled through this improvement of the Soul Seal ceremony.
He confirmed without hesitation in his heart: "Yes."
A warm current surged from the depths of his heart, rapidly spreading throughout his body.
Similar to every previous profession change, but with subtle differences.
This time, the energy was deeper, carrying an ancient rhythm, mysterious and profound as if stemming from a primeval legacy.
His Perception Ability instantly improved, and the molecular structures of surrounding objects seemed to unfold before his eyes.
Ordinary tables, chairs, walls, and tools became complex compounds made up of countless tiny particles, each material possessing its unique structure and energy characteristics in his view.
Even more wondrous, he could not just see these structures; he could intuitively understand how they formed, how they changed, and how to modify and enhance them through Alchemy.
[Occupation change successful!]
[Occupation obtained: Alchemist (Two Stars)]
[Basic Attribute Enhancement:
Spiritual Power: 3.8→3.99 (+0.2)
Magic Power: 2.1→2.55 (+0.45)]
[Special Bonuses:
1. Moderate increase in the speed of gaining skill experience related to Alchemy
2. Improvement in Material Perception Ability
3. Moderate enhancement of control over material changes]
Every profession change brought about substantial ability enhancements, and this time was no less profound.
Ron took a deep breath, sensing the changes in his body and spirit.
Indeed, it became more challenging to improve further, but despite this, the 4.0 Spiritual Power benchmark required for the Advanced Apprentice was just within reach.
The only pity was that the breakthrough in Spiritual Power seemed only achievable through the Meditation Technique, and the Advanced Apprentice was undoubtedly a key node.
[Detected Profession Synergy: Alchemist + Wizard Apprentice + Alchemist + Bloodline Knight]
[Acquired Synergy Bonuses:
1. Increased efficiency in energy extraction during Alchemy
2. Increased rate of extracting material essence
3. Increased conversion efficiency of reaction energy]
Ron looked at the variety of synergy bonuses, slightly satisfied with the burgeoning power within him.
This was the snowball effect brought about by multi-class professions:
Different paths of cultivation not only did not interfere with each other but, to some extent, formed a perfect complement, causing the overall strength to make a qualitative leap.
The synergy effects seemed not to end there; after all, when he advanced as an Alchemist, there were skills that advanced.
And during the employment as Alchemy Apprentice, two skills also underwent fusion.
So the next step should be—
[Detected Skill Synergy: Magic Potion Refining (Proficient) + Alchemy (Mastery)
→Material Refining (Proficient 30/100)]
With the prompt from the transparent panel, a stream of brand-new knowledge and enlightenment instantly rushed into Ron’s consciousness.
"Material Refining," as a fusion skill, not only inherited all the advantages of Magic Potion Refining and Alchemy but also realized a sort of breakthrough transcendence in essence.
Ron couldn’t wait to test this new skill.
He picked up several materials from the workbench and casually began mixing them.
Surprisingly, the previously intricate process of Magic Potion Refining, requiring precise measurements, strict temperature control, and complex procedures, now seemed remarkably smooth.
He could precisely grasp the optimal amounts and timing for adding various materials solely by intuition.
It was as if each material was actively ’conversing’ with him, telling him how they should be combined and transformed.

chapters.title: Chapter 218 - 159: Triune Unity (3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 218: Chapter 159: Triune Unity (3)
The complex process that originally required dozens of steps has been greatly simplified.
Not because any steps were skipped, but because the "Material Refining" skill allowed him to handle multiple steps simultaneously, adjusting and optimizing in real-time during the process.
In just half an hour, a "Awakening Potion" that would normally take several times longer to complete had already perfectly formed.
And when Ron picked up this magic potion, he discovered another astonishing aspect:
The quality of this potion far exceeded the highest level he was able to refine before.
The purity of the liquid, the stability of the energy, and the durability of the effect all reached an unprecedented height.
"This is really... the feeling is just amazing..."
Ron then quickly took out an ordinary crystal to attempt energy crystallization extraction.
This is a basic alchemy technique used to seal specific energy within a crystal, forming the basic materials for various alchemy tools.
In the past, this process required at least two hours of meticulous operation and relied heavily on complex guiding devices and specialized alchemy tools.
But now, he only needed to concentrate, hold the crystal in both hands, and then guide the energy to flow along a specific path.
In just ten minutes, a perfect "Fire Element Crystal" had already formed, with its energy concentration and stability undoubtedly far surpassing the products available on the market.
"Material Refining..."
Ron whispered, his eyes flickering with delight:
"This is not merely the simple addition of two skills, but a whole new ability form."
He suddenly recalled the clues that Thompson and Lady Allen had mentioned before:
The Ancient Alchemist, the legendary profession that combined the three major wizardry techniques into one.
"Magic Potion Making represents the combination of potions and energy, alchemy represents the transformation of material and structure..."
Ron organizing his thoughts:
"Then the third major wizardry technique is the communication between runes and energy—Enchantment!"
Thompson had subtly mentioned that true ancient alchemists mastered these three core techniques and could create miracles beyond ordinary imagination.
Ron summoned the Library of Consciousness’s collections, swiftly noting these connections:
"Magic Potion Making—Potions and Energy—Partially Mastered (Alchemist Two Stars)
Alchemy—Material and Structure—Partially Mastered (Alchemy Master Two Stars)
Enchantment—Runes and Energy—Not yet Mastered (???)"
He then thought of the new advanced trait he had just acquired: Three-in-One.
"Three-in-One..." Ron murmured to himself: "is the Ancient Alchemist..."
From the current linkage effects, once he finally mastered all three major core techniques, some even more astonishing composite skill might emerge.
Perhaps that is the key to reaching a higher level.
"Enchanter..." Ron mused to himself: "It is said to be an existence even rarer than a Bloodline Modifier."
He recalled the various self-activating arrays and persistent devices he saw at the school, all of which depended on the meticulous rune effects engraved by enchanters.
Ordinary apprentices and official wizards who did not master Rune Magic could only copy runes rigidly without understanding the deeper principles behind them.
Including himself, they knew what the runes did but not why, only replicating existing runes without the ability to improve them based on needs.
The result was that these replicas often had lower efficacy, shorter duration, and were prone to unstable side effects.
However, the runes engraved by a true enchanter were worlds apart from these replicas.
It is said that runes left by a professional enchanter can still be effective even decades later, while ordinary replicas might fail within a few months.
Enchanters comprehend the fundamental principles behind the runes, allowing them not only to replicate existing runes but also to create entirely new rune combinations based on specific needs.
They can even imbue the runes with their own will and spirit marks, making their effects more powerful and lasting.
"To complete the path of the ancient alchemist, Enchantment is an indispensable link."
Ron firmly wrote down this goal in the Library of Consciousness.
But the problem is, in the Black Mist Jungle, there are almost no official wizards specializing in Enchantment, making opportunities to systematically learn this field exceedingly rare.
All clues point to one place—the Central Rich Lands where the Crystal Tower is located.
There, at the center of the Ring Abyss Continent Group, is said to have a more complete wizard system and richer extraordinary resources.
The Crystal Tower is not only one of the most prosperous supernatural gathering places in the Ring Abyss Continent Group but also a treasure trove of various rare extraordinary knowledge.
It is said that it has a complete Enchantment Element, specifically cultivating experts in this rare profession.
"It seems the future path is clear."
Ron closed his notebook, his eyes filled with a determined sparkle.
Becoming an Alchemist is not the end, but a necessary path to reach a higher level.
The legend of the Ancient Alchemist undoubtedly presents him with a grander possibility.
But ahead are the advancements to Magic Potion Professor and Alchemy Master, as well as the most core Enchanter, which may only be realized after he reaches an official wizard status.
Three-in-One could very well be the ideal state he wants to achieve...

chapters.title: Chapter 219 - 160: Golden Oak Queen
chapters.content:
Chapter 219: Chapter 160: Golden Oak Queen
Dale stood in the courtyard, gazing at the towering ancient tree, her silver hair gently billowing in the wind.
The tree’s branches were sturdy, its roots buried deep underground, appearing as if it had been growing on this land for hundreds of years.
But Dale knew this was her "Ailan Mama."
"Sister Lily, when will Ailan Mama wake up?"
The Little Sea Siren looked up, her purple-blue eyes filled with longing and anticipation.
She reached out her small hand, gently stroking the rough bark of the ancient tree, just as Ailan used to caress her head with vines.
Lilia squatted down, hugging the Little Sea Siren’s shoulders, feeling a bit flustered.
Although she had been living in the workshop for some time, she actually knew very little about the transformation process of tree spirits.
Ron had only told her to take good care of Dale, and he would handle the rest. As a student, she wouldn’t ask about the core secrets of others.
"Well..."
Lilia carefully chose her words, her mind racing to find a suitable explanation.
She didn’t want to disappoint the Little Sea Siren, but she also didn’t want to give an inaccurate promise:
"Sister Ailan needs enough time to complete her transformation, just like a butterfly needs to rest in its cocoon. But I believe she will soon come back to you."
At that moment, the door of the laboratory was pushed open, and Ron came out.
His eyes were bloodshot, and his lab coat was marked with traces left by various materials.
"Master!"
Dale immediately turned to Ron, her eyes filled with even stronger anticipation:
"When will Ailan Mama finally wake up? It’s been so many days, I miss her so much."
Upon hearing the inquiry, Ron walked over to the ancient tree, frowning slightly.
He extended his right hand, pressing his palm against the rough surface of the trunk, and activated his "Extraordinary Recognition" ability.
His Spiritual Power, like invisible tendrils, penetrated into the trunk, sensing the life state and energy flow within.
The energy flow inside the ancient tree displayed an orderly spiral pattern, indicating the transformation process was stable and healthy.
The core consciousness of the tree spirit was in a dormant state, but its Life Energy was more vigorous than ever before.
He could clearly sense the ancient power within Ailan being gradually awakened, reshaping her entire existence bit by bit.
"Don’t worry, Dale."
Ron withdrew his hand, showing a rare gentle smile:
"Ailan is undergoing an important transformation. Based on my observations, her state is very stable; she should return to us in a brand-new form within two weeks at most."
"Really?"
Dale’s eyes lit up, and she tightly hugged Ron’s leg:
"I miss Ailan Mama’s juice and petal candy so much! Sister Lily’s is delicious too, but the taste is different."
This comment brought a flicker of embarrassment to Lilia’s face, but she quickly smiled, considering it the innocence of a child.
Besides, she knew that her talent in gardening and dealing with plants was far inferior to Ailan’s, especially when it came to those homemade floral sweets.
Ron gently stroked the Little Sea Siren’s silver hair, his gaze remaining on the ancient tree, his thoughts drifting back to half a month ago...
.........
It was another weary night, and he was conducting experiments on the energy isolation layer.
After a brief nap while leaning on the lab table, he planned to rest for a moment before continuing the next round of tests.
Yet the door of the laboratory was gently knocked, and when it opened, Ron saw Ailan standing outside.
The tree spirit’s vines swayed with a hesitant rhythm, and a hint of unease showed between the branches and leaves.
"Ailan? Is there something you need so late?"
He was somewhat surprised, as the tree spirit had always respected his work schedule and rarely disturbed him during experiments.
Ailan’s leaves danced lightly in the air, writing a line of words:
"Master, I have an important request."
Sensing the abnormal emotional fluctuation of the tree spirit, Ron stepped aside to let her into the laboratory.
Under the cold light of the Magic Crystal Lamp, Ailan, usually calm and serene like still water, exuded a near-anxious aura tonight.
Her vines trembled slightly, the edges of her leaves even appearing a bit yellow—symptoms of intense emotional fluctuation in a tree spirit.
"What’s happened?"
Ron closed the door, a touch of concern flashing in his eyes, with some guesses already forming in his mind.
Ailan’s thick vine trembled slightly, seemingly hesitant, but soon, a resolute line of text emerged on the leaf:
"I want to request a Bloodline Modulation from you, just like the one for Dale."
Ron wasn’t particularly surprised; he had long noticed the subtle changes in Ailan recently.
Since Lilia came to the workshop, many tasks originally handled by Ailan had gradually been transferred to this human girl.
Though Ailan never showed a hint of dissatisfaction, anyone attentive enough could notice her increasingly frequent solitary times and the occasional complex gaze directed at Lilia.
Even Lilia herself had sensed this behavior.
Typically, tree spirits were known for their calm and detached nature, rarely experiencing intense emotional fluctuation.
This was why many of them became Elder Tree-men and Sages, possessing a mindset that could be described as innate recorders.
Yet, looking at this once silent and non-contentious tree spirit, who could even be described as Zen-like.
Now tormented by negative emotions, she developed a strong desire for self-change.
He was somewhat surprised by the intensity of Ailan’s emotions hidden within; her current behavior truly resembled that of a human.

chapters.title: Chapter 220 - 160: Golden Oak Queen (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 220: Chapter 160: Golden Oak Queen (Part 2)
The leaves of Ailan continued to write:
"I know my limitations. As an ordinary tree spirit, the help I can offer is too limited. Miss Lilia can take care of Dale, manage accounts, and handle miscellaneous tasks. She even learned how to make petal candy..."
The tree spirit seemed to have put great effort into writing these words.
Her leaves paused for a moment, seemingly searching for a more accurate expression:
"I saw little Dale becoming stronger due to bloodline modulation, and I also hope to be able to..."
The leaves paused again, finally writing a few simple and direct words:
"...become more useful."
Ron could read more meanings behind these words:
A longing for belonging, a pursuit of value, and even unmentionable jealousy and fear.
The tree spirit feared being replaced, feared losing the "home" she had managed to find.
"I understand..."
Ron sighed softly, realizing that Ailan had always been the most silent and diligent member of the workshop, quietly undertaking countless trivial tasks without ever asking for any reward.
His tone then became serious:
"You know bloodline modulation is a dangerous process, especially for creatures like you. The life structure of a tree spirit is complex and intricate, and unlike the juvenile Dale, you’ve already matured, making modulation even more dangerous."
He paused, looking directly at Ailan:
"Moreover, complete modulation means you will bear my exclusive mark, just like Dale, which means that as long as I wish, your life will be entirely under my control."
This was not just a warning but also a probe.
Ron needed to confirm whether Ailan fully understood the depth and irreversibility of this connection.
This is also a trait inherent in the wizardry of bloodline modulation itself.
So after understanding this, he no longer considered buying completely modulated "works" from other modulators.
Ailan’s vines danced with determination, and the words on the leaves were deeper and more powerful than usual, as if generated with all her might:
"I fully understand and accept this, Master. In fact, I crave this connection."
Ron was silent for a moment, beginning to calmly weigh the pros and cons in his mind.
From an objective standpoint, the bloodline of a tree spirit indeed has astonishing growth potential.
Ailan had previously displayed abnormal signs of bloodline activation, as well as various humanoid transformations.
Now, after confirmation through "Extraordinary Recognition" and "Tracing," he verified that the tree spirit possessed the ancient bloodline of a Star Ring level "Forest Nymph."
Once fully activated, she would possess the powerful ability to manipulate plants and communicate with the forest.
If this bloodline could be successfully activated, Ailan would achieve a qualitative leap, not only significantly enhancing the workshop’s defense capabilities but also aiding his longer-term plans.
More importantly, among all the creatures dependent on him, Ailan’s initial loyalty was the highest.
Unlike Dale’s innocence and Lily’s initial pragmatic considerations, Ailan’s actions were driven purely by gratitude and recognition.
This pure emotion, at this moment, has become the strongest connection.
"Alright, I will help you."
Ron finally made his decision:
"I will design a gradual modulation plan to ensure the safety of the entire process. However, you must strictly follow my instructions. Any slight deviation could lead to severe consequences."
Ailan’s vines danced joyfully, like a child receiving a beloved toy, with grateful words appearing on the leaves:
"Thank you, Master. I will strictly follow every instruction."
Ron activated the dual abilities of "Extraordinary Recognition" and "Tracing," further probing Ailan’s bloodline status:
[Tree Spirit "Ailan"
Bloodline Origin:
Forest Nymph (Star Ring)
→ Golden Oak Queen (Quasi-Star Ring)
→ Ancient Tree Fairy (Golden Ring)
→ Ordinary Tree Spirit (Silver Ring)]
The Golden Oak Queen, according to legend, was a special plant directly inspired by the Earth Mother Goddess, and then evolved step by step into a pure natural being, often possessing the ability to rule forests and communicate with all trees.
The Ancient Tree Fairy, on the other hand, is the diluted product of that bloodline, still retaining the powerful ability to manipulate plants.
Perhaps there are other routes to choose from, but "Tracing" in its current state can only reveal the closest evolutionary route to the creature.
In the following days, Ron fully devoted himself to Ailan’s bloodline modulation work.
The essence of a tree spirit’s life is completely different from other creatures; conventional bloodline modulation methods do not apply.
Ron ultimately determined a three-stage plan:
The first stage is bloodline awakening, using special catalysts to activate the dormant bloodline within Ailan;
The second stage is energy reconstruction, guiding the activated bloodline energy to flow along a specific path, reshaping the internal structure of the tree spirit;
The third stage is complete transformation, allowing Ailan to enter a cocoon-like state to complete the final form change.
To implement this plan, Ron collected various rare natural attribute materials from the market:
The essence of Morning Dew Flower, capable of enhancing life energy;
The roots of the Sun Tree, containing abundant positive energy;
Fragments of Light Crystal, which aid in stabilizing the flow of bloodline energy...
Each material was carefully purified by Ron and mixed according to a specific golden ratio of 1:3:7, forming a special bloodline enhancer tailored to the constitution of tree spirits.
When Ron injected those precious material mixtures into the tree spirit’s root system, her vines twisted in agony, with burn marks even appearing at the edges of the leaves...

chapters.title: Chapter 221 - 160: Golden Oak Queen (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 221: Chapter 160: Golden Oak Queen (Part 3)
On the tenth day of the bloodline activation, Ron noticed a subtle change in Ailan’s state.
Her energy fluctuation became unstable, the vines sometimes shrank and sometimes swelled, and the frequency of runes flickering on the leaves increased as if heralding some significant transformation to come.
"Master, I feel... a call."
Written on Ailan’s leaves, the text appeared and disappeared due to the energy fluctuation:
"My bloodline is telling me that I need to enter a special dormant state to complete the final metamorphosis."
Ron immediately realized that this was the omen of the Third Stage—complete metamorphosis.
In his research, a tree spirit needs to undergo a complete "death and rebirth" process to truly awaken its full potential.
"Are you sure you want to enter the final stage now?"
Ron cautiously asked, "Once it begins, it cannot be interrupted."
Ailan’s vines swayed resolutely:
"Yes, Master. I can feel the energy within me has reached a critical point. If I don’t quickly enter the metamorphosis state, I might be injured due to energy overload."
After experimental tests, Ron agreed to her request.
Ailan chose the center of the backyard, where the soil was deep, sunlight abundant, and underground water veins rich, as the ideal place for metamorphosis.
When the last leaf was fully grown, the tree spirit’s consciousness sank into slumber, beginning the final metamorphosis process.
She appeared like an ordinary ancient tree, but Ron knew that under that heavy bark, a new life was being nurtured.
......
Recalling this, Ron sighed gently, looking at the ancient tree before him, a hint of anticipation in his eyes.
Through "Extraordinary Recognition," he could sense the astonishing energy potential contained within the tree.
Ailan’s bloodline was evolving towards an ancient tree fairy, perhaps even a higher-level Golden Oak Queen.
"Will Ailan Mother be different when she wakes up?"
Dale asked, looking up, her purple-blue eyes flickering with concern:
"Will she... not recognize us?"
Ron noticed the Little Sea Siren’s worry and shook his head gently:
"Her appearance might change a bit, but her heart is still the Ailan Mother who loves you. The essence of the soul won’t disappear due to a change in form, just like you’ve become stronger after eating so much ’special food,’ yet you are still our little Dale."
The Little Sea Siren seemed comforted by this answer, nodded happily, and skipped into the house:
"I’m going to draw a picture for Ailan Mother and give it to her when she wakes up!"
Ron and Lilia exchanged a glance, then both turned towards the workshop.
"Teacher, I’ve sorted the accounts for today, but I’m a bit uncertain about the order for that batch of Star Core Grass..."
Lilia said, taking out a thick ledger, looking somewhat unsure.
Since Ailan entered the metamorphosis state, the daily operations of the workshop had fallen on her shoulders.
Despite her astonishing learning ability, she still found it somewhat overwhelming to handle matters requiring experience.
Ron glanced at the ledger, pointing out several areas needing revision:
"The pricing of Star Core Grass should consider the harvesting moon phase. Those collected during a new moon are valued thirty percent higher than during a full moon. This batch was harvested during the waning gibbous phase, so the price should be fifteen percent below the benchmark, not twenty percent."
Lilia carefully noted these points, but her face couldn’t hide her fatigue.
Despite giving her all, managing the workshop’s procurement, sales, inventory, and daily maintenance was truly too burdensome for someone just beginning to learn.
"Ailan Sister always managed to arrange everything perfectly."
Lilia sighed softly, saying:
"I finally realized she silently did so much work, never flaunting, making the entire workshop run like a precise clock. I’ve tried my best, but still feel somewhat..."
Ron nodded, feeling some emotions swell up in his heart as well.
It’s those seemingly insignificant daily tasks that form the foundation of the workshop’s operation.
Ailan’s silent contributions, which kept everything in perfect order, are often only truly recognized when they’re gone.
Just then, a sharp screech came from a distance.
A large macaw flew into the courtyard, its feathers shimmering brightly in the sunlight, circling a few times in the air before landing on Ron’s outstretched arm.
"Lord Ron! Urgent message! Urgent message!"
The parrot squawked in an exaggerated tone, now quite familiar with this young man.

chapters.title: Chapter 222 - 61: Scorpion
chapters.content:
Chapter 222: Chapter 61: Scorpion
Ron took the note, unfolded it, and started reading, his brows gradually furrowing, and his expression turning serious.
"What’s wrong, teacher?" Lilia leaned in, asking with concern.
"The rules of the Bloody Gladiatorial Games have changed."
Ron handed the note to her:
"They’ve canceled the final duel, replacing it with a mixed beast fight involving both apprentices and slaves. The final ranking will be determined by the masters based on performance scores."
Lilia finished reading the note, her face losing its color:
"A mixed beast fight? Doesn’t that mean that not only the slaves have to fight, but the masters have to go on the field themselves?"
"Exactly."
Ron’s brows were tightly knitted, but his eyes flashed with a strange light, not of fear, but a faint expectation mixed with calm contemplation:
"It seems like the difficulty and risk of this gladiatorial event have increased significantly."
He pondered for a moment, his mind already calculating various possibilities, considering the optimal strategies and potential risks.
Then, a look of determination flickered in Ron’s eyes:
"However, this is also an opportunity. If Dale and I can demonstrate excellent coordination in battle, the possibility of achieving a high ranking will increase significantly."
"But, teacher..." Lilia looked at him with worry:
"Those combat slaves are specially modified monsters, extremely dangerous. Many participants are skilled in combat magic, while your area of research leans more toward Magic Potion Making and Alchemy..."
"Don’t worry, Lilia."
Ron calmly interrupted her, his tone carrying an undeniable confidence: "I am well prepared."
.........
The final stage of the Bloody Gladiatorial Games was a massive circular arena.
The ground was covered with a layer of light brown, specially made sandy soil, surrounded by energy shield walls several dozen meters high, engraved with protective and isolation runes.
These runes not only protect the audience from the aftermath of the battles but also prevent participants from fleeing during the matches.
The high stands around were packed with apprentices of various ranks, eagerly chatting, their eyes sparkling with excitement and anticipation.
Ordinary apprentices wore gray and white robes, while the advanced apprentices were notable in their purple-edged gray robes, creating a distinct visual hierarchy.
For those who lived in the Black Mist Jungle year-round, such bloody and thrilling scenes provided more vitality and excitement than monotonous study and cultivation.
At the highest point of the stands sat a row of luxurious seats, occupied by figures wearing the robes of Official Wizards.
They were today’s judges and the absolute authorities in this academy.
Vice Principal Hayek stood alone at the edge of the high platform, his robe slightly resonating with the air, creating a bizarre visual distortion;
Behind him, in the seats, sat the slender Soron Griffith, his eyes flashing with sharp scrutiny;
On his right was the purple-eyed Yuni Seraphin, playing with a sparkling crystal ball in her hand.
Other masters were also in place, examining the participants on the field with interest, occasionally whispering among themselves.
The presence of these Official Wizards, especially Vice Principal Hayek, cast an invisible pressure over the entire venue.
Ron stood in the contestants’ waiting area, beneath the apprentice’s gray robe was a fitted soft armor, ensuring good protection.
At his waist hung a silver pocket watch, and he carried a few energy crystals capable of amplifying magic power, just in case.
Dale stood beside him; compared to the near-starving small creature she used to be, she now had the form of a human girl, her silver hair braided by Lilia, dressed in a light armor designed for combat.
"Master, you don’t look nervous at all."
Dale looked up at Ron, her eyes glowing with a predator-like excitement.
Ron smiled slightly:
"A moderate amount of nervousness helps maintain alertness, but too much can affect judgment."
"I will protect you!"
Dale said confidently, puffing out her chest, her voice filled with determination, then she playfully winked:
"Besides, I can’t wait to taste those rare creatures."
Looking around, Ron could see other participants making their final preparations.
Most apprentices brought various bizarrely modified slaves.
Particularly eye-catching was a multi-legged creature covered in a black carapace, its eyes like burning coals, each step causing a slight tremor in the ground.
This was the work of a highly ranked advanced apprentice, reportedly created by fusing the bloodlines of an underground centipede and a Fire Salamander.
Holt stood not far from him, wearing his usual calm and cautious expression.
Beside him was an Earth Elemental Golem nearly five meters tall, its entire body dark brown, covered in dark rugged rock, looking exceptionally solid.
Ron nodded slightly in greeting, and Holt returned a brief nod.
The two of them were each contemplating how they should display their prowess in the upcoming battle.
Even though they were opponents on the field, they had a few acquaintances privately, at least confirming that the other would not become their primary target.
Trish and Li Yue stood on the other side of the arena.
The form of the Leopard Woman had become longer and more powerful than before, with her muscles beautifully contoured yet full of strength. Her beast-like eyes flickered with a dangerous light.
The brown-haired girl turned her head upon feeling Ron’s gaze, nodding slightly in greeting, with a complex expression flickering in her eyes.
Her expression held a familiarity towards an old friend, yet couldn’t hide the sharpness towards a competitor.
Without exception, all the combat slaves exuded a sense of danger, with some even requiring special chains to control them to prevent them from going berserk prematurely.
"An interesting lineup," Ron evaluated silently in his heart:
"Apart from Trish and Holt, the other people’s slaves are mostly hastily made; they appear fierce on the surface but must have significant internal flaws. In contrast, although Dale’s bloodline isn’t as aggressively modified, its stability and endurance are much stronger."
There were several contestants Ron wasn’t familiar with, and their combat slaves took on various forms:
There was a scorpion-man covered in black shell all over, a six-armed creature from the Otherworld, and a bear-man race engulfed in ghostly blue flames.
Most of these contestants bore arrogant expressions, evidently confident in their combat slaves. They kept a cautious distance from one another, their eyes filled with vigilance and hostility.
The atmosphere in the stands became even tenser. As Deputy President Hayek slowly raised his hand, the entire Beast Fighting Arena was plunged into a brief silence under the pressure of his magic.
"The finals of the Bloody Gladiatorial Games will serve as the ultimate test with a beast battle."
Hayek’s voice wasn’t loud, yet it clearly reached every corner of the arena:
"The winner takes all, the loser is nothing. Final rankings will be based on your performance in battle."
As his words fell, Hayek traced a complex magic trajectory in the air with his hands.
Purple lines interwove in the air, forming an exquisite three-dimensional magic structure.
Each line was precise to an astonishing degree, and the flow and control of energy exhibited an almost artistic beauty.
"This is the magic control ability of an Official Wizard..."
Ron silently recorded it in his heart, although he showed no emotional fluctuation on his face.
Through his Extraordinary Recognition Ability, he recorded the details of this magic control in his Library of Consciousness, preparing for the day he would handle similar techniques himself.
In the past few months, Soron and Yuni had privately revealed some information about Official Wizards to him during guidance sessions.
What Hayek demonstrated now was not some complex magic construct, but an advanced application of Spiritual Power and Magic Power — sophisticated techniques only mastered by Official Wizards.
This ability doesn’t rely on specific magic models but directly manipulates energy through fine magic control and guidance to form visible entities.
It is this advanced magic application that allows Official Wizards to almost never need servants.
They can accurately manipulate everything around them using this technique:
levitating objects, cleaning environments, and even condensing water and fire from the air to meet everyday needs.
To ordinary people, these abilities are akin to miracles, but in essence, they’re just fine control over magic.
"This is true magic mastery."
Ron contemplated silently, a hint of longing flashed in his eyes:
"Not relying on fixed models, but shaping magic at will as an artist molds clay. One day, I will reach this level, even surpass it."
But at this moment, he had to focus on the imminent crisis.
The magic lines in Hayek’s hands increased, gradually forming a huge energy network.
The magic lines interwove to create a complex three-dimensional structure, like an invisible net.
As it unfolded, energy particles in the air began to vibrate intensely, forming a visibly rippling wave.
Next, with a sharp wave of his hand, the magic lines instantly transformed into chains that plunged into the ground.
With an ear-splitting roar, the center of the arena ground suddenly cracked open, and a giant creature was hauled out by the magic chains.
It was a Scorpion — most of its body resembled a giant lion, covered in dark golden mane.
Its tail rose high, ending in a keratinized, cold-glinting poison barb, shimmering with an ominous green light.
The entire creature exceeded seven meters in length, lying on the ground, its ruby-like eyes alone were as large as dinner plates.
Each claw tip on its massive forepaws sparkled sharply, capable of easily tearing steel;
The poison barb on its scorpion tail continuously dripped venom, producing a loud corrosive sound as it hit the ground, instantly dissolving the sandy ground into a small pit.
The Scorpion was tightly bound by magic chains, appearing to be in a semi-conscious state, panting heavily, with unfocused eyes.
Yet even in this state, the pressure it exuded caused all the combat slaves on the field to show signs of unease.
Ron’s face remained calm and unruffled, but he quickly activated his Extraordinary Recognition Ability inwardly, carefully observing the Scorpion.
[Scorpion (Hybrid Modulation)
Bloodline Purity: Golden Ring 86% (Relatively Unstable)
Status: Energy Not Fully Activated (Current Strength About 50%)
Danger Level: Extremely High (Currently Middle Level)]
Special Abilities: ??? (Not Fully Manifested)]
Ron’s heart sank slightly but he maintained his calm.
This Scorpion was far more dangerous than it appeared; it seemed to be in some sort of semi-awakened state now.
If it fully awakened, its danger would probably exceed the anticipation of all the contestants.

chapters.title: Chapter 223 - 162: Blood Feast
chapters.content:
Chapter 223: Chapter 162: Blood Feast
Ron adjusted his breathing lightly, quickly contemplating several possible strategies in his mind.
He immediately transmitted his thoughts to Dale with Spiritual Power:
"Maintain distance, don’t take the initiative to attack. The true strength of this Scorpion far exceeds what it appears; for now, we’ll only perform long-range harassment and wait for the right moment."
Dale nodded gently, showing absolute trust in her master’s judgment.
On the high platform, Hayek’s voice rang out again: "Finals, begin."
With the command, the Magic Chains suddenly disappeared, and the Scorpion wobbled its massive body, seemingly still adjusting to the abrupt return of its freedom.
Its movements were sluggish, and its gaze remained muddled, but Ron caught an unusual detail:
The energy flow within that huge body was gradually accelerating, like a volcano about to awaken.
The participants did not act immediately, all cautiously observing the terrifying creature.
The air was filled with an almost palpable tension, as if an invisible string had been pulled to its limit.
After a moment of silence, one participant standing at the front took the initiative to attack.
He was a short but muscular Intermediate Apprentice, with a conceited smile on his face, clearly confident in his combat abilities.
"I’ll go first!"
He directed the six-armed Otherworld creature to charge fiercely at the Scorpion, while he quickly constructed a Magic Model and unleashed a series of fireballs.
This seemed to be a signal, and the other participants soon began to act.
A tall participant controlled a composite creature of shells and tentacles, launching acid from afar;
Another manipulated an insect creature with several pairs of wings, constantly harassing the Scorpion’s view.
Various spells and energy attacks rained down on the Scorpion, turning the battlefield chaotic and sending energy fluctuations rippling everywhere.
The Scorpion’s attention was drawn by an apprentice with a Lizardman, its tail raised high like a deadly scythe.
The apprentice was panic-stricken, but his Lizardman Slave reacted quickly, stepping forward to shield with its Scale Armor against the first blow.
Taking advantage of the moment, various chaotic attacks struck its huge body, though the creature simply flipped over with indifference.
Holt’s Earth Elemental Golem advanced steadily, each step causing the ground to quake slightly.
Ron knew Holt initially joined the Candidate Wizard ranks as part of the Law Enforcement Team, his combat experience notably extensive.
Perhaps he chose the Earth Elemental Golem for its versatility, with its only drawback being relatively slow speed, but otherwise without weaknesses.
The Earth Elemental Golem was massive and sturdy, even taller than the half-crouching Scorpion.
At this moment, the advantage of choosing the Golem immediately became apparent: its body made of Earth Element is completely immune to toxins, making it the ideal choice against the Scorpion.
The giant stone fist struck directly at the Scorpion’s head, producing a dull thud, yet only causing the giant beast to jolt its head.
"The Earth Elemental Golem indeed was a wise choice for this duel."
Ron continued analyzing, while also focusing on the Scorpion’s reactions.
The opponent’s choice was undoubtedly well thought out, but whether this frontal assault tactic could be consistently effective remains to be seen.
Trish and Li Yue opted for guerilla tactics, with the speed and agility of the Leopard Girl being her greatest advantage.
Ron noticed that the brown-haired girl’s gaze briefly rested on Dale, seemingly contemplating whether to offer assistance.
But soon, she shook her head and turned in another direction.
In such competition, even friends must first consider their own interests.
Compared to Cynthia, Li Yue appeared more nimble in battling the Half-beastman, her form shimmering like a phantom, inflicting tearing damage on the Scorpion repeatedly.
Her precise claw strikes hit the Scorpion’s joints, each attack drawing a small amount of blood, then swiftly retreating to dodge the lazy counterattacks.
The audience in the stands began to buzz with discussions, most gazes focused on the participants taking the initiative in their attacks.
In contrast, Ron and Dale’s conservative strategy seemed particularly conspicuous—or perhaps, attracted some disappointed looks.
"Look at that Alchemist, truly only dares to hide behind."
"Haha, what kind of display can an Alchemist have in battle? Him reaching the finals is a miracle itself."
"His slave is a Sea Siren, right? What can it even do in this kind of land battle?"
Disregarding the idle chatter from the stands, Ron at this moment remained calmly observing the shifts in the battlefield.
In his view, those eager to showcase themselves were the truly ignorant ones.
Through Extraordinary Recognition, he already knew the danger this Scorpion posed.
Making a rash move would only make oneself the first batch of sacrifices.
In front of the Scorpion, those contestants who charged forward seemed to find confidence.
Although the monster was massive, its movements were sluggish, seeming not fully awake yet, with almost no effective defense against the many attacks.
Its counterattacks appeared fierce, but its slow speed allowed most combat slaves to easily evade them.
The first six-armed creature from the Otherworld to charge in, under its master’s control, climbed onto the Scorpion’s back with six arms simultaneously gripping the vital points, trying to subdue the beast with the Strangulation Technique.
Its master shouted triumphantly from the side: "See that? This monster is nothing to fear!"
For a moment, the scene presented a spectacle where the contestants seemed to have the upper hand.
Holt’s Earth Elemental Golem moved in without hesitation, its massive stone fists pounding the beast’s body repeatedly, producing dull thudding sounds.
The Scorpion’s poison sting retaliated, but every strike was easily blocked by the golem’s rocky body, rendering the toxin ineffective against the lifeless Elemental Body.
Trish and Li Yue watched the situation from the sidelines, seemingly assessing whether to engage more deeply in the battle.
Their eyes occasionally glanced towards Ron, clearly wondering what the companion who has remained observant was plotting.
"Trish!" Ron suddenly called out from afar, warning: "The Scorpion is not fully awake yet, don’t get too close!"
Trish was slightly taken aback upon hearing this, looking over with a complex expression.
She seemed to be contemplating whether to trust Ron’s warning, as in this gladiatorial contest, everyone was for themselves, and no one truly considered others.
After a moment’s thought, she ultimately chose to act cautiously, signaling Li Yue to keep some distance, using the dart tied to her thigh for harassment rather than recklessly getting close like the other contestants’ slaves.
Ron understood her mindset—in this gladiatorial contest, they were all competitors.
She couldn’t entirely trust others, even if they had a good private relationship.
Such a mindset was common in the Wizard World; Ron was long accustomed to it.
Amidst this atmosphere of vigilance and suspicion, the Scorpion, which had been almost passively taking hits, suddenly let out a low growl.
Then, with lightning speed, it bit down on the nearest combat slave, a scorpion-man controlled by a low-ranking contestant.
With a crisp "crunch," the scorpion-man’s upper body was bitten clean off, blood splattering, staining the surrounding sand a dark red.
Its limbs tumbled in the air, entrails strewn about, emitting a foul stench.
The Scorpion lowered its head, swallowing the remaining half of the carcass whole, its movements incredibly swift, unlike its previous languid state.
During the devouring, its eyes shimmered with a strange light, as if absorbing some kind of energy.
The scorpion-man’s master let out a tragic scream, his face instantly turning pale, clearly suffering a mental rebound from the slave’s death.
He staggered back a few steps and then collapsed to the ground, losing his combat abilities, and was soon swiftly moved off the field by the Elemental Servants.
Subsequently, the Scorpion’s thick tail sting hooked.
The arrogant six-armed creature clinging to the Scorpion’s back was similarly impaled without resistance, then brought to the giant mouth amidst struggles...
Amid an indescribable sound of chewing, its master—the short and stout Apprentice—was likewise carried off by the Elemental Servants.
These two sudden sacrifices instantly tensed the atmosphere on the field.
The contestants paused their offensive, starting to reassess the situation.
Some bore expressions of fear, obviously regretting their earlier reckless behavior.
Ron seized the opportunity, quickly adjusting his strategy:
"Dale, we can show a bit of our strength now."
He ordered through spiritual transmission, without a trace of panic:
"But for now, stay on the periphery to harass, but don’t draw too much attention, aiming to make it expend more energy."
The Little Sea Siren’s eyes flickered with solemnity, then she swiftly took action.
From her back emerged a wing-like structure formed by condensing water elements, with faintly visible flowing patterns on the surface.
