This was a special technique developed by Ron and Dale over several weeks—Water-shaped Wings.
Using water elements to provide the basic structure while wind elements supplied power and directional control, forming a special ability capable of effectively gliding in non-arid zones.
Dale leaped gracefully, her water wings instantly unfurling, carrying her gliding across the battlefield.
Unlike floating, this gliding relied on the wind, conserving more energy without losing much agility.
The spectators let out exclamations of surprise, seemingly unprepared for a Sea Siren to exhibit such astonishing mobility on a land battlefield.
For Dale, who demonstrated gliding capability, the only real threat from the Scorpion was its thick, retractable tail sting...

chapters.title: Chapter 224 - 163: Equal Training System
chapters.content:
Chapter 224: Chapter 163: Equal Training System
Dale’s small hand opened, and the Chain Water Bombs launched from the Water Wings fell like raindrops.
In the crackling sound of tiny explosions, they struck the Scorpion, creating remarkably dense wounds on its body.
The Scorpion’s tail flicked like lightning, but Dale, well-prepared, easily dodged it.
Upon missing its target, the giant creature seemed to instantly lose interest in this cute little morsel.
It lunged forward, devouring another Combat Slave, its half-crouched body gradually starting to move, ignoring Dale’s dense water bombs like a dive-bomber.
The fine wounds on its body continued to heal visibly as it feasted greedily.
Meanwhile, Ron also commenced his action, deploying his focused technique of Spiritual Interference.
With the advanced course learning and Soron’s private guidance, combined with his "Lag Circle" trait, its power was astounding.
The Scorpion hit by it noticeably slowed, its head shaking continually, trying to rid itself of the disturbing interference.
Ron swiftly constructed a Magic Model, releasing invisible sound waves from his fingertips, striking the Scorpion’s sensitive areas like its ears and eyes with precision.
Although these Sound Wave Vibrations were invisible, their effect was exceptionally pronounced.
Unfortunately, the "Ring of Brilliance" and "Slime Splash" weren’t suitable for this occasion, otherwise, the hindrance effect would be even better.
Off-guard, the Scorpion was hit by successive penetrating attacks, dark blood even seeping from its mouth and nose, its movements visibly slowed...
This series of maneuvers was as smooth as flowing water, with hardly a pause, showcasing Ron’s extremely high level of magic control.
His aim was clear—exhaust the Scorpion’s energy and attention, while searching for its weaknesses, preparing for the final decisive strike.
The other participants on the field cast amazed glances, especially Trish, who was closest, a hint of disbelief flashing in her eyes.
It was well-known that Alchemists often lacked combat prowess, but Ron’s effectiveness in long-range attacks was second only to Holt among those present.
His precise magical control and calm tactical consideration displayed a combat sophistication quite inconsistent with his Alchemist identity.
However, contrary to Ron’s expectations, the Scorpion didn’t shift its focus here due to his harassing attacks.
Instead, its stinger hooked upward, snatching another slave in the rush of the wind, this time a gigantic insect with numerous wings.
Ron continuously unleashed restrictive attacks, alternately using Sound Wave Vibration and Spiritual Interference.
In fact, the Scorpion’s tail hook missed Dale earlier due to his timely use of Spiritual Interference Wave impact during its attack, otherwise, the Little Sea Siren couldn’t have evaded so easily.
Ron frowned, watching the Scorpion’s decreasing movements, simply crouched down, devouring relentlessly...
The creature was focused on crunching the crispy hard objects in its mouth.
It seemed particularly fond of this, with a higher desire to hunt individual insects compared to other slaves.
Up on the high platform, a barely visible smile appeared at the corner of Hayek’s mouth.
"Interesting, it seems my specimen has absorbed enough blood energy."
Ron certainly couldn’t hear this, but through his Extraordinary Recognition Ability, he saw the massive energy fluctuation erupting like a volcano inside the Scorpion after it completely swallowed its last bloody bite...
His heart tightened, confirming his ominous premonition.
He immediately realized the situation might rapidly worsen, quickly warning Dale through mental contact:
"Prepare for retreat, the Scorpion might be about to fully awaken!"
Meanwhile, on the battlefield, the participants still attacking the Scorpion up close were completely unaware of the impending danger.
Following Ron’s successful attacks, they seemed to mimic his actions, becoming more confident, with their tactics becoming increasingly aggressive.
But then, the originally sluggish Scorpion suddenly burst into incredible speed, its eyes sharpening like knives, and its muscles seeming to swell invisibly.
More terrifyingly, an invisible oppressive aura emanated from it, making all the participants present feel a sudden jolt of heart-pounding fear.
The Scorpion’s figure flickered, and its poisonous stinger pierced out like lightning.
Instantly, it penetrated a Combat Slave controlled by a participant, a beast engulfed in ghostly blue flames.
The sting pierced through the bear’s chest, injecting the green venom instantly into its body.
The scorching blue flames were extinguished in an instant, and the robust bear’s body slumped to the ground like a marionette with its strings cut, its life rapidly fading.
Even more horrifyingly, the Scorpion did not stop; with a sweeping motion of its massive front claw, it slammed the same participant against the Shield Wall.
A dull thud echoed as the participant’s body crashed heavily against the Rune-Inscribed Wall.
Blood spilled from their mouth, the light in their eyes dimming quickly, clearly having lost consciousness.
The participant’s chest and abdomen were torn by the claw strike, exposing white ribs, blood and fragments of internal organs scattering across the ground.
This series of actions was as fluid as running water, swift enough that almost everyone didn’t react in time, and the atmosphere on the battlefield turned deathly silent in an instant.
Many participants’ faces were filled with fear, their legs weak, completely losing the courage to fight.
Ron observed all this, keeping a calm expression but with his vigilance elevated to the highest level internally.

chapters.title: Chapter 225 - 163: Equal Opportunity Cultivation System (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 225: Chapter 163: Equal Opportunity Cultivation System (Part 2)
He immediately adjusted his breathing, bringing his mental state to its peak while closely observing every movement of the Scorpion, looking for possible weaknesses.
From previous observations, he had already discovered that although the Scorpion was remarkably fast, it had a short pause whenever it changed direction;
More importantly, although its venomous sting had a wide range, it required a short recharging period after use.
A grasp of these would at least enable a full retreat during its attack.
The Scorpion’s next target was the multi-legged creature covered in black carapace that had been attacking it consistently.
It took large strides forward, moving so fast it nearly left a blur, and in an instant, it was in front of its target.
The arrogance on its owner’s face had long vanished, replaced by pure terror.
He seemed dumbfounded by the sudden change, reacting a half-beat too slow.
By the time he wanted to order his slave to retreat, it was already too late.
The claws sliced through the air like knife blades, ripping the multi-legged creature’s body into halves in an instant, its innards and blood splattering across the ground.
The final screeching sound it made was utterly shrill, as if accusing its owner’s incompetence in its dying breath.
Then with a sharp turn, the tail sting struck towards Li Yue with lightning speed.
The Leopard Woman reacted swiftly, almost instinctively rolling backward, but she was still a step too slow.
Although the venomous sting didn’t hit a vital spot, it left a grim wound on her arm.
"Li Yue!" Trish exclaimed, immediately starting to cast a healing spell, trying to slow the spread of the poison.
But judging by Li Yue’s expression, the poison was spreading at a speed beyond Trish’s expectations.
The Leopard Woman’s arm swelled quickly, her skin turning an unnatural purple, clearly a sign of poisoning.
Her breathing became more and more rapid, and her eyes began to lose focus, a large amount of sweat seeped from her pores, mingled with blood streaming onto the ground.
Ron watched silently, calculating various possibilities in his mind.
At this moment, rushing forward to help would only put himself in danger.
Moreover, with the Scorpion’s speed, he would likely be intercepted before he could reach Trish.
Analyzing the situation calmly, preserving his strength, and waiting for the right moment was the best choice.
With a major force disabled, the Scorpion turned towards its most despised target—the Earth Elemental Golem of Holt.
The Earth Elemental Golem was indeed, as everyone expected, the ideal choice to fight against the Scorpion in this battle.
Its inorganic traits rendered the poison entirely ineffective, and its sturdy rocky body could withstand most physical attacks.
This was the reason why Holt dared to let the Golem remain at the frontline position.
But at this moment, the Scorpion had clearly fully awakened, its strength far exceeding everyone’s expectations.
It emitted an earth-shattering roar, raising its front limbs high, carrying immense power, and struck directly at the chest of the Earth Elemental Golem.
This strike was evidently more forceful than all previous attacks, even bringing a frenzied whistling sound in the air.
"Boom!"
Under this blow, the chest of the sturdy Earth Elemental Golem cracked directly, nearly a third of its upper body was shattered!
The Golem’s arms detached from its body, falling to the ground with a dull thud.
Then more rubble fell from its broken body, revealing the vulnerable energy core inside.
The once-unbreakable defense now seemed so fragile, as if it would completely collapse in the next second.
Holt’s face turned pale instantly, evidently suffering from the mental rebound of his Elemental Body being attacked.
He staggered back a few steps, disbelief written all over his face.
Even someone like him, an experienced Law Enforcement Team Captain, was intimidated by the Scorpion’s power, unable to remain calm.
At this moment, all the participants felt an almost suffocating pressure.
"That slap just now was clearly approaching the level of an Official Wizard. Outside, it could potentially blow up a small hill..."
Ron was secretly assessing in his heart while continuing to look for a winning opportunity.
The battlefield had turned into a sea of chaos and panic, most of the survivors had lost the courage to fight, only hoping to retreat unharmed.
Yet, amid this chaos, Ron captured a critical detail:
After several consecutive high-intensity attacks, especially the all-out strike against the Earth Elemental Golem, the Scorpion’s movements seemed to slow slightly.
The dark golden mane had also lost its previous luster, and the crimson glow in its eyes dimmed a bit.
"I understand a bit now..." Ron silently analyzed in his mind:
"It seems this Abyss creature’s burst period cannot last long, each time only maintaining for a short period, then it must consume blood or energy attacks to absorb new energy."
Thinking of this, he immediately adjusted his tactics based on this discovery:
"Dale, continue to keep your distance, but be ready to attack on my signal. We need to exhaust its stamina and strike when it enters a weakened state."
On the high platform, the observing Masters were closely watching the situation on the field.
"This Alchemist named Ron is quite interesting."
Commented a female Master wearing a deep blue robe:
"Most of the participants have lost their composure, only he still maintains calm and rational judgment."
"Indeed." An elderly man with white hair nodded in agreement:
"He seems to have already seen through the weaknesses and combat patterns of the Scorpion, such observational skills are rare among Apprentices."
The Vice Principal Hayek stood beside them, his face without any expression, yet a subtle emotion surged in his heart.
"If I had not given the priority training rights to Soron and Yuni last time, perhaps this little fellow would have been my student now..."
According to the talent equalization system of the School, each Official Wizard needs to leave the priority training rights to other wizards of the same level after selecting a mentoring object for a period.
Because Hayek successfully trained Corina last time, he received enough benefit corrections.
So for a long time, he lost the priority guidance rights over newly discovered geniuses.
"But that’s fine." Hayek quickly adjusted his mindset:
"The Scorpion experiment has already gathered sufficient data, and I can also take this opportunity to see the true level of these candidate sequences."
On the battlefield, the Scorpion began a new round of predation.
It set its sights on another participant who couldn’t escape in time, a female Apprentice controlling a half-human half-snake creature.
With a swift leap, the Scorpion charged forward, opened its bloody mouth wide, about to swallow the snake person whole.
At the critical moment, Holt’s voice came from the side: "Everyone avoid it! Fighting separately will only get us killed one by one!"
He controlled the broken Earth Elemental Golem, forcefully launching a charge, crashing into the Scorpion’s side.
Although the Golem was already incomplete, the collision still made the Scorpion’s attack deviate from its original trajectory, temporarily saving the female Apprentice.
Ron saw this and remained calm.
This short cooperation actually benefited everyone:
Only by depleting the Scorpion’s stamina can they increase everyone’s survival chances.
"The time has come." Ron said softly, then raised his hand to signal Dale.
The Little Sea Siren immediately swooped down from high above, drawing a beautiful arc with her hands in the air.
A series of Water Elemental Bullets were released from her fingertips, accurately hitting the Scorpion’s eyes, causing it to howl in pain.
Simultaneously, Ron began his action.
He activated the Transformer’s Skin, then dashed towards the scattered corpses on the battlefield.
In the chaotic battlefield, no one noticed the energy fluctuations on him that were completely concealed.
Once the Transformer’s Skin was activated, it quietly began absorbing the lingering Soul Energy on the battlefield.
With biological deaths exceeding a certain time, souls naturally dissipate.
And from what he knew, there seemed to be no Masters currently within the school proficient in Necromancy.
So Ron wasn’t worried about his secret absorption of Soul Energy being detected by those Masters.

chapters.title: Chapter 226 - 164: Soul Absorption
chapters.content:
Chapter 226: Chapter 164: Soul Absorption
"99.1%..." Ron felt the charging of the Transformer’s Skin slightly increased, but it was still short of being fully charged.
Holt’s command clearly had an effect.
The remaining contestants, although reluctant to fully trust each other, at least formed a temporary understanding—keeping their distance, harassing from a distance, and depleting the Scorpion’s stamina.
Ron seized the opportunity and unleashed Sound Wave Vibration again, this time targeting the joint of the Scorpion’s front limbs, successfully rendering one of its front paws temporarily immobile.
"Everyone, attention!" He started to look for opportunities to organize the others:
"Its burst phase is over; now it’s looking for an energy source. If we can continue to deplete its stamina, it will eventually be weakened!"
The surviving contestants, upon hearing this, revitalized like grabbing onto a life-saving straw.
Although they still didn’t fully trust Ron, the current situation left them no choice but to try this plan.
Trish struggled with all her might to support the poisoned Li Yue, occasionally using Plant Entanglement to restrict the Scorpion’s movements.
Her attacks were precise and efficient, hitting the Scorpion’s weak points every time.
"Didn’t expect his understanding of battle to be so deep, what a pity..."
The brown-haired girl felt a bit regretful for not listening to Ron’s advice to retreat further earlier.
Ron didn’t know Trish’s mental activity; he just continued to focus on his tactics.
He knew that it was crucial to lead the Scorpion into its weakest state, preparing for the final charging of the Transformer’s Skin.
The ensuing battle was like a carefully choreographed dance.
Each contestant found their place and role, forming a loose but effective attack network.
The Scorpion grew more and more irritable, but also increasingly weak.
Its attacks were still fierce but no longer able to maintain the previous high speed and accuracy.
More importantly, it began to frequently seek out blood prey, obviously in desperate need of energy replenishment.
"Just hold on a little longer!" Holt shouted, his Earth Elemental Golem almost disintegrating but still persistently standing at the frontline.
Ron seized the opportunity, releasing the strongest Spiritual Interference Wave.
This invisible attack acted directly on the Scorpion’s Spiritual Core, causing it to let out a painful howl.
"It’s now!" He signaled to Dale.
The Little Sea Siren immediately understood her master’s intention. She dove down from the sky, her hands crossing.
Water Element gathered around her, forming dozens of Water Swords, shimmering with a cold light.
——Thousand Water Blade Attacks!
This was Dale’s strongest skill, also the killer move designed by Ron specifically for her.
Dozens of water swords simultaneously shot at the Scorpion, each one accurately piercing its vital spots.
The Scorpion let out a shrill howl, its body wobbling as if it could fall at any moment.
The Scorpion was now at the end of its strength, its movements extremely slow, and the light in its eyes almost extinguished.
"The final blow!" Holt shouted, maneuvering the Earth Elemental Golem, which was almost down to half its body, to launch the final charge.
The Golem slammed into the Scorpion’s chest, knocking it to the ground.
The other contestants saw this and launched their strongest attacks.
Various energy beams shot toward the Scorpion from all directions, firmly pinning it to the ground.
The Scorpion let out one last weak hiss, then completely lost its life signs.
The moment the battle ended, the entire arena fell into a brief silence, followed by deafening cheers.
"It’s time." Ron thought silently and quietly activated the Transformer’s Skin’s last energy absorption.
The remaining Soul Energy from the Scorpion’s corpse was quickly absorbed, and the Transformer’s Skin began to heat up slightly, emitting a faint buzzing sound.
"99.5%...99.7%...99.9%...100%!"
An unprecedented energy fluctuation came from the Transformer’s Skin; Ron could feel it was undergoing some essential change.
[Charge Complete!]
[Rare Artifact - Transformer’s Skin can now advance to: Glorious Legacy - Thousand Transformations]
"Succeeded!" Ron felt joy in his heart but maintained a calm exterior.
This was a key step in his plan, but not yet the final victory.
On the high platform, the Masters were conducting the final scoring and discussion.
"Extremely outstanding performance." One Master commented with appreciation in his eyes:
"Especially that Alchemist; his calmness and tactical analysis skills are remarkable."
"Not only that." Soron, standing beside, began to supplement because it was his favored Apprentice, and he naturally had the opportunity to say a few good words:
"According to my observation, his Sea Siren exhibited a unique Water and Wind Dual Attributes ability, which is clearly the result of careful Modulation. It seems his talent in Bloodline Modulation is also quite exceptional."
"This is not surprising." Yuni appropriately interjected at this moment, as if coordinating with Soron in advance:
"He himself is an outstanding Alchemist, and these Extraordinary Skills have many things in common. Someone with talent in Magic Potion Making can often excel in Bloodline Modulation too."
Vice-Dean Hayek was silent for a moment, finally speaking:
"This test has achieved the expected goals. Based on each one’s scores and my observations, the final ranking and rewards distribution will be announced next."
His gaze lingered on Ron for a moment, with a hint of complex emotion flashing in his eyes.
"What a pity, such a rare all-round genius, snapped up by Soron and Yuni."
Hayek secretly thought:
"However, the School’s quota equal distribution system has its reasons. When a genius distributes too much, the benefits will fall short. After nurturing Corina last time, I really should let the opportunity go to them."
Hayek walked to the edge of the high platform and loudly announced:
"The final of the Bloody Gladiatorial Games is over. Please all participants return to the designated area to await the final judgment and reward distribution."
Ron calmly retreated to the edge of the field, with Dale landing beside him, her water wings already dissipated.
The Little Sea Siren looked exhausted but excited, clearly satisfied with her performance in the battle.
"Well done, Dale," Ron softly praised, as the plan in his mind had already moved forward another step.
The Shapeshifter’s skin could advance at any time to the "Glorious Legacy: Thousand Transformations."
Next was to strive for the Stand-In Puppet, along with the Active Demon Sword refined from Soul Steel.
The day when his "Melting Furnace Concept" would become a reality might not be too distant.
And all of this would be the foundation for his path to supremacy.
......
Hayek’s voice echoed across the arena as all the surviving participants quietly awaited the final judgment.
After the life-and-death battle just now, only six participants remained on the battlefield.
Among them, Holt’s Earth Elemental Golem was almost crumbling and could barely maintain form;
Trish’s Li Yue was barely clinging to life under the erosion of poison, requiring immediate treatment;
The combat slaves of the other participants were also battered, with only Ron’s Dale remaining relatively intact, despite the water wings’ maintenance consuming much of her stamina.
"According to the scores from each master and my observations," Hayek announced:
"The final ranking of this Bloody Gladiatorial Games is as follows: First place, Ron Ralph!"
This result left many present showing expressions of surprise, yet it was not unexpected.
The calm judgment and precise tactics Ron exhibited throughout the battle, along with the unique abilities Dale displayed, truly stood out.
"Second place, Holt! Third place, Trish! Fourth place..."
Hayek continued announcing the rankings, then turned to reward distribution:
"According to tradition, the first place will receive the special reward of this gladiatorial games—the Stand-In Puppet, eight complete Magic Stones, and the choice of any one book from the school’s precious collection.
The second and third places may choose three advanced Magic Potions or one advanced Alchemy Item, and will receive a reward of five and three Magic Stones respectively. The remaining participants will receive corresponding Magic Stone rewards according to their ranking..."
Ron’s heart sped up slightly, but he remained outwardly calm.
The Stand-In Puppet was precisely his main objective for participating in the gladiatorial games.
"All rewards will be distributed tomorrow. Now, all participants please leave the field to receive necessary treatment and rest."
With Hayek’s announcement, the Bloody Gladiatorial Games officially ended.
The participants gradually left the arena, with some Healing Apprentices from the school already waiting at the exit, prepared to provide necessary treatment for the injured participants and combat slaves.
Ron walked towards the exit with Dale, feeling numerous gazes focusing on him, filled with surprise, admiration, and, of course, jealousy.
"Congratulations, Ron." Holt approached, extending his hand to him: "Your performance truly deserved first place."
"Thank you for your critical help, Senior Holt."
Ron touched his hand briefly, then let go: "Without your Earth Elemental Golem holding off the Scorpion, the situation could have been more dangerous."
Holt shook his head:
"It was just a temporary measure. In such a circumstance, everyone knows that only cooperation can increase survival chances. Moreover, your observation and judgment truly turned the tide."
He glanced at his nearly disassembled Earth Elemental Golem and smiled wryly:
"Looks like I need to cultivate a new combat partner."
After exchanging a few words, Holt left with his broken Earth Elemental Golem.
As Ron was about to leave, he heard Trish’s voice calling from behind: "Ron, wait a moment."
He turned to see Trish supporting the weakened Li Yue approaching.
The Panther Woman’s arm still had an unhealthy purple hue, but it was no longer spreading, clearly having received preliminary treatment.
"You foresaw the Scorpion’s traits, didn’t you?" Trish directly asked, eyes filled with inquiry.
Ron nodded to admit: "Abyss creatures on land usually act this way—having a short burst period, they need to replenish power by devouring blood or absorbing energy attacks."
"No wonder you maintained distance, only conducting remote harassment," Trish mused:
"This tactical analysis ability doesn’t seem like what a regular Alchemist should possess."
Ron chuckled softly: "Everyone has their own secrets, don’t they?"
Trish gave him a look, seeming to want to say something, but eventually just nodded:
"Congratulations on achieving first place. That Stand-In Puppet is indeed a valuable prize; I hope it proves useful."
"Thank you," Ron politely replied: "How is Li Yue’s injury? Does she need a Special Antidote?"
"It’s under control," Trish shook her head, declining his offer:
"There are masters who master Healing Magic in the school specifically responsible for these matters, so there’s no need to trouble you."
After a brief farewell, Ron left the arena with Dale.
"Master, we won!" As soon as they exited the arena, Dale couldn’t contain her excitement, cheering softly.
"Yes, we became champions," Ron smiled, patting her head:
"Your performance was excellent, especially that final Water Blade, which almost dealt a fatal blow to the Scorpion."
Dale’s face flushed, clearly overjoyed by her master’s praise:
"I was just acting on your guidance; your tactics were the true key."
"It’s our victory together," he shook his head with a laugh, ruffling the Little Sea Siren’s silver hair, holding her hand as they headed towards the workshop.
The battle was over, though the phase of claiming rewards and calculating rank points had to wait until tomorrow.
After all, after a tough battle, everyone needed rest...

chapters.title: Chapter 227 - 165: Why Don’t I Have This?
chapters.content:
Chapter 227: Chapter 165: Why Don’t I Have This?
Hayek stood in the center of the arena, his eyes slightly closed, feeling the residual energy fluctuations around him.
The aftermath of the battle still echoed throughout the field, with scorched marks in the corners.
In the center lay a mess of sand and dirt, and the massive scorpion-lion corpse lay like a small mountain in the middle of the field.
"Strange... the soul resilience of Abyss creatures is usually much stronger than ordinary creatures; it shouldn’t dissipate so quickly."
The vice-dean frowned slightly, his fingers gently sweeping through the air.
A mini detection array took shape in the air, then transformed into dense energy threads that pierced into the scorpion-lion’s corpse.
After a few seconds of traversing the interior of the corpse, the magic silk threads began to pulsate in a special rhythm, conveying the detection results to Hayek.
After the battle, there should be a significantly thick presence of soul energy on the field.
Especially for such a Golden Ring level hybrid modulation creature, its soul energy should take several days or even a week to completely dissipate.
However, at this moment, the energy had already become so thin it was almost nonexistent, as if rapidly absorbed by some invisible force.
"Perhaps its energy structure is inherently unstable?"
Hayek mused to himself, then shook his head:
"It’s not unheard of, just rare."
This experiment had already provided plenty of valuable data—the stability of this scorpion-lion, ordered from some supplier at the Abyss outpost base, was far less than expected.
The instability of its internal structure even affected the preservation time of soul energy, which is a serious defect for experimental creatures.
"Seems like there’s no need to purchase from there anymore in the future."
Hayek contemplated, already considering finding better supplier alternatives.
Even for a Moon level wizard like him, the price of such Abyss hybrid modulation creatures is by no means cheap.
But after going through the Crystal Tower’s public account reimbursement, he felt no burden at all, and could even pocket some profit.
Thinking of this, Hayek gently raised his hand, drawing out several complex magic trajectories with his fingertips.
As these trajectories formed, the dirt and sand around the arena began to move on their own, gradually returning to their pre-battle level state.
The scorched marks were easily wiped away by a magic storm, broken rocks reassembled, and even the corroded pits were filled with fresh soil.
This precision down to the millimeter in material manipulation is one of the hallmark abilities of an official wizard.
Finally, Hayek turned his attention to the scorpion-lion’s corpse.
He traced a complex hexagram array in the air with both hands, with each magical line containing the tempered knowledge of his centuries-long wizarding career.
The blue-white magic silk threads enveloped the massive scorpion-lion corpse like a spider’s web, gradually permeating its every fiber.
Various decay processes would be frozen, while preserving the remaining life energy, ensuring that during the anatomy guidance the next day, this corpse would still retain sufficient freshness and research value.
"Its life energy is exceptionally strong, which is characteristic of Abyss creatures."
Hayek nodded in satisfaction:
"Even though the soul energy dissipated faster than usual, the tissue vitality is still high enough to support the entire anatomy guidance process."
He cast one last glance over the arena, making sure everything was restored to its original state, then lightly waved his sleeve, causing a ripple of magic to spread, extinguishing all the maintenance arrays.
"Tomorrow’s anatomy guide will be very interesting, especially for that young alchemist."
For such an apprentice displaying rare omnipotent talent, Hayek slightly regretted not being able to bring them under his tutelage.
But as the vice-dean, he still retained a unique privilege—organizing dissection courses.
By imparting knowledge face to face to many potential wizard seeds, he could also obtain a reasonable amount of favors.
No matter how much political maneuvering or resource competition there might be, nothing surpassed this direct and effective method of acquiring "favors."
In the Extraordinary World, power is the ultimate measure of everything.
And "favors" are the key to maintaining such power.
For him, guiding this group of exceptionally gifted young people, especially the likes of Ron, Holt, and Trish, the "favors" gained would be all the more substantial.
These elites among elites could often understand the imparted knowledge more profoundly, thus generating purer "favors."
"After handing out the competition prizes tomorrow, then conducting the anatomy guidance, I haven’t actually seen much of this Abyss creature, it’s worth a good study, maybe there will be some unexpected discoveries."
Hayek took one last look at the scorpion-lion’s corpse encapsulated by an energy shield, and then turned to leave the arena.
Behind him, the light blue energy shield emitted a faint glow, encompassing the fearsome hybrid modulation creature perfectly preserved within, as elemental servants automatically moved forward to prepare to transport it to a designated location.
.........
When night fell completely over the Black Mist Jungle, the lights in the workshop remained bright.
Ron pushed open the workshop door, with Dale happily following behind.
As they stepped into the foyer, Lilia hurried up to them, her face filled with both anticipation and worry.
"Teacher! You’re back safely!"
The girl’s voice carried undisguised joy, but there was a hint of concern in her eyes:
"How did the competition turn out? Did those combat servants or the vice-dean’s experimental subjects hurt you..."
Her words revealed the concern she had been harboring these past days.

chapters.title: Chapter 228 - 165: Why Don’t I Have That?_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 228: Chapter 165: Why Don’t I Have That?_2
Ever since learning that Ron would participate in the dangerous Bloody Gladiatorial Games, the girl had been worried, as everything she had was deeply tied to the workshop.
Although rationally, she knew that with her mentor’s ability, there shouldn’t be much danger, emotionally, she couldn’t help but worry.
Ron looked at the girl before him, who was relieved at his safe return, and his heart also stirred slightly.
"Champion." He uttered this simple word, his voice full of ease and freedom.
Although it was just a simple word, it made Lily instantly open her eyes wide, her mouth slightly agape.
Then, a radiant smile spread across her face, one Ron had never seen before.
Seeing his usually calm and reserved student so happy, Ron couldn’t help but chuckle softly.
This reaction was even more enthusiastic than his own, yet understandable. After all, this victory meant the workshop’s reputation would be further enhanced.
"I knew it! I knew the mentor could do it!"
Her voice trembled slightly, and her hands clutched tightly together unconsciously:
"With your thorough preparations and Dale’s diligent training, it’s no wonder you’d become champions!"
"Dale and I just performed to our usual level."
Ron said casually, yet the corners of his mouth could not help but lift.
It was a rare moment of relaxation for him. In this small workshop, he generally did not always maintain that calm and restrained image.
Dale proudly puffed out her chest on the side, her face carrying a childlike pride:
"The master is the most amazing person I’ve ever seen! He knew all the enemy’s weaknesses, and every attack was just right! I just acted on the master’s instructions."
Lily couldn’t wait to pull the two towards the dining room, her face unable to hide her excitement:
"I’ve prepared a sumptuous dinner, guessing you’d have a big victory, so I wanted to celebrate specially. There’s baked fish, mushroom soup, and Dale’s favorite sweet berries..."
Seeing Lily’s cheerful back, Ron’s heart was slightly moved.
This girl, who had come to rely on him due to her family’s upheaval, had been taken in as his assistant because of her special talent, had undoubtedly fully integrated by now.
Lily placed the last dish on the table, the dining room filled with an enticing aroma.
Ron, Dale, and Lily sat around the table, candlelight adding a touch of warmth to the simple celebratory dinner.
"Mentor, try this baked fish."
Lily carefully forked the largest piece of fish into Ron’s bowl, her eyes sparkling with anticipation:
"I used that special herb you mentioned last time, it should make the taste more unique."
Ron took a bite and nodded in approval: "The taste is indeed good, the herb pairing is just right."
Dale, who had already been eagerly eating, had her cheeks puffed slightly because they were full, like a greedy little squirrel.
Swallowing the food, she looked at Lily with bright eyes:
"Sister Lily, you should see how the master performed in the Beast Fighting Arena! He was amazing! That big monster..."
Dale gestured with both hands:
"Was this big! The poisonous stinger on its tail was as sharp as a sword! But the master was not afraid at all, he stood there as if he had seen through everything."
Ron slightly shook his head, a smile on his lips:
"I just observed and discovered a pattern, any careful person could do it."
"That’s not true!" Dale put down her knife and fork again:
"The master’s Sound Wave Attack was amazing! Even though it was invisible, that big monster was shaken to the point of nose bleeding!"
She excitedly mimicked the painful expression of the scorpion, exaggeratedly shaking her head, making Lily chuckle.
The girl curiously looked at Ron: "Mentor, was that experimental creature really as terrible as Dale said?"
Ron put down the spoon in his hand, his expression becoming serious:
"Even more dangerous than Dale described. It was a scorpion from the Abyss; even showing just a part of its power was enough to tear a normal Advanced Apprentice to pieces."
His gaze shifted to the darkness outside the window, as if recalling that life-and-death battle:
"If not for everyone eventually forming a temporary cooperation, the casualties would have been even more severe."
Dale proudly puffed out her chest: "But my Thousand Water Blade Attacks made it howl in pain directly!"
She mimicked the spellcasting movements, her tone full of pride:
"All the techniques the master taught me were put to use! Especially the Hydrofoil Gliding, it made me the only servant capable of moving agilely!"
Admiration flashed in Lily’s eyes: "Dale, you were really brave."
"That guy named Holt was amazing too!"
Dale, stuffing mushroom soup into her mouth, spoke unclearly:
"The Earth Elemental Golem he controlled was right in front of the scorpion, even if it got smashed to bits..."
Ron nodded:
"Holt the senior is indeed worthy of respect, his tactical skills and adaptive ability are outstanding."
As if thinking of something, he gently shook his head:
"It’s just a pity that Trish’s Li Yue was badly injured, that kind of abyssal toxin is very troublesome."
Worry flashed in Lily’s eyes: "Is Li Yue’s situation serious?"
"The School should have a way to heal her, but it will take time."
Ron took a sip of tea, his expression calm:
"Trish has some proficiency in natural healing as well, coupled with the resources of the School, it shouldn’t be a major problem."
Speaking of natural healing, his gaze involuntarily turned outward, where a towering ancient tree stood, appearing particularly mysterious in the moonlight.

chapters.title: Chapter 229 - 165: Why Don’t I Have This?_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 229: Chapter 165: Why Don’t I Have This?_3
Dale seemed to notice where Ron’s gaze was directed, and she set down her bowl, with a tone full of longing:
"When will Mom Ailan wake up? I miss her so much."
Lilia gently patted Dale’s head:
"According to the teacher’s observations, it should be very soon. Maybe by the time we return with our prizes tomorrow, Sister Ailan will have awoken?"
"Really?" Dale’s eyes brightened instantly, turning to Ron for confirmation.
Ron nodded slightly: "Indeed, according to the transformation process, Ailan is very likely to complete her final transformation within these two days."
"Will she be more powerful than the previous Mom Ailan?" Dale asked curiously.
"Of course." Ron smiled gently:
"After her transformation, Ailan will be much stronger in plant control, and our workshop’s defense will be greatly enhanced as a result."
Lilia nodded thoughtfully:
"No wonder Sister Ailan looked forward to this transformation so much. It truly is a rebirth for her."
After dinner, the young girl skillfully began to tidy up the mess of cups and plates on the table. Seeing Ron getting up, she wiped her hands on her apron and asked with concern:
"Do you need a break? I’ve prepared hot water and..."
"Thank you for your concern, Lilia, but I need some private time now."
Ron gently interrupted her:
"There are some important matters to deal with."
Lilia immediately understood the meaning, tactfully nodding:
"I understand, Teacher. If you need any help, please feel free to call me."
She knew that the teacher often needed to focus on some secretive research, and the best help was not to disturb him at those times.
Ron nodded in satisfaction, he appreciated such emotionally intelligent students, and then turned to Dale:
"You also need to rest well, today’s battle consumed a lot of Energy. Although your performance was excellent, your body needs time to recover. How about going for a nice bath with Sister Lily later?"
The Little Sea Siren nodded, despite the excitement in her eyes, she could feel the exhaustion after a hard-fought day:
"As you command, Master. I’ll head to the bathroom with Sister Lily at once!"
With that, she hurriedly pulled the apron-clad girl beside her, Lilia slightly flustered:
"Wait, Little Dale, I haven’t finished cleaning up yet..."
......
In the steam-filled bathroom, the sound of water could be heard trickling.
Dale cheerfully soaked in the specially made large bathtub, her silver hair floating on the water like a fine silver silk.
She would sometimes dive underwater and sometimes emerge, her face radiating pure joy.
"Sister Lily, come in! The water temperature is just right!"
The Little Sea Siren splashed the water, sending droplets flying.
Lilia was carefully undoing buttons on the side, smiling slightly as she heard this:
"Don’t be in such a rush, I’m coming right in."
She slowly let down the last piece of clothing, revealing her graceful and slender body, delicately stepping into the pool.
Dale’s gaze was immediately captured, a trace of curiosity flashed in her violet-blue eyes.
Lilia’s figure had developed quite maturely, with beautiful curves and skin as smooth and delicate as fine porcelain.
In contrast, despite the Sea Siren’s rapid growth in recent days, her body still remained childishly slender.
"Sister Lily."
Dale couldn’t help but swim a little closer, her eyes shining with envy:
"Your body is so beautiful!"
She reached out a little hand, curiously pointing at the two objects on the girl’s chest:
"Why don’t I have these?"
Lilia’s cheeks instantly flushed red, hurriedly covering with her arm:
"Dale! Staring like that is too impolite."
Although her tone carried a hint of reproach, her eyes showed a touch of tenderness:
"You’re still young, in a few years you’ll naturally develop."

chapters.title: Chapter 230 - 166: Thousand Transformations
chapters.content:
Chapter 230: Chapter 166: Thousand Transformations
"It’s not small at all!" Dale stood with her hands on her hips, disgruntled:
"I’ve already defeated so many strong opponents in the arena!"
Lilia chuckled softly, reaching out to tidy Dale’s tousled silver hair:
"In terms of combat ability, you are indeed strong. But the body’s development follows its own rules, you can’t rush it."
Dale pouted, unconvinced, but quickly replaced it with a sly smile:
"Lily sister, do you wish that our master would notice your beautiful body more?"
Lilia’s face turned red instantly, the blush spreading to her ears as she waved her hands in panic:
"What nonsense are you talking about! The teacher is my guide, I have only respect and gratitude for him!"
"Really?"
A mischievous glint flashed in Dale’s eyes as she exaggerated her usual tone mimicking Lilia’s voice:
"’Teacher, do you need hot water?’
’Teacher, this dish has your favorite herbs.’
’Teacher, I have washed and ironed your robe.’
Lilia, both embarrassed and annoyed, scooped up water to splash at Dale:
"You naughty girl! Say that again and I won’t help wash your hair anymore!"
Dale dodged nimbly, giggling:
"Lily sister is blushing! Blushing!"
She spun in the water, the splashes like a string of pearls:
"I see Lily sister always sneaks a few extra glances at him whenever she hands something to the master!"
Lilia sighed, smiling helplessly:
"Dale, the teacher is very good to us, I’m just trying to repay his guidance to the best of my ability."
Her voice softened, a touch of warmth in her eyes:
"Without him, I wouldn’t know what fate awaited me. He gave me the opportunity to learn and see my own value."
Dale suddenly quieted down, swam over to Lilia, and gently leaned on her shoulder:
"The master is very good to us. He saved my life and taught me so many skills, making me this strong."
The little Sea Siren’s voice suddenly took on a tinge of melancholy:
"But, it seems like the master never needs anyone’s help; he’s always researching alone late into the night."
Lilia gently stroked Dale’s wet silver hair, her voice tender and firm:
"That’s why we have to do our best to help him with those everyday chores, so he can focus on the truly important research."
There was a hint of determination in her eyes:
"I believe the teacher has aspirations beyond the ordinary, and what we can do is support him as best as we can in our roles."
Dale nodded thoughtfully, then returned to her usual lively self:
"But Lily sister, if the master needs a partner, would you be willing?"
Lilia’s face flushed again; she hurriedly grabbed a sponge, changing the subject:
"Alright, stop saying that, let me help clean the bloodstains off your back!"
Dale laughed triumphantly but obediently turned around, still muttering:
"Lily sister is shy, Lily sister is shy..."
With water splashing and laughter echoing in the bathroom...
Meanwhile, on the other side, once Ron confirmed he was alone in the room, he headed straight for the deepest part of the second-floor laboratory.
This was a special room protected by multiple isolation arrays, specifically used for those absolutely confidential experiments.
He carefully checked the integrity of the array, ensuring there were no tiny breaches or energy leaks.
For the upcoming ceremony involving his most core abilities’ advancement, he could not afford the slightest mistake.
The array runes were activated one by one, each precisely embedded into its preset position, forming a perfect energy loop.
Ron’s fingers lightly traced through the air, his spiritual power flowing precisely into each node like water.
When the last protective rune lit up, the entire room was enveloped in a layer of pale blue energy film, completely isolating it from the outside world.
He could feel the subtle energy fluctuations as the array activated, like an invisible net blocking out all external energy disturbances.
Subsequently, he began to activate the Transformer Skin which had already charged to 100%.
At this moment, the Transformer Skin was no longer the dull silvery-grey liquid he had initially acquired but had a lustrous sheen like molten moonlight, flowing and changing.
"Are you sure the advancement process won’t generate noticeable energy fluctuations?"
Ron asked in a low voice, caution in his tone, brows slightly furrowed, fully vigilant.
After all, it was the core area within the school, any unusual energy fluctuations might attract unnecessary trouble.
The Transformer’s voice echoed in his mind:
"Master need not worry. The advancement process mainly occurs on the soul level and will not produce externally perceivable energy fluctuations. Moreover, with the protection of these isolation arrays, even if there’s slight energy leakage, it won’t be detected by the outside."
Ron pondered for a moment, then nodded in agreement:
"Then, let’s begin."
He sat cross-legged, placing the Transformer Skin in his palm.
The silver liquid gleamed with an eerie light under the candlelight, as if something inside it was awakening.
It no longer lay quietly there but actively flowed across Ron’s palm, as if it had a life of its own.
Ron took a deep breath, adjusting his breathing rhythm to calm his heartbeat.
Then, he slowly closed his eyes, carefully extending his spiritual power to establish a connection with the Transformer Skin.
As his spiritual power delved deeper, he could feel the astounding energy contained within the Transformer Skin.
It was an ancient and profound force, like a dragon long asleep finally opening its eyes.
The energy was complex and ever-changing, yet it possessed an indescribable order and beauty.
"Can we start?"
Ron finally confirmed, his voice calm, but his Spiritual Power already tinged with a cautious anticipation.
"Ready to start at any time, Master."
The Transformer responded, its mechanical tone devoid of any emotional fluctuation:
"Once started, the process cannot be interrupted. Please ensure you have enough time reserved. I must remind you that once the advancement is complete, I will be deeply bonded with you, which is a necessary process preset for the subsequent upgrade to ’Exclusive Weapon.’ Please be prepared accordingly."
Upon hearing this, Ron gently closed his eyes, took a deep breath, and let his consciousness sink deep:
"Begin!"
In that instant, it was as if lightning pierced through his entire being.
An invisible torrent of energy erupted from the skin of the Transformer, surging directly into the depths of Ron’s soul.
This was not ordinary Magic Power or Spiritual Power; it was a more elemental energy, acting directly at the soul level.
He could feel every inch of his Spiritual Space being washed by this energy, like a long-dry riverbed suddenly welcoming a mountain flood.
Initially, the sensation was both painful and wonderful, indescribable.
But as the process deepened, the pain gradually subsided, replaced by an unprecedented clarity and acuteness.
His range of perception began to expand rapidly, not only able to sense every cell in his body but also able to detect the tiniest energy fluctuations in the air.
Simultaneously, the skin of the Transformer underwent astonishing changes.
The silver liquid began to flow violently, writhing as if alive.
This energy fluctuation was extremely intense, like a silent gale raging in a confined space.
What was once just a piece of silver liquid now began to differentiate into countless tiny structures, like a miniature universe being born.
Each tiny structure had its specific function, interconnected, forming a perfect whole.
Ron could keenly perceive these changes, as if witnessing the creation of an artwork from nothing.
He could feel the connection between the skin of the Transformer and himself becoming more intimate, almost inseparable.
It was no longer just something attached to the surface of his skin but became a part of his body, like a special second skin, merging with the Essence of Life.
The process of advancement lasted an interminable time, yet it seemed just a moment.
When Ron finally opened his eyes, he found that only a few minutes had passed outside, but within him, earth-shattering changes had occurred.
[Advancement successfully completed:
Rare Artifact - Skin of the Transformer → Glory Legacy - Thousand Transformations]
[Thousand Transformations (Glory Legacy) Effect:
Perfect Isolation: Capable of forming triple Energy Barriers, isolating internal and external energy interactions
High Tier Simulation: Capable of simulating the appearance and partial abilities of a designated target, with enhanced simulation accuracy
Record (Active Ability): Consumes 1% energy to record a move, which can be released unidirectionally upon selection, but its power cannot be controlled by the self
Note: Can only record moves not exceeding two tiers above oneself, requiring close proximity to record
(Currently limited to Morning Star Level Mage or below)]
[Charging Progress: Current 0/100%
Special Note: Certain abilities will be unlocked again when the charge reaches 50%
Upon reaching a full charge of 100%, it can serve as a key item for advancing to an epic Profession (Four Stars) and evolve into an Exclusive Weapon]
Ron read the information on the panel carefully, each line making his heart race, various possibilities rapidly spreading in his mind.
"Perfect Isolation" was the most critical ability in his plan.
It would provide solid protection for his soul splitting plan, ensuring that there would be no energy leakage or interference during the division.
"High Tier Simulation" was an extremely practical ability, able to play a significant role whether used for hiding identity or integrating into specific environments.
The most surprising was undoubtedly the new active ability named "Record."
Being able to record and release others’ moves meant he could directly use others’ Skills, greatly expanding his combat options.
Although it had limitations—it could only record moves not exceeding two tiers above himself, and close contact was necessary to record them.
But this was already an extraordinarily powerful ability.
Ron immediately thought of an excellent application scenario:
Learning from Official Wizards willing to demonstrate spells during paid consultations and then secretly recording the powerful magic they cast.
"If I can record a high-power spell from an Official Wizard Level during each consultation, over time, I can have a powerful card deck."
Ron calculated in his mind, a glint passing through his eyes.
He tried to slightly mobilize the energy of the Thousand Transformations and immediately felt an unprecedented sense of control.
In the past, the skin of the Transformer was more like an external tool, needing to issue commands through intent and then wait for execution.
Now, the Thousand Transformations were like a part of his body, even more intimate than the body itself, no longer merely an attached relation, but more like a part connected by blood and flesh.
Just like his skin, muscles, bones, they became an inseparable part of his body.
Now, just a slight adjustment of thought, and the Thousand Transformations would respond immediately.
Thinking of this, he raised his hand, and with a gentle thought, the surface of his arm was immediately covered with a layer of silver sheen.
This sheen rapidly transformed, forming appearances of various materials—steel, wood, crystal, everything.
The speed of its changes, the accuracy of its forms, were far beyond what was possible before.
"Truly astonishing control precision."
Ron admired, as the past changes of the skin of the Transformer always had subtle unnatural parts.
But now, these changes could almost rival real materials, with even texture and feel perfectly matching.
He further tried, concentrated, recalled the sharp claws of the Scorpion.
The next moment, his fingers had transformed into claws identical to those of a Scorpion, even the patterns on them were nearly the same.
Ron lightly scratched the table, and the hard wooden surface immediately bore several deep grooves.
"The recording ability..."
He pondered this newly gained active ability and its potential uses:
"I can only record abilities not exceeding two tiers above mine, currently I can only record Apprentice and Morning Star Mage level moves."

chapters.title: Chapter 231 - 167: Stand-In Puppet
chapters.content:
Chapter 231: Chapter 167: Stand-In Puppet
At this stage, for him, a strike from a Morning Star Level Wizard is already a force sufficient to break the balance.
Previously, the scorpion’s claw strike was only close to the output of an Official Wizard, yet it shattered the incredibly solid Earth Elemental Golem into pieces.
Not to mention that true wizards can also use Super Magic Techniques, making their destructive power even more formidable if recorded...
Ending his thoughts, Ron carefully checked the function of "Perfect Isolation" again.
This is precisely the most crucial part of his plan — the energy barrier used to safely split the soul.
He focused his Spirit to form a miniature energy barrier area within his body.
Surprisingly, this area indeed formed three layers of isolation as stated on the panel.
The first layer blocks energy, the second layer blocks the spirit, and the third layer is specifically for soul fluctuations.
The three layers superimposed almost completely block the interaction of internal and external energy.
"Too perfect..."
Ron nodded in satisfaction.
The soul splitting safety issue that had always troubled him now had a reliable solution.
But then he frowned again.
The charging of Thousand Transformations had reset to zero, which means its subsequent ability development still requires the absorption of soul energy.
"Once fully charged, it can be used as a key item for advancing the epic profession (Four Stars)..."
Ron mulled over this hint repeatedly, his eyes flickering with thoughtful light.
The Three Stars {Black Wizard} and {Crown Knight} are invincible at the Official Wizard level.
So this so-called Four Stars epic profession might be directly targeting the level of a Great Wizard.
And the Pocket Watch of the Time Guardian corresponding to the Time Guardian could be a terrifying profession that can control the flow of time.
To most apprentices, becoming an Official Wizard is already the highest pursuit.
But the ceiling of the Extraordinary World is naturally much higher than this.
Above the Official Wizard, there are Great Wizards who can traverse the starry sea and destroy stars or even vast galaxies with a wave of a hand. Above the Great Wizard is the Witch King, who rules over numerous conquered planes.
And according to legends, there are even higher-level existences:
Those called "Demon Gods," great beings who can change rules with mere thoughts.
Thinking of this, he quickly calmed down; with his current little Karami strength, he couldn’t be too complacent.
Ron meticulously recorded this speculation about epic professions into the Library of Consciousness, marking it as an important clue to be verified.
Outside, the night in the Black Mist Jungle was deep, and the faint moonlight penetrated the thick fog, casting a silver veil over this mysterious land.
His gaze passed through the mist and fell on the looming School tower in the distance.
"This is just the beginning."
Ron silently thought to himself: "And there’s the Stand-In Puppet and the Master Sword..."
In the Furnace Plan, these three items each have different roles:
Thousand Transformations is responsible for energy isolation and the spiritual barrier, ensuring the stability of the entire system;
The Stand-In Puppet is responsible for soul splitting and doppelganger control, providing additional movement capability;
The Master Sword is responsible for force aggregation and pollution transformation, turning negative effects into positive power.
These three coordinate to form a complete power cycle system.
Allowing Ron to benignly acquire those powers usually considered forbidden while avoiding risks.
"Tomorrow, once I get the Stand-In Puppet, the plan will enter the next stage."
He looked at the distant tower, calm and determined.
Everything was advancing according to the plan, step by step, steadily.
.........
In a rare moment, the Black Mist Jungle cleared up in the morning.
Sunlight penetrated the perennial mist, shedding warm light upon the Central Tower.
A few passing apprentices cast envious and curious glances toward the tower, discussing yesterday’s astonishing battle and the upcoming precious rewards.
"I heard the vice dean offered an Abyssal Treasure as the grand prize this time! It’s a rare gem he brought back from the Crystal Tower!"
A tall and thin apprentice excitedly told his companion next to him.
"That scorpion was reportedly brought back from the Abyss 3rd Floor. Surviving before such a creature alone is no easy feat, let alone someone being able to coordinate everyone to fight together."
An older apprentice commented solemnly, his tone filled with respect for the recently debated figure.
Inside one of the large rooms of the Central Tower, various prizes had long been set up, shimmering with the unique phantasmagoric glow of Extraordinary Items.
The victors of the Bloody Gladiatorial Games had been waiting there for some time, each wearing an expression ranging from hopeful to expectant.
Ron stood on the side, his face calm, only his slightly clenched hands betrayed a bit of inner emotion.
As time went by, more and more apprentices gathered in the room to wait.
He paid no attention to the occasional whispers, his focus entirely on the upcoming reward ceremony.
Especially the Stand-In Puppet, which could become a crucial part of his soul splitting plan.
Holt, with a calm face and upright posture, showed only slightly bluish circles under his eyes, indicating he perhaps didn’t sleep well last night;
Beside Trish was her inseparable bodyguard Li Yue, the panther lady, though treated, still looked weak;
The other surviving contestants appeared either excited or nervous, awaiting their respective rewards.
Vice Dean Hayek, wearing a deep purple Wizard’s Robe, stood in the center of the platform with a dignified and calm demeanor.
Soron and Yuni stood on either side, their gazes occasionally lingering on Ron.

chapters.title: Chapter 232 - 167: Stand-In Puppet (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 232: Chapter 167: Stand-In Puppet (Part 2)
When the last contestant stepped into the hall, Hayek raised his right hand lightly, and the entire space fell silent instantly, as if an invisible cloth had enveloped all sounds.
"In yesterday’s duel, you demonstrated wisdom, courage, and strength."
The vice dean’s voice was not loud, but it could be heard clearly in every corner:
"Today, the School will fulfill its promise and award you the rewards you deserve."
He nodded slightly to his assistant beside him, signaling the start.
By convention, the rewards are collected in reverse order.
Ron maintained his composure, but his eyes didn’t miss any detail, observing every contestant’s reaction.
Those ranked lower couldn’t hide the disappointment and envy on their faces.
When they received those dozens of magic stone fragments, the slight trembling of their fingers did not escape Ron’s observation.
These subtle changes were quickly analyzed and categorized into psychological patterns, stored in the "Character Observation" category of the Library of Consciousness.
Soon, it was the turn of the contestant who ranked fourth, this resolute-looking Advanced Apprentice, who chose a bottle of Vitality Potion along with a complete magic stone.
A brief satisfaction flashed in his eyes, quickly returning to the common indifference seen among apprentices.
"A fairly good choice," Ron silently evaluated:
"The market price of a Vitality Potion is equivalent to about sixty magic stone fragments. Adding the magic stone itself, the total value is close to one and a half complete magic stones. This choice ensures immediate gain and provides some protection in case of danger."
"Third place, Trish Lind."
The brown-haired girl walked forward slowly, still maintaining that calm and composed demeanor.
Beside her, Li Yue had mostly recovered from the poison erosion, though her movements were still a bit sluggish, her complexion had improved significantly.
"You may choose three advanced magic potions or one advanced alchemy item, in addition to three complete magic stones."
Hayek’s voice was steady and authoritative.
Trish did not make an immediate choice but looked towards Ron with a hint of hesitation, a complex emotion flashing in her eyes.
"Vice Dean, before making a choice, I would like to exchange opinions with Apprentice Ralph, may I be permitted?"
Trish’s request surprised many present.
Ron frowned slightly; he didn’t like such unexpected situations but maintained his impeccable calm appearance.
Hayek seemed slightly surprised but nodded in consent.
The brown-haired girl walked slowly to Ron’s side and said in a low voice:
"I’ve heard your level in magic potion making is close to that of a senior alchemist, is that true?"
Ron roughly understood her intention but answered cautiously:
"Rumors tend to exaggerate. However, Magic Potion Making is indeed one of the fields I focus on."
"It seems to be true." A sharpness flashed in Trish’s eyes:
"In that case, choosing other ready-made magic potions would be somewhat wasteful. I’m considering exchanging for a magic potion formula that enhances Natural Affinity. Can you refine it?"
Ron quickly evaluated the pros and cons in his mind.
Formulas have long-term value, and with his mastery of magic potion techniques, he has slightly surpassed some senior alchemists.
Plus, with the "Material Refining" fusion skill, refining such complex magic potions was no longer a challenge.
More importantly, to almost get a formula for free—only a fool would refuse.
But he still pretended to think it over, throwing the choice back:
"These types of magic potions usually have a complex formula and require high spiritual control. However, it should be within my capability. Do you have any specific ideas?"
"I can consolidate this selection privilege, along with the additional magic stones, to exchange for a complete formula. Master Corina hinted at a hidden option like this to me yesterday."
Trish looked Ron directly in the eye:
"In exchange, I hope you can refine six batches of finished magic potions for me, delivered in stages, the last batch completed within two months. This way, I can fully utilize the effects before the Bloodline Altar opens."
Ron quickly calculated costs and profits in his mind.
Such a complex magic potion formula is priced at least at five to six complete magic stones on the market, and refining six batches of finished products, the material cost is about one or two magic stones roughly.
Even considering the extra time and effort invested, this is still a transaction destined to be profitable.
"Agree, but you need to provide me the complete formula, and I will prepare the rest myself."
Ron replied calmly, his tone devoid of any emotional fluctuations.
"Deal."
Trish nodded in satisfaction, turned around, and walked back to face Hayek to explain her choice.
The vice dean raised his eyebrows slightly, apparently a bit surprised by this choice.
He signaled an assistant to bring over an exquisite crystal box.
The crystal box was completely translucent, covered with protective runes on the surface, and inside, faintly visible, was a roll of parchment glowing softly.
"A wise choice, Apprentice Trish."
Hayek commented, his voice carrying a trace of appreciation:
"Enhancement of Natural Affinity has a significant effect on activating Forest Elf bloodline, it seems you are well prepared for the Bloodline Altar."
Trish accepted the reward, solemnly saluted the Masters, then returned to her place, a barely noticeable smile emerging on her face.
Ron noticed the way she tightly held the scroll box in her hand, as if grasping the hope for the future.
"Indeed, her choice over directly taking three ready-made magic potions is much wiser, thanks to the hidden option her mentor mentioned."
Ron evaluated in his mind:
"Six successive enhancements of Natural Affinity are enough to take her Forest Elf bloodline a step further, increasing the success rate of gaining something from the Bloodline Altar."

chapters.title: Chapter 233 - 167: Stand-In Puppet (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 233: Chapter 167: Stand-In Puppet (Part 3)
"Second place, Holt Elvin."
The head of the procession stepped forward slowly, his demeanor as steady as a mountain.
"You can choose three advanced magic potions or one advanced alchemy item, plus five complete magic stones."
Holt’s response was crisp and decisive: "I choose the alchemy item ’Heart of the Earth’."
This answer seemed to be exactly what Hayek anticipated; he nodded slightly and signaled his assistant to bring a heavy black ebony box.
When the box was opened, inside was a fist-sized brown crystal, its surface covered with tiny patterns resembling the veins of the earth.
Inside the crystal, some sort of energy seemed to flow slowly, like an underground stream, emanating a sense of weight and timelessness.
"’Heart of the Earth’, capable of repairing earth element structures and enhancing their toughness and strength," Hayek explained succinctly:
"For your combat style, this is undoubtedly the most suitable choice."
Holt accepted the wooden box and magic stones, bowing respectfully to the masters in gratitude, his eyes showing a relieved expression.
Ron keenly caught this subtle change and immediately analyzed it.
"He knew the contents of the prize long ago and had even decided on his choice before the battle."
Ron inferred internally:
"This suggests that Holt also likely learned about the prize list in advance through his master. Indeed, connections are indispensable anywhere, both Trish and Holt have their masters tell them the choices; luckily, I don’t need to make a choice..."
Finally, it was time for the most anticipated highlight, the first prize.
"First place, Ron Ralph."
There was a special note of attention in Hayek’s voice:
"You will receive the special reward of this contest—a Stand-In Puppet, eight complete magic stones, and the option to pick any one book from the school’s rare collection."
Ron walked up calmly, sensing countless eyes in the hall focusing on him.
Among them were envy, jealousy, and even some indescribably complex emotions.
The Vice Dean personally retrieved an exquisite black ebony box, its surface engraved with intricate protective runes, having an oddly cold feeling to the touch.
When the box was opened, an oddly shaped humanoid puppet lay silently inside.
The puppet was entirely grayish-green, as if weathered by countless years of erosion, its body covered in twisted, complex runes.
These runes were not simply engraved but seemed to naturally grow on the puppet’s surface like blood vessels, forming a complex energy network.
Most unsettling were its eyes:
Two dark red gemstones were embedded within, glimmering faintly even in darkness, as if something inside was observing the outside world.
"The ’Stand-In Puppet’, originating from the Great Abyss Fourth Layer, contains a Soul Stone capable of housing consciousness."
Hayek explained, his voice carrying a tone of objective calm:
"However, its effect is not as ideal as rumored."
Ron took the wooden box, bringing it slightly closer, carefully observing every detail of the puppet while awaiting Hayek’s further explanation.
"Ordinary people have only one soul; when using this item, a portion of consciousness must be separated and injected into the puppet."
Hayek continued to explain:
"This leads to a fundamental dilemma—dual tasking is extremely difficult for most apprentices. If too little consciousness is injected, the puppet acts mechanically stiff; if too much, the main body becomes weakened."
Hayek paused slightly, as if observing Ron’s reaction:
"More importantly, this duplicate cannot exceed one hundred meters from the main body, and the copied strength cannot reach the level of an Official Wizard, as if there exists some inherent limitation."
"Therefore." With a touch of resignation in the Vice Dean’s tone:
"This Abyssal Treasure holds little value in the eyes of Official Wizards, at most serving as a decoy in times of crisis. But during the apprentice phase, it still has its unique uses."
On the surface, Ron listened earnestly, displaying an aptly mixed expression of gratitude and slight disappointment.
Yet inside, he was boiling, having instantly discerned the true value of this "Stand-In Puppet" through the panel’s hints and his Extraordinary Recognition Ability.

chapters.title: Chapter 234 - 168: The "Insight" Trait
chapters.content:
Chapter 234: Chapter 168: The "Insight" Trait
[Rare Artifact: Stand-In Puppet (Pending Activation)]
[Current Energy: 0/100%]
[Effect: Creates a perfect stand-in that shares abilities with the user and can endure part of the user’s soul
(Holders of the Special Talent "Dual Soul" will be able to trigger more hidden effects)]
[Maximum Distance: Initial 100 meters, can increase with charging]
[Note: More functions can be unlocked after charging]
An uncontrollable excitement surged in Ron’s heart, yet he maintained a calm expression on his face, even deliberately showing a subtle hint of regret.
The Official Wizards could not discern the true value of this treasure because they couldn’t combine it with the "Dual Soul" talent, naturally failing to activate its full potential.
For ordinary wizards, this is indeed just an auxiliary tool with many limitations;
but for Ron, it was practically a treasure tailor-made for him.
He could not only fully integrate his second soul into the puppet, achieving genuine clone combat, but also use this opportunity to practice the gradually forming "Melting Furnace Concept."
"Thank you for the detailed explanation, Vice Dean." Ron responded steadily:
"I will make good use of this treasure."
Hayek handed over eight complete Magic Stones to Ron and then presented a specially made badge:
"This is special access to the Library. With this badge, you can select a book from the Treasure Area within a month. Be cautious with your choice because once selected, it cannot be changed."
Ron solemnly accepted the badge, feeling a slight energy fluctuation from the touch.
"Thank you for the generous reward from the School."
He nodded slightly, speaking politely, yet in his eyes, he was already calculating how to maximize the use of this valuable privilege.
After all the prizes were distributed, Hayek spoke again:
"Next, I will conduct an anatomy guide on yesterday’s specimen. Interested contestants can stay; this is a rare learning opportunity."
"Here it comes, this is also the part I’ve been eagerly anticipating," Ron thought to himself.
The anatomy guide could provide precious firsthand Extraordinary Biology knowledge, possibly being the key to breaking through the introductory bottleneck of "Extraordinary Biology."
Of course, he wasn’t the only one thinking this way; except for one contestant who was injured in the head, everyone else chose to stay.
The chance to witness the dissection skills of a Moon Level wizard firsthand is incredibly rare, and even members at the forefront of the sequence wouldn’t miss it.
Furthermore, this time the specimen was a rare Abyssal Creature—a Scorpion, whose internal structure and energy system were of extremely high value for researching biological adaptability in the Abyss environment.
Ron deliberately chose the frontmost position, less than two meters from the dissection table, to capture each detail to the fullest extent.
The Vice Dean gestured, and several Elemental Servants pushed in a large dissection table with the defeated Scorpion’s corpse from yesterday lying on it.
Even in death, the creature still exuded a chilling aura, as if death could not completely erase its fierce nature.
"The Scorpion, a native creature of the 3rd Floor of the Abyss, known as ’Desert Monarch’ by explorers."
Hayek began his explanation, his voice carrying a professional composure:
"They are hybrids of lions and giant scorpions, having traits of both, but with a unique magic power structure, enabling them to survive and reproduce in the harsh environment of the ’Black Sand Wilderness.’"
In the Vice Dean’s hand suddenly appeared a dazzling Energy Scalpel, a magical advancement application, capable of precisely cutting any material without damaging its surrounding structure.
"Observe its skin structure closely."
Hayek made a perfect incision on the Scorpion’s body, pointing to the incision:
"At first glance, it seems like regular hair, but each strand is actually a micro magic power conduit, capable of absorbing and storing energy from the environment, which is key to their survival in harsh conditions."
Ron simultaneously activated Extraordinary Recognition and Tracing Ability, meticulously observing every detail.
The internal structure of the Scorpion was far more complex than its exterior, with organs arranged following a peculiar energy pattern, distinct from ordinary creatures.
He could see those energy flow paths invisible to the naked eye, as well as the complex interactions between various organs.
"This is its first heart, dedicated to handling regular blood circulation."
Hayek skillfully extracted a deep red organ larger than a human head: "And this second heart, responsible for magic power circulation, is the core of its energy system."
"Dual heart structure..."
Ron silently recorded in his mind:
"Such a design allows it to maintain two completely different circulation systems simultaneously, one for normal physiological functions, the other dedicated to extraordinary energy management; this is one of the key evolutionary traits for adapting to the Abyss environment."
As the dissection progressed, Ron felt a wondrous understanding emerging in his heart.
The once scattered points of knowledge in Extraordinary Biology were now forming a coherent and vividly clear network through the real-life demonstration of this complete specimen.
The function of each organ, the direction of every energy path, the traits of each tissue, all formed a three-dimensional, systematic structure in his cognition.
"Its poison gland structure is extremely intricate,"
Hayek pointed to a green sac-like object inside the scorpion’s tail:
"It can simultaneously generate three different toxins, adjusting the proportion according to the traits of its prey. If you observe carefully, you’ll find an organ similar to a ’memory organ’ inside the poison gland, storing resistance information of different creatures."

chapters.title: Chapter 235 - 168: "Insight" Trait (2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 235: Chapter 168: "Insight" Trait (2)
This discovery greatly surprised Ron. He couldn’t help but raise his hand to ask a question, an inappropriate action that drew sidelong glances from other contestants.
Under the strict hierarchy of the School, apprentices typically should not interrupt a Master’s lecturing.
"Do you have a question, Apprentice Ralph?" However, Hayek was not angry; instead, he showed a hint of curiosity.
"May I ask, sir, if this kind of ’memory unit’ is related to their feeding behavior?"
Ron inquired cautiously, his eyes sparkling with a thirst for knowledge:
"I noticed that the Scorpion seems to prioritize weaker targets when it attacks, is it because it can extract information from its prey, forming some kind of biological memory database?"
This question made Hayek’s eyes flash with admiration:
"A very keen observation! Indeed, Abyssal creatures generally have the ability to acquire information through predation. When the Scorpion devours its prey, it not only digests its flesh and blood but also absorbs some life information, storing it in this special tissue."
The Vice President began to dissect the poison gland more meticulously, showing the apprentices its internal structure:
"That is also why many Abyssal creatures are relatively vulnerable when they first encounter unfamiliar prey but can quickly find the most effective attack method upon the second encounter. They can ’learn’ the weaknesses and resistances of prey, continually evolving their attack strategies."
Subsequently, during further dissection, Hayek continued to showcase more of the Scorpion’s extraordinary organ structures:
"The skeletal structure of the Scorpion is infused with various minerals, related to special elements in the Abyssal environment."
"Its nervous system presents a distributed network, rather than being concentrated in the head. This design is meant to enhance its survival capabilities in battle."
Meanwhile, Ron occasionally raised questions that hit the mark, demonstrating an astonishing understanding of extraordinary biological structures:
