The room was spacious and solemn inside, with a massive crystal platform at the center, surrounded by energy control columns of various shapes.
At each corner of the room stood a gray-robed recorder, holding a special recording device used specifically for measuring and recording spiritual power fluctuations.
Soron Griffiths was already waiting inside, along with two other mentors Ron wasn’t very familiar with.
Among them was a short but sharp-eyed elderly woman, and the other was a middle-aged man with a metal eyepatch over his left eye.
"Ron Ralph." Soron stepped forward, his tone calm and formal:

chapters.title: Chapter 264 - 178: Returnee from the Abyss (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 264: Chapter 178: Returnee from the Abyss (Part 3)
"Today we will officially test your spiritual power level and magic control ability to confirm whether you meet the standard of an Advanced Apprentice."
"Thank you for your arrangement, Lord Griffith." Ron bowed slightly, his voice steady.
Soron briefly introduced to his two colleagues: "This is Master Mariana Hall, responsible for spiritual power theoretical research; and this is Master Drake Anson, responsible for magic stability testing."
The two masters nodded in acknowledgment, their eyes carrying a scrutinizing gaze.
Mariana seemed particularly curious about this young Advanced Apprentice candidate, her old but bright eyes seeming to see through Ron’s every thought.
"First is the basic spiritual power measurement."
Soron pointed to the central crystal platform: "Please stand on it and release your spiritual power, letting it flow naturally."
Ron stepped onto the crystal platform, took a deep breath, closed his eyes, and began to release his spiritual power.
As his spiritual power gradually unfolded, the crystal platform began to emit a soft blue glow, which became increasingly bright, eventually forming a bright energy ball that encapsulated Ron entirely.
The recorders in the four corners of the room immediately became busy, the instruments in their hands emitting slight buzzing sounds as they recorded various parameters of spiritual power.
"Spiritual power scale reached 4.2... This already exceeds the Advanced Apprentice standard line."
Mariana Hall commented in surprise: "Moreover, the purity and stability are quite excellent, with almost no impurities or fluctuations."
Soron nodded, seemingly unsurprised by this result:
"Next is the magic control test. Ron, please demonstrate three spells that you have mastered well, particularly paying attention to the stability and precision of energy flow."
Ron began to demonstrate his spells one by one: Sound Wave Vibration, Slime Splash, and Ring of Brilliance.
But unlike ordinary casting, he deliberately slowed down the construction process during the demonstration, allowing the three masters present to clearly observe each step of energy flow and magic structure.
"Look at this magic construction process."
Drake Anson commented softly, raising his brow slightly under the metallic eyepatch:
"The position of each energy node is precise to an incredible degree, this level of control... is more like an experienced Magic Constructor than an Apprentice."
"The most surprising thing is the thought network structure he formed."
Mariana added:
"Most apprentices, when first reaching the standard of Advanced Apprentices, have thought networks that are often sparse and fragile, taking years to consolidate and encrypt. But his network... is already quite dense and sturdy."
When Ron completed the demonstration of the Ring of Brilliance, the entire room was bathed in warm golden-red light.
Under his control, the ring changed shapes, from a simple circle to a shield, and then to a glowing longsword, each transformation smooth and precise, without any energy leakage.
A hint of appreciation flashed in Soron’s eyes:
"This magic usually can only maintain a fixed form, yet you seem to have endowed it with a high degree of malleability."
The test lasted nearly half an hour, and in addition to basic magic, Ron also demonstrated, upon request, his fine control over spiritual power.
"Alright, the test is concluded."
Soron finally announced, after a brief exchange with the other two masters, turning to Ron:
"Apprentice Ralph, based on today’s test results, we unanimously believe you have reached, or even surpassed, the standards of an Advanced Apprentice."
He took out an official certification document, signed his name on it, and handed it to the other two masters for confirmation:
"From today onwards, you officially become an Advanced Apprentice of the Black Mist School. This means you will receive more resources and permissions, as well as increased expectations and responsibilities."
"Thank you for the guidance and recognition from all masters."
Ron respectfully accepted the document stamped with the seals of the three, feeling a surge of satisfaction inside.
When the two masters prepared to leave, Drake Anson suddenly stopped and turned to Ron:
"Young man, your Ring of Brilliance is somewhat special. That kind of light flame trait... is not an effect that ordinary Fire Elemental magic can achieve. Have you performed some modification?"
Ron cautiously nodded: "Yes, Lord Anson. I attempted a special fusion of the Light Element and Fire Element, creating a more stable and malleable composite energy form."
Drake nodded slightly, the metallic eyepatch glinting coldly in the light:
"An interesting direction. Magic modification is a necessary path to becoming an Official Wizard, and you seem to have already taken the first step."
After the two masters and several recorders left, only Ron and Soron remained in the room.
Soron’s expression became more relaxed than before:
"Your performance is impressive, Ron. Especially that kind of precise control over spiritual power, which is top-tier even among Advanced Apprentices."
Ron humbly lowered his head: "This is thanks to your careful guidance, Lord Griffith."
Soron shook his head, a complicated light flashing in his eyes:
"No, this is your own talent and effort. I merely provided some direction."
He hesitated slightly, as if considering whether to say the next words:
"Ron, I think you should know, the sequence’s quarterly evaluation will soon take place."
"Yes, my lord, I am preparing for it."
"With your current achievements—holding dual roles as an Advanced Apprentice and Bloodline Modifier, in addition to your performance in the gladiatorial arena, you have a great chance of securing a spot in the top ten or even top five."
Soron’s voice was low and cautious: "This means you will be almost guaranteed a spot at the Bloodline Altar."
Ron’s heart beat slightly faster, but outwardly he remained calm:
"That would be a great honor."
Soron’s eyes became deeper:
"The Bloodline Altar... is a double-edged sword. It can bring great enhancement but is equally fraught with risks. Many have entered, but have not emerged as they were."
Ron could sense the hint and concern in Soron’s words, which surprised him a bit.
All along, Soron had given him the impression of a businesslike, serious master who rarely showed personal emotions.
"I will heed your advice, Lord Griffith."
Ron responded sincerely: "Whether it is researching Abyss creature samples or participating in the Bloodline Altar, I will maintain the necessary caution."
Soron seemed satisfied with this answer, nodding gently:
"Very well. Wisdom lies not only in the pursuit of knowledge but also in knowing when to stop."
This statement was almost identical to what Master Maxim had said earlier, sending a jolt through Ron’s heart.
The fact that two senior Wizards had coincidentally given the same warning might not be a coincidence.
"Lastly, regarding the sequence evaluation meeting."
Soron’s expression returned to formality: "I will do my utmost to secure the position you deserve; your talent deserves more recognition."
Ron nodded in gratitude: "Thank you for your support, Lord Griffith."
Leaving the Central Tower, his mood was exceptionally complex.
On the one hand, he felt some satisfaction with today’s dual certification success;
On the other hand, the warnings from Maxim and Soron made him reassess his research direction and progress.
The sunset light spilled over his shoulders as Ron looked at the two certification documents in his hands:
Advanced Apprentice and Bloodline Modifier, without a doubt, he once again took a big step closer to becoming a true Wizard.

chapters.title: Chapter 265 - 179: Dust Settles
chapters.content:
Chapter 265: Chapter 179: Dust Settles
Lily adjusted her apprentice robe, ensuring each crease was smooth and orderly.
"I must complete the mentor’s task well..." the young girl murmured to herself in front of the mirror.
Ron had already instructed her the day before to fulfill the important agreement with Lady Allen on his behalf.
He himself was too busy attending the quarterly meeting of the Candidate Wizard sequence to visit in person.
Lily placed the specially crafted box containing precious materials into a storage pouch, and after double-checking the list, she left the workshop.
The morning’s dim light pierced through the year-round mist of Black Mist Jungle, casting a hazy silver edge on the path.
She adjusted her collar again, took a deep breath, and headed toward Lady Allen’s Magic Pharmacy.
This was her first solo trip since becoming Ron’s apprentice; though she was very familiar with the route, there was still a bit of nervousness in her heart.
The road to Lady Allen’s Herb Store wasn’t far, but it required passing through the Candidate Apprentice Area.
This was where Lily had briefly stayed in the past and was the starting point of her escape from the Intermediate Apprentice who coveted her.
As she swiftly walked through the main path of the Candidate Apprentice Area, several familiar faces caught her attention.
They were a few former Candidate Apprentices who had been in the same cohort as her, gathered together in quiet conversation.
Upon seeing Lily, their eyes immediately locked onto the shiny Elementary Apprentice Badge on her chest.
"Is that... Lily?" a tall, thin boy muttered in surprise, "She’s already become an Elementary Apprentice?"
"I heard she’s now working in the workshop of that talented Advanced Apprentice, Ron Ralph, as his private assistant."
Another girl bit her lip, her eyes flashing with envy.
Their whispers weren’t intentionally hidden; Lily could clearly hear every word.
This was in stark contrast to the contemptuous and skeptical looks she had received upon previously arriving at the Candidate Area.
As she approached, these Candidate Apprentices suddenly became exceptionally respectful, even parting to make way for her.
"G-good morning, Senior Lily."
A noble lady who had previously ignored her even cautiously greeted her, her voice full of apprehension.
Lily nodded slightly in acknowledgment, her heart swirling with complex emotions.
She had never been someone who took pride in her elevated status, but now she had to admit that the stark contrast brought by a rise in status truly was satisfying.
"Is this the benefit of being attached to the powerful?"
She questioned herself, then shook her head to dismiss the thought:
"No, my current position is earned through my own efforts. The mentor already said, he merely gave me the opportunity, not charity."
Passing through the Candidate Dormitory Area, she soon arrived at Lady Allen’s Herb Store.
The familiar shop still exuded that unique herbal scent, and the wind chime at the door gently swayed, producing a crisp sound.
As she pushed open the door, Lily felt a bit anxious.
To her, Lady Allen was both a mentor and the first person to provide her shelter.
"Come in, don’t just stand at the door."
A familiar husky voice called from inside the shop.
Lady Allen was sitting behind the counter, busying herself with some herbs, her piercing green eyes as sharp as ever.
"Good day, ma’am," Lily greeted softly as she approached the counter.
"Seems that brat didn’t have time to see me and sent you, this little girl, instead."
Lady Allen put down the pestle, inspecting the young girl in front of her: "I must say, you’ve changed quite a bit following him."
Lily felt as if those eyes could see through her soul, causing her to slightly lower her head, avoiding direct eye contact.
"Carrying Ron’s magic power trace."
The old woman sniffed: "Seems that kid’s taught you plenty. An Elementary Apprentice Badge, already? How long has it been? Three months? Four months?"
"Four months and seven days, ma’am," Lily answered softly.
"Alright, stop pretending."
Lady Allen waved impatiently, but a gentle light flickered in her eyes: "Have a seat, the tea’s in the usual spot, pour it yourself."
Lily adeptly walked to the corner table, pouring a cup of hot tea for both herself and Lady Allen.
This was a habit she formed while working here; whenever Lady Allen grew tired of reading or potion-making, she would always prepare a cup of warm tea.
"The mentor asked me to bring all the materials you needed."
Lily sat opposite Lady Allen and took out the meticulously packaged box:
"Along with his greetings and thanks."
Lady Allen ignored the latter half of the sentence, merely raising an eyebrow: "All of them? He’s collected them all?"
Lily nodded and carefully opened the box.
Inside, the remaining three rare ingredients were arranged neatly, each sealed in special containers to maintain optimal condition.
"Night Talk Pollen"—a powder produced by flowers that bloom only on the full moon night, emitting a faint silver glow, said to allow the dead to briefly speak their final memories.
"Dream-Eating Spider’s Eye Fluid"—a semi-transparent milky white liquid, from a special spider species on the second layer of the Abyss, capable of letting the user see scenes from another’s dreams.
And the last, also the most precious and rare: "Illusion Songbird’s Throat Bone."
This nearly extinct bird’s throat bone could imitate any sound and transform sound waves into special spiritual waves.

chapters.title: Chapter 266 - 179: Dust Settles (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 266: Chapter 179: Dust Settles (Part 2)
When Lady Allen saw the final material, a clear look of astonishment appeared in her eyes:
"The Illusion Songbird’s Throat Bone? This thing is nearly extinct in the Black Mist Jungle region. Where did he get it from?"
"He probably acquired it through contacts with Magnus Master and the Alchemist Association."
Lilia replied softly, "Teacher has been gathering these materials through various channels for some time now."
Lady Allen snorted lightly through her nose, but a trace of satisfaction flickered in her deep green eyes:
"That boy has never let me down..."
Her voice was so soft it was almost as if she was only speaking to herself, then she raised her head to look at Lilia:
"How have you been doing by his side? Have you achieved your intended goal?"
Lilia was startled, uncertain what Lady Allen meant.
Was she referring to her escaping Keynes’s predicament? Or the possible relationship between her and Ron?
She recalled she had never explicitly stated her "goal" to Lady Allen.
"I... I think I’ve basically achieved it."
Thinking of this, she lowered her head and stammered:
"The teacher has been good to me, giving me the opportunity to learn and providing a safe and comfortable living environment."
Lady Allen gave her a meaningful look, seemingly reading more into her words, but did not pursue the topic further.
Lilia glanced around, suddenly noticing changes in the familiar shop:
"Madam, what about Fina? I haven’t seen her."
"Oh, that girl, I’ve sent her away."
Lady Allen waved her hand nonchalantly:
"I’ve assigned her to the Alchemist Association branch of the school, where she’s now responsible for some basic potion refining tasks."
"Do you mean... she was transferred from here..." Lilia was a bit surprised, then cautiously used a neutral term.
"Heh, she was simply eliminated by me, not everyone is suited to stay here with me."
Lady Allen stood up, leaning on her cane, her voice turning a bit cold:
"She has decent talent in Magic Potion Making, and her technical accumulation isn’t an issue, but she lacks necessary... determination and adaptability."
Lilia couldn’t help but think of Fina’s always cautious nature; Lady Allen’s assessment didn’t seem incorrect.
"Elimination..." she murmured softly to herself.
Fina’s talent was clearly enough to support her future as a Professional Alchemist, which was why she had gone to great lengths to please her back then.
If someone like her was eliminated, what standards did Lady Allen have?
Upon realizing this, she suddenly became aware of something...
"Um, Lady Allen." Lilia gathered the courage to ask: "Is teacher... the only student you recognize?"
Lady Allen glanced at her, the sharpness of her gaze making Lilia feel a surge of tension.
"That boy indeed has many unusual traits."
The old woman smirked, speaking slowly: "But nothing is absolute. Perhaps one day, I might meet a student better than him, who knows?"
Her words sounded somewhat perfunctory, but Lilia keenly noticed the look of pride in Lady Allen’s eyes as she spoke.
"Don’t overthink it." Lady Allen seemed to see through her thoughts:
"This world has never been equal. Some people are meant to reach the top, while others are better suited for foundational work. Fina is doing well at the association too, much better than always being scolded by me here."
"Alright, enough reminiscing, let’s get down to business."
As she spoke, she pulled out two items from a drawer:
A delicate black sealed box and an envelope shimmering with faint silver light.
Complex protective runes were engraved on the sealed box, each line intricately designed, forming a perfect sealing array;
While the envelope was shrouded in a layer of magic barrier, with runes faintly circulating on its surface.
That was a self-destruct mechanism. If anyone attempted to forcibly open it, its contents would immediately turn to ash.
"I’ve already verified the materials, now you hand these over to him."
Lady Allen handed the two items to Lilia:
"Tell him, the final stage of ’Star Eater’s Ravings’ is extremely dangerous, and he shouldn’t attempt it lightly without sufficient preparation."
Lilia carefully took these two precious items, feeling a heavy sense of responsibility:
"I will deliver them to the teacher as they are."
"And..." Lady Allen hesitated, uncharacteristically showing an uncertain expression:
"Tell him, the path I couldn’t finish back then, I hope he can walk it to the end."
Lilia nodded in agreement, although she didn’t quite understand the meaning of this statement, she could feel the strong regret contained within it.
The old woman suddenly extended her calloused hand, gently caressing Lilia’s cheek:
"You, girl, are not bad either. Compared to Fina, who already had decent talent, your growth makes me feel even more gratified."
This unexpected tenderness left Lilia stunned in place, not knowing how to react for a moment.
As she spoke, Lady Allen pulled out another parchment scroll, its seal much less stringent than that of the box:
"I suppose you still don’t have any meditation techniques other than the Basic Meditation Technique, right? This is a gem-level meditation method I used during my apprenticeship. Though it’s not as powerful as the set I gave that boy, it excels in being consistently stable."
Gem Level Meditation Method?
Lilia had indeed been troubled by this matter before. She and Ron had agreed to find a chance to purchase a set from other masters, suitable for apprentice stages only.

chapters.title: Chapter 267 - 179: When the Dust Settles (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 267: Chapter 179: When the Dust Settles (Part 3)
Currently, Lilya is still raising funds, and Ron has been paying her an assistant’s salary.
She already has a little treasury with over two hundred Magic Stone Fragments, but it’s still far from the basic Meditation Technique needed for advancement.
Unexpectedly, Lady Allen helped her resolve it directly?
"Alright, stop standing there stupidly."
The elderly woman resumed her usual sharp tone:
"Quickly take these things back to that brat. Remember, don’t let anyone see the box, and definitely don’t let anyone touch it."
"Yes, madam."
Lilya bowed deeply, carefully placing several items into her bag: "Thank you for all your help."
When leaving the Herb Store, the girl’s mood was complex and heavy.
Dark clouds gathered in the sky, seeming like it was going to rain again.
Lilya quickened her pace; the rain in Black Mist Jungle always carried a strange smell and prolonged exposure would make the skin itch.
Passing through the marketplace, she habitually looked around
Carrying such important items now, she had to be extra cautious.
Just as she was about to leave the market area, a figure suddenly entered her sight.
It was Ogg Keynes, an Intermediate Apprentice with past ill intent towards her, standing by the roadside with a few companions, laughing and chatting.
Lilya instinctively wanted to avoid him, but then calmed down, walking past them expressionlessly.
She was no longer that isolated Candidate Apprentice.
Keynes noticed her, a hint of surprise flashed in his eyes.
But soon returned to normal, even nodding slightly in greeting, his eyes seemingly carrying a hint of... respect?
He certainly wasn’t afraid of her, but of Ron standing behind her.
A rapidly rising Advanced Apprentice, who had gained widespread attention from the upper ranks of the School, a genius with dazzling achievements in various fields.
The clouds in the sky grew heavier, and distant thunder faintly resounded.
"Teacher will be very glad to receive these."
She whispered to herself, fingers grazed the wooden box tucked close, a smile surfaced on her lips.
The girl quickened her steps back, her mind held only one thought—return to the workshop, to the place which had truly become her home.
.........
Today, the conference hall at the Black Mist School Central Tower was exceptionally solemn and majestic.
Beneath the high dome, circular long tables were arranged in sequence, each seat had a nameplate engraved with a number.
In the center of the hall, a giant three-dimensional projection slowly rotated, displaying a complex pyramid-shaped structure—the Bloodline Altar’s three-dimensional model.
Ron wore a neat apprentice robe, adorned with the double emblem of Advanced Apprentice and Professional Alchemist on his chest.
This time, he arrived early at the venue, sitting quietly in his seat.
Fourteenth seat, this was his position after the last evaluation meeting.
Though it was already a quite good ranking, the gap with those higher seats at the front of the hall was still apparent.
People began arriving one after another, Chief Holt remained calm and steady as usual, nodding to Ron upon arrival.
Other sequence members arrived subsequently, each person’s face showing varying degrees of anticipation or nervousness.
Once the appointed time arrived, Vice President Hayek’s voice echoed in the hall:
"Now that everyone is here, let’s start the evaluation meeting."
He wore a deep purple robe, his chest decorated with a complex badge of office, looking stern and unapproachable.
"First, let’s confirm the two main topics of this meeting: the allocation of Bloodline Altar slots opening in a month, and filling the vacant seats following Oliver and Cynthia’s defection."
The whispering in the conference hall instantly fell silent.
The Bloodline Altar and rank shifts, these topics were enough to make any sequence member hold their breath.
"Regarding the Bloodline Altar," Hayek continued:
"As per official notification from the Crystal Tower, we, Black Mist School, have five slots as usual. Considering the altar’s traits and risks, participants must possess sufficient strength and compatibility."
His gaze swept over each of the sequence members present, lingering a bit longer on some.
His eyes seemed to assess everyone, as though evaluating something.
"First, let’s address some necessary procedural issues.
Regarding Oliver West and Cynthia Novik’s defection, the School has established a special investigation team, now formally announcing their removal from the Candidate Wizard sequence."
A murmur rose in the hall, but soon quieted down again.
Hayek continued: "The vacant sequence seats will be filled based on the latest evaluation. Now, let’s move on to the main topic—the adjustment of sequence rankings."
He gestured, the Crystal Ball in the center of the hall emitted a gentle light, projecting a transparent ranking list.
The list displayed each member’s name, current ranking, and various evaluation indicators.
"Based on this quarter’s comprehensive performance, the top five positions in the sequence remain unchanged:
Holt Elvin remains in the first place, Herbert Levin and Caitlin Gardner maintain second and third places respectively."
The result was expected, Holt’s strength had always been far ahead in the entire sequence, no one questioned his chief position.
However, the subsequent ranking adjustments drew the entire room’s attention.
"Due to recent performance and achievements, Ron Ralph will be promoted from the fourteenth to the sixth position, directly taking over the original seat of the defector Oliver."

chapters.title: Chapter 268 - 179: When the Dust Settles (Part 4)
chapters.content:
Chapter 268: Chapter 179: When the Dust Settles (Part 4)
This decision was like a stone cast into a calm lake, immediately causing ripples.
Surprised whispers filled the hall, with many eyes focused on Ron.
An eight-level leap! This is almost unheard of in the history of the School.
Hayek seemed to expect this reaction and added:
"This decision is based on multiple objective criteria, including but not limited to:
Recent outstanding performance in the Bloody Gladiatorial Games, formal acquisition of the Bloodline Modifier certification, and successful passage of the Advanced Apprentice certification.
Additionally, strong recommendations were provided by both Master Soron and Master Yuni."
Ron’s expression remained calm, though he felt a slight joy in his heart.
This significant progression in ranking is not only recognition of his efforts but also a crucial step toward entering the Bloodline Altar.
"Furthermore," Hayek continued, "Trish Lind has been promoted from tenth place to seventh place, right after Apprentice Ralph."
Though Trish’s leap is not as astonishing as Ron’s, it is still quite remarkable.
Ron looked towards the brown-haired girl, meeting her gaze filled with complex emotions.
There was joy, admiration, and a faint trace of competitiveness.
Hayek then announced several other ranking adjustments, mostly minor ascensions or descensions, causing no significant stir.
"The above are the main changes in this quarter’s sequence ranking,"
Hayek concluded, "Please adjust your seats according to the new ranking."
Ron stood up and walked to the seat representing sixth place—Oliver’s former position.
As he sat down, he could feel the gazes from all directions.
But he was already accustomed to such attention.
Ever since becoming an Elementary Apprentice, every step of his progress had been accompanied by various speculations and discussions.
These external voices could no longer shake him.
Once everyone was seated according to the new ranking, Hayek moved to the second topic of the meeting—distribution of spots for the Bloodline Altar.
"In one month, the Bloodline Altar will open again. This is a rare opportunity for participants to deeply comprehend and enhance their bloodline potential."
Hayek’s voice became more solemn:
"According to the agreement with the Crystal Tower, we have obtained five participation spots this time.
Considering various factors, the School has decided to allocate these spots as follows:
One seat each goes to the top three, Holt Elvin, Herbert Levin, and Caitlin Gardner, with the remaining two spots given to Ron Ralph and Trish Lind."
This allocation plan immediately caused some dissatisfaction.
Especially among the two Advanced Apprentices who were directly skipped over despite being ranked fourth and fifth, their expressions visibly darkened.
However, since it was a decision made by many mentors and the vice-dean, these apprentices naturally dared not complain.
The status gap between Apprentices and Official Wizards is distinctly pronounced.
No one dared to oppose at this time; anyone seated in this hall was certainly no fool.
"Alright, the allocation of spots is settled."
Seeing everything finalized, Hayek looked around the hall:
"The five apprentices who received spots, please stay after the meeting, as we need to provide some important information and guidance regarding the Bloodline Altar."
The meeting proceeded to discuss some internal affairs of the School and external threats, mainly regarding the latest intelligence and defense measures related to the Eye of the Abyss organization.
After the quarterly meeting officially ended, other apprentices gradually left, leaving only the five who received spots for the Bloodline Altar and a few mentors.
"Congratulations on gaining this rare opportunity."
Hayek walked up to the five, with a rare warmth in his voice:
"The Bloodline Altar is not only an opportunity to enhance oneself but also an important investment from the School in you."
Soron stepped forward, adding:
"While the Bloodline Altar is full of opportunities, it also carries risks. Throughout history, many apprentices encountered accidents within, sometimes even losing their lives. Therefore, thorough preparation and a cautious attitude are extremely important."
His gaze paused on Ron for a moment, eyes showing an indescribable complexity:
"Especially you, Apprentice Ralph. As a Bloodline Modifier, your expertise will be a crucial pillar for the team."
Ron nodded in acknowledgment: "I will do my best to ensure the team’s safety and success."
After the meeting, as everyone else had dispersed, Hayek suddenly called out to Ron:
"Apprentice Ralph, come with me for a moment."
Ron was a bit puzzled, but quickly followed in Hayek’s footsteps.
Hayek led Ron to a quiet little room and, after ensuring no disturbances, began speaking:
"I’ve been observing your progress, Apprentice Ralph. Your growth rate is remarkably fast, and you have the rare development of versatility, which is very impressive."
Ron cautiously responded: "It’s all thanks to the excellent environment the School provides and the guidance from all the mentors."
Hayek smiled slightly: "False humility means nothing to me. You and I both know your achievements primarily stem from your own talent and effort."
He took out a Recording Crystal from inside his robe, on which floated a complex Magic Model:
"I have here a Magic Model that might suit you now."
Ron accepted the Crystal Ball, sensing the intricate structure of the recorded magic within.

chapters.title: Chapter 269 - 180: Flowing Shield Wall
chapters.content:
Chapter 269: Chapter 180: Flowing Shield Wall
Hayek took a Crystal Ball from inside his robe, which emitted a peculiar halo in the dim room.
The intricate structure of the internal Magic Model resembled a precisely crafted three-dimensional maze, causing Ron to gaze in breathless attention.
"These are two quite mature Magic Models, both results of my research during my younger years."
Hayek softly said, his tone devoid of any emotional fluctuation, as if merely stating a simple fact:
"As a rapidly growing Advanced Apprentice, you need a more diverse Magic System."
He pointed to the Magic Model on the left inside the Crystal Ball, a complex structure interwoven with various Elemental Energies, resembling a constantly rotating vortex:
"Hybrid Elemental Missile—a highly malleable advanced Attack Magic. With each Elemental Attribute fused, its power and Penetration Power will increase significantly, but the difficulty of control also grows exponentially."
Hayek’s finger gently brushed across the surface of the Crystal Ball, and the model responded immediately, displaying the effects of different elemental combinations:
"The most basic dual-element combinations, like fire and wind, can produce a high-temperature cutting effect; fire and earth form explosive impact;
more complex multi-element fusions can even create various special state composite attacks."
In these demonstrations, Ron could clearly see the subtle relationships of mutual catalysis and counteraction between elements.
This was completely consistent with the theory he learned in "Elemental Guidance Basics," yet the practical application was far more intricate and complex than the theory.
"With your current Spiritual Control precision, you can manage at most two elements simultaneously, which is already sufficient for most situations."
Hayek calmly evaluated.
Then, he pointed to the Magic Model on the right, which was an even more densely complex energy grid structure, presenting a semi-transparent shield:
"Flowing Shield Wall—unlike an ordinary Shield, it requires a specific medium for Casting, and the strength of the Shield Wall generated directly correlates to the Traits of the medium."
The model in the Crystal Ball transformed, demonstrating the effects of using different media:
"A Shield Wall formed from ordinary water possesses substantial flexibility and can absorb impacts;
Metal Powder provides higher physical defense;
and certain special materials, like Crystal Stone Powder, can even grant the Shield Wall the ability to resist specific energy attacks."
Ron noted that this Magic Model’s energy structure appeared more precise and adaptable.
The energy distribution points were numerous, each capable of independent adjustment, endowing the entire spell with astonishing adaptability.
"When Spiritual Control precision is sufficiently high, the Shield Wall can be shaped, turning it into a semi-solid tool, which not only defends but can also entrap enemies or create temporary passages and platforms."
Hayek spoke with pride:
"I once used this spell to fend off a swarm attack in the ’Sea of Eternal Night’ on the Abyss Fifth Layer; using a special metal as the medium, I formed a completely enclosed protective sphere, successfully safeguarding the entire exploration team."
Ron carefully weighed the two options.
He already had a fair amount of Attack Magic, from the initial Sound Wave Vibration to the Ring of Brilliance, along with the Erosion Chapter he was currently studying, forming a relatively complete attack system.
However, his means of Defense were significantly lacking, especially with the upcoming journey to the Bloodline Altar.
Moreover, speaking of rare materials, he now possessed a treasure like Soul Steel, whose remarkable malleability undoubtedly aligned perfectly with "Flowing Shield Wall."
After consideration, he made his decision: "I choose Flowing Shield Wall, sir."
Hayek nodded slightly, seemingly unsurprised by this choice:
"The importance of Defense often only reveals itself at critical moments. Particularly in environments filled with unknown variables such as the Bloodline Altar, an extra line of defense can mean an extra chance of survival."
The Magic Model on the right side of the Crystal Ball enlarged, becoming more distinct, with each Energy Node and Flow Path more prominent:
"The basic construction of the Flowing Shield Wall is relatively simple, but its essence lies in precise energy distribution and medium interaction. Initially, you might only maintain a planar shield, but as your proficiency increases, you can shape more complex forms."
Ron memorized every detail of this Magic Model.
Such direct transmission of a Magic Model is a priceless Treasure to any Apprentice, allowing a bypass of the painstaking process of self-exploration, significantly shortening the mastery time.
Moreover, the other party didn’t specify that he could only obtain one Magic Model; perhaps in the future, he could consider offering other compensation to exchange with Hayek for the "Hybrid Elemental Missile" he also greatly coveted.
"Speaking of the Bloodline Altar..." Hayek’s voice suddenly became deeper, and his eyes turned profound:
"Since you’ve chosen the ’Abyssal Creatures Atlas,’ you have already embarked on the path of exploring the Abyss’s essence. This is good, as the connection between the Bloodline Altar and the Abyss is much closer than most people imagine."
Ron instantly felt the deep meaning in the deputy head’s words, and his breathing unconsciously slowed down, like an explorer standing at the entrance of an unknown cavern.
"Most people think the Bloodline Altar is merely a special trial site, but in reality, its essence is far more complex."
Hayek’s voice lowered, his eyes reflecting deep brilliance:
"The Bloodline Altar is actually a remnant trace of an ancient Sorcerer King’s world conquest."
Ron’s brow furrowed slightly: "A remnant trace of world conquest?"

chapters.title: Chapter 270 - 180: Flowing Shield Wall_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 270: Chapter 180: Flowing Shield Wall_2
"To be precise, it’s the collision afterimage produced when the Witch King forcibly pulled the world he had conquered into our world."
Hayek explained:
"Integrating dimensions is no easy task. At the moment the two worlds collided, the dimensional turbulence tore apart the space structure, resulting in only part of the conquered world successfully integrating, while the scattered remnants are what we now know as the Bloodline Altar."
A rare worry flashed in Hayek’s eyes:
"What’s worse is that over time, this afterimage has resonated with the Abyss, and certain areas have been tainted by Abyssal Power, bearing obvious Abyssal Traits."
A flash of insight crossed Ron’s mind:
"So the trials at the Bloodline Altar are essentially a preview of Abyss exploration?"
"You’re not wrong." Hayek confirmed without reservation:
"In fact, all wizards aspiring for higher realms, whether from the Crystal Tower in the Central Lands or the Black Mist School on the fringe, ultimately cannot avoid the hurdle of Abyss exploration. It’s only there one can find the key to breaking through the existing rules and limitations."
Ron’s thoughts flashed back to the terrifying Silver Scales Maxim had shown a while ago, the permanent imprint and warning left by the Abyss.
Yet, even in the face of such risks, wizards seem unable to resist the temptation of the Abyss—this in itself is enough to demonstrate its allure.
"In the Bloodline Altar, you will face threefold challenges."
Hayek continued, his voice carrying a warning:
"The contamination and curses of Abyssal Power, the vengeful spirits and wraiths of the conquered world, and the anomalies of the dimensional turbulence itself. These often intertwine to form an unpredictable and dangerous situation."
Ron’s brain worked at high speed, trying to integrate this new information with the known theories of the Abyss.
Maxim’s warnings, and the seemingly mysterious descriptions in the Abyssal Creatures Atlas, were now forming a clearer picture in his mind.
"I still have many questions, sir."
Ron couldn’t help but ask, "About the connection between the Abyss and the wizard’s path, and why—"
"Since you have chosen the Abyssal Creatures Atlas," Hayek interrupted him, lifting his hand with an undeniable authority in his tone:
"Then many answers should naturally be sought from it. Selwyn Audric is one of the few wizards who truly understands the nature of the Abyss and can retreat unscathed; his works are far more valuable than my scattered words as a latecomer."
The Vice Dean gave Ron a meaningful look:
"When you can truly understand the full content of that book, your understanding of the wizard’s path will ascend to a whole new level."
As the meeting was about to end, Hayek added a sentence, his tone containing a peculiar complex emotion:
"Remember, in the Bloodline Altar, team cooperation is not just a fancy concept. The allocation of those five positions is not done casually; each person carries specific duties and significance."
As Ron stepped out of the room, his mind surged with emotions, the joy of the Magic Model almost drowned by the weighty information about the Bloodline Altar.
An intense thirst for knowledge burned within him, but it was accompanied by caution and vigilance.
He had learned from Maxim’s painful experiences that Abyss exploration is no child’s play, and every step must be carefully verified, proceeding with caution.
In the hall, the other high-sequence members who had secured a spot were still talking, but they gradually quieted when they saw Ron approaching.
Holt stepped forward proactively, his usually stern face showing a rare hint of relaxation at this moment:
"When I saw you at the herb store a year ago, I never expected you could secure the sixth position in the sequence. It’s quite an astonishing achievement."
These words were both a compliment and a subtle reminder—any newly risen star would attract more attention and caution.
"Haha, it’s all thanks to the guidance of my predecessors, especially you and Soron the Master, and of course, my own Special Talent."
Ron was neither overly modest to the point of affectation, nor recklessly confident to the point of being off-putting.
Holt nodded slightly in acknowledgment of this answer:
"Speaking of which, I have successfully used the ’Heart of the Earth’ to reshape the Earth Elemental Golem, enhancing its overall combat power by at least thirty percent."
When he said this, a barely noticeable pride flashed in his eyes, a natural expression of accomplishment:
"This way, our combat capability in the Bloodline Altar will be more reliable."
Ron’s heart was moved, with Holt proactively mentioning team cooperation, aligning with Hayek’s earlier hint.
Clearly, the School preferred participants to form a harmonious whole, rather than acting individually.
"Your Earth Elemental Golem is one of the most powerful elemental constructs I’ve seen," Ron habitually engaged in some polite banter:
"Having such combat support indeed makes one feel much more assured."
After a brief conversation, Ron politely bid farewell to Holt, noticing Trish standing not far away.
"Looks like we’ll be companions again." Trish said as she approached.
Her voice carried a subtle complex emotion—both the joy of securing a position and a faint unease at Ron’s rapid rise as a "competitor."
Those brown eyes shimmered with an amber-like luster beneath the Magic Crystal Lamp, seemingly trying to see through Ron’s calm exterior thoughts.
"Yes, I hope we can support each other."

chapters.title: Chapter 271 - 180: Flowing Shield Wall (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 271: Chapter 180: Flowing Shield Wall (Part 3)
Ron calmly responded, then remembered something and took out a carefully sealed crystal bottle from his pocket:
"This is the last batch of Natural Affinity Potion, according to the formula we agreed upon before. All refined with the best materials, the effect should be far superior to the ordinary version."
Trish took the box, carefully opened it for a look, and showed a satisfied smile: "Thank you, the quality looks quite good."
She put the potion away but did not leave immediately, instead, after a slight hesitation, she spoke again:
"Actually, I have another request... regarding Li Yue."
Ron raised an eyebrow, somewhat surprised by the shift in topic:
"Your leopard woman?"
He recalled that silent and reticent alien race guard, who always stood behind Trish, shadowing her yet rarely speaking.
"Yes." Trish nodded, lowering her voice somewhat:
"During the Bloody Gladiatorial Games, Li Yue came into contact with the scorpion’s venom and managed to survive it, seemingly developing some resistance to that venom. I’ve tried to help her with preliminary bloodline modulation to enhance this trait, but the effect was not ideal."
She stepped closer and said softly:
"I hope you—a real Bloodline Modifier—could help. I suspect Li Yue has some sort of special hidden bloodline that requires more professional guidance to be activated."
A living case involving the activation of a special bloodline was exactly the practical material Ron urgently needed for his research.
"This is indeed an interesting topic."
Ron nodded, a glint of interest flashing in his eyes:
"I would be happy to provide assistance, as it would also accumulate more practical experience for my research."
"That’s great!" Trish showed obvious joy:
"Do you have time to go now? I live with my Master, and she has already given permission, so we can proceed directly to the residence."
When mentioning her Master, Trish’s expression turned subtle:
"Speaking of which, my relationship with Master Corina might be somewhat similar to the type you have with Lilia... a mentorship dynamic."
When she mentioned Lilia’s name, she furrowed her brows imperceptibly, an expression that was fleeting.
Were it not for Ron’s sensitivity to micro-expressions, he might not have noticed this subtle change.
"Just that our relationship might be more... formal. After all, she is my officially recognized Master, while Lilia is merely your apprentice."
There was a trace of deliberate understatement in Trish’s tone, as if emphasizing a certain distinction.
"I need to return to the workshop first to prepare some necessary tools and materials, and to consult related materials for some preparation. How about tomorrow?"
Ron said, already formulating a plan for the bloodline modulation of the leopard woman.
He had already done in-depth research on the scorpion’s venom gland’s properties, and how to merge it with a special bloodline was a highly challenging topic.
Trish gave him an address: "Tomorrow... I will be waiting for you in advance. To avoid unnecessary trouble, please do not mention this address to anyone else."
Before parting, she seemed to want to say something more but ended up only smiling lightly, then turned and left, leaving a faint fragrance lingering in the air.
......
Ron walked out of the Central Tower, took a deep breath, feeling the subtle relaxation of his lungs expanding.
The conversation with Trish lingered in his mind for a moment, but it was soon replaced by more urgent matters.
The bloodline modulation of the leopard woman Li Yue was indeed an interesting research topic and could provide precious practical material for his academic accumulation, but right now more important matters awaited him.
"The final stage meditation method prepared by Lady Allen..."
This thought stirred a mix of anticipation and unease in his heart.
The first stage of "Star Eater’s Ravings" had already given him an unprecedented power boost, and the second stage and final stage were bound to lead him into deeper realms of mystery.
But at the same time, the unusually cautious attitude of the other party also forced him to weigh the potential risks within it more heavily.
And then there was the "Abyssal Creatures Atlas"... following Hayek’s hint, he began to realize the book’s value far exceeded his imagination.
If it truly contained Selwyn Audric’s insights into the essence of the Abyss, it would be undoubtedly crucial preparation for the upcoming journey to the Bloodline Altar.
Thinking of this, Ron quickened his pace.
By the time he returned to the workshop, it was already nearing dusk.
The distant clouds were colored a brilliant orangish-red by the sunset, like flames burning on the horizon, bringing a fleeting touch of warm color to the shadow-covered forest.
As he pushed open the workshop’s door, a familiar, reassuring scent greeted him.
The fresh aroma of herbs, the warm scent of wood, and the faint smell of Ailan’s specially-made pastries were discernible.
"Master, you’ve returned!" Lilia’s voice came from the side; she seemed to have been waiting in the lobby.
Ron turned his head and saw the girl’s face filled with undisguised joy. She cherished a box in her hands dearly—the very exquisite black sealed box that Lady Allen had given her.
"I have completed your task, Master."
She quickly approached, respectfully offering the sealed box and a letter:
"Lady Allen instructed me to personally hand them to you."
Ron nodded, accepting the two items, feeling the peculiar energy fluctuations emanating from the black sealed box.
Even through the intricately designed seal, he could still sense the deep power within—an aura of mystery related to the essence of the starry sky.
"Did Lady Allen say anything else?" Ron inquired while checking the seal’s integrity.
Lilia nodded, her expression turning serious:
"Madam specifically warned that the final stage of ’Star Eater’s Ravings’ is extremely dangerous and not to be attempted without sufficient preparation."
She hesitated, seemingly recalling Lady Allen’s words:
"And... she mentioned that the path she couldn’t complete back then, she hopes you can reach its end successfully."
Hearing this, Ron was slightly taken aback, then fell into thought.
The hidden meaning behind these words couldn’t help but remind him of the complex emotion that flitted through Lady Allen’s eyes when he asked her before.
It seems Lady Allen had once attempted but stopped halfway due to some reason, perhaps... this is also connected to her unique condition?
"How does she look...?" Ron suddenly asked, his voice carrying a rare note of concern.
Lilia was slightly startled, then understood the content of her teacher’s inquiry:
"Madam appears the same as usual, even more spirited; additionally, when she mentions you, there’s a special kind of... pride in her eyes."
She said the last word lightly, yet Ron heard it distinctly.
He nodded gently, carefully storing the sealed box and letter:
"I understand. By the way, is everything normal at the workshop?"
Lilia swiftly switched to the role of assistant, reporting succinctly and orderly:
"Everything is proceeding according to plan, Master. Dale’s daily training has not paused, and she has mastered seventy percent of the new Water Elemental Technique; Ailan’s condition is also stable, she’s tending to the rare herbs in the garden; as for the workshop’s orders..."
She retrieved a meticulously compiled ledger from her pocket:
"All records are here, including every income and expenditure. Recently, several advanced apprentices have shown particular interest in your improved ’Awakening’ Potion, inquiring if they can purchase in bulk."
Ron took the ledger, quickly skimmed through it, and felt satisfied with Lilia’s management skills:
"Well done. Accept orders for the ’Awakening’ Potion but strictly control the output, limiting each customer to three bottles."
He set the ledger aside casually: "I have important research to conduct next. Do not disturb me unless in case of urgent matters."
Lilia nodded respectfully: "Understood, Master. I will arrange everything to ensure you are not disturbed."
Ron watched Lilia’s departing figure, secretly assessing this apprentice’s growth in his heart.
In just a few months, she had grown remarkably, not only advancing her skills in Magic Potion Making but also serving as the core gear that made the entire operational system work seamlessly.
Thinking of this, he quickened his steps.
When he returned to the workshop, the sky had already turned a vivid orange-red by the setting sun, bringing a brief warmth to the shadowed forest.
He pushed open the workshop door, and a familiar, comforting scent enveloped him.
The fresher fragrance of herbs, the warming aroma of wood, and the faint scent of Ailan’s special pastries could be faintly discerned.
"Master, you’re back!" Lilia’s voice came from the side, as she seemed to have been waiting in the hall.
Ron turned his head and saw the girl, unable to hide the joy on her face as she held a box reverently—it was the very exquisite black sealed box that Lady Allen had entrusted her with.
"I have completed your assignment, Master."
She quickly stepped forward, respectfully handing over the sealed box and letter:
"Lady Allen instructed me to personally give this to you."
Ron nodded, received the two items, and felt the peculiar energy emanating from the black sealed box.
"Did Lady Allen say anything else?" Ron asked, his voice holding a rare touch of concern.
Lilia’s voice came from the side, she seemed to be waiting in the hall the whole time with a barely concealed delight on her face:
Ron turned his head and saw the girl, unable to hide her delight. She was holding a box in her hands with great reverence—the very exquisite black sealed box that Lady Allen had given her.
"I already completed your commission, Master."
She quickly stepped forward, handing over the sealed box and a letter with both hands respectfully:
"Lady Allen asked me to give this to you personally."
Ron nodded, receiving both items and feeling the peculiar energy emanating from the black sealed box:
"Did Lady Allen have anything else to say?" Ron asked, his voice carrying an unusual note of concern.
Lilia seemed to hesitate slightly as she answered:
"Well, she did mention that you should be especially careful with the final stage of ’Star Eater’s Ravings,’ as it’s particularly dangerous. She wants you to be well-prepared for what lies at the end."
Ron listened to her words, a rare note of concern in his voice.
He was reminded of Lady Allen’s complex emotions that had briefly flashed across her face when she spoke of his journey ahead.
Looks like Lady Allen thinks it’s more than just a regular meditation technique...
He exhaled slowly, feeling a wave of eager anticipation mixed with anxiety course through him.
The first stage of "Star Eater’s Ravings" had already brought him unprecedented power, and the second and final stages were bound to lead him deeper into the mysterious realms of understanding.
Moreover, the other exceptional book, the "Abyssal Creatures Atlas"... With Hayek’s tip, he began to realize its value far exceeds his imagination.
If it truly holds Selwyn Audric’s insights into the essence of the Abyss, it would undoubtedly be essential preparation for the upcoming visit to the Bloodline Altar.
Thinking about this, Ron quickened his pace.
When he returned to the workshop, the sky was already a bright orange-red, like flames burning on the horizon, bringing a momentary warmth to the forest engulfed in shadow.
As he pushed open the workshop door, a familiar sense of comfort enveloped him.
The fresh scent of herbs, the warm presence of the wood, and the faint aroma of Ailan’s handcrafted pastries were all discernible.
"Teacher, you’re back!" Lilia’s voice came from the side, she seemed to have been waiting in the hall all along.
Ron turned his head, seeing the undisguised delight on the girl’s face, as she carefully held a box in her hands—the very exquisite black sealed box Lady Allen had entrusted her with.
"I have completed your commission, Teacher."
She quickly stepped forward, respectfully offering the sealed box and letter:
"Lady Allen insisted that I hand this to you personally."
Ron nodded and took the two items, feeling the peculiar energy emanating from the black sealed box.
Even as he checked the seal on the box, Ron was already contemplating his imminent research plan on the leopard woman’s mysterious bloodline modulation.
He had already conducted in-depth research into the scorpion’s poison gland characteristics, and finding a way to merge this with the special bloodline was an intriguing challenge.
Ron quickened his steps at the thought of this.
By the time he returned to the workshop, dusk was approaching.
The distant clouds were painted a vivid shade of orange-red by the sunset, like flames burning along the horizon, bringing a brief moment of warm color to the shadowed forest.
Opening the workshop door, a familiar and reassuring scent greeted him.
The fresh fragrance of herbs, the warm scent of the wood, and the faint aroma of Ailan’s special pastries wafted gently.
"Teacher, you’re back!" Lilia’s voice came from one side, and she seemed to have been waiting in the hall, with an unmistakable joy on her face, holding dear a box that Lady Allen had entrusted to her personally.
"I’ve already completed your task, teacher."
She hurriedly approached, dutifully handing over the sealed box and the letter:
"Madam Allen asked me to hand this to you personally."
Ron nodded and carefully took the items, sensing a peculiar energy emanating from the black sealed box related to the essence of the Abyss itself.
If it truly contained Selwyn Audric’s insight into the nature of the Abyss, it would undoubtedly be a crucial preparation for the upcoming journey to the Bloodline Altar.
Having absorbed this, Ron hastened his steps.
He returned to the workshop as the day approached dusk.
In the distance, the clouds were dyed a brilliant orange-red by the sunset, like flames burning along the sky’s edge, bringing a momentary warm hue to the jungle shrouded in shadows.
As he opened the workshop door, a familiar, reassuring scent enveloped him.
The fresh fragrance of herbs, the warmth of wood, and the faint scent of Ailan’s specially made pastries were discreetly discernible.
"Master, you’re back!" Lilia’s voice came from the side, and she seemed to have been waiting in the hall all along with barely contained excitement on her face, holding a box in her hands—none other than the exquisite black sealed box given to her by Lady Allen.
"I’ve completed your commission, Master."
She quickly stepped forward, respectfully handing over the sealed box and letter:
"Lady Allen asked me to personally deliver this to you."
Ron nodded, accepting the items and feeling the strange energy emanating from the intricately sealed black box.
"Did Lady Allen have anything else to say?" asked Ron, with an unusual hint of concern in his voice.
Lilia’s voice came from the side, and she seemed to have been waiting in the hall:
"Teacher, you’re back!"
Ron turned his head, seeing a girl with unmistakable delight on her face, holding the exquisite black sealed box given to her by Lady Allen, treating it with utmost care.
"I’ve completed your assignment, Master."
She quickly approached, respectfully handing over the sealed box and letter:
"Lady Allen insisted I hand this to you personally."
Ron nodded, taking the items in hand, feeling the strange energy waves emanating from the black sealed box, sensing a peculiar energy emanating from it.
"Did Lady Allen have anything else to say?" Ron asked, his voice tinged with rare concern.
She paused, as if remembering those words Lady Allen told her:
"And she said, whatever you do, make sure you’re well-prepared for the final stage of ’Star Eater’s Ravings,’ it’s especially dangerous if you’re not ready for it."
With that thought in mind, Ron picked up his pace.

chapters.title: Chapter 272 - 181: Soul Anchoring
chapters.content:
Chapter 272: Chapter 181: Soul Anchoring
Multiple protective arrays are set up here, not only to block external magic power fluctuations but also to prevent internal energy leakage.
He carefully disengaged the array and pushed the door open to step inside.
The room was softly lit, with a research table crafted from special materials at the center, and protective runes carved on the surrounding walls.
Ron placed the black sealed box and the letter aside and went straight to the sealed area to retrieve the heavy "Abyssal Creatures Atlas".
Since the intense mental shock last time, he had temporarily set aside reading this forbidden book.
But now, with his promotion to Advanced Apprentice and the acquisition of the Bloodline Altar qualification, he must quickly absorb more knowledge about the Abyss.
The pages slowly unfolded in his hands, and the animated text and images appeared once again before his eyes.
This time, he deliberately avoided the Chapters that might trigger intense spiritual waves, directly flipping to the section describing the intersection of the Abyss with the outside world.
"The intersection of the Abyss and the outside world is not a fixed physical boundary, but a gradient change in energy density..."
Ron read this passage carefully, his eyes flickering with focused light:
"Due to the ’Dimensional Great Voyage’ at the end of the Second Era, many otherworlds collided and merged with the Main World, thus creating countless exotic realms, and once they come into complete contact with the Main World, they inevitably get affected by this special energy gradient..."
As he delved deeper into the reading, Ron gradually connected these descriptions with Hayek’s explanations of the Bloodline Altar:
"The most famous exotic realm is the ’Bloodline Domain,’ a semi-independent space torn open by ancient wizards, generating a large number of smaller ’Bloodline Altars’. Here, bloodline potential is completely activated, and the essential form of life often reveals itself..."
"Bloodline Altar!" A trace of excitement flashed in Ron’s eyes.
Continuing to read further, the book detailed the traits of this "Bloodline Altar":
"Unlike the Abyss, the Bloodline Altar, as a type of exotic rift, is not an absolutely dangerous environment, but the trials it contains often exceed ordinary endurance capacity.
Each entrant will face the truth of their own bloodline, ancestral memories buried deep within genes will be awakened, forming various illusory or tangible challenges..."
"Most critically, the connection of the Bloodline Altar with the Abyss makes its internal environment highly sensitive to spiritual contamination.
Those who enter carrying spiritual contamination often trigger more dangerous mutation reactions..."
This warning made Ron furrow his brows.
He realized that before entering the Bloodline Altar, he must ensure his mental state is at its best, otherwise, he could fall into a dangerous situation during the trials.
The book continued:
"The trials of the Bloodline Altar usually consist of three stages:
The first stage is ’Recurrence,’ where the explorer will experience historical fragments of their own bloodline;
The second stage is ’Resonance,’ where bloodline energy begins to interact more deeply with the explorer;
The final stage is ’Transformation,’ where bloodline potential is fully released, and the explorer may undergo a fundamental enhancement..."
"However, not everyone can complete all three stages. Most explorers reach their limits by the first or second stage. Forcing through these limits often leads to catastrophic consequences..."
Ron memorized this information deeply, understanding why the School places such importance on the opening of the Bloodline Altar.
For any apprentice aspiring to walk the path of a wizard, this is a rare opportunity.
Not only to gain a deep understanding of the essence of one’s bloodline but also the possibility of achieving a qualitative leap.
However, this opportunity comes with enormous risks, and those who rashly attempt it may pay a painful price.
With his mental state relatively stable at the moment, Ron decided to continue exploring the content he was more curious about.
He first turned to the Chapter he had only read the beginning of last time: "Abyssal Materials and Rare Treasures," continuing from where he left off.
The book elaborately listed the unique materials of each Abyssal layer, not only describing their appearance and basic properties but also analyzing their "overwriting" effect on the laws of the Surface World:
The first and second layers’ "Blood Crystal" — a red crystal capable of automatically absorbing and storing life energy.
The book revealed that Blood Crystal is actually a manifestation of primal consciousness in the Abyss, "learning" the rules of the material world by absorbing life energy from surrounding creatures.
The third layer’s "Black Sand Essence" — a black crystallization compressed from countless micro life forms.
This material possesses astonishing space manipulation traits, capable of folding and twisting space at the microscopic level.
Moderate usage can create spatial bags or storage devices with capacities far exceeding their appearances, while large-scale usage can create short-range teleportation gates or spatial traps.
The fourth layer’s "Reshaping Resin" — a semi-transparent liquid extracted from ancient trees in the Twisted Jungle, displaying a constantly changing rainbow hue.
The most amazing trait of this material is its ability to blur the boundaries of life forms, allowing the user to temporarily acquire the traits or abilities of other creatures.
The book recorded that an alchemist used reshaping resin to craft the "Hundred Facets Hide," enabling the wearer to switch freely between different biological forms.
But the cost is equally terrifying — prolonged use leads to the user’s body and soul "forgetting" their original form, eventually becoming an amorphous biomass.
The fifth layer’s "Time Amber"...

chapters.title: Chapter 273 - 181: Soul Anchoring (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 273: Chapter 181: Soul Anchoring (Part 2)
And the later "Maze Crystal," "Soul Metal," "Void Fragment"...
As Ron read these contents, he couldn’t help but feel a surge of emotion.
The descriptions of these Abyssal Materials far exceeded any extraordinary material knowledge he had previously encountered, completely transforming his understanding of alchemy and magic’s essence.
The abyssal materials seemed not merely resources and tools, but a medium to directly manipulate the essence of reality.
Through them, a wizard sufficiently knowledgeable and skilled in the art could even briefly transcend the constraints of the universe’s established rules, achieving effects unimaginable by conventional magic.
But what intrigued Ron the most was the detailed analysis of the relationship between Black Wizards and the Abyss:
"The path of the Black Wizard is essentially a road leading closer to the essence of the Abyss.
The so-called ’Awakening’ is, in fact, the transformation of part of one’s existence into an abyssal form, thereby acquiring abilities that surpass conventional laws.
This is not merely a gain in power, but a fundamental transformation of one’s form of existence."
"The area below ’Maze Domain’ in the Abyss Sixth Layer has long been a hub of activity for various Black Wizard organizations.
These regions, due to the traits of ’Maze Turbulence,’ constantly restructure their spatial configuration, making it difficult for outsiders to locate and track them.
More importantly, the deeper regions of the Abyss are rich with deep chaos energy, an ideal place for Black Wizards conducting advanced awakening rituals."
"Particularly noteworthy is the ancient organization ’Eye of the Abyss.’
Unlike common Black Wizard groups, they do not pursue simple power accumulation; instead, they are dedicated to the grand design of ’abyssalizing’ the material world.
Through special rituals, they attempt to gradually weaken the boundaries between reality and the Abyss, with the ultimate goal of complete integration of both."
"The core creed of the ’Eye of the Abyss’ is ’Cognition is Reality’ — they believe that by altering the cognitive patterns of enough intelligent beings, they can fundamentally rewrite the foundational rules of reality.
Their missionaries predominantly infiltrate various academic institutions, using twisted knowledge and special spiritual influence techniques to gradually change the mindset of their contacts."
This description sent a chill down Ron’s spine.
The goal of the ’Eye of the Abyss’ was far grander and more terrifying than he had imagined, seeking not only power but reconstructing the entire reality.
The part that truly shook Ron was the book’s explicit correlation between the Abyss and the Path of the Great Wizard:
"Since the First Era, the path of progression for a Great Wizard has always been inseparably linked to the Abyss.
According to reliable records, every individual successfully promoted to Great Wizard has invariably undergone a ritual known as ’Abyssal Baptism,’ usually below the 7th Floor ’Soul Abyss.’"
The book specifically mentioned a key technique known as "Soul Anchoring," a core method mastered by all successful Great Wizards:
"The essence of Soul Anchoring is dividing and anchoring part of one’s soul to a specific object in the material world before entering the Abyss.
These objects are usually personal items with deep connections to the wizard, such as weapons, magic wands, or jewelry.
The anchored objects provide a ’reality reference point’ during the abyssal baptism, preventing the wizard from being completely assimilated by the Abyss."
"The highest-level Soul Anchoring can preserve a wizard’s core memory and personality even when their consciousness is eroded by the Abyss.
It allows them to ’reset’ themselves in critical moments, a vital safeguard for surviving the ritual."
Ron’s heartbeat accelerated, and he immediately thought of his "Melting Furnace Concept."
This description of Soul Anchoring bore an astonishing resemblance to his envisioned soul splitting and energy isolation techniques!
Moreover, the book also mentioned an advanced technique called "Pollution Transformation," which was almost the key component of his "Melting Furnace Concept":
"A few outstanding wizards have mastered a special technique that doesn’t simply block or remove abyssal contamination but transforms it into pure energy.
The core of this technique is creating an ’Energy Recycling System’ that channels abyssal contamination into a specific container or medium, undergoes a series of complex energy conversions, and ultimately ’purifies’ it into usable pure energy."
"Selwyn Audric himself is believed to have mastered the basic form of this technique, which is also key to his ability to survive for nearly a century in the Abyss while maintaining a clear mind.
His ’Transformation Furnace’—a specially designed alchemy device, is said to convert abyssal contamination into energy that extends life and enhances spells."
Ron closed the book, taking a deep breath, feeling a wave of dizziness.
The content of the "Abyssal Creatures Atlas" far exceeded his expectations, not only providing an incredibly rich source material for his study of Extraordinary Biology but also offering critical theoretical support and technical details for his "Melting Furnace Concept."
He even began to wonder if his encounter with this book was truly a coincidence.
This description of "Pollution Transformation" and "Soul Anchoring" aligned so perfectly with his independently conceived "Melting Furnace Concept" that it seemed almost unbelievable.
"This can’t just be a coincidence..." Ron murmured softly, his eyes gleaming with a contemplative light.
But what left Ron most uneasy was the content on the last page of the book—an epilogue seemingly added at random, with handwriting distinct from the main text, as if written later:
"If you’ve read this far, remember:
Knowledge will respond to the seeker, just as the Abyss will respond to the summoner.
I once thought I was studying the Abyss, until I realized the Abyss was ’studying’ me.
No matter your purpose, stay vigilant.
Because now, ’they’ already know of your existence.
——S. Audric"
Ron carefully closed the book and locked it in a specially designed rune security box.
The knowledge from the "Abyssal Creatures Atlas" was both exciting and unsettling, requiring him time to digest the information and integrate it with his own research and plans.
"Abyss..." he murmured to himself, his eyes flickering with complex reflections: "The perfect blend of danger and opportunity, or a meticulously designed trap?"
"Take it slow, one step at a time."
Ron whispered to himself encouragingly, his eyes glinting with determination, "Handle the tasks at hand first, then consider the more distant future."
He closed the book, his thoughts swirling like turbulent waves.
This information was undoubtedly crucial for the upcoming journey to the Bloodline Altar, but to fully understand its mysteries might require more clues.
Ron’s gaze fell on the black sealed box, which contained the final stage of the "Star Eater’s Ravings," possibly providing another piece of the puzzle he needed.
He took a deep breath, carefully returning the "Abyssal Creatures Atlas" to the storage box, then walked towards that mysterious sealed box.
Where his fingers touched, he could feel a peculiar energy fluctuation, a mysterious rhythm akin to the depths of the starry sky, both distant and profound, as if from the edge of the universe.
Ron recalled once again Lady Allen’s warning passed through Lilia: not to attempt rashly without sufficient preparation.
And that more meaningful statement: She had not been able to walk the path to the end, hoping he could reach its conclusion smoothly.
"Lady Allen..." Ron murmured softly: "What did you encounter on this path?"
He pondered for a moment, deciding to first check the magically sealed letter.
Carefully removing the letter, Ron noticed the runes covering its surface were lightly flowing, as if possessing their own life.
He knew the fundamental principles of this sealing magic — only the designated recipient could open it; any unauthorized attempt to read it would lead to the content’s self-destruction.
His spiritual power gently touched the envelope’s surface, and Ron could feel the magic inside "verifying" his identity.
Moments later, the runes suddenly lit up with a golden radiance, then dispersed like water ripples, and the envelope unfolded automatically, revealing the parchment inside.
The handwriting on the parchment seemed to be written with some special ink, shimmering with a bluish glow under dim light:
"Ron, I have some matters that require me to temporarily leave the School. Do not tell anyone about this.
However, by the time you return from the Bloodline Altar, I will likely be back.
Then come to the herb store to find me, as I have something important to give you in person."
This was entirely different from what he had imagined. Such information could have been relayed through Lily as a verbal message; why was there a need to use a magically sealed letter?

chapters.title: Chapter 274 - 182: Meditation Technique Traits
chapters.content:
Chapter 274: Chapter 182: Meditation Technique Traits
"After you finish reading the letter, leave it alone, it will self-destruct.
Additionally, I have also sealed the final stage of the Meditation Technique, and now is not the time for you to view it."
Ron gazed at the letter in his hand, which shimmered with a faint silver light, and fell into deep thought.
The letter’s content seemed simple, yet it stirred countless questions in his mind.
"Is Lady Allen leaving the Black Mist Jungle?"
Ever since stepping into this fog-shrouded peculiar place, Lady Allen seemed to have always been a part of that herb store, inseparably intertwined.
That dim shop filled with the scent of herbs was like an extension of the old woman’s body, and she was the soul of the shop.
"From the time I entered the Black Mist Jungle until now, it seems no one has ever mentioned her leaving the shop..."
Ron furrowed his brows, contemplating various possibilities.
The school has extremely strict controls over the actions of Wizards, especially special beings like Lady Allen.
Clearly, her every move is likely under some form of secret surveillance.
"Is this why such a high-level confidentiality method like the Magic Sealing Letter was used just to convey such simple information?"
Ron lightly tapped the table: "Clearly, the lady has her own plans and doesn’t want those high-ranking officials of the school to know."
Combining this with what Lady Allen and Magnus had both hinted at, that they came to the Black Mist Jungle to "retire" after failing in struggles, further set off alarm bells in his mind.
He would have Andre check near the herb store to see if it was indeed closed or just under a guise of still being open.
As soon as the letter left his hand, it combusted on its own...
Ron frowned slightly and carefully further destroyed the ashes of the letter.
Then he turned his gaze to the black sealed box emitting faint energy fluctuations—inside it was the final stage of the "Star Eater’s Ravings".
Now is not the time... he wouldn’t be foolish enough to throw himself into a sea of fire just to satisfy his curiosity.
"The cultivation of the second stage already brings sufficient challenges..." Ron mused to himself, recalling his recent meditation experiences.
Compared to the basic stage, the second stage of Meditation Cultivation was a completely different level of experience.
The "ravings" from the depths of the starry sky became clearer, continuous, like some invisible tentacles constantly tearing his mental body, disturbing his spiritual focus.
The first few days of cultivation were almost a torture.
Ron was unable to maintain ten minutes of continuous meditation; the mental rending agony forced him to repeatedly interrupt, then resume after a brief rest in an endless cycle.
Every time he emerged from the meditation state, he found himself drenched in sweat, panting heavily as if waking from a nightmare.
"These ravings..." he fell into painful memories: "were like countless tiny needles piercing into the mind from all directions simultaneously."
And this was after he had adapted to the ravings following his battle with that tentacled monster in his consciousness; otherwise, the condition would have been even worse.
This experience made him better understand why Lady Allen had sternly warned him that the "Star Eater’s Ravings" was unlike any other Meditation Technique.
But a sudden inspiration changed everything.
That day he suddenly thought, since his "Erosion Chapter" came from the ravings of the starry sky monster, and since ravings could cancel each other out...
Could he possibly use the melody of the "Erosion Chapter" to counteract the disturbances caused by the ravings during meditation?
And indeed, as he had anticipated, when he recalled the melody of the "Erosion Chapter" during meditation, the whispers that had been troubling his meditation became less piercing to his mental body.
It was as if the two fluctuations canceled each other out, or rather, the "Erosion Chapter" created a "Mind Barrier" that blocked those invasive ravings.
Ron opened the music notebook on the lab table, where he had detailed the parameters and effects of each attempt:
"First movement in D minor, employing sufficient intensity of spiritual power fluctuations, to form the first layer of interference;
E major with vibrato technique, creating a resonance effect with the ’Zi’ syllable;
Special finger combinations simulate the ’Clu’ syllable, completing the final structure..."
These intricate technical details were the valuable experiences he acquired through countless attempts and failures.
Sometimes, to adjust the exact frequency of a note, he would need to experiment continuously for over a dozen hours.
And every successful breakthrough brought him an indescribable sense of satisfaction, like uncovering layer upon layer of mystery, gradually approaching a grand truth.
[You have comprehended the skill: Erosion Chapter (Beginner)]
[Note: This skill has a strong correlation with "Star Eater’s Ravings" and Sound Wave Vibration]
Acquiring the skill was quite a pleasant surprise.
But the true value of the second-stage Meditation Technique was far from just this.
With his rank rising and access privileges increased, he delved into various materials about Official Wizards in the School Library.
Among them, the section on Meditation Techniques mentioned that when cultivation reaches the critical point of spiritual power for an Official Wizard, some Gem Level and above meditation techniques grant cultivators their own unique traits.
These traits would integrate with one’s Magic System, endowing spells with unique effects, distinguishing them from the casting mode of all ordinary Wizards.
