Just like every Official Wizard has their signature personal spell, the "Meditation Technique Traits" are a core advantage offered only by Gem Level and above meditation techniques.

chapters.title: Chapter 275 - 182: Meditation Technique Traits_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 275: Chapter 182: Meditation Technique Traits_2
"This is a crucial step in advancing from an Advanced Apprentice to an Official Wizard..."
Ron calculated in his mind: "A completely personalized magical trait that can open up entirely new research directions for me."
But what followed was the concern about the increasing spiritual contamination.
As the depth of meditation increased, the accumulation rate of spiritual contamination also intensified.
Although the reset function of the Time Guardian Pocket Watch could still effectively clear these contaminations, Ron keenly realized that as he approached the critical point of an Advanced Apprentice, relying solely on the Pocket Watch would inevitably be inadequate.
"Although the reset capability of the Pocket Watch is powerful, it has its limits too."
Ron frowned in contemplation:
"Once the level of spiritual power approaches that of an Official Wizard, the complexity and intensity of contamination will correspondingly increase, and whether the Pocket Watch can fully cope with it remains unknown."
This dilemma further strengthened his determination to expedite the practice of the "Melting Furnace Concept."
"A more thorough solution must be found before reaching the critical point." Ron planned in his mind:
"After returning from the Bloodline Altar, immediately attempt the transition to Demon Hunter and Magic Swordsman, then focus on advancing to an Official Wizard, ultimately using the Active Demon Sword as the ’furnace’ carrier to fundamentally solve the contamination problem."
This plan is interconnected, step by step, with each link being crucial.
"Multi-career integration, mutual reinforcement..."
However, he still had another task at hand—helping Trish with the leopard lady’s bloodline modulation.
After all, he had promised this, and it would also serve as a practical test of his Bloodline Modifier abilities.
Ron arranged all the necessary tools and materials, having already constructed a detailed bloodline modulation plan in his mind.
The research on the traits of the Scorpion Venom Gland was very thorough, the key lies in how to perfectly integrate this trait with the leopard lady’s existing bloodline, to avoid potential rejection reactions.
"Every step must be precise to the millimeter..." he reviewed the venom gland research notes:
"Any slight deviation could trigger unpredictable bloodline conflicts."
In the late-night laboratory, only he remained with the silently operating complex instruments.
Moonlight filtered through the window, casting a silvery-white patch on the floor.
Ron sighed, temporarily setting aside various thoughts, focusing his energy on the most urgent task at hand.
"Orderly advance, step by step."
He finally admonished himself: "Even the most complex puzzles are composed of small segments."
The next morning, Ron brought the carefully prepared bloodline modulation tools and materials and went to Trish’s residence as agreed.
On the way, he once again reviewed the complex operation process about to be undertaken.
Bloodline modulation, being such a precise task, once started, must be completed in one go, any mistake halfway could lead to catastrophic consequences.
The wind stirred the dark blue leaves on the branches in the Black Mist Jungle, creating a strange rustling sound.
Following the address provided by Trish, he arrived at a small villa located in the East District of the school.
This two-story stone building appeared simple and ancient, with faintly glowing vine plants climbing on its walls, outlining the building’s silhouette in the morning light.
The entire building was enveloped in an almost invisible energy barrier, a sign of an advanced protective array.
As Ron approached the door, an invisible touch of spiritual power swept over him like a radar, thoroughly checking his identity traits.
The precision and intensity of this spiritual power probing clearly exceeded the level of an Advanced Apprentice.
The door opened automatically, and Trish was already waiting in the foyer.
She wasn’t wearing her apprentice robe, but a simple light green casual outfit, her already attractive face appeared even more youthful.
"Thank you for coming."
The young lady greeted warmly, a courteous yet polite smile on her face:
"The master is attending to some matters and will be here shortly. Li Yue is already waiting in the preparation room."
Ron nodded, following Trish through the elegantly decorated corridor, subtly observing his surroundings.
Sensitivity to the environment had become his instinctive reaction.
The corridor was lined with various peculiar collections:
Specimens sealed in crystals, fragments of stone slabs inscribed with ancient runes, liquid creatures floating in specially made containers, constantly changing forms...
Each item revealed the owner’s deep interest in mysticism.
"Most of these are the master’s collections over the years."
Following Ron’s gaze, Trish explained, with a faint hint of pride in her tone:
"She often takes me to study the traits of these extraordinary creatures. Here, you might be interested in this one."
She stopped in front of a special glass case, which contained a well-preserved small creature, its form somewhere between a butterfly and a jellyfish, with thin, cicada-wing-like membranes covered in complex glowing patterns.
"The Star Abyss Moth, reportedly found only in specific areas of the ’Twisted Jungle’ on the Abyss Fourth Layer."
Trish explained, her voice filled with an obsessive fascination for mystical knowledge:
"Master Corina says they can move between different layers of the Abyss without being tainted by curses, one of the very few creatures with such an ability."
Ron remained expressionless, yet his heart was stirred.
If this creature were indeed as Trish described, possessing a natural ability to resist Abyssal Curses, then the research value of its bloodline traits far exceeded that of ordinary specimens, potentially even becoming a key piece in unraveling the mystery of Abyss Adaptability.
"A very rare specimen."
He commented, his voice full of interest:

chapters.title: Chapter 276 - 182: Meditation Technique Traits_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 276: Chapter 182: Meditation Technique Traits_3
"If there’s a chance to study its bloodline structure, we might gain some vital data on Abyss Adaptability."
Trish smiled and nodded but did not respond. It was unclear if she didn’t catch his hint or simply didn’t want to continue the conversation.
Next, they arrived at a spacious basement.
The lighting inside was soft, with a specially-made White Jade Platform in the center, engraved with complex Array patterns.
On the shelves by the wall were various precision instruments and potions, ranging from basic extractors to advanced energy stabilization devices, making it appear to be a professional bloodline research laboratory.
Li Yue was already waiting beside the stone platform.
Unlike her usual silent demeanor, she was slightly nervous, unconsciously rubbing her sleeves with her fingers.
Upon seeing Ron enter, she slightly bowed her head in greeting, a flicker of conflicting emotions, hope and caution, in her eyes.
"Thank you, my lord, for willing to help me," she said softly, her voice calm and subdued.
Ron nodded and began quickly adapting to the environment and assessing the available resources:
"Trish has already informed me of some details, but I need a more detailed understanding of your bloodline conditions and the specific circumstances of the toxin contact."
His eyes surveyed this well-equipped laboratory, impressed by what he saw.
The quality and quantity of these devices, even surpassing the school’s public laboratory facilities, clearly reflected Corina’s stringent requirements for experimental conditions.
Li Yue nodded and, under Trish’s guidance, lay down on the stone platform.
"During my last battle at the gladiatorial tournament, I was brushed directly by a Scorpion venom gland spike. At the time, there was brief intense pain and paralysis, but I quickly returned to normal."
Because she was lying down, the leopard woman’s voice was somewhat muffled.
Ron took out a set of specially-designed detection tools and began conducting a comprehensive bloodline scan of the leopard woman.
His palm hovered a few centimeters above Li Yue’s body, Spiritual Power penetrating her body like thousands of tiny probes.
With the dual traits of "Extraordinary Recognition" and "Tracing," her bloodline structure gradually became clear in his spiritual vision.
"Interesting..." Ron slightly frowned, discovering some unexpected situations.
The bloodline structure inside Li Yue’s body was far more complicated than any Alien Race he’d encountered before.
The outermost layer featured the Leopard Race’s characteristic bloodline, the foundation of her race;
But deeper within, there lay an older and more powerful bloodline, hidden beneath layers of seals, only revealed by faint fluctuations at certain nodes.
The energy fluctuation pattern of this bloodline was extremely unique, holding the wild explosive power of a beast, yet exuding an indescribable noble aura—this should be the so-called Monarch Bloodline.
It was noteworthy that within the area of contact with the Scorpion Poison, this hidden bloodline seemed to have already begun a faint awakening, forming a preliminary adaptive response.
"Now I can see why your previous attempt at poison gland substance fusion failed."
Ron continued testing, analyzing:
"This latent bloodline possesses a strong rejection instinct, automatically resisting the infiltration of foreign bloodlines. It doesn’t reject the toxin itself but any foreign bloodline that’s not ’pure’ enough."
Ron took several specially formulated reagents from the toolbox, mixing them according to precise proportions in a small crucible, then dropped a bit of Li Yue’s blood into it.
The liquid immediately reacted, turning deep purple and emitting a faint glow.
He then conducted several more precise tests, trying to identify the exact type and activation possibility of the latent bloodline.
"I have a revised plan," Ron thought for a moment and said:
"Instead of forcibly injecting new bloodline traits, it’s better to temporarily suppress part of this latent bloodline, making the integration with the toxin capability much easier."
Trish’s eyes lit up: "This completely exceeds my expectations! Thank you, I will try to provide a reward that satisfies you."
Ron nodded, taking out several Scorpion venom gland samples that had been processed from the toolbox.
Through his special purification process, these poison glands had been stripped of most impurities, retaining only the core toxin components and traits.
He carefully placed the samples in a detection dish, beginning to study how to merge them with Li Yue’s latent bloodline traits.
"Your claw area is where the toxin contact is most frequent, and it’s the least likely to trigger the instinctive response of the bloodline."
Ron spoke to the leopard woman, striving to boost her confidence to slightly reduce the rejection:
"I’ll attempt to concentrate the poison gland substance in this area for transplantation while trying to expand the claw’s retractable function."
After preparations were complete, Ron took out a small bottle of Guiding Potion:
"Li Yue, you’ll need to drink this first. It will temporarily decrease the rejection level of your bloodline, creating conditions for the subsequent operation."
The leopard woman nodded, took the potion, and drank it in one gulp.
Seconds later, her body started to glow slightly, the spots on her skin becoming more pronounced.
"Let’s begin," Ron took a deep breath, focusing his Spiritual Power on Li Yue’s hand area.
His Spiritual Power infiltrated along a specific path, searching for those latent bloodline nodes.
Li Yue let out a low growl, a sound that resembled not a human but a roar akin to some ancient beast.
Her eyes turned completely golden yellow, pupils contracting into thin slits.
Her entire body tensed as if ready to leap into an attack at any moment.
"Calm down, Li Yue! I’m here."
Trish stepped forward confidently and gently:
"Focus, feel this power, but don’t let it control you."
Under Trish’s calming influence, Li Yue’s emotions gradually stabilized.
Ron seized the opportunity to guide those activated energies, channeling them towards the preset path.
"Phase one completed."
About ten minutes later, Ron finally relaxed:
"The latent bloodline suppression is temporarily in place. Now we can proceed to phase two—the poison gland transplantation."
Ron mixed the poison gland extract with a specially-made fusion medium, forming a viscous dark purple liquid.
At first, everything went smoothly.
Each minute energy node was rearranged under his control, like a massive complex three-dimensional puzzle gradually taking shape.
The poison gland substance was accepted by Li Yue’s bloodline, starting to merge with the claw tissue.
However, when the fusion was halfway through, a rejection reaction suddenly occurred.
Li Yue gritted her teeth in pain, her body beginning to show redness and abnormal energy fluctuations.
"Rejection reaction." Ron immediately identified the problem:
"Even though the latent bloodline was suppressed, the purity of foreign matter is still insufficient."
Trish seemed a bit concerned: "Is it dangerous?"
"The risk is within controllable limits."
Ron responded briefly, already adjusting his Spiritual Power output mode:
"I’ll monitor life signs throughout, and if any severe anomaly appears, I’ll stop immediately."
His Spiritual Power, like countless invisible threads, wandered through Li Yue’s bloodline, dismantling those rejection structures, then reassembling them according to a new pattern.
Every step had to be precise down to microseconds, as any slight mistake could collapse the entire process.
This process lasted nearly twenty minutes, with Ron wholly focused, his forehead sweat already soaking his collar.
Finally, when the last rejection point was successfully reassembled, the entire fusion process was completed.
"It’s done," Ron retracted his Spiritual Power, with a hint of exhaustion in his voice:
"The poison gland substance has completely integrated into the claw structure, and I’ve extended the claw’s retractable capability as well."

chapters.title: Chapter 277 - 183: Beneath the Crown
chapters.content:
Chapter 277: Chapter 183: Beneath the Crown
Li Yue sat up from the lab table, delicately flexing her fingers, surprised to discover that she could freely control the length of her nails.
When she focused her spirit, the claws could even extend to twice their original length, forming sharp weapons.
And when she controlled further, a faint purple glow began to emanate from the claws, indicating the activation of poison.
"This is... unbelievable," Trish exclaimed, her eyes flashing with excitement:
"You’ve not only completed the poison fusion but also endowed her with the ability to control the poison!"
Li Yue tried retracting her claws, then extending them once more.
The process was smooth and natural, with no discomfort at all.
"Thank you, Lord Ralph."
She rarely smiled: "This power... will allow me to better protect my master."
"Your bloodline potential is far more than this."
Ron assessed: "If there’s an opportunity for a more comprehensive bloodline activation, you might exhibit more surprising abilities."
As he spoke, he packed away various samples of the Leopard Woman’s tissue that he had "conveniently" collected during the bloodline modulation phase into preservation containers.
This was also one of the reasons he gladly agreed to this bloodline modulation, the Monarch Bloodline must be of great research value.
The brown-haired girl also turned around at this moment, preparing to retrieve the Magic Stone Money Bag, turning a blind eye to Ron’s small actions.
Ron carefully stowed away the samples he collected, preparing to conduct a final examination on the Leopard Woman, when a powerful wave of magic power suddenly came from outside the door.
The oppressive feeling made the air become stagnant, as if it had been suddenly infused with an invisible viscous substance.
Even someone like Ron, an Advanced Apprentice, felt a moment of trepidation.
This was the unique "Radiation Field" of an Official Wizard.
The door silently opened, and a figure in a white robe drifted in like a specter.
"It seems things are progressing smoothly," a hoarse voice sounded.
The voice was as sharp as metal scraping, yet it carried a kind of undeniable authority.
Ron looked up and saw Corina draped in a white robe, her familiar exquisite mask on her face.
"Master." Trish immediately stood up to pay her respects, her tone filled with evident awe.
Ron also bowed respectfully: "Lady Corina."
"No need for formalities."
The White-robed Mage’s gaze swept between Ron and Li Yue, finally resting on the Leopard Woman’s completely transformed claws.
"An interesting improvement," she remarked, her voice containing a hint of imperceptible appreciation:
"More complex and effective than I originally thought. The level of poison guidance and structural reshaping is already equivalent to that of a professional Modulator, Maxim’s judgment is indeed accurate."
Ron’s heart stirred, sensing something abnormal:
"Lady Corina, do you have something specific to tell me?"
"Hehe, you’re quite perceptive."
The White-robed Mage slightly tilted her head, chuckling softly, her eyes behind the mask sparkling with mysterious light:
"You’re right, I arranged for Trish to invite you over because I heard about your unusual interest in the Abyss."
"As for Li Yue’s bloodline modulation..." Corina continued, her voice calm to the point of coldness:
"If you hadn’t demonstrated this level, I would have asked Maxim to personally intervene. He’s an old friend of mine and an expert in Abyss-related research."
Ron’s alertness heightened; the situation was far more complex than it appeared on the surface.
An Official Wizard showing special attention to an Advanced Apprentice often signifies some special task or trial subtly unfolding.
"Is Lady Corina also interested in Abyss research?"
He cautiously inquired, attempting to discern the other’s true intentions.
"Not ’also interested,’ young man, but ’was once obsessed with it.’
Corina’s voice carried a trace of undetectable bitterness:
"However, your performance earlier truly exceeded expectations. This fusion technology is already approaching the level of a senior Modulator. Li Yue’s value has greatly increased, warranting extra compensation."
With that, she took out a complete Magic Stone from inside her robe and handed it to Ron:
"This is your modulation fee."
Ron accepted the Magic Stone, sensing the pure energy contained within.
A complete Magic Stone is more valuable than a simple hundred Magic Stone Fragments, enough to purchase a single-person dwelling in Black Mist Jungle.
"Now, please come to my laboratory once."
Corina turned to head for the door: "There are some things I need to discuss privately."
She turned to Li Yue and Trish:
"You two go rest first, I have some matters to discuss privately with Apprentice Ralph."
The two nodded respectfully and then left the room.
Ron silently followed the White-robed Mage, passing through several winding corridors to arrive at a room half-hidden in the shadows.
Corina lightly touched a rune on the door frame, and the heavy stone door slowly opened inward.
The light in the room was dim, ghostly blue Magic Crystal Lamps flickering on the walls, illuminating various strange instruments and devices.
"Come in," she gestured for Ron to follow inside.
Ron clutched the Silver Pocket Watch in his arms, letting the "Thousand Transformations" on his body awaken.
He felt a slight unease rising in his heart; if Corina bore him any malice, she wouldn’t have used such cumbersome methods.
As Ron stepped in, the stone door automatically closed, the room’s Protective Array silently activated, isolating all magic power fluctuations and sounds from the outside world.
Corina went straight to the only chair in the room and sat down, crossing her legs, a beautifully curved calf revealing from the edge of the white robe.

chapters.title: Chapter 278 - 183: Beneath the Crown (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 278: Chapter 183: Beneath the Crown (Part 2)
She looked at Ron standing three meters away from her, not feeling offended, just let out a soft laugh and got straight to the point:
"No need to be so tense. I heard you are deeply interested in the Abyss, even going so far as to spend a fortune to purchase parts of the Scorpion from that gladiatorial event. This unusual interest in the Abyss reminds me of myself when I was young."
Her words carried an inexplicable emotion, as if it were a memory, yet also a warning.
"The pursuit of knowledge is the nature of all wizards."
Ron cautiously replied, "And the Abyss, as a realm full of unknowns, naturally draws exploration."
"But not all explorations are harmless."
Corina slowly raised her hand, reaching for her mask:
"Some truths, once seen, can never be forgotten."
Saying so, she slowly unveiled her mask, revealing the true face underneath.
Ron felt a sudden jolt of fear.
The silver-haired witch’s face was nothing like that of a normal human.
It was a face severely distorted.
The skin appeared unnaturally pale, almost transparent, with the wriggling blood vessels visible underneath.
The left cheek was covered with scattered silver scales, very similar to those on Maxim, yet the range was broader.
The right eye had completely transformed into an oval, with no pupil, only constantly shifting light patterns flowing on the surface.
The lips were almost nonexistent, replaced by a crack that nearly traversed the entire lower half of the face, revealing peculiar teeth inside that did not conform to human physiology as she spoke.
Even with Ron’s current mental fortitude, this sudden visual shock made him involuntarily take a step back, fingers clenching instinctively.
Corina noticed his reaction but showed no displeasure.
On the contrary, she seemed accustomed to such a response.
"No need to panic, Apprentice Ralph."
She said calmly, her voice still that harsh metallic scraping sound.
But now Ron could see it was because her vocal cords had completely mutated:
"This is the greatest gift the Abyss has left me, unless I achieve the rank of Great Wizard, it cannot be erased in a lifetime."
Ron averted his gaze, the more he looked, the more he felt a chill creeping up his spine.
This degree of mutation far exceeded the silver scales displayed by Maxim.
He quickly controlled his reaction, regaining his usual composure: "You are also an Abyssal Explorer?"
"Indeed."
Corina nodded: "Maxim should have already mentioned his experience to you. At that time, I had just been promoted to Morning Star Mage not long. We were part of the same exploration team, entering the Abyss Sixth Layer ’Maze Domain’ together."
She slightly wobbled her crossed legs, restraining some of the radiating field from her body, signaling Ron to come closer:
"That exploration, we paid a heavy price. Out of twenty team members, only the two of us came back alive, and our current condition, you have already seen."
Ron cautiously moved to a distance of two meters from Corina, listening intently.
This was a rare opportunity to hear about the real situation of the Abyss from another personal experience.
"But it was precisely this exploration that allowed my spiritual power to increase at a speed much higher than ordinary people."
Corina continued, that silver eye flickering with strange light:
"My spiritual talent is only fourth-class, but at less than fifty years old, I reached the critical point of the Morning Star Level, which is almost impossible on the normal meditation path.
Many wizards unwilling to venture into the Abyss, even if they meditate hard for a lifetime, would only reach my current level."
She caressed the scales on her face, her expression complex:
"But the price is what you see, once stained by the curse of the Abyss, it can never be completely cleansed.
It becomes a part of you, constantly reminding you of the reality of that experience."
Ron nodded slightly: "But you still seem to think this exchange is worthwhile?"
"The answer to this question depends on each person’s pursuit."
Corina’s voice grew deeper:
"For those wizards eager to break conventional limits and seek higher realms, the Abyss is a shortcut, but at the same time it is a road full of thorns."
She suddenly changed the subject: "By the way, I heard you are practicing a special meditation technique?"
Ron was startled, but showed no outward reaction:
"Yes, a Gem Level meditation technique taught by Lady Allen."
"’Star Eater’s Ravings’, right, heh... This meditation technique is almost known to everybody among the Official Wizards at the Crystal Tower."
Corina directly said the name, catching Ron a bit off guard:
"’Star Eater’s Ravings’ is an introductory method preceding the Crown Meditation Technique. This meditation technique, leading to higher levels, often helps cultivators accumulate spiritual power faster, but it also accelerates the accumulation of spiritual contamination."
Her voice carried a warning:
"This meditation technique will make you more susceptible to the influence of curses when entering the Abyss. Moreover, to cultivate to higher levels, you must also enter the Abyss for breakthroughs. This is precisely why I specifically asked to meet you today, as we already have an unbreakable tie with the Abyss."
’Star Eater’s Ravings’ actually has such a hidden peril. Damn it, Lady Allen never told him about these risks previously, could it be...
"There’s no need to think too ill of Lady Allen. The meditation technique can actually be changed after being promoted to an Official Wizard, and shifting from a high-tier technique to a lower-level one will be easier, whereas the reverse might be challenging."

chapters.title: Chapter 279 - 183: Under the Crown_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 279: Chapter 183: Under the Crown_3
Corina twirled the mask in her hand and explained lightly:
"Lady Allen perhaps simply thought your potential was greater, and thus chose to go all the way in one step."
Ron remained silent for a moment, digesting this information: "Are you trying to give me a warning?"
"It’s not just a warning, but also giving you a chance to consider carefully in advance."
The silver-haired witch continued:
"Everyone has the right to choose their own path, but such choices should be based on a full understanding of all possibilities."
She pointed again to her own distorted face:
"If you wish to climb to higher levels, this might be what you look like in the future, or possibly even worse."
The witch raised a hand covered with scales and slowly traced it through the air:
"The abyss grants power, but also brings a curse. Those taints and distortions will follow you like a shadow for a lifetime."
"Yet thanks to Trish’s ’favor,’ the taints and distortions on me are much better than before. This is also the reason I strive to cultivate her, the ’favor’ brought by an excellent student far surpasses any healing potion."
Corina looked toward what was probably the west outside the wall, continuing:
"I plan to return to the Crystal Tower in the Central Lands after Trish has promoted to Advanced Apprentice and completed the upcoming bloodline altar trial. The resources and research environment there are far superior to this marginal school."
Her gaze returned to Ron:
"With the talent and progress you’ve shown, I believe you will also step through the gates of the Crystal Tower in the near future."
When Trish becomes an Advanced Apprentice, she plans to take her directly to the Crystal Tower, rather than compete for the school-promised ’Key’ Potion with them?
Ron was a bit puzzled, about to ask something.
Corina saw his expression and could roughly guess what he was thinking:
"It seems that since you just advanced to the top ten of the sequence, no one has notified you of the hidden details."
"The Candidate Wizard sequence is held every ten years, but the Key Potion needed to break through to Official Wizard is allocated by the upper Crystal Tower with only one bottle."
Her voice carried a rare emotional fluctuation:
"Waiting in the marginal school or heading earlier to the resource-rich Central Lands—this choice is not difficult. The earlier Trish breaks through to Official Wizard, the sooner she can bring greater ’favor’ to me, which is beneficial to both of us."
Ron mentally noted this key information.
Every ten years, one bottle of Key Potion, which means that only one person in each sequence of Candidate Wizards can obtain the opportunity for an official breakthrough.
In the midst of casual conversation, Corina also revealed more information about the Crystal Tower, and some advice regarding the upcoming bloodline altar trial.
To Ron, this information was undoubtedly a valuable reference.
As the discussion neared its end, Corina put the mask back on, concealing her horrifically distorted visage.
"Your bloodline modulation techniques and magic potion-making are quite excellent."
She said, her voice regaining that metallic calmness:
"If there is an opportunity in the future, I wouldn’t mind cooperating with you more deeply. Of course, the premise is that you can stand out in the Crystal Tower."
After saying this, Corina turned around, and the tightly shut stone door automatically opened at that moment.
Ron respectfully bowed and took his leave, and when he exited the underground level, he felt the burden on his shoulders grow a bit heavier.
In the entrance hall, a brown-haired girl was waiting for him, her eyes full of complex emotions:
"It seems the teacher told you a lot."
Ron nodded and did not reply, as he was not in the mood for small talk at the moment.
"Then head back soon, it’s late." Trish escorted him to the door, softly speaking:
"Your performance today was truly stunning, Ron. I think... I underestimated you before."
Ron smiled softly: "Then let’s cooperate well together in the bloodline altar."
"Mm... you’ve always been a reliable companion."
Walking on the way back, his thoughts kept revolving around Corina’s distorted face and the secret information she revealed.
The allure and danger of the abyss, the double-edged effect of special meditation techniques, and the scarcity of resources and competition in the Candidate Wizard sequence... these are all realities he must cautiously face.

chapters.title: Chapter 280 - 184: Scorpion Transformation
chapters.content:
Chapter 280: Chapter 184: Scorpion Transformation
In the darkness of the night, within the most concealed Meditation Room of the workshop, Ron sat cross-legged in the Array, surrounded by a circle of extinguished Magic Crystal Lamps.
Only two blue candles burned in front of him, their flames motionless in the windless environment.
This was the meditation environment he had specifically designed for the second stage of the "Star Eater’s Ravings," capable of isolating external disturbances to the maximum extent and enhancing the Spiritual Resonance with the "Starry Sky."
Deep breath, empty thoughts, Ron slowly closed his eyes and began tonight’s meditation practice.
The familiar Ravings soon echoed in his mind, but unlike the initial fear and resistance upon first contact, he had now learned how to coexist with it.
As the depth of Meditation increased, Ron felt his consciousness seemed to leave his body and float in the boundless Starry Sky.
Countless twinkling stars surrounded him, and in the distant darkness, some vast and ancient presence seemed to be watching him.
The feeling was both terrifying and bizarre, chilling yet irresistible.
The Ravings echoed in the sea of consciousness, while Ron used the Mind Barrier formed by the "Erosion Chapter" to combat it, guiding the flow and accumulation of Spiritual Power in the process.
[Erosion Chapter (Beginner) Experience Points +1]
Time became blurry in this state; it could have been an hour, or maybe three.
When Ron finally awoke from Meditation, he found that dawn was breaking, with the first rays of sunlight quietly spilling through the window crevices.
But more shocking was the change in his Spiritual Power — having broken through to Advanced Apprentice just about two months ago, his Spiritual Power had already reached an astonishing 4.4 points!
"This rate of growth..." Ron incredulously looked at his attributes panel: "At least several times faster than the first stage."
This was indeed not an ordinary Meditation Technique but a shortcut capable of significantly accelerating Spiritual Power growth and leading to higher realms.
"The introductory method of the Crown Meditation Technique..."
Ron lightly felt the abundant Spiritual Power within him: "Then the Crown Meditation Technique itself, how astonishing must its Effect be?"
He could understand why the dissemination of such a Meditation Technique was strictly limited.
Such rapid Spiritual Power growth, without corresponding protective means, would quickly spiral out of control due to Spiritual Contamination.
Ron took out the Time Guardian Pocket Watch, gently stroking the patterns on its surface, his heart filled with gratitude.
It was this rare antique that enabled him to safely walk this perilous path.
However, when he activated the Purification process, he found that the Energy required was more than ever before.
[Successfully reset negative state: Spiritual Contamination, Energy -10]
"The consumption increases each time..."
Ron frowned.
This meant that with further increases in Spiritual Power, the complexity and intensity of the contamination were also simultaneously growing, even possibly soon exceeding the Pocket Watch’s single purification capacity.
"Must accelerate the practice of the ’Melting Furnace Concept.’"
Ron decided that before his Spiritual Power reached the Critical Point, he must find a more fundamental solution for contamination handling.
But this issue could still be temporarily controlled, and the urgent task was to use this time to elevate Spiritual Power to the highest possible level, preparing for the trial of the Bloodline Altar.
Ron exited the Meditation Room and came to the main hall of the workshop.
Lilia had already gotten up and was preparing breakfast.
Seeing Ron, the girl smiled and greeted him, "Good morning, teacher. How was the Effect of last night’s Meditation?"
"Beyond expectations." Ron succinctly replied, taking the hot tea Lilia handed to him: "Where are Dale and Ailan?"
"Sister Ailan went to the back mountain to gather herbs, saying that some night-blooming plants need to be harvested before sunrise."
Lilia replied while busying herself, "Dale is still sleeping; yesterday’s training left her exhausted."
Ron nodded, though the growth of the Little Sea Siren was astonishing, her recovery speed of physical and Spiritual power still did not match that of an adult Sea Siren.
Adequate rest is very necessary for her.
"I’ve prepared the breakfast you like." Lilia placed a dish of appetizing food on the table:
"Do you have any special plans for today, teacher?"
"Same as usual, staying in the laboratory. You can just keep my lunch warm." Ron replied as he enjoyed his breakfast: "Some findings from the past few days are very interesting, and I’d like to do further research."
He looked sideways at the girl: "And you? What are your plans today?"
"I’m planning to organize the herbal storage, then continue practicing the Basic Magic Potion Making you taught me."
Lilia answered earnestly:
"Sister Ailan said she would bring back some fresh piyi grass, which is a key ingredient for making Enhancing Potions."
Ron nodded with satisfaction.
Her learning attitude had always been proper, with rapid progress.
"Great. If you have any questions, feel free to ask me anytime."
Ron finished the last sip of tea and headed toward the laboratory.
In the laboratory, a seemingly ordinary puppet lay quietly in a specially crafted energy isolation box.
Ron carefully took it out, placed it on the central lab table, and sensed the peculiar Energy Fluctuation emanating from the puppet.
The research over the past few weeks had given him a deeper understanding of this Abyssal Treasure.
The Stand-In Puppet could not only replicate the user’s appearance and basic abilities but also acquire additional Traits and strengths by absorbing Abyssal biological tissues.
The initial discovery was purely coincidental.
During a routine energy test, the Stand-In Puppet was placed next to a Scorpion tissue sample.

chapters.title: Chapter 281 - 184: Scorpion Transformation (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 281: Chapter 184: Scorpion Transformation (Part 2)
Ron was surprised to find that the puppet began to display an unusually active state, seemingly attracted by those organizations.
Through the "Extraordinary Recognition" detailed energy scan, Ron discovered that the stand-in puppet had a near "craving" reaction to the Scorpion Organization, as if it recognized some sort of energy fluctuation from a common source.
"The stand-in puppet comes from the Abyss Fourth Layer, while the Scorpion is from the 3rd Floor..."
Ron recalled the descriptions in the "Abyssal Creatures Atlas," and had a bold conjecture:
There might exist a certain degree of mutual affinity between items and creatures in the Abyss that could lead to energy resonance or fusion under specific conditions.
With this hypothesis, Ron started a series of strictly controlled experiments.
He first had the stand-in puppet come into contact with a minimal amount of Scorpion Organization, observing the reaction;
then gradually increased the amount of contact, closely monitoring the puppet’s energy fluctuations and morphological changes.
Today, he planned to conduct a bolder experiment — let the stand-in puppet absorb some of the main organization of the Scorpion.
Ron took out two preservation boxes from the cold storage, opening them to reveal dark green tissue and a large heart still emitting astonishing vitality.
These were the poison gland tissue from the scorpion tail and the second heart, maintained for activity through special treatment.
"If the experiment succeeds, the stand-in puppet should be able to gain some of the Scorpion’s abilities."
Ron activated the surrounding protective array, ensuring that even if the experiment had unexpected outcomes, no dangers would leak out.
Once everything was ready, he took a deep breath and gently placed the poison gland tissue and heart on the puppet’s chest.
In just a few seconds, odd changes occurred — the tissue began to melt into a dark red liquid, quickly seeping into the puppet’s body.
At the same time, the lines on the puppet’s surface started to undergo subtle changes, with some lines becoming sharper and distorted, emitting a faint purple glow.
"The reaction is stronger than anticipated..."
Ron closely observed the process, documenting every detail.
After absorption was complete, the surface of the puppet returned to calm, but the overall aura had a noticeable change:
A dangerous and aggressive energy surged within it, like a dormant beast.
[Active Abyssal Material has been automatically absorbed, charging progress +1%]
[Current Energy: 1%/100%]
"This... turns out the puppet actually is able to recharge after absorbing active Abyssal Material, this was quite a lucky hit."
He felt a slight joy in his heart, if relying solely on Krypton Magic Stone for recharging, his small coffer wouldn’t be able to handle it, after all, one Magic Stone is only 1% charging progress.
But now, let’s first try the enhancement effect from the puppet’s absorption of Abyssal Material.
Ron invested a small portion of awareness into the puppet, attempting to activate it.
The puppet immediately responded, slowly standing up with movements more fluid and natural than before.
But the real surprise was yet to come — when Ron attempted to mobilize the toxin gland energy just absorbed...
The puppet suddenly mutated, a sharp tail barb grew out from its back, the tip glinting with a purple toxic glow.
"Incredible..." Ron murmured in awe, controlling the puppet to swing the tail barb, drawing a purple trajectory in the air.
Then, he tried further morph control and was astonished to find the puppet’s entire structure had become exceedingly malleable.
Not only the tail barb, but the limbs could grow stronger and more vigorous, even the face could partially mutate to display beastly features.
"It’s just like..." Ron’s eyes lit up: "A kind of organism fusion!"
He suddenly recalled the description of "Morph Resin" in the "Abyssal Creatures Atlas."
This special material from the Abyss Fourth Layer could blur the boundaries of life forms, granting objects the traits or abilities of other organisms.
The stand-in puppet evidently contains this material or similar components.
And when Ron reduced his awareness investment, leaving only basic control, the puppet surprisingly exhibited a nearly instinctive combat intuition.
It autonomously adjusted its posture, launching a series of defense and attack maneuvers, as if inheriting some of the instincts of the Scorpion.
"It’s just like having a semi-autonomous combat partner."
Ron was thrilled, watching the puppet move flexibly under his minimal control.
These discoveries immediately led him to consider more possibilities: if the stand-in puppet could assimilate Scorpion Organization, then in theory, could it also assimilate other Abyssal creature organizations?
What kind of ability changes would different kinds of Abyssal creature organizations bring?
What effects would arise from the simultaneous fusion of multiple organizations?
Ron’s "Conception" trait was running at full capacity at this moment, a grand blueprint gradually forming in his mind:
A super-powered puppet that combines multiple Abyssal organism traits, equipped with various environment adaptation abilities, multiple attack methods, and possibly a certain level of autonomous awareness and judgment ability...
And when the stand-in puppet’s energy reaches 50%, unlocking dual-channel function and further advancing it to become a [Demon Hunter] with profession leveling up, these abilities will leap further!
While all capabilities simultaneously feed back to his body, letting him reap the full benefits without any risks.
.........
Deep within the earth veins, a beehive-like cave was surrounded by dense black mist.
A layer of squirming mutated tissue covered the cave walls, dark purple liquid flowing on the surface, emitting a suffocating stench.
At the deepest part of the cave, a semi-solid, semi-liquid grotesque mass slowly writhed.

chapters.title: Chapter 282 - 184: Scorpification_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 282: Chapter 184: Scorpification_3
At first, it looked like some kind of gigantic rotting mushroom.
But upon closer inspection, you would notice countless tiny tendrils and bulges on its surface, opening and closing with a certain rhythm, as if breathing.
In the core of this mass, two humanoid figures could vaguely be seen tightly entwined, seemingly in some kind of twisted embrace.
"We... survived..."
A voice emanated from the disgusting flesh mass.
The voice was muffled, yet it could faintly be recognized as Oliver’s, though mixed with some strange sensation.
"Of course..."
Another voice arose, wet and viscous, like a liquid flowing through a narrow gap:
"That attack from Hayek was terrifying... but fortunately, the Holy Disc gave me something good..."
Cynthia’s voice was even less human than before, with a peculiar note of euphoria.
The writhing mass gradually stretched and deformed, slowly revealing a more concrete form:
Two bodies were connected by some kind of purple-black tissue, sharing some organs like conjoined twins.
Oliver’s upper body barely maintained a humanoid shape, though his skin had turned an unnatural ashen color.
The right side of his face was completely distorted, where a massive tentacle eye had grown, constantly contracting and expanding with his emotions.
His left arm had completely disappeared, replaced by a thick tentacle covered with suction cup-like organs.
And Cynthia’s transformation was even more thorough; her hair had turned into a mass of blue-purple tendrils, floating in the air like jellyfish tentacles.
The most bizarre aspect was her abdomen, where a giant vertical slit extended from her chest to her lower belly, resembling a gigantic maw filled with sharp teeth, intermittently opening and closing.
Oliver trembled as he reached out with his remaining right hand, touching his distorted face:
"I remember we were shattered into pieces by the energy impact... then your tendrils enveloped me... after that, my memory became blurry..."
"I protected your core consciousness with my main body, and then used an Abyssal Material..."
Cynthia let out a wet and eerie laugh, her voice sounding as if it came from underwater:
"I didn’t expect, at the brink of life and death, that the Abyssal Material would merge with us... the survival instinct provoked by emergency, truly a miraculous adaptation..."
Oliver stayed silent for a moment, observing their entwined body with his tentacle eye.
He could feel an unprecedented pleasure flowing through their shared tissue, as if they were constantly indulging in joy together.
"Abyssal Material? We... merged?" His voice carried a hint of shock and confusion.
"Not entirely..."
Cynthia’s tentacle strands brushed across Oliver’s cheek, feeling sticky yet soft:
"It’s more like a symbiotic relationship... our flesh and consciousness partially blend, sharing energy and perception..."
Her voice grew deeper and more alluring:
"How does it feel? This sensation brought by symbiosis... isn’t it wonderful?"
Oliver closed his one remaining human eye, immersing himself in this new perception.
Indeed, he felt an unprecedented power and clarity.
The chaotic thoughts and impulses that once troubled him seemed to be quelled after continuous pleasure by a calmer awareness.
"My spirit... is more stable."
He discovered in surprise: "Those insane impulses and hallucinations aren’t as intense anymore."
"This is the advantage of a higher awakening level..."
Cynthia said with satisfaction, her slit abdomen opening slightly to reveal the dark red writhing tissue inside:
"When your awakening reaches a certain level, you’re no longer passively affected by pollution, but actively coexisting with it..."
He tried to move their deformed symbiotic body, feeling the new strength.
The way of moving was clumsy and bizarre, Cynthia’s numerous tendrils writhing on the ground, propelling their entire body forward, producing a wet friction sound.
Oliver inquired, his facial tentacle eye turning towards Cynthia: "What should we do next?"
"Of course, go to the Bloodline Altar..." Cynthia chuckled:
"Yes... the place you’ve always dreamed about."
Her slit abdomen opened wider, exposing the multi-layered muscle tissue inside like an organ:
"There, we can complete a true awakening transformation... elevating the awakening level to rival that of an Official Wizard..."
Oliver fell into thought.
The Bloodline Altar... the opportunity he dreamed of during his apprentice days.
Countless days and nights, he fantasized about gaining the qualification to enter, using the altar’s power to undergo a qualitative change.
However, now they were going in this deformed state, with a completely different goal.
Not to further enhance themselves, but to use the altar’s energy to complete an abyssal awakening.
"The School will closely monitor the opening of the Bloodline Altar..." Oliver said worriedly:
"The Vice Dean, other Masters, and the terrifying Guardian of the Crystal Tower, they will all be present. In our current state, if we’re exposed, we’ll be annihilated."
"We don’t need to confront them directly..."
Cynthia’s voice became even more sinister:
"The Bloodline Altar is a semi-plane space, with countless hidden entrances... and once the altar opens, the energy fluctuations will cause a lot of interference, enough to cover our actions..."
Oliver could feel Cynthia’s excitement, the places where they intertwined ceaselessly transmitting her sensations to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 283 - 184: Scorpion Transformation (Part 4)
chapters.content:
Chapter 283: Chapter 184: Scorpion Transformation (Part 4)
He couldn’t help but let out a breath, submitting once again, his eyes already starting to roll back.
"And more importantly..."
Cynthia was already accustomed to this, merely caressing Oliver’s face with her tendrils: "We will have help..."
"Help?" Oliver jolted awake, his tendril-eye swiftly contracting: "Who will help us?"
"The ’Eye of the Abyss’ wasn’t completely annihilated... Mr. Holy Disc had foreseen the School would take action, that’s why he left early."
Cynthia let out a moist laugh:
"He will assist us at the crucial moment, and the fact that we survived this time is thanks to the abyssal material he provided..."
Oliver fell into silence.
Mr. Holy Disc, the mysterious representative of the "Eye of the Abyss," he never truly understood that person’s background or purpose.
But one thing was certain — that man was definitely not someone to be trusted.
"Are you sure he’s helping us, and not using us?"
"Using? Helping? Such concepts hold no meaning in the presence of higher-level beings..."
Cynthia’s voice turned ethereal and dreamy:
"We are all part of the ’Sanctuary Plan’... As long as we can achieve transformation and reach a higher level of awakening, nothing else matters..."
Oliver wanted to argue but found his thoughts being assimilated by Cynthia’s perspective.
This assimilation wasn’t forced, but rather a subtle infiltration, like two differently colored liquids slowly mixing.
Their consciousness was gradually merging, the boundaries becoming increasingly blurred.
"How long..." he asked softly, "When will the Bloodline Altar open?"
"Soon..." Cynthia’s voice became ethereal and distant:
"I can feel the frequency of the energy fluctuation accelerating... In about half a month, the altar will open..."
She suddenly lifted her head, as if listening to some distant sound:
"And I know who will enter the altar..."
"Who?"
"Ron Ralph..." Cynthia uttered the name, her voice filled with a kind of morbid excitement:
"That always-unexpected guy... He’s finally stepping into our hunting grounds..."
Oliver’s emotions surged violently, the tendril-eye contracted sharply, secreting a kind of black slime:
"Ralph?! That damned...!"
The surface of their shared body began to undergo dramatic changes.
Black spikes protruded from beneath the skin, muscles, and tissues started to expand and twist uncontrollably under the stimulus of angry emotions.
"Calm down..." Cynthia’s voice pierced through Oliver’s anger:
"Your emotions will interfere with our fusion process... We are not stable enough yet..."
Her tendrils caressed Oliver’s face, soothing his emotions:
"Ron Ralph... yes, he’s a threat, but he’s also an opportunity..."
"Opportunity?" Oliver’s voice was filled with doubt.
"There’s something special about his aura..." Cynthia mused thoughtfully:
"I’ve never been able to determine what it is, but ’Mr. Holy Disc’ seems to have a particular interest in him..."
"We need more energy..."
Cynthia interrupted Oliver’s thoughts:
"Before the Bloodline Altar opens, we must accumulate as much strength as possible to stabilize our symbiotic state..."
"Do you have a plan?"
Cynthia’s slit abdomen opened, emitting a burst of laughter:
"There are many abandoned mines in this area... They’re often visited by adventurers and treasure hunters..."
Oliver understood her meaning, tendril-eye shimmering with excited light: "Fresh prey..."
"Yes..." Cynthia’s voice grew even more low and hungry:
"Their lives... their pain and fear... will all become our nourishment..."
Their shared body started to wriggle towards the cave’s exit, leaving a trail of moist slime.
As they wriggled, the mutant tissue on the cave walls seemed to sense something, ceasing its twitching.

chapters.title: Chapter 284 - 185: Memory Fluid
chapters.content:
Chapter 284: Chapter 185: Memory Fluid
Ron lit the Magic Crystal Lamp in the workshop, its pale blue light dispelling the shadows of the night.
Lately, he has been focusing much of his attention on the "Sound Wave Vibration" magic he has long been researching.
This magic has been developed in the direction of "Erosion Chapter" through the ravings of the starry sky monster, "Zi...Kru...Niyage...Rotip...".
Yet, amidst constantly using this variant of the "Erosion Chapter," he can feel the ravings generated during meditation seem to be an extension of the monster’s ravings...
His current research direction is to further expand the "Erosion Chapter" based on the ravings during meditation while combating it.
Making it able to directly affect the magic model without the aid of instruments, usable in sudden encounters.
He stood up and paced the room for a moment, trying to clear his thoughts.
"Teacher, dinner is ready." Lily’s voice came from outside the door, interrupting his thoughts.
"I’ll be there shortly." Ron rubbed his temples, turned around, and opened the door.
Lily stood at the door, wearing a pale blue apron, her hair carrying the scent of food.
She looked curiously at the exhausted Ron: "Studying that magic again?"
"Yes, it’s still not going very well." Ron sighed and followed her towards the dining room.
In the dining room, Dale was already impatiently seated at the table, her big purple-blue eyes shining with anticipation.
Seeing Ron enter, she immediately jumped up:
"Master, I trained for five whole hours today without feeling tired! And the webbing between my fingers can retract completely now!"
She excitedly showed her little hands.
The membrane between her fingers was indeed gone, only a faint blue trace could be seen at her fingertips.
"Well done." Ron smiled and patted her silver hair, feeling a little more relaxed.
Ailan walked in from the courtyard, holding a plate of freshly picked berries.
Compared to her earlier tree spirit form, her appearance now barely revealed any non-human traits.
Only those emerald green eyes and the tendrils that occasionally stretched out from beneath her skirt in place of arms made her unusual.
"Tonight’s berries were ripened with my own pollen, should taste better."
Ailan said softly, placing the plate on the table, then walked over to Dale, kindly tidying her somewhat disheveled hair.
Seeing this warm scene, the gloom and urgency in Ron’s heart gradually lessened.
As they enjoyed dinner, Ron glanced at the six-string guitar that he had bought earlier and hung on the wall as decoration, and suddenly had a flash of inspiration.
Since the Erosion Chapter was played using an instrument, developing it further based on this method and constructing "Sound Wave Vibration" in magic construction as an instrument capable of producing sound...
Dale blinked:
"Is Master going to play music? I remember you seem to practice the violin often?"
"No, Dale."
Ron shook his head, eyes continuing to linger on the six-string guitar on the wall, a bold idea gradually forming in his mind.
"Perhaps I’ve found the breakthrough to improve the magic." His eyes sparkled with inspiration.
Lily followed his gaze to the six-string guitar: "Is it about the Erosion Chapter?"
"Exactly." Ron nodded, his thoughts increasingly clear:
"I have been trying to separate violin playing from magic model consideration, but if it can be constructed into the resonance structure of an instrument within the magic model..."
Ailan pondered: "You mean to make the magic model not just an energy structure but able to produce sounds?"
"Exactly!"
Ron’s eyes sparkled with excitement: "Just like a soundbox, but not formed physically, constructed by spiritual power instead."
After hastily finishing dinner, he immediately returned to the laboratory.
Inside, Ron stood at the center, took a deep breath, raised his hands slightly, and started to channel spiritual power.
The magic model of "Sound Wave Vibration" slowly took shape before him, a complex structure woven from countless energy threads, with a gradient of blue-violet.
"If the magic model is constructed into the resonance structure of a violin..."
Ron closed his eyes, recalling the internal construction of a violin—soundbox, bridge, strings, soundboard...each part has its own vibrational traits.
His spiritual power began to reshape the magic model following this thought.
First forming a cavity structure similar to a soundbox, then four strings of different frequencies, along with carefully designed "bridges" and "soundboards"...
"The difficulty in forming this structure lies in..."
Sweat beaded on Ron’s forehead: "Each part must possess specific energy density and vibrational traits."
After several attempts, the magic model finally presented a new form.
No longer just a mere energy assembly, but a miniature "mental instrument," its internal structure precisely mimicking the resonance principle of a violin.
"Now, try injecting the energy pattern of the ravings..."
Ron recalled the mysterious syllables heard in meditation, and melded their "tones" into the strings of the magic model.
With the infusion of spiritual power, those strings began vibrating at particular frequencies, producing a disturbing low raving sound.
"Zi...Kru...Niyage...Rotip..."
The sound does not transmit through physical media but directly forms on a spiritual level.

chapters.title: Chapter 285 - 185: Memory Fluid_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 285: Chapter 185: Memory Fluid_2
[Sound Wave Vibration (Proficient) Experience Points +1]
The moment the magic was triggered, Ron felt an unprecedented sense of control.
The entire magic model was like a precise instrument, producing a perfect "tone" under his spiritual power control.
Even more exciting, this structure no longer required the aid of physical instruments and could be fully constructed and released in advance.
"This is far beyond my expectations..."
He adjusted his breathing, deciding to try further.
If the first step was to transform the magic model into an instrument structure, then the second step was to expand the "melody" content.
Ron closed his eyes again, entering a meditative state, seeking more mysterious syllables from the depths of the starry sky.
His consciousness sank deeper into meditation, and the familiar starry scene unfolded before his eyes, countless stars flickering in the darkness.
But this time, he tried to go even deeper, letting his consciousness reach those regions emitting ravings.
"No need to reach the core, just capturing more syllable fragments..."
As the meditation went deeper, those stars seemed to come alive, starting to move according to some peculiar Rhythm, emitting more complex sounds.
"Zi... Klu... Nyag... Rotip... Sale... Hom..."
The new combinations of syllables resonated in his consciousness, each carrying an indescribable ancient power.
Ron cautiously recorded these new syllables while being alert to possible spiritual contamination.
Fortunately, with previous experience, he could better maintain his mental barrier to prevent those dangerous energies from directly affecting his mind.
Returning to reality, Ron immediately tried to integrate the newly gained syllables into the improved magic model.
"Constructing a soundbox... adjusting the strings... injecting a new syllable sequence..."
This time, the magic model became more complex. When the magic was released, six syllables sounded almost simultaneously, forming a short but powerful "composition."
The air in the training room seemed to twist because of this "composition," with some small objects starting to vibrate uncontrollably, and even a few books fell off the shelf.
"The power has indeed increased," Ron evaluated: "But the difficulty of control has also multiplied."
The new structure of more syllables needs extremely high precision of spiritual control.
"There’s hope!" Ron thought with joy, he moved to the training ground, and an invisible ripple spread from his palm, hitting the target across.
The target’s surface didn’t crack as usual; instead, it twisted bizarrely before beginning to dissolve in a strange manner.
It wasn’t physical fragmentation but a deeper kind of erosion, as if its material structure itself was being corroded by some force.
"Teacher?" Lilia’s voice came from the other side of the courtyard, with a hint of concern:
"It’s already late. Are you alright?"
"Come here, Lilia." Ron responded with a smile, his voice filled with undisguisable excitement:
"I think I’ve had a major breakthrough."
As Lilia approached, she was surprised to see the target slowly dissolving:
"What kind of spell effect is this?"
"Erosion Wave."
Ron explained with a strange gleam in his eyes: "I’ve succeeded in merging sound wave vibration with ravings."
He once again concentrated, constructing the improved "sound wave vibration" magic structure, this time targeting another target.
An invisible ripple spread out again, and the target’s surface was immediately covered with an eerie purple-black, then began to decompose from the inside.
This decomposition wasn’t ordinary physical destruction; it felt more like the target’s very "existence" was being consumed by some force.
"Oh my..." Lilia gasped: "This effect... is simply incredible."
"It’s not just that." Ron smiled slightly:
"This erosion effect should have additional impacts on living beings, especially on a spiritual level."
"But, Teacher..." Lilia hesitated for a moment:
"This power... feels somewhat off, are you sure it’s safe?"
Ron became serious:
"Every power has two sides, the key lies in the user’s control. How to harmlessly tame them through various experiments is also the meaning of research."
Lilia seemed to want to say more, but ultimately just nodded:
"You must be very tired, want to take a break? I brewed some calming tea."
Ron then realized that he was indeed exhausted, his forehead covered in cold sweat, and his hands trembling slightly.
Such high-intensity spiritual power control had clearly consumed a lot of his physical and spiritual strength.
"Thank you, Lilia." He accepted the teacup handed by the girl, sipping the warm liquid carefully, allowing his weary mind and body a moment of relaxation.
Early the next morning, Ron went to the workshop’s backyard again, preparing to test his discovery from last night.
Ailan was soothing a rare herb, which had shown restlessness after sensing the remnants of Ron’s magic.
"This erosive energy does make plants uncomfortable."
Ailan said softly, her fingers gently stroking the trembling leaves of the herb:
"They can sense a ripple not belonging to the original world."
Ron nodded, which exactly confirmed his hypothesis:
The impact of the erosion wave indeed transcended normal physical damage, reaching deeper into the existence of life forms.
"I need a sturdier target to test the effect." He looked around, finally locking his gaze on a stone pedestal.
It was one of the fixed targets, extremely sturdy and with certain anti-magic properties, making it hard for ordinary magic to cause noticeable damage.

chapters.title: Chapter 286 - 185: Memory Fluid_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 286: Chapter 185: Memory Fluid_3
"Master, are you going to cast a spell?"
Dale asked excitedly, her large purple-blue eyes shimmering with anticipation: "Can I help?"
"Just watch this time." Ron smiled as he patted her head:
"This new magic isn’t stable enough. For safety’s sake, all of you should stand back a little."
The three of them retreated to a safe distance. Ron took a deep breath and began to construct the magic model.
This time, he didn’t rush to release it. Instead, he first sorted through the rhythm of the ravings in his mind, allowing them to naturally merge into the energy structure of the sound wave vibration.
When the two types of energy reached perfect resonance, Ron suddenly opened his eyes and issued a command to the stone pedestal:
— Sound Wave Oscillation - Erosion State!
An invisible ripple spread out from his palm, striking the hard stone pedestal.
The surface of the pedestal didn’t immediately show signs of erosion as expected, but over time, a strange transformation began to appear:
The texture of the stone pedestal started to twist as if rearranged by some invisible force from within.
Dozens of seconds later, the entire stone pedestal suddenly emitted a muffled sound, surface densely covered with cracks, then imploded in a miraculous way, turning into a pile of dust.
"This... is simply unbelievable."
Lilia stared at the pile of dust in shock, her voice trembling slightly: "It looks like it was dissolved by some force from within."
"Amazing!" Dale clapped excitedly, her face full of admiration:
"Master’s magic is truly marvelous!"
Ailan remained silent, but a trace of worry flashed in her emerald eyes.
As a plant life form close to nature, she could more profoundly sense the terror contained in this magic.
Ron himself was also somewhat surprised.
This effect far exceeded his calculations, even he felt the power surged a bit too quickly.
The eroding sound waves not only destroyed the physical structure of the stone pedestal but seemed to affect some of its essence, causing it to lose the ability to maintain its form.
"This kind of effect..." he murmured to himself:
"It’s like ’concept erosion’ described in the Abyssal Creatures Atlas."
He recalled the descriptions from that forbidden book about the upper layers of the abyss.
The energy there no longer adheres to ordinary physical laws but directly influences the concept and essence of things.
The Erosion Chapter also seemed to exhibit similar traits, albeit to a much lesser extent.
He nodded to the three of them, signaling they could continue with their activities, and returned to the laboratory alone.
The progress was too fast... Was it because the effects of "ravings" and sound wave vibration were overly compatible?
Or had this set of introductory methods from the so-called "Crown Meditation Technique" begun to gradually show its unique terrifying traits?
In any case, at least for the current stage, the extending eroding effects of sound wave vibration undoubtedly provided him with a significant advantage in battle.
And with just six syllables, it could demonstrate such frightening power. If truly woven into a complete composition and then amplified with an amplifier, he couldn’t even imagine the effect...
......
"Dale, focus!"
In the training ground, Ron sternly watched the little sea siren who constantly got distracted.
Dale was trying hard to maintain the stable form of a water ball, but her attention was clearly elsewhere.
Specifically, on a batch of newly bloomed flowers that Ailan had planted on the other side of the courtyard.
"I’m sorry, Master."
Dale stuck out her tongue, a bit embarrassed as she withdrew her gaze and refocused on the water ball in front of her.
Ron shook his head and smiled wryly:
"Alright, today’s training is over for now. You can go look at those flowers, but don’t touch them; some might irritate the sea siren’s skin."
"Great! Thank you, Master!"
Dale cheered, the water ball instantly lost control and became a puddle, but the little sea siren had already hopped and skipped towards Ailan’s side.
Watching Dale’s departing figure, Ron sighed slightly.
The growth of the little sea siren was astonishing, but her attention was still easily distracted, which was an area he needed to focus on training.
"Since that’s the case, I can concentrate on practicing." Ron mumbled to himself as he took a small bag of fine sand from his pocket.
Ever since learning the "Flowing Shield Wall" magic from Hayek, he had invested a considerable amount of time into practice, but the progress was relatively slow.
This one-ring magic’s precision demands exceeded any spell he had encountered before.
Even with a complete magic model, truly mastering its essence remained incredibly challenging.
Ron poured a small handful of sand into his palm, took a deep breath, and began guiding his spiritual power into each tiny grain.
Although he had thought of using Soul Steel as a medium, at this early stage, he could only practice using basic materials.
Spiritual power fell like fine rain, evenly covering every grain of sand, causing them to float up and form a palm-sized small shield.
"First step successful..."
Ron maintained this state and then attempted to gradually expand the shield’s range while ensuring that the energy density in every area remained perfectly consistent.
This process tested the precision of spiritual control immensely; any fluctuation could cause the entire structure to collapse.
Just as the shield extended to about half a meter in diameter, a voice called from afar:
"Teacher, there’s a guest looking for you."
Ron’s attention was interrupted, the shield immediately wobbled, but he quickly adjusted his mindset and stabilized the energy flow.

chapters.title: Chapter 287 - 185: Memory Fluid_4
chapters.content:
Chapter 287: Chapter 185: Memory Fluid_4
"Who is it?" Ron did not turn around, still focused on stabilizing the shield wall.
"Prince Andre." Lilia answered, "He says he has an urgent message for you."
Andre’s visit was indeed unexpected, but Ron knew his old friend would not interrupt his research without reason.
It must be something important.
"Ask him to wait a moment, I’ll be there shortly."
Ron cautiously dispelled the magic, letting the grains of sand slowly fall back to the ground before turning to face Lilia.
The girl was curiously staring at the sand, clearly intrigued by the magic just performed.
"What kind of magic is that, teacher? It doesn’t look like an ordinary shield."
"Flowing Shield Wall, a more advanced form of protective magic."
Ron briefly explained, "At your current level, it’s too early to deal with this kind of magic. For now, let’s go meet Andre."
In the reception room, Andre, dressed in a simple robe, was sipping tea in small sips.
Seeing Ron enter, he immediately put down his cup, his face displaying a rare serious expression.
"Ron, I’ve looked into the matter you asked about." He got straight to the point:
"Lady Allen’s shop is indeed closed, but strangely, there are no official records of her departure within the school."
Ron frowned slightly.
Lady Allen’s departure was evidently more complicated than he had imagined.
"And there’s something even stranger."
Andre lowered his voice, "A protective barrier was set around the herb store to block spying. Ordinary apprentices passing by don’t even sense the shop’s existence, as if it has always been an empty lot."
Ron and Lilia exchanged a glance, reading the same confusion and concern in each other’s eyes.
"Do you need me to investigate further?"
Ron thought for a moment and shook his head:
"Not for now. Since Lady Allen is being so cautious, there must be a reason. Our interference might bring her unnecessary trouble."
He turned to Lilia, smiling slightly:
"Could you prepare some refreshments for us? Andre and I have some matters to discuss."
The two conversed for a while longer, mainly about their respective progress.
Andre also mentioned an important piece of news, that his father, the king, has been increasingly unwell recently.
It would be best if he remained in this state of illness, making it easier for Andre to seize the throne...
Sending off the Thirteenth Prince, Ron thought with some malice.
He then returned to the training ground, deciding to continue practicing the "Flowing Shield Wall."
This time, he did not use ordinary sand but retrieved a specially composed powder from the laboratory:
Mixed from particles of various attributes, theoretically forming a more comprehensive protective barrier.
"Let’s test this new medium..."
Ron poured a small handful of compound powder into his palm, beginning to channel spiritual power into it.
Unlike ordinary sand, this compound powder was more sensitive to spiritual power, yet harder to control.
Every different component required precise energy ratios, like playing a complex concerto, ensuring every part harmonized perfectly.
The synergy of multiple professions showcased its astonishing effects at this moment.
He could perceive and adjust every minor energy fluctuation with unprecedented precision.
Slowly and steadily, a translucent shield with a rainbow hue formed before him.
Unlike the monotonous transparency of a regular shield, this shield displayed flowing rainbow colors, each representing the energy fluctuations of different elements.
Once the entire shield stabilized, Ron began shaping it—a key feature of the Flowing Shield Wall.
Under the guidance of spiritual power, the shield transformed from a flat shield to a spherical encasement, then into a hexagonal prism, each shift smooth and natural without the slightest stiffness.
For the time being, Ron devoted a significant amount of time to practicing the Flowing Shield Wall.
He experimented with various mediums, from simple sand and water to complex metal powders, crystal stone powder, and even herbal extracts containing special energy.
Each medium required different spiritual control techniques, granting the shield different traits.
Water formed a flexible and elastic shield;
Metal powder structured a firm and rigid barrier;
Crystal stone powder offered specific energy resistance;
Herbal extracts bestowed the shield with certain healing or boosting effects.
During a joint training session with Dale and Lilia, Ron tried to use the Flowing Shield Wall to defend against Dale’s Water Arrow attack.
"Ready, Dale?"
Ron held a specially made handful of iron sand, prepared for casting.
"Anytime, Master!"
Dale excitedly waved her small hands, increasing the humidity around them as water molecules began to gather.
"Let’s begin!"
The Little Sea Siren suddenly waved her hand, dozens of crystal-clear water arrows attacking Ron from all directions.
Meanwhile, Ron rapidly crafted magic, a circular shield with a metallic sheen forming around him.
Water arrows struck the shield, making a series of crisp sounds, but none could penetrate the metal defense.
Ron sensed every impact, subtly adjusting the energy density of different shield sections to maintain its overall stability.
"Hit harder, Dale!"
Ron encouraged, while evaluating the shield’s durability in his mind.
The Little Sea Siren bit her lip, a mischievous glint in her eyes: "Be careful, Master!"
She clasped her hands together, then suddenly parted them, making the air around them instantly dry.
All water condensed into a gigantic water spear, over ten times larger than ordinary water arrows.
The spearhead crystallized into a thick layer of ice, glinting coldly in the sunlight.
"Amazing!" Lilia exclaimed from the side, never having seen Dale unleash such a powerful attack.
Ron was also taken aback but reacted swiftly.
He quickly reinforced the area of the shield where the water spear would hit, shaping the entire structure into an arc to better disperse the impact force.
"---Go!" Dale shouted, launching the giant water spear like a projectile, crashing into the shield heavily.
Boom!
A muffled sound echoed as energy ripples resonated across the shield, yet it remained intact.
The water spear ricocheted off, shattering into countless water drops in the air, scattering everywhere.
"Success!" Ron beamed with satisfaction.
It was then he noticed something peculiar:
The shield’s surface began to automatically adjust, becoming more solid, especially in the area that the water spear had struck.
"Strange... I didn’t actively adjust it..."
Ron closely observed this alteration, suddenly realizing what had occurred.
The shield seemed to have "remembered" the attack pattern and automatically reinforced the relevant area, preparing for a similar future assault.
[Tier One·Flowing Shield Wall (Novice) Experience Points +1]
[Breakthrough! Tier One·Flowing Shield Wall (Novice 50/50) → Tier One·Flowing Shield Wall (Proficient 1/100)]
[Additional Trait Acquired: Memory (The shield can have limited memory, actively defending against previously dealt attack types)]

chapters.title: Chapter 288 - 186: Morphing Resin
chapters.content:
Chapter 288: Chapter 186: Morphing Resin
"Memory..." Ron murmured to himself, his eyes sparkling with a glow of delight.
This added trait turns the Flowing Shield Wall from a passive defense tool into an adaptive protection system capable of self-learning and evolution.
As the number of uses increases, the Shield Wall will become increasingly difficult to breach, especially against repeated attacks of the same type.
"Dale, one more time!"
Ron instructed the other to continue attacking: "Use the same attack as before!"
Although the Little Sea Siren was somewhat confused, she complied nevertheless.
When the second identical massive Water Spear struck the Shield Wall, Ron deliberately made no additional reinforcements, only maintaining basic Spiritual Power input.
To everyone’s surprise, the Shield Wall easily repelled the attack, and this time there was almost no Energy Fluctuation, as if it had been prepared all along.
"Are you fully... mastering this advanced magic?"
Lilia gazed at the scene in disbelief, her voice filled with admiration.
"Not just that." Ron explained:
"Its defense effect is even stronger than I imagined, Dale’s attack power earlier has already reached a level comparable to the signature magic of an Advanced Apprentice."
He began pondering more possibilities of this ability:
If the Shield Wall is exposed to various different types of attacks—physical impact, flame scorch, frost freeze...
Could it gradually form a comprehensive defense system?
"Lilia, help me prepare some test devices." Ron turned to the young girl, his eyes sparkling with excitement:
"I need to test the limits of this memory ability."
In the following days, Ron dedicated himself to in-depth research on the Flowing Shield Wall.
He designed a series of tests, confronting the Shield Wall with various different types of attacks—Dale’s water-based assaults, Ailan’s manipulative plant lashes, and even elemental impacts simulated with Alchemy Device.
Each test confirmed the remarkable strength of Fluid Memory—the Shield Wall indeed "learns" and adapts to various attack patterns, becoming increasingly difficult to penetrate.
Moreover, this memory ability seems to have a certain degree of generalization.
For instance, after "learning" how to counter Dale’s Water Arrow, the Shield Wall exhibited improved resistance against other types of piercing shots, though not as perfect as against specifically learned attacks.
"It’s almost like possessing some primitive intelligence..."
Ron silently perceived the literal flow of it, watching the Shield Wall automatically adjust its structure to counter the new wave of attacks.
During the research, Ron also discovered another astonishing trait of the Flowing Shield Wall:
It could easily change form depending on the user’s intent, forming various complex geometric shapes.
This shaping ability not only helps to enhance the defensive effect but also endows the Shield Wall with more tactical uses.
In simulated combat, Ron successfully used the Flowing Shield Wall to capture a fast-moving target—a vine cluster controlled by Ailan.
The Shield Wall swiftly deformed from a flat Shield to a closed spherical cage, completely enveloping the vine inside.
"In the Bloodline Altar, the value of this ability is immeasurable."
Ron summarized as he looked at the special composite powder in his hand:
