```
"Why do you think he did that?" Trish curiously asked, a hint of confusion in her tone:
"Such a powerful wizard, shouldn’t need to display their power in this way, right?"
"Perhaps...he was giving us a lesson."
Ron mused: "For true upper echelons, just a thought can shatter the body and mind of the weak."
The apprentices in the square gradually dispersed, returning to their posts or accommodations.
But Ron noticed that everyone’s eyes had subtly changed, with some becoming more determined, their eyes ignited with the flame of pursuing strength.
The arrival of the Dark Sun Wizard, in a way, changed these young apprentices’ worldview.
"Ron, what are you thinking about?" Trish watched his dazed expression and asked curiously.
"I was thinking..." Ron’s voice was deep, a rare eagerness flashing in his eyes:
"The Crystal Tower...what kind of place is it truly? The knowledge, resources, and opportunities there must far exceed what we can imagine, to cultivate such existences."
Trish nodded, a hint of yearning flashing in her eyes as well.
The two walked in silence on the way back, each immersed in thoughts of their future paths.
Occasionally, other apprentices would pass by, each casting envious glances towards them:
The qualification to participate in the trial of the Bloodline Altar was an honor in itself.

chapters.title: Chapter 300 - 192: Hand of a Hundred Arts
chapters.content:
Chapter 300: Chapter 192: Hand of a Hundred Arts
In a spacious conference room at the Central Tower of the Black Mist Jungle, five Candidate Wizard sequenced members face Vice Dean Hayek and several Masters, their expressions solemn.
"You five have been selected to participate in this Bloodline Altar trial." Hayek’s voice was steady and authoritative:
"This is both an honor and a challenge. The environment inside the altar is complex, filled with danger, but also endless opportunities."
Ron and the other four—Trish, Holt, and two other sequence members he’s not very familiar with—stood in a line, bodies straight, expressions focused.
"Considering the uniqueness of the trial, the School has decided to provide necessary equipment support to each participant."
Hayek waved his hand, and Soron stepped forward, holding five exquisite velvet bags.
"These are specially crafted spatial bags," Soron explained as he distributed them:
"Each can accommodate about five cubic meters of items, much more than ordinary space equipment."
Ron accepted the soft deep blue bag, feeling the peculiar energy fluctuation emanating from it.
The bag appeared ordinary, only palm-sized, yet it could hold so many items; it was indeed a rare strategic resource.
"Of course, this advanced equipment is the property of the School," Hayek added, his gaze sharp:
"After the trial, the School will take thirty percent of the value of any items withdrawn from inside as a usage fee. This is a fair exchange."
Ron examined the spatial bag in his hand closely, already calculating in his mind.
This equipment was indeed precious, but the 30% ’tax rate’ was not low either.
"There is another option," Soron continued:
"You can also choose not to use the spatial bags provided by the School and prepare equipment entirely on your own. Of course, this means you will lose this convenience, and anything taken from the altar will be entirely yours."
After the meeting concluded, the five members each left to prepare their own equipment.
Ron headed straight to the School’s trading center, his mind clear with a plan.
The trading center is located on the eastern side of the School, a semicircular white building where various resource transactions occur frequently.
Ron smoothly threaded through the bustling crowd, arriving at a counter labeled "Rare Material Exchange."
"I need Black Sand Essence," Ron stated directly to the staff behind the counter:
"The smallest size."
The opposite was an elderly woman, with graying hair but unusually sharp eyes.
She looked Ron up and down, seemingly assessing the reliability of this young apprentice.
"Black Sand Essence?" She raised an eyebrow, "That is not a common commodity, young man. Even the smallest size requires two whole Magic Stones."
"I know the price," Ron calmly took out two prepared whole Magic Stones from his pocket:
"I demand impeccable quality, any flaw will not suffice."
After the transaction was complete, Ron briskly returned to the workshop.
Even though he felt some pain giving away two Magic Stones, this investment was necessary for the upcoming plan.
"Spent so many Magic Stones again..."
Ron looked at the thumb-sized dark red crystal in his hand, sighed lightly: "Magic Stones really don’t last long."
Inside the workshop, Ron quickly entered the laboratory to begin preparing to refine his own spatial bag.
Black Sand Essence is a unique ’Abyssal Material’ from the first layer of the Abyss and the key material for making space equipment, containing natural spatial folding traits.
The essence of refining a spatial bag is to draw out the spatial energy from Black Sand Essence and fix it onto a specific carrier.
He took a piece of high-quality Sub-dragon Hide and cut it into the appropriate shape according to a specific pattern.
"This process is much simpler than I imagined." Ron murmured to himself, skillfully drawing complex runes on the Sub-dragon Hide:
"It’s even easier than making an Alchemy Bomb."
The key lies in the layout of the guide lines and the construction of the initial space.
Black Sand Essence itself has spatial attributes; it’s just necessary to establish the correct energy guiding path and activate it through specific alchemy reactions to form a stable small sub-space.
Ron’s fingers deftly purified several rare alchemy materials to their most suitable state and accurately adorned crucial nodes on the surface of the Sub-dragon Hide.
The "Material Refining" skill played a significant role at this moment, allowing him to intuitively feel the interaction between materials and precisely control every reaction link.
Three hours later, a small dark brown bag lay quietly on the lab bench, its surface faintly showing flickering rune patterns.
He carefully reached into the mouth of the bag, feeling his arm seemingly enter an invisible space far beyond the capacity the bag’s exterior size could hold.
"Succeeded!" Ron’s eyes showed a sense of accomplishment: "Its capacity is even a third larger than the ones provided by the School."
He took out a pocket watch to check the time.
There were less than twelve hours left until the official commencement of the Bloodline Altar, and he needed to urgently complete the remaining preparations.
Meanwhile, at the top tier of the administrative tower of the Black Mist School, Thompson stood inside Hayek’s office, holding a thick file.
"This is my observational report on Ron Ralph."
Thompson handed the file to Hayek, his voice calm but with an obvious note of admiration: "I believe you should personally review it."
Hayek took the file and quickly flipped through it.
As he read deeper, his brows gradually furrowed, his eyes revealing a flash of surprise.
"Alchemy Bomb? He successfully made an Alchemy Bomb?"

chapters.title: Chapter 301 - 192: Hand of a Hundred Arts (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 301: Chapter 192: Hand of a Hundred Arts (Part 2)
Hayek looked up at Thompson, his tone filled with disbelief:
"This kind of technique usually requires at least ten years of alchemy study to master."
"Not only that," Thompson added:
"He also successfully refined a spatial bag. As far as I know, he just exchanged for a Black Sand Essence at the trading center, probably intending to make the space equipment himself."
Hayek lowered his head and was silent for a moment, placing the document on the table.
"This young man’s alchemy has already reached the level of a professional alchemist, and his progress far exceeds the norm."
He pondered and said, "This seems incongruent with the ’Medicinal Body Resonance’ talent recorded in his file."
At that moment, the office door was gently knocked on, and then Valen appeared at the door.
"Sorry to interrupt, Hayek."
The Dark Sun Wizard smiled warmly: "I came to get some historical material on the bloodline altar."
"Master Valen, please come in." Hayek immediately stood up to welcome him, while Thompson bowed and exited through a hidden door: "Coincidentally, there’s something I wish to consult with you."
Valen walked into the room, his gaze falling on the documents on the table, seemingly having sensed something from Hayek’s expression.
"Is it about the young member in the sequence?" he asked softly.
Hayek briefly introduced Ron’s situation, especially highlighting his extraordinary performance in alchemy, Magic Potion Making, bloodline modulation, and other areas.
"Recently, he has not only been able to make alchemy bombs but also mastered the technique for making space equipment, and all this within just a few months."
Hayek concluded: "Such a speed of progress is unprecedented in my teaching career."
A rare look of surprise flashed in Valen’s eyes. He took the document and looked through it carefully again, his expression gradually becoming deep.
"Interesting... very interesting."
The Dark Sun Wizard slowly spoke:
"This comprehensive extraordinary talent reminds me of some rarer types of talents... ’Natural History’, ’Enlightened Ones’, ’Eye of Wisdom’, or perhaps the ’Hand of a Hundred Arts’..."
"You mean... he might have those talents rarer than ’Medicinal Body Resonance’?" Hayek asked in astonishment.
"Very possibly." Valen nodded:
"Especially the ’Hand of a Hundred Arts’, a talent allowing the possessor to swiftly master any skill upon contact, is one of the most precious among the second tier talents."
The room fell into brief silence as both pondered the implications of this discovery.
"In any case," Valen eventually broke the silence:
"Such a genius should not be missed. Hayek, I suggest placing him on the priority observation list."
"Already arranged," Hayek responded:
"If he truly possesses such rare talents, the upper levels of the Crystal Tower will certainly be interested in him."
A gleam of insight flickered in Valen’s eyes:
"Yes, talents like these should serve a broader stage."
He paused briefly, his voice becoming lower:
"I have a suggestion—when he approaches the threshold of becoming an Official Wizard, do not easily give him the ’Key Potion’, even if his hope for promotion is higher than the top of the sequence."
"You mean..." A hint of understanding flashed in Hayek’s eyes.
"Yes, have him sign a soul contract for lifelong service to our Crystal Tower in exchange for the ’Key Potion’."
Valen said calmly: "Such a genius must be closely bound to our Crystal Tower."
Hayek pondered briefly and finally nodded in agreement:
"I understand, Master Valen, I will closely monitor his development."
......
The day when the bloodline altar is opened has finally arrived.
On the great square in the central region of the School, an inconspicuous circular stone platform had now become the focal point of the ceremony.
Around the stone platform, complex array patterns emitted a ghostly blue glow, and the air was filled with an ancient and mysterious energy fluctuation.
Valen stood in the center of the stone platform, accompanied by Hayek and several other Wizards.
Surrounded by dozens of Apprentices, all here to witness the event.
Ron and four other candidates stood at specific positions on the edge of the array, each having a small array node in front of them, connected to the central large array.
The ten Apprentices from the Crystal Tower were also in position, their attire noticeably different from the Black Mist School’s Apprentices:
Their more exquisite robes were embroidered with complex runes, adorned with various refined alchemy equipment.
Among them, some had skin with a metallic sheen, eyes glittering with strange runes, and arms seemingly capable of extension and transformation.
These were manifestations of bloodline mutation, indicating they had undergone various degrees of self-modification.
Although these Apprentices from the Central Lands behaved courteously, without demonstrating any disdain.
Ron still sensed an intrinsic superiority in their conduct and speech—a confidence and composure deriving from a long-term presence in resource-rich environments.
"Don’t be nervous," Trish’s voice came from beside him:
"We’ve all agreed to find each other and form a team once we’re inside."
Ron only nodded: "I am fully prepared."
He lightly patted the spatial bag he made, which contained various Magic Potions, alchemy tools, and emergency supplies.
Holt also approached with a solemn expression:
"I heard this trial is different from usual, possibly involving deeper abyss influences, everyone must be cautious."
Valen’s voice suddenly rang out across the square, clear and powerful, without using any amplification magic, yet audible to everyone.
"The bloodline altar originates from a captured special space fragment."
The Dark Sun Wizard’s voice carried a calming power:
"Due to the plane collision, it has some connection with the abyss, yet does not entirely belong to the abyss. This unique nature makes it an ideal site for bloodline purification and trial."
Valen walked slowly to the center of the array, continuing his explanation:
"Once inside the altar, you will be randomly scattered to different areas. There, you will face various challenges—entanglement from vengeful spirits, attacks from abyss creatures, and minor effects of abyss curses."
His gaze swept over each participant:
"Your goal is to traverse these obstacles, reach the central region of the bloodline altar world, and complete the final trial. Upon success in the trial, you can either open the exit or evoke the emblem I give to teleport away, which will be considered an automatic withdrawal from the trial. The content of the trial differs each time, and this time is no exception."
Ron listened intently, committing every detail to memory.
"You may wonder why Official Wizards don’t personally participate in such trials."
Valen seemingly foresaw the question many present held:
"This is due to the rule set by the Great Wizard who captured this space fragment—the bloodline altar is only open to Apprentices who have not reached the level of Official Wizards."
He explained:
"On one hand, the bloodline enhancement effect within the altar is almost negligible for Official Wizard level improvement;
On the other hand, it represents a tradition of giving to the younger generation, embodying a kind of ’ancient rule.’
Therefore, entities with the strength of Official Wizards cannot pass through the spatial channel connecting to the altar."
Ron was thoughtful, understanding why such a precious resource was reserved for Apprentice usage.
This was both a legacy and an investment in the future of young people, through which the Great Wizard could continuously harvest "benefits."
"Now." Valen’s voice took on a solemn tone: "The bloodline altar trial officially begins!"
As his words fell, the stone platform in the center of the array suddenly emitted dazzling blue light.
The energy beams extended from the center outward, connecting to each participant’s standing node.
Ron felt a wave of dizziness, as everything in his vision began to twist and warp.
His consciousness seemed to be stretched, twisted, and then thrown into an endless void.
In this void, he vaguely saw a massive crack, deep and dark, emanating a chilling aura.
That was the entrance to the abyss, with dark chaotic fumes swirling out, like countless tendrils reaching out to engulf him.
Ron felt an indescribable oppression, as if an invisible force was attempting to invade his spirit and bloodline.
This was the abyssal curse, striving to leave an imprint on him.
"Resist... must resist..."
Ron silently chanted in his heart, while mobilizing all his Spiritual Power to erect a defensive barrier.
Just as he was about to be swallowed by the darkness, a beam of light suddenly appeared from the other side of the void, like a path of life guiding him forward.
Without hesitation, Ron darted towards the golden light, feeling his consciousness fiercely pulled, and then...
Amidst a whirlwind, his feet finally touched solid ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 302 - 193: Activated Ruins
chapters.content:
Chapter 302: Chapter 193: Activated Ruins
In an instant, a strong sense of distortion and tearing swept over his entire body.
This feeling was far more intense than he imagined—as if every inch of skin was simultaneously pierced by countless fine needles, and every nerve was pulled to the limit.
Space folded, twisted, and reassembled in front of his eyes, and countless illusions and residual shadows appeared in his view.
In his daze, he seemed to see countless horrified faces wailing in the darkness, as if hearing the whispers and snickers of some ancient language.
"Concentrate!"
Ron forced himself to stay alert; the experience from the last simulation battle device immediately made him realize that the curse was taking effect.
Abyssal curse!
Unlike the simulated effect in the simulation battle device, the real curse was more complex and multi-layered.
He could feel his flesh creeping, as if countless tiny creatures were crawling under the skin.
At the same time, his thoughts began to become chaotic, with various bizarre ideas constantly emerging, trying to erode his sanity.
It was as if he was simultaneously afflicted by a dual curse of physical mutation and spiritual distortion.
Ron immediately activated his bloodline power, a strong surge of heat erupted within him, the power of the Red Blood Flying Dragon swept through his body like flames.
The strong bloodline power of the Dragon Species was like a barrier, temporarily resisting those strange changes trying to erode his flesh.
Meanwhile, he quickly entered a meditation state, spiritual power circulated within him, forming a special mental defense.
"Zi...krulu...niag..."
He also silently recited the syllables of the Erosion Chapter, using this mysterious power from the starry sky to counter the curse from the abyss.
This method of fighting poison with poison was surprisingly effective—the twisting forces from two completely different sources counteracted each other within him, allowing him to remain clear-headed.
"The effect is better than expected." Ron relaxed slightly in his heart.
Last time in the simulation battle device, it was the simulated curse of the third and fourth layers of the abyss.
And now, what he was facing, although it combined the dual effects of body and spirit, seemed to be much weaker, probably only equivalent to the first and second layers.
As he pondered, the teleportation process finally ended.
The distorted space around him gradually stabilized, and an unfamiliar world unfolded before his eyes.
Ron stood on a bizarre plain.
The ground was some semi-coagulated dark red substance, slightly elastic underfoot, like stepping on a thin meat carpet.
The sky presented an unnatural purple-black color.
No sun, no moon, only some oddly-shaped dark clouds floating, occasionally flashed with faint red lightning.
In the distance, some twisted and deformed mountain outlines loomed, those "peaks" looked more like the curled backs of some giant creature.
More unsettling was that the entire environment seemed to be "alive":
The ground faintly fluctuated with the breath, the air was filled with a fishy-sweet smell, as if standing inside some gigantic creature.
"Is this inside the Bloodline Altar..."
Ron cautiously surveyed the surroundings, carefully using spiritual power to probe the energy fluctuations around him.
After confirming the area was safe, he quickly opened the spatial bag.
"Dale, come out."
After a slight spatial fluctuation, the silver-haired Little Sea Siren emerged from the spatial bag.
As soon as she appeared, she noticeably felt uncomfortable.
Her large violet-blue eyes immediately widened, and her slender body began to tremble violently.
"Mas... Master..." Dale’s voice was hoarse and painful: "Here... feels awful..."
Ron immediately supported the Little Sea Siren, who almost collapsed.
"Endure it, Dale, this is the influence of the abyssal curse, don’t resist it, learn to adapt."
Dale nodded, but her skin had already begun to show unnatural changes:
Small patches appeared as grayish-white, as if rapidly dehydrating.
Ron quickly retrieved a bottle of light blue potion from the storage bag, which he had prepared in advance.
"Drink this, it’s the ’Abyss Adaptation Agent’, it can help reduce the effect of the curse."
Dale tremblingly received the bottle and gulped the potion down her throat in one go.
The effects were almost instantaneous—her skin gradually returned to its normal color, and her breathing stabilized.
"Thank you, Master..." Dale softly said, her voice much steadier than before, albeit still carrying fear:
"This place... is even scarier than I imagined."
"This is just the beginning." Ron solemnly warned:
"The road ahead will only get harder. But don’t be afraid, remember everything I’ve taught you, we can pass this trial."
The Little Sea Siren nodded resolutely, trying to stand straight.
"Master, this place... feels like... a battlefield?"
She looked around, puzzled.
This indeed seemed like the remains of an ancient battlefield, but distorted by the power of the abyss.
Numerous twisted and deformed metal fragments were scattered on the ground.
Those which might have been shields, spears, or swords, had now fused into the ground, morphing into malformed protrusions.
Some giant bones protruded from the ground, but they clearly were not human bones—too massive and twisted, their shapes too strange to recognize.
Further away, remnants of banners half-buried in the blood-colored soil swayed lightly in the wind.
The insignia on them were blurred, but several different national or racial symbols could be faintly discerned.
"You’re right, Dale. This should be an ancient battlefield eroded by abyssal power."
Ron crouched down and lightly touched the ground with his sword tip.
The layer that appeared to be soil cracked open a seam, revealing dark red muscle-like fibers underneath.

chapters.title: Chapter 303 - 193: Activated Ruins_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 303: Chapter 193: Activated Ruins_2
"This soil... should be said to be a kind of living tissue. The whole space has been transformed by Abyssal Power, becoming some kind of semi-living existence."
Dale shivered slightly, instinctively drawing closer to Ron, speaking in a barely audible whisper:
"So... we are now standing on the body of some... gigantic creature?"
"More like the entire battlefield has been imbued with some twisted ’life.’"
Ron explained:
"The ’Abyssal Creatures Atlas’ mentions similar phenomena—the Abyss Fourth Layer can transform death zones into ’Activated Ruins,’ a form that condenses death and decay into a special energy shape."
As they conversed, the distant ground suddenly began to heave violently, and a massive object emerged from the blood-red soil.
It was a misshapen corpse, standing at least two meters tall.
Covered in rusted ancient armor, but the armor and the flesh have completely merged, indistinguishable.
Its head showcased a bizarre hybrid form:
The basic contour of a human skull, yet bearing four glowing eyes, with a jaw extending into a lizard-like shape, full of sharp teeth.
Most terrifyingly, its chest had a huge opening, inside which squirmed countless tentacle-like organs, occasionally extending out as if sniffing the surrounding air.
"Master! What is that?" Dale stared fearfully at the colossal being.
"Forgotten Warrior..." Ron replied in a low voice, a hint of caution flashing in his eyes:
"But unlike the original low-level undead, this creature is a fusion of undead traits and multiple alien bloodlines, an Abyssal mutant."
He quickly drew his sword, simultaneously retrieving a potion from his waist, swiftly gulping it down to enhance his abnormal resistance.
"Watch out for its tentacles, they might carry corrosive toxins."
The Forgotten Warrior had evidently noticed their presence.
Its four glowing eyes simultaneously turned towards them, emitting lights of various colors.
It let out a deafening roar, a sound mixed with piercing noise and some deep resonance, like thousands of souls wailing in unison.
"Master, let me handle this!" Dale was already prepared for battle, swiftly condensing the Water Element between her hands.
"Act according to plan." Ron commanded in a deep tone: "Your resistance isn’t strong enough; I’ll approach with the Shield, you handle remote disruption and support."
Before the words were out, the Forgotten Warrior strode heavily towards them.
Each step left deep gouges on the blood-colored earth, the soil around it responding to its movement by writhing, as if echoing its existence.
Ron did not retreat; instead, he charged forward.
"Ring of Brilliance!"
Golden-red light flames burst from his body, forming a dazzling armor that clung invisibly around him.
The Forgotten Warrior suddenly swung a massive arm.
The deformed limb, fused with armor, was covered in sharp bone spikes, capable of piercing an ordinary person in one blow.
Ron agilely sidestepped the attack, simultaneously slashing his sword in an arc, precisely targeting the opening in the Forgotten Warrior’s chest.
The cores of such monsters are often hidden within these special structures.
As the longsword pierced in, the Forgotten Warrior let out a painful howl.
The tentacle-like organs abruptly wrapped around, attempting to drag the weapon and its wielder into the chest cavity.
But upon contact with the "Ring of Brilliance" defense net, they immediately emitted a sizzling noise reminiscent of grilling squid on an iron plate...
"Dale, now’s the time!"
The Little Sea Siren sprang into action, her hands moving swiftly.
Moisture in the surrounding air rapidly gathered, forming dozens of sharp ice blades.
"Crystal Arrow Rain!"
The ice blades shot like arrows at the Forgotten Warrior, accurately severing the tentacles extending from its chest, cutting them one by one.
The Forgotten Warrior staggered back, the severed tentacles spewing a foul-smelling black liquid, which upon hitting the ground instantly corroded it, sizzling into small pits.
Ron took the opportunity to swiftly distance himself from the enemy.
He had already noticed the severed tentacles were regenerating at a visible rate.
"This is the regeneration ability of Abyssal creatures... We must find its core."
He carefully observed the movement patterns of the Forgotten Warrior.
This Abyssal mutant, blending various alien traits, far surpassed ordinary creatures in strength and defense.
In addition to its dreadful regenerating ability, conventional attack methods could hardly yield a lasting effect.
"It’s time to use that move... Hope my previous thinking wasn’t wrong."
Ron took a deep breath, quickly constructing a complex Magic Model with his Spiritual Power.
"Sound Wave Oscillation - Erosion State!"
An invisible wave emanated from his palm, enveloped in the eerie ravings from the starry sky depth, directly striking the Forgotten Warrior.
Almost instantly, the Forgotten Warrior’s movements became sluggish.
Its body surface appeared countless black spots, as if being corroded by some invisible force.
The tentacles within its chest flailed madly, seemingly trying to shake off this abnormal state, but the effect was minimal.
"It’s working!" Ron felt a surge of joy.
As with the previous encounter with the Half-blooded Serpent Demon, the ravings’ mysterious energy from the starry sky indeed had a strange suppressive effect on Abyssal creatures, like some natural bane.
The Forgotten Warrior let out a howl of agony, its body armor starting to peel away, revealing the decayed flesh beneath.
Its four eyes flickered with struggling light, then it made a surprising move:
It suddenly plunged a hand into its own chest cavity, retrieving a crystal emitting a purple glow, unmistakably its core.

chapters.title: Chapter 304 - 193: Activated Ruins_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 304: Chapter 193: Activated Ruins_3
Unexpectedly, the forgotten warrior stuffed the crystal into his mouth and began to chew it vigorously!
"Is it... committing suicide?" Dale was momentarily bewildered by the seemingly foolish act.
"He’s trying to make the core explode!" Ron immediately understood the warrior’s intention.
The crystal shattered in the forgotten warrior’s mouth, and purple energy dispersed into the air like smoke.
The next moment, the forgotten warrior’s body began to swell dramatically, with countless cracks appearing on the surface of his skin, from which purple light shone through.
"Run!"
Ron grabbed Dale, swiftly pulling away while constructing the sturdiest Flowing Shield Wall.
Boom!
The forgotten warrior’s body exploded in an instant, transforming into a purple-black energy cloud that spread in all directions.
The Flowing Shield Wall blocked most of the impact, but some energy penetrated the defense, forming a strange blood mist in the air.
Just as Ron was about to check on the Little Sea Siren in his arms, a peculiar movement caught his attention.
The Stand-In Puppet at his waist seemed to have developed its own reaction, emitting a faint suction.
The next moment, the purple-black blood mist was rapidly drawn into the puppet, as if it were conscious.
"What’s this...?" Ron immediately sensed the anomaly.
The Stand-In Puppet hung quietly at his waist, but its surface had already undergone a subtle transformation.
A layer of faint purple lines appeared on the originally smooth surface, sprawling over the entire puppet like veins.
At the same time, the puppet seemed to be slowly absorbing the energy from the blood mist, with its faint energy indicator slightly brightening.
Ron immediately checked the status of the Stand-In Puppet:
[Actively absorbed active Abyssal Material, charging progress +1%]
[Current energy: 3%/100%]
"It... absorbed the Abyssal energy and autonomously charged?"
Previously, the demonic puppet also reacted and completed charging during experiments with the live tissues of the scorpion and snake demon.
But this behavior of autonomously absorbing energy during battle to complete charging did indeed surprise him a bit.
He gently inserted a trace of Spiritual Power, trying to awaken the Stand-In Puppet.
The puppet reacted instantly, but this time its transformation speed and smoothness surpassed those of the past.
Moreover, its shape changes were more diverse.
The previously fused traits of the snake demon and scorpion seemed to have been enhanced somehow.
"The energy of the Abyssal creatures seems to have strengthened its ability to metamorphose..." Ron mused.
If the Stand-In Puppet could autonomously absorb and integrate the traits of Abyssal creatures, then perhaps it could reach its charging goal more quickly.
He carefully put away the Stand-In Puppet, feeling more hopeful about the journey ahead.
"Master, are you okay?" Dale asked with concern.
"I’m fine," Ron replied, snapping out of his earlier surprise:
"But we need to be more cautious. The monsters here are clearly different from regular Abyssal creatures, their self-destructive behavior... is very unusual."
The Little Sea Siren nodded firmly: "Don’t worry, Master, I will be more careful."
Ron carefully observed the surroundings, looking for possible clues or targets.
On this distorted battlefield, there must be a core somewhere.
Finding it and completing the trial is the purpose of this journey.
But for now, understanding the rules of this environment is more urgent to better handle the challenges ahead.
......
Meanwhile, Trish had also been teleported to another area of the Bloodline Altar.
After a dizzying whirl, the brown-haired girl found herself in a strange swampy area.
Unlike the battlefield where Ron was, the ground here was covered with a thick dark green liquid, emitting a pungent stench.
The sky appeared a sickly yellow-green, with bizarre flying creatures occasionally swooping by, emitting screeching cries.
"Abyssal curse..."
Trish immediately felt the suffocating pressure, as if her muscles and bones were being slowly twisted by some force.
But as Corina’s student, she had long undergone special training to resist the influence of the Abyss.
"Isolation Barrier!"
A pale green Energy Barrier spread from her body, forming a translucent protective shield that temporarily resisted the erosion of the Abyssal curse.
Trish looked around and found a slightly luminous stone monument not far from the center of the swamp, with complex rune patterns carved on it.
"That stone monument might be related to whether I can reach the core area."
The key to the passage to the core altar might be within it.
But the problem was, between her location and the monument was a vast, bottomless swamp, stepping in rashly was tantamount to suicide.
She took a small bottle from her waist and drank the liquid inside.
This was an adaptation potion specially prepared for her by Master Corina, allowing her to move freely in such environments temporarily.
The effect of the potion was almost immediate.
A faint green glow appeared on the surface of her skin, and the flow of blood in her body became more rapid and forceful.
"I hope this is enough to reach the monument."
Trish cautiously stepped onto the swamp surface, letting her toes gently touch the viscous green liquid.
Surprisingly, under the effect of the potion, her body became exceptionally light, almost able to float on the swamp surface instead of sinking into it.
"Master’s potion... truly lives up to the Crystal Tower’s technology."
She continued to advance cautiously, staying vigilant.
This "miracle" wouldn’t last long, and she needed to reach the target quickly.

chapters.title: Chapter 305 - 193: Activated Ruins_4
chapters.content:
Chapter 305: Chapter 193: Activated Ruins_4
Just as she approached halfway to the stone monument, the swamp suddenly began to churn violently.
A massive creature slowly rose from the mud, its body composed of countless small corpses assembled together, emitting a nauseating stench of decay.
Its "skin" was made up of countless tendrils and vines, constantly writhing, extending and contracting as if alive.
The head was a gigantic flower-like structure, with a large mouth full of sharp teeth at its center.
"Swamp Assembler..." Trish’s face turned pale as she recognized the terrifying abyssal creature:
"Why would a creature from the Abyss’s second layer appear here?"
The Swamp Assembler had clearly noticed her, the "flower" turned in her direction, emitting a peculiar buzzing sound.
Then its entire body began moving towards her, with every step, small parts of corpses fell off its body, only to be replaced by new tissue immediately.
Trish knew she couldn’t possibly face such a terrifying creature head-on.
The only option was to reach the stone monument as quickly as possible, complete the task, and leave the area.
Unlike Ron, she couldn’t bring a combat partner into the altar.
The strict rules of the Bloodline Altar limited each participant to enter alone, only Ron, with his champion privileges, was allowed to bring an assistant.
Faced with the crisis, Trish could only rely on her own abilities.
She swiftly awakened the dormant Forest Elf bloodline in her, a surge of green energy rushed out from within her, quickly spreading around.
The energy seeped into the depths of the swamp, establishing connections with those mutated plant lives.
Moments later, dozens of massive vines suddenly shot up from the swamp, each as thick as a child’s arm, with sharp thorns covering their surface.
Under Trish’s spiritual guidance, these vines whipped towards the Swamp Assembler like flexible whips, temporarily ensnaring it.
"This should buy some time."
Trish didn’t stop but rather quickened her pace towards the stone monument.
The Swamp Assembler let out an enraged roar, its immense strength causing the vines to start snapping one by one.
But each vine that snapped was quickly replaced by two new ones sprouting from the swamp, continuing to entwine around its body.
Seizing the opportunity, she traced a complex symbol with her hands over her chest, chanting a spell.
"Vines of the swamp, heed my call, become my shield and spear!"
Countless vines erupted from the swamp, twining around her like long green serpents.
Meanwhile, Holt’s situation wasn’t any less grim.
He had been transported to a canyon-like setting, with towering cliffs on either side, yet those "rocks" appeared more like some kind of fossilized gigantic bones.
The sky was an unnatural orange-red, as if under the perpetual glow of sunset, although no sun was visible.
The air was laden with a metallic taste, each breath seeming to inhale fine iron filings.
"The power of the curse... is stronger than expected."
Holt felt the abyss influencing him, the nausea and dizziness nearly causing him to collapse.
But he quickly regained control over his state.
As a member of the Law Enforcement Team, he had undergone specialized anti-interference training, enabling him to remain calm in extreme environments.
"Earth Elemental Golem, appear!"
Holt quickly retrieved a crystal stone from his storage bag, and upon infusing it with spiritual power, a five-meter-tall Earth Elemental Golem rose from the ground.
Its entire body was deep brown, covered with a tough stone-like armor.
Holt’s strength almost entirely depended on this Earth Elemental Golem.
As an Earth Element Specialization expert, he dedicated all his research and resources to this field.
Making his golem far superior to other constructs of the same class in terms of strength, defense, and durability.
"Start the exploration."
He commanded the golem to lead the way while he followed cautiously, vigilantly observing the surroundings.
The canyon was deathly silent, the only sound being their footsteps echoing between the stone walls.
Holt noticed some strange white crystals scattered across the ground.
Upon closer inspection, he was surprised to find they seemed to be some kind of crystallized bone tissue.
"These should be crystalized bones, mentioned in the Abyssal Creatures Atlas; they typically appear in certain areas of the Abyss’s 3rd Floor, known as the ’Field of Dead Bones’..."
After repeatedly verifying that it was harmless through various tests, he cautiously collected the crystal into his storage bag, as it could be a valuable research material.
Proceeding for about half an hour, the canyon gradually widened, eventually opening into a circular basin.
In the center of the basin stood a stone structure resembling an altar.
Surrounding it were seven tall stone pillars, each topped with a floating red crystal, emitting a faint glow.
"That’s the control point."
Holt was about to approach the altar when he suddenly felt a mild tremor under his feet.
The trembling grew increasingly intense, soon the entire basin was shaking violently, as if an earthquake had struck.
The Earth Elemental Golem immediately assumed a defensive stance, arms crossed in front of its chest, bracing for impact.
The ground in the center of the basin suddenly split open, and a massive figure burst from underground.
It was a gigantic worm-like creature, at least twenty meters long and over three meters in diameter.
Its body surface was covered with thick bone-like armor, forming ring-shaped protective layers, appearing impregnable.
The head had no eyes, only a circular mouth.
Inside were rows of circular saw-like teeth, constantly rotating with a chilling grinding noise.
"Bone Worm..." Holt’s voice trembled:
"One of the predators of the Abyss’s 3rd Floor..."
The worm seemed to sense the presence of intruders.
It swayed slightly before lunging towards Holt with astonishing speed.

chapters.title: Chapter 306 - 194: Wind Listener
chapters.content:
Chapter 306: Chapter 194: Wind Listener
Ron and Dale cautiously moved through the twisted battlefield, constantly on guard for potential threats around them.
"Master, look over there!" Dale suddenly pointed into the distance, her voice tinged with excitement.
Following her direction, Ron saw a massive building ruin.
It was a structure that might have once been some kind of temple or fortress, but now it had been distorted beyond recognition by abyssal energy.
The walls curved at impossible angles, and muscle-like tissue had grown between the stones, making it look like a skinned human organ.
The most striking feature was a tower in the center of the ruins, its top flickering with a ghostly blue light, like a beacon guiding the way.
"That must be it," Ron judged, "It’s likely the control point we’re looking for."
They quickened their pace toward the ruins, but the closer they got, the more Ron felt a strange unease.
The air was permeated by an unusual energy fluctuation, not the corrosive power of the abyss, but something older and purer.
"Master... something is watching us," Dale suddenly whispered, her keen Sea Siren senses picking up the anomalies around them.
Ron nodded; he too felt the sensation of being watched.
It was as if countless eyes were hiding in every shadow of the ruins, coldly observing the two intruders.
"Stay alert, don’t stray too far from me," Ron cautioned, his hand already resting on the hilt of his sword.
However, they reached the entrance to the ruins without encountering any attacks.
The eerie silence only heightened their unease.
The interior of the ruins presented a surreal scene.
Walls and floors were covered with a layer of pulsating flesh, occasionally twitching irregularly, making moist sounds;
Countless translucent sack-like structures hung from the ceiling, with vague humanoid outlines visible inside, but they were not entirely human, instead, they were some indescribable twisted beings;
The air was filled with a humid and cloyingly sweet smell, like the insides of some large creature.
Ron carefully avoided the quivering flesh on the ground, searching for a path to the central tower.
"Master, what are those?" Dale pointed to some strange symbols on the walls.
The symbols looked like some kind of ancient script.
But the lines twisted and flowed unnaturally, seeming to slither like a living thing on the stone walls.
Ron approached to examine them, only to find that the symbols subtly changed under his gaze, becoming harder to decipher, as if willfully avoiding comprehension.
"They must be ancient writings twisted by abyssal power, possibly documenting the history or purpose of this place."
Ron speculated but knew that now wasn’t the time to study ancient civilizations; they had to find the control point quickly.
Passing through a series of warped corridors and rooms, they finally reached an open space at the center of the ruins.
It seemed to have been a hall or a place of worship, now reduced to a ruin.
But the central altar remained intact, surrounded by several half-collapsed stone pillars.
On the altar stood the glowing tower, and they had to go through the altar to enter the tower.
"We are here, but..." Ron cautiously surveyed the surroundings:
"It’s too quiet, something’s not right."
Just as he finished speaking, the air around the altar suddenly warped, rippling like the surface of water.
Several blurry figures emerged from the air, gradually taking solid form.
They were five humanoid creatures wearing tattered armor, their skin a pallid gray covered with black patterns, eyes hollow yet glowing with ghostly blue light.
Their movements were perfectly synchronized, as if controlled by a single consciousness, drawing weapons from their waists and forming a circle around Ron and Dale, hemming them in the center.
"Shadow Nightmare Hunters..." Ron immediately recognized the creatures:
"Warriors who died on ancient battlefields, their souls twisted by abyssal power, turned into semi-corporeal beings."
Dale nervously moved closer to Ron, her hands starting to gather water elements, ready for battle.
"Master, they... seem to be waiting for something."
Indeed, the five shadow nightmare hunters did not attack immediately but remained on alert, as if awaiting a signal.
Ron stepped forward experimentally, and the five hunters reacted instantly, pointing their weapons at him, yet still refraining from attacking.
"They’re guarding the altar..." He quickly understood the situation:
"We have to deal with them to approach the control point."
He swiftly assessed the situation.
Shadow Nightmare Hunters are known for their speed and synchronized attacks, but their degree of materialization is low, giving them some resistance to physical attacks.
Conventional weapons have limited effect on them, but magic can counter them effectively.
"Dale, we need to coordinate," Ron said softly:
"You prepare the water prison technique, I’ll draw their attention."
The Little Sea Siren nodded, quietly stepped back a few paces, and began forming complex gestures, as water elements slowly gathered around her.
Ron, in turn, infused his longsword with spiritual power, coating it with a thin layer of light flame, the result of combining the "Ring of Brilliance" with his swordsmanship.
"Let’s go!"
He suddenly burst into action, charging towards the nearest shadow nightmare hunter at incredible speed.
The five hunters immediately sprang into motion, their actions as fast as lightning, launching an attack on Ron almost simultaneously.

chapters.title: Chapter 307 - 194: Wind Listener (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 307: Chapter 194: Wind Listener (Part 2)
Ron’s sword skill had already reached the Master Level, able to handle the assault of five enemies with ease.
His every strike was extraordinarily precise.
Everywhere the Light Flame Sword Blade swept, a faint crack would appear on the body of the Shadow Nightmare Hunter, emitting a painful screech.
"Now, Dale!"
Ron suddenly retreated a step, creating space for the Little Sea Siren’s magic.
—— Water Prison Technique!
Dale clapped her hands together fiercely, and the surrounding Water Element instantly coalesced, forming a massive water sphere, encasing all five Shadow Nightmare Hunters together.
The semi-corporeal warriors struggled in the water, but their movements became unusually slow, as if trapped in a quagmire.
"Sound Wave Oscillation - Erosion State!"
Ron seized the opportunity, launching his strongest magical attack once again.
Invisible ripples passed through the water sphere, directly affecting the bodies of the Shadow Nightmare Hunters.
The effect was immediate — the five Shadow Nightmare Hunters let out a simultaneous, shrill scream.
Their bodies began to twist violently, as if torn by some invisible force.
Black lines quickly spread, covering their entire bodies.
Soon after, these lines started to collapse, transforming into countless black particles that scattered in the water.
"We succeeded!" Dale exclaimed joyfully as she watched the enemies within the water sphere gradually disintegrate.
However, at that moment, the black particles suddenly began to gather, forming a vortex-like black cloud.
The vortex spun faster and faster, eventually condensing into a brand-new figure.
A huge, semi-transparent humanoid form, entirely pitch-black, with only its eyes and chest emitting a ghastly blue light.
"Fusion...?" Ron watched this scene in astonishment. "The Shadow Nightmare Hunters can actually fuse into a stronger existence."
This newborn monster waved a hand, and Dale’s Water Prison Technique was effortlessly shattered like paper, turning into splashes of water that scattered everywhere.
"Master, watch out!"
Dale had just cried out when the black giant instantly teleported right in front of Ron.
With a punch launched, the speed was so fast that its movement was almost invisible.
Ron didn’t panic, raising his sword to block.
The Flowing Shield Wall around his body began to function, providing him with a special defense against blunt force.
The massive fist, accompanied by a heavy whooshing sound, slammed down, only causing the fluid protection to dent inward.
Ron staggered back, his complexion looking slightly off.
He brushed his waist, and a shadow rapidly expanded, rushing towards the giant’s face...
.........
Meanwhile, in another section of the Bloodline Altar, a group of young people dressed in special robes were gathering together.
Their robes, although still gray, had crystal-like, shiny silver patterns trimming the collar and cuffs, starkly different from the apprentices of the Black Mist School.
Embroidered on the back was a pattern of a Crystal Tower, clearly indicating their identity — the elite apprentices of the Crystal Spire.
"Is everyone here?"
A young man standing in the center of the crowd asked, his voice carrying an indisputable authority.
His most notable feature was an unusually large pair of ears, almost twice the size of a normal person’s and much sharper, looking like two small fans from a distance.
This was the leader of the Crystal Spire apprentice team — Eliot Oswalt, a genius apprentice known among his peers as the "Wind Listener."
"Everyone’s here, Eliot."
A female apprentice with light gray hair responded, her eyes an unnatural purple, with her hands wrapped in dense silver runes:
"Jacqueline just reached this area through the link."
Eliot nodded, this female apprentice also possessed a Special Talent, serving as the team’s vice leader.
Just then, his large ears twitched slightly, as if catching some faint sound.
Everyone held their breath, knowing Eliot was using his Special Talent — the "Wind of Listening."
This was an extremely rare Special Talent, considered powerful even in the second tier.
Those with this talent could perceive energy fluctuations in the surrounding environment through their ears and translate them into information.
Simply put, his ears could "hear" information undetectable to ordinary people.
Including energy flow, spatial fluctuations, and even certain conceptual existences.
A moment later, Eliot opened his eyes, a trace of seriousness appearing on his face.
"The situation is more complicated than we anticipated." He looked around, his voice low:
"I’ve already ’heard’ some information about this altar’s trial."
The apprentices of the Crystal Spire immediately gathered around, their expressions turning solemn.
"Firstly, this space is indeed deeply tainted by the Abyss, but it seems that some force has limited the strength of the curse, allowing us to endure."
Eliot explained, his large ears still twitching, seemingly continuing to receive information.
"Secondly, I’ve ’heard’ a very important piece of information — the altar generated doppelgangers significantly enhanced in bloodline traits using us trialists as templates."
"Doppelgangers?" A robust male apprentice asked in surprise.
"Yes, Kaiser." Eliot confirmed:
"Each participant in the trial has a corresponding doppelganger in the center of the altar.
Defeating your own doppelganger can significantly enhance your bloodline; defeating someone else’s doppelganger allows you to gain part of their Elemental Affinity and some ability enhancements."
This news sparked a buzz of whispers, a glimmer of excitement and caution flashing in everyone’s eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 308 - 194: Wind Listener (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 308: Chapter 194: Wind Listener (Part 3)
"What about those abyssal mutants on the periphery?" Jacqueline asked, "Do they have any value?"
Eliot shook his head:
"Almost none. Their organs can be extracted as experimental materials, but they are difficult to process and mostly consume our energy and resources. The real value lies in the clones at the center of the altar."
He straightened his body, and his tone became more resolute:
"So, our strategy is clear—get through these peripheral areas as quickly as possible, head to the altar center, and kill our respective clones to gain bloodline enhancement. And then..."
He paused, a cold glint flashing in his eyes:
"If given the opportunity, we can also kill the clones of the Black Mist School apprentices. Those clones can also provide us with enhancement. At that time..."
"Every man for himself," Kaiser grinned, revealing a malicious expression.
Eliot didn’t directly respond, but his tacit approval was clear.
"Now, we need to move forward. According to the energy fluctuations, the nearest teleportation gate is in that direction."
He pointed to a distant hill covered in purple-black vines.
Just as the Crystal Tower Squad was about to set off, the surrounding environment suddenly changed.
The ground began to writhe, bulging like a living creature, forming undulating waves;
The clouds in the sky thickened, forming a disquieting spiral pattern;
The air was filled with a pungent sulfur smell, as if something was burning.
"They’re here." Eliot said calmly, his ears already catching the enemy’s movements.
As soon as the words fell, the ground around them burst open, and dozens of abyssal creatures poured out from the cracks.
These creatures were of various shapes, but all bore significant abyssal characteristics.
Some seemed like twisted humanoid forms, yet with too many limbs;
Some resembled a hybrid of insect and reptilian features;
There were some with no fixed shape at all, just a mass of continuously changing fleshy substances.
"Prepare for battle!" Eliot ordered, as he drew a magic wand made of crystal from inside his robe.
—First Ring: Atmospheric Cutting
With his action, the wand glowed a faint green.
The surrounding air twisted abruptly, forming an invisible wind blade that instantly sliced the nearest three abyssal creatures in half.
Other Crystal Tower apprentices immediately took action, displaying combat capabilities far beyond ordinary advanced apprentices.
Jacqueline’s hands danced, and lightning flashed between her ten fingers.
A giant electric grid quickly formed, enveloping a group of approaching abyssal crawlers, turning them into ash.
Kaiser, on the other hand, displayed astonishing physical strength.
His arms swelled to double their size in an instant, covered in a layer of red scales, and he could punch large abyssal mutants flying several meters with ease.
Another slim male apprentice—Noren, demonstrated precise elemental control abilities.
Ice-blue threads extended from his fingertips, coiling around enemies like flexible snakes, then rapidly tightened, freezing and slicing them into pieces.
Most impressive was a seemingly frail female apprentice—Lina.
With her eyes closed, dozens of mini light spheres floated around her.
Each one precisely shot at different enemies, penetrating their bodies, leaving smoking holes.
"Coordinated Formation!"
Eliot shouted, and everyone immediately moved to their predetermined positions, forming a perfect circular defensive formation.
This formation allowed everyone to maximize their advantages while compensating for each other’s weaknesses, showcasing extremely high combat efficiency.
Despite the large number of abyssal creatures, they were quickly cleared away by the orderly attacks of the Crystal Tower elite squad, without causing any casualties.
"Team cooperation ability—perfect."
Eliot commented, looking at the battlefield with satisfaction, "It seems the training was not in vain."
"The guys from the Black Mist School certainly don’t have this kind of camaraderie, nor the spiritual link our Lina’s talent provides."
Kaiser scoffed, "I bet they’re fighting individually right now, in complete disarray."
"Never underestimate any opponent."
Eliot warned:
"Especially that alchemist named Ron. It’s said that he possesses the special talent of ’medicinal body resonance,’ progressing at an astonishing speed."
Jacqueline mused, "I heard he’s a half-muggle with an initial spiritual power of only a Sixth-class Star..."
"Now he’s an advanced apprentice, and even ranks among the top candidates for the wizard lineup." Eliot reminded everyone:
"Such rapid progress is truly extraordinary."
"I’m actually quite looking forward to meeting his clone."
Kaiser grinned, "A guy with an alchemist background, how much fighting power could he possibly have..."

chapters.title: Chapter 309 - 95: The Third Hand
chapters.content:
Chapter 309: Chapter 95: The Third Hand
The black giant’s punch was as powerful as a mountain, and ordinary defense seemed like paper against such force.
Fortunately, Ron’s Flowing Shield Wall was not a common defensive technique.
Under the impact of the giant’s punch, it formed a special buffer structure, dispersing most of the shock around.
Even so, Ron felt a sharp pain in his chest, his whole body uncontrollably flying back several meters, nearly crashing into a stone pillar.
However, this level of attack, though strong, was still within his expectations.
"Master!"
Dale exclaimed in panic, water elements rapidly condensing at her fingertips, preparing to strike.
Her large violet-blue eyes were filled with worry and anger, her small body trembling slightly due to the imminent release of power.
"Don’t worry, Dale."
Ron’s voice was surprisingly calm, his fingers stroking the Stand-In Puppet at his waist, "I still have my secret weapon to use."
"It’s time to test your strength."
A portion of consciousness was slowly infused into the Stand-In Puppet.
With a massive influx of Magic Power, the inconspicuous little puppet immediately reacted.
It quickly expanded, its size growing to that roughly equal to a human within seconds.
Ron could feel part of his consciousness diverging into the puppet, forming a unique dual perception.
He could sense his own condition while also perceiving the surrounding environment through the puppet.
The black giant seemed to sense some kind of threat, its previously calm demeanor becoming wary, its dark blue eyes fixed intensely on the transforming puppet.
Under Ron’s mental control, the puppet’s exterior began to change.
Smooth surfaces revealed countless tiny scales, shimmering with a metallic sheen like snakeskin, integrating the Snake Demon traits;
Its limbs grew robust and powerful, with clear muscular contours, showcasing the strength of the Scorpion;
A tail, full of power, grew from its back, the tip’s stinger radiating a faint purple glow.
Ron could sense the innate memories of both the Snake Demon and Scorpion circulating in the puppet’s "consciousness."
All those combat techniques and bodily control experiences became resources he could call upon.
But the puppet itself lacked independent will, merely acting as a highly sophisticated tool, completely under Ron’s mental command.
"Dale, step back."
Ron instructed, simultaneously using the Spiritual Link to maneuver the Stand-In Puppet into a combat stance.
The black giant hesitated not at all, raising its hand with a powerful straight punch aimed directly at the puppet’s head.
The punch was swift, the air was split, creating a piercing whooshing sound.
Ron didn’t instruct the puppet to dodge, but directed it to raise an arm to meet the giant’s fist head-on.
This choice stemmed from his precise calculation of the puppet’s capabilities.
From previous experiments, he had confirmed the puppet’s special capacity to absorb Abyssal Material.
"Boom!"
The collision of forces produced a deafening, dull sound.
A shockwave spread from both centers, lifting loose stones from the ground several inches.
To Dale’s astonishment, the Stand-In Puppet not only didn’t get knocked back by the massive force but the black giant’s fist emitted a sizzling noise.
At the moment of contact, the giant’s fist seemed to hit some extremely unstable substance.
After a strange ripple appeared, it began to crumble as though being corroded.
Black material flaked from the giant’s fist, dripping like ink.
Yet these materials didn’t scatter onto the ground, instead being directly absorbed by the puppet’s skin.
"Just as I anticipated!"
Excitement flashed in Ron’s eyes.
This ability to absorb Abyssal Energy was indeed one of the most valuable traits of the Stand-In Puppet, and the effect was far more significant than he imagined.
At the same time, through the link with the puppet, he felt a peculiar energy flow.
The absorbed Abyssal Energy didn’t entirely assimilate into the puppet but underwent some special filtering, retaining only the useful parts.
This process was so similar to what he once envisioned in the "Melting Furnace Concept!"
The black giant seemed to realize the crisis, instantly withdrawing its damaged right hand, while its left turned into a sharp blade to sweep toward the puppet’s waist.
Ron, through the Spiritual Link, commanded the puppet to dodge.
The puppet’s movements had the incredible flexibility of the Snake Demon and fused with the explosive power of the Scorpion, easily evading the sweep.
While dodging, it used the scorpion’s tail to suddenly thrust forward, aimed straight at the giant’s chest.
The stinger pierced the black giant’s chest and immediately triggered a series of energy reactions.
The black giant’s body rippled like a lake struck by a massive rock.
Those originally stable black materials began to wobble and separate irregularly.
"Keep attacking!"
With a thought, Ron commanded the Stand-In Puppet to launch a fierce, relentless assault.
Under Ron’s control, the puppet demonstrated astonishing combat skills:
Right fist aimed straight at the giant’s soft ribs, left leg sweeping a trip, scorpion tail shadowing the movements to target vulnerabilities.
```
Each attack is incredibly precise, without any waste, perfectly combining the Snake Demon’s precision strike and the Scorpion’s ferocious power.
What satisfies Ron most is that whenever the puppet comes into contact with the black giant, a portion of black energy is absorbed.
As a result, the giant continuously weakens, while the puppet grows stronger.
"Boom!"
Another heavy punch, the puppet’s right fist slammed into the black giant’s abdomen like a cannonball, causing a dull thud.
The black giant staggered backward, a huge void appeared between its chest and abdomen, black energy constantly spilling from the wound.
Ron unhesitatingly manipulated the puppet to follow up.
The left leg swept out horizontally, precisely kicking the black giant’s knee.
"Crack!"
Although the body is composed of energy, it emitted a sound similar to bones fracturing.
The black giant’s right leg bent at an incredible angle, the entire body lost balance, leaning to one side.
Catching this moment, he used a spiritual link to control the puppet with both hands.
——like a lion tearing apart prey, fiercely grabbing the sides of the black giant’s head.
The claws directly sank into the black giant’s head, then fiercely pulled outward...
"Crack... Boom!"
The black giant’s head exploded like fireworks, transforming into countless black fragments scattered in the air.
"Amazing, Master!"
Dale jumped up in delight, her previous worries vanishing.
Ron did not indulge in this brief victory.
He noticed that although the black giant’s body lost its head, it still stubbornly regrouped, attempting to continue fighting.
This regeneration ability is one of the terrifying traits of abyss creatures.
But what surprised him even more was the reaction of the stand-in puppet at his waist.
After absorbing a large amount of black energy, it autonomously grew a third arm!
This new arm extended from the right shoulder blade, with a completely different structure from the original arms.
It was covered with dark purple scales all over, fingertips sharp as claws, emitting a faint blue glow.
"This is... the puppet adapting and integrating the newly absorbed energy." A hint of amazement rose in Ron’s heart.
He quickly adjusted his tactics, commanding the third arm to reach forward and penetrate the black giant’s chest, directly grabbing the glowing core.
That is the energy center after the merger of the Shadow Nightmare Hunter.
With the core held in hand, the black giant’s body completely lost support.
Like a sand sculpture washed by waves, it quickly collapsed, turning into a pool of black liquid, gathered at the stand-in puppet’s feet.
Ron controlled the stand-in puppet to pick up the core, meanwhile reaching out to touch the pool of black liquid, starting massive energy absorption.
As energy continued to be absorbed, the stand-in puppet’s body began undergoing subtle changes:
The surface became smoother, the muscle lines clearer, and the overall silhouette closer to a human form.
Most crucially, the third arm completely integrated into the overall structure, as if it was naturally present.
"Master... It... is becoming more like a living being." Dale said softly, with a hint of unease and curiosity in her voice.
"Don’t worry, it’s entirely under my control."
Ron reassured, while checking the stand-in puppet’s status through the spiritual link.
He could clearly perceive a data point:
[Automatically absorbed active abyssal material, charging progress +5%]
[Current energy: 8%/100%]
"Energy increased by 5%."
Ron calculated in his mind: "If in the future we truly explore the Great Abyss, the charging progress should increase very quickly."
50% charging level is the critical point for the stand-in puppet to unlock the "two-way interaction" trait.
Upon reaching this level, not only can the puppet fully replicate Ron’s abilities, but Ron can also, to some extent, acquire the traits absorbed by the puppet.
"Then, I can transfer the stand-in puppet to the Demon Hunter profession..."
Ron calculated in his mind, a slight curve unconsciously forming at the corner of his mouth:
"Gain all the Demon Hunter’s ability enhancements without bearing any transfer risk and side effects."
Imagining that possibility — the extraordinary perception ability, enhanced constitution, toxin resistance, and various specialized skills of the Demon Hunter, all utilized for oneself.
Yet, without having to endure the painful bodily transformation process and long-term side effects, a wave of anticipation arose in Ron’s heart.
Especially when facing various mutated creatures or "Awakened", the Demon Hunter possesses unique "demon hunting" attribute enhancements brought by professional traits, an advantage that other professions cannot replace.
As his thoughts flowed, the puppet already completed the energy absorption, quietly standing there, awaiting the next command.
At Ron’s gentle thought, it immediately shrank, returning to its original size, transforming back into an ordinary small puppet, returning to his hand.
"Now, it’s time to deal with the final matter."
He stowed away the stand-in puppet and walked towards the glowing stone pillar at the center of the altar.
The surface of the stone pillar was filled with ancient runes, emitting a faint blue light.
Ron used "Extraordinary Recognition" to carefully study these runes and discovered they formed a complex teleportation array.

chapters.title: Chapter 310 - 196: Land of Duel
chapters.content:
Chapter 310: Chapter 196: Land of Duel
"This should be able to transport us to the altar’s core region." He analyzed as he reached out to touch the stone pillar.
An unusual energy wave immediately spread from the point of contact, and the light of the stone pillar suddenly intensified, causing the surrounding air to warp and deform.
"Dale, hold onto me!" Ron advised, and the Little Sea Siren immediately grabbed his sleeve tightly.
In the next moment, a strong blue light enveloped them, and the surrounding scenery began to distort rapidly.
Their bodies were being pulled by an invisible force, flying toward an unknown destination...
Meanwhile, in another part of the Bloodline Altar, Trish was struggling on the edge of life and death.
The Swamp Assembler’s attacks were growing more ferocious, and each collision made the vine barrier she constructed tremble and sway.
Even worse, this terrifying creature seemed able to absorb the vines it destroyed, making itself more powerful.
"Damn... At this rate, I won’t last much longer..." Trish gritted her teeth, sweat soaking through the lining of her long robe.
Her Forest Elf bloodline provided her some advantage in plant manipulation, but most plants in this environment had already been contaminated by Abyssal Power.
They were slow to respond to her commands, and each summoning consumed a large amount of Spiritual Power.
In desperation, Trish decided to take a risky new approach.
"If they’ve already been contaminated by the abyss... then perhaps..."
She closed her eyes, took a deep breath, and changed her summoning method.
Instead of resisting the Abyssal Power within the plants, she attempted to resonate with it, borrowing rather than rejecting that abnormal energy.
To her surprise, the previously sluggish swamp plants suddenly became extraordinarily active!
Countless vines, glowing with a purple-black hue, extended from the depths of the swamp, ten times more than before.
"I see... these Abyssal Plants... are more sensitive to specific summoning methods!"
Trish’s eyes brightened with a glimmer of hope.
She immediately adjusted her strategy, no longer simply commanding the plants, but allowing her Spiritual Power to flow into them like water, guiding them to act according to her will.
The Swamp Assembler seemed to sense the threat, emitting a furious roar as it accelerated toward Trish.
Yet every step it took was obstructed by countless newly grown vines, which were not only numerous but extremely resilient, even capable of swift regeneration after being destroyed.
"This regenerative ability... is completely unlike ordinary plants!"
Trish was amazed to find that these swamp plants had astonishing vitality, significantly enhancing the effects of her Natural Magic.
Taking advantage of the moment, Trish quickly retrieved a vial of emerald potion from her storage bag and drank it without hesitation.
This was a Bloodline Activation Agent specially prepared by Master Corina, capable of greatly enhancing her affinity with Natural Elements in a short period.
The effect was almost immediate—her Forest Elf bloodline power was instantly activated, a faint green glow suffusing her body, with tiny leaf-vein patterns appearing on her skin.
As Trish adapted to her surge in power, she marveled at the peculiar connection she formed with these Abyssal Plants.
She could sense the presence of every plant in the swamp, as if they had become extensions of her own body, bending to her will.
"Now’s the time!" Trish traced a complex symbol with her hands in front of her chest, chanting a spell.
Countless thick vines converged from all directions in the swamp, weaving into a gigantic net that completely ensnared the Swamp Assembler.
No matter how it struggled and roared, it could not break free from the cage woven by Abyssal Plants.
Trish didn’t waste the opportunity and immediately dashed toward the stone monument.
All the while, she keenly noted some special plants in the swamp and the tissue fragments dropped in the battle with the Swamp Assembler.
"These materials... they emit unusual energy fluctuations."
Trish stopped and quickly used isolating containers to collect several seeds from swamp plants, along with a small fragment of the Swamp Assembler’s tissue.
These seeds emitted a faint purple light in her hand, immediately responding when she infused a bit of Spiritual Power at her fingertips, forming a miniature energy circuit.
"As casting media, their effect should be quite extraordinary."
Trish carefully secured these materials and continued her run toward the stone monument.
When her hand finally touched the stone monument’s surface, an indescribable sense of relief surged in her heart.
The stone monument instantly illuminated brightly, enveloping her within.
During the teleportation, Trish considered the newly acquired materials in her pocket, already contemplating how to integrate them into her Magic System.
"Perhaps Ron will be interested in these materials."
She thought: "With his skill in material recognition, he should be able to better utilize the value of these Abyssal Materials."
In the canyon region, Holt’s situation was even more dire.
The bone worm’s drill-like oral apparatus spun as it crashed into the Earth Elemental Golem, emitting a piercing metal grinding sound.
The golem’s right arm was completely severed in the attack, stones and soil scattering everywhere.
Despite this, Holt remained calm, continuously channeling Spiritual Power, ensuring the golem continued to fight.
"This kind of power... it’s practically cheating..." he whispered through clenched teeth, his expression already tinged with despair.
The bone worm’s combat capability far exceeded his expectations.
That drill attack, capable of effortlessly crushing any substance, was inflicting tremendous damage even on the Earth Elemental Golem, known for its durability.

chapters.title: Chapter 311 - 196: Dueling Grounds (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 311: Chapter 196: Dueling Grounds (Part 2)
The most despairing thing is, the speed of the bone worm does not match its size at all.
Its mobility both above and below ground is astonishing, making it difficult for Holt’s giant statue to capture its trajectory.
"Against this kind of enemy, even an Advanced Apprentice can hardly resist..."
Holt even began to feel that he might perish here today: "Just like the Scorpion at the gladiator arena, but now it’s just me alone..."
At this point, the giant statue was already in tatters:
The right arm completely lost, the left leg severely damaged below the knee, a large hole in the chest, with the Energy Core faintly visible.
While it seemed the bone worm was just starting to stretch its body, constantly emitting deafening howls, circling the altar, looking for the next chance to attack.
"Continuing like this is certainly a dead end..." Holt quickly pondered a strategy.
Going head-to-head with the bone worm is clearly unwise, he needs to take a different approach.
Observing the environment around the altar carefully, Holt noticed that the seven stone pillars seem to form some kind of Energy Array.
Each time the bone worm approached a stone pillar, the red crystal would glimmer slightly.
"These stone pillars... might be some kind of defense mechanism!" Holt had a flash of inspiration.
He ordered the giant statue to grab a huge rock and throw it with all its might at the nearest stone pillar.
Once the red crystal atop the stone pillar was hit, it immediately erupted with a dazzling red light, directly towards the bone worm.
The bone worm let out a painful shriek, its body suddenly bounced up, clearly injured.
"Just as I thought!" Holt’s eyes lit up, and he immediately changed his tactics.
He no longer let the giant statue confront the bone worm directly, instead instructed it to attack the crystals atop the remaining six stone pillars.
The bone worm seemed to sense Holt’s intention, frantically charging towards the giant statue, trying to stop it.
A race against time began — the giant statue, dragging its damaged body, dodged the bone worm’s attacks while striving to activate the remaining pillars;
while the bone worm pursued relentlessly, trying to completely destroy the giant statue before it completed its task.
Holt was fully focused, constantly channeling Spiritual Power into the giant statue, even if it meant enduring immense mental strain.
When the sixth stone pillar was activated, the bone worm was already within reach, its malicious giant maw almost devouring the head of the statue.
At the critical moment, the statue used its last ounce of strength to lunge towards the final stone pillar.
"Boom!"
The statue and the bone worm collided with the pillar simultaneously, with the red crystal activating at the same time, the statue was completely destroyed, scattering into countless fragments.
However, as the seven pillars were all activated, the entire altar began to emit a dazzling red light.
Seven beams converged at the center, forming a massive energy vortex.
The bone worm was stunned by the sudden light, letting out painful shrieks, its body convulsing uncontrollably.
Meanwhile, Holt took this opportunity to dash towards the altar’s center, while quickly retrieving the giant statue’s core.
The statue’s destruction would only consume a large amount of his Magic Power, as long as the Energy Core of the "Heart of the Earth," the gladiator arena runner-up reward, wasn’t damaged, he could have a chance to construct another statue.
When Holt’s feet touched the central platform, a powerful Energy Fluctuation immediately enveloped him, the surrounding scenery began to twist and distort.
At the last moment as he was transmitted away, he glanced back at the gigantic, writhing worm, with a sigh in his heart:
"To succeed... truly it was fortunate. Among the Black Mist School, apart from Trish and me, others would hardly break through such a level of Guardian alone..."
But then, Holt recalled the Alchemist who displayed astonishing power at the gladiator arena—Ron.
"Perhaps... Ron would find it much easier than I did..."
With this vague thought, Holt’s figure completely disappeared into the dazzling light, heading towards the unknown altar core region...
.........
Trish was the first to arrive at the Bloodline Altar core area.
When the dazzling light faded, what lay before her surprised her—it was entirely different from the peripheral areas.
Gone was the suffocating Swamp, the twisted and deformed creatures were absent, and even the oppressive feel characteristic of the Abyss lightened significantly.
Instead, there was a misty, open plain, the ground paved with rough gravel.
The air carried a slight moisture but lacked the nauseating stench.
"Here... there are almost no traces of the Abyss." Trish surveyed her surroundings, her brows slightly furrowed.
Judging from the terrain, this area is circular, the ground gently inclined towards the center.
The overall impression felt like a deliberately crafted arena, specifically prepared for some kind of duel or ritual.
"It’s as if someone intentionally purified this region, creating a battlefield setting."
She looked through the fog, trying to discern more details, but the thick mist obscured her sight, allowing her to see only a few dozen meters around.
"I have to ensure my safety first, then wait for the others to arrive."
Trish took a deep breath and retrieved a small cloth bag from her Storage Bag, gently untying the knot.
The bag contained a special spore plant, displaying a pale green, glowing faintly in her palm.
This was one of the special plants she began cultivating after awakening her Forest Elf bloodline—Perception Spores.
They could spread with the wind and relay information about the surrounding environment to their master.
"Go, my little scouts."
Trish gently blew towards them, and the spores scattered like tiny snowflakes into the mist surrounding her.

chapters.title: Chapter 312 - 196: Field of Duel (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Chapter 312: Chapter 196: Field of Duel (Part 3)
A moment later, she closed her eyes, connecting her spiritual power with the spores, and began to receive the information they transmitted back.
Through this method, she could roughly "see" the terrain and objects within a radius of several hundred meters.
Although not very clear, it was enough to provide a basic warning function.
"No signs of hostile creatures... at least for now."
She let out a slight sigh of relief and then sank into thought.
"The experiences in the Swamp area... those Abyssal Plants responded to me in an entirely different way."
Recalling her encounters in the Swamp, Trish still felt a trace of incredulity.
When she changed her summoning method, no longer rejecting the Abyssal Energy in those plants, but instead trying to resonate with it, a miracle occurred.
"Those vines’ vitality... it was incredible. They were not only numerous but also extremely tenacious and with a strong regeneration ability."
This special connection allowed her to trap the Swamp Assembler, buying time to reach the control point.
